touchdesigner_version: 2023.11xxx / 2025.30000+ (validate POP params on the live build)
note: Tool-mapped workflow recipes for touchdesigner-bridge-mcp — GUIDES, not gospel. Each recipe is ONE proven way to make façade projection-mapping CONTENT with this server's real typed tools; TouchDesigner offers many valid approaches, so treat a recipe as a worked example to understand and ADAPT. Each is an ordered sequence of tools plus the parameters that actually move the result, with a per-step landmark (the OUT_ null to plant) + verify (the cheap read to run). Data-only: recipes never run themselves. TouchDesigner's job is CONTENT CREATION; the physical warp/blend onto the real surface is done downstream by the media server (Pixera/disguise). Output/export is WIRE-ONLY by design — the recipe builds and wires the network with active/record OFF; the operator fires the record/stream. Grounded in Derivative wiki research + validated render-lane findings; validate exact param values against the live node UI for hero work.

routing.input_element: a building / a 3D model of a façade (.obj / .abc / .fbx / .usd)
routing.geometry_class: poly mesh -> rendered 2D image (TOP)
routing.notes: static .obj renders directly from a File In SOP; FBX -> fbxCOMP; animated -> alembicSOP.

routing.input_element: generative pattern / energy / light-sweep / abstract texture (no geometry); OR post-processing an existing render
routing.geometry_class: pure TOP network (2D image)
routing.notes: the bread-and-butter façade content lane; feedback trails, composites, colour/tone.

routing.input_element: a point cloud / drone photogrammetry scan of a building
routing.geometry_class: position data in a TOP -> instanced points -> rendered image
routing.notes: TD ingests a finished cloud (photogrammetry is external). TOP-instancing is the documented path; POP family is forward-looking. pointtransformTOP (normalize/align) is NOW in the catalog -- use it for the align step.

routing.input_element: aligning content to the real building surface / matching a camera or projector
routing.geometry_class: camera framing (ortho or perspective)
routing.notes: author framing only; the media server (Pixera/disguise) owns the physical warp.

routing.input_element: finished content -> media server (Pixera/disguise) or a 4K file
routing.geometry_class: output op (wire-only)
routing.notes: WIRE-ONLY: the bridge wires the op with active/record OFF; the operator fires it. HAP file is the safest default; NDI/Spout for live. renderstreamoutTOP (frames back to disguise) is NOW in the catalog -- the disguise return path is available (see live_media_server_feed).

routing.input_element: a segmented / pre-sectioned building model (multiple OBJ parts, e.g. section_00.obj … section_NN.obj exported per-part from Houdini) that you want to light/animate PER SECTION
routing.geometry_class: N poly meshes -> N addressable Geometry COMPs -> one rendered 2D image (TOP)
routing.notes: The pre-sectioned model is the EASY-MODE input (already meshed+segmented+UV'd, one OBJ per architectural part). One material per object is MANDATORY — TD cannot scope a material to part of a merged mesh, so each section must be its own geometryCOMP. Build the rig first; then animate with height_sweep_choreography (or any per-section choreography). If handed a single merged building.obj or a raw point cloud, this lane does NOT apply — segmentation is upstream (Houdini).

routing.input_element: a built per-section rig (sec00..secNN + mat00..matNN emit surfaces) that you want to animate as a travelling light 'height sweep' revealing sections bottom->top over time
routing.geometry_class: CHOP network exporting matNN:emitr/g/b (data-only animation driver)
routing.notes: Invoked as a task ON an existing per_section_material_rig. Drives each section's emission from a single ping-pong LFO by section height — a smooth vertical wipe, entirely via CHOP-export (no expressions, no code). Sibling-parent requirement: the driver null and the materials must share a parent for autoname export to resolve.

routing.input_element: a per-section rig + want ACTUAL VIDEO/imagery projected onto each surface
routing.geometry_class: moviefileinTOP(s) -> each section's phong emitmap (UV-registered) -> one rendered 2D image (TOP)
routing.notes: Invoked as a task ON an existing per_section_material_rig. Drives ACTUAL video onto each section by setting matNN.emitmap = a moviefileinTOP with emitmapcoord=uv0 (samples the section's baked UVs). emitmap is MULTIPLIED by emit color, so the height_sweep_choreography export onto emitr/g/b reveals/fades the video per section for free. Prefer one shared content TOP (UVs place it); windows keep a blank emitmap + emit 0. Needs UVs on the sections; N distinct clips = N GPU decodes.

routing.input_element: a per-section rig + want sections sequenced/revealed over a timeline — a cued show
routing.geometry_class: cue table (tableDAT from cues.csv) -> timerCHOP eased channels -> per-section emit/opacity export + scene crossfades
routing.notes: Invoked as a task ON an existing per_section_material_rig. Show-structure layer: a cue table (literal per-section values loaded from a working-dir cues.csv via tableDAT.file) feeds a timerCHOP with Ease In/Out interpolation (On Done = Re-Start) to glide each section through its cues, applied via the proven autoname CHOP-export or wire-only masking, with scene arcs via crossTOP/switchTOP. Layers on the height sweep (mult) and per-section video. Data-only: no expressions/Python/callbacks.

routing.input_element: a finished façade composite + need projector keystone/alignment and output to projector/file/media-server
routing.geometry_class: cornerpinTOP numeric keystone -> aligned null -> windowCOMP / moviefileoutTOP / NDI / Spout (wire-only)
routing.notes: Invoked as a task on a finished composite (OUT_facade_video / OUT_render / OUT_choreo). Applies a DATA-ONLY 4-corner keystone (cornerpinTOP pin* corners, mapping=perspective), plants an aligned null, then WIRES the output: a windowCOMP perform window to the real projector (multi-display aware), or moviefileoutTOP / ndioutTOP / syphonspoutoutTOP. WIRE-ONLY: window not opened, record/active OFF. The on-site 6-point/hand-dragged calibration is a HUMAN step whose numbers get typed back via set_par.

routing.input_element: a per-section rig you want to LIGHT/ANIMATE with colors, brightness, opacity, washes or color-sweeps -- WITHOUT video
routing.geometry_class: per-section emit color/brightness driven data-only (matNN:emitr/g/b export)
routing.notes: The no-video light lane over per_section_material_rig: emit is 3 exportable scalars, so brightness x per-section RGB = arbitrary per-section color+brightness+fade. Route A keyframes color via a write_csv cue table; Route B multiplies constant colors by an animated brightness.

routing.input_element: a per-section rig where real WINDOWS/recesses must stay BLACK (projected content off the glass)
routing.geometry_class: grayscale UV-space mask multiplied into the emit content (windows=0 -> black texels)
routing.notes: The punched-out-black-windows look. Mask x content in TOP space -> assign the product to emitmap (uv0). Mechanism data-only-buildable; a window-aligned mask for irregular arches is an upstream Houdini-baked/painted asset.

routing.input_element: a finished facade composite that must be split across >=2 OVERLAPPING projectors with an invisible blended seam
routing.geometry_class: per-projector crop+keystone+ramp-mask+gamma+multiply -> per-projector window (masks sum to 1)
routing.notes: The data-only native stand-in for camSchnappr Auto-Blend / projectorBlend. Blend-unity; overlap width/corners/gamma are human-measured on-site and typed back via set_par. Extends projection_align_and_output.

routing.input_element: a live external controller (OSC app / lighting console, music/audio, a DMX-ArtNet-sACN desk, or MIDI) that should drive the facade in real time
routing.geometry_class: live-input CHOP -> rename to matNN:emit -> the shared autoname-export apply-block (reactive facade)
routing.notes: Reactive / externally-controlled facade. Swap ONLY the source node (oscin/audio/dmxin/midiin); the rename->merge->null->autoname-export apply-block is identical to the sweep. One exporter per param; wildcard-capture rename is order-robust.

routing.input_element: RUN THE SHOW / show control / playback transport: a built facade rig that must run as a timed show -- cues, GO buttons, next-cue, looping, or timecode/LTC/SMPTE sync
routing.geometry_class: timerCHOP transport (segments + fraction + GO via the pulse actuator) -> selects cues that drive the shared export apply-block; optional timecode lock
routing.notes: The RUN-THE-SHOW layer above choreography. Timer walks a segments table (write_csv); GO = the allowlisted `pulse` actuator (start/cue/goto*); external triggers = toggle exports; timecodeCHOP locks to LTC/MTC/system for festival sync. Reuse facade_cue_choreography's cue table + apply-block. Keywords: show control, run the show, playback, cue, GO, transport, timecode, LTC, SMPTE, sequencing.

routing.input_element: a segmented building model + a content video, and you want to project video on surfaces / project video / spray video onto a building / video mapping — one call to import the sections and blast the clip onto each façade surface
routing.geometry_class: N OBJ parts -> import_segmented_model builds sec*/mat* (UVs intact) -> per-section emitmap (uv0) -> one rendered 2D image (TOP) -> WIRE-ONLY 4K file
routing.notes: The end-to-end video-mapping flow: copy the section OBJs UNDER the working dir (assets/sections/ — the F2 path confinement blanks external paths), import_segmented_model to build the whole sec*/mat* rig in ONE call (it forces the File In SOP to CONSTANT mode so the real OBJ loads, not TD's defgeo sample box), then set_par_many drives a moviefileinTOP onto every matNN.emitmap with emitmapcoord=uv0. For driving video onto an EXISTING hand-built rig, or for the sweep-modulated reveal, see segmented_facade_video_content. Keywords: video on surfaces, project video, spray video onto a building, video mapping.

routing.input_element: a finished facade composite you need to WARP onto a curved / multi-plane / irregular surface -- freeform warp / mesh warp / warp video onto a mesh / bend content to follow a building (the data-only analog of kantanMapper / MadMapper mesh warp)
routing.geometry_class: TOP composite + a data-only remapTOP UV map (identity UV field + control-grid offset) -> warped TOP
routing.notes: The data-only analog of kantanMapper: build an identity UV field (rampTOP+reorderTOP), add a control-grid offset (write_csv->tableDAT->dattoCHOP->choptoTOP->blur), remapTOP applies it. Bypassing the offset reproduces the source exactly; a non-zero grid visibly bends content. The interactive per-vertex drag is the HUMAN step; numbers typed back via CSV/set_par. Keywords: freeform warp, mesh warp, warp video onto a mesh, kantan, bend content onto a surface.

routing.input_element: drive DMX / Art-Net / sACN OUTPUT from TouchDesigner -- control lights / fixtures / LED / wash from TD, DMX output, art-net output, pixel-mapping in sync with the projection
routing.geometry_class: CHOP channel-set (per-slot / per-fixture values) -> dmxoutCHOP universe (Route A); coloured POP -> dmxfixturePOP -> dmxoutPOP (Route B). WIRE-ONLY, active=off
routing.notes: TD as a lighting SOURCE. Route A CHOP->dmxoutCHOP (active=off held); Route B POP->dmxfixturePOP->dmxoutPOP for pixel-mapping. dmxoutCHOP.active DEFAULTS ON -> bridge MUST set off; going live is the operator's wire-only step. artnetDAT.callbacks is a denied code-sink and is NOT the output path. Keywords: DMX output, art-net, sACN, control lights, fixtures, LED, wash, pixel mapping.

routing.input_element: project content FROM a calibrated projector onto a 3D building / spatial projection mapping onto geometry / map a projector onto a mesh (a real projector's lens + position, not a flat 2D warp and not a camera match)
routing.geometry_class: 3D geometry lit by a projector frustum (or projector-baked UVs) -> rendered 2D image (TOP)
routing.notes: the projector-frustum path: a lightCOMP cone with projmap (projmapmode=useview) or projectionPOP-computed UVs from a calibrated projector cameraCOMP; calibrate via focal/aperture or a measured 4x4 in projmatrixop. Distinct from mesh_freeform_warp (2D remapTOP warp) and camera_match_facade (virtual-camera registration).

routing.input_element: map video/images onto MULTIPLE flat or quad surfaces -- several shop windows, stage flats, sign faces, building faces treated as quads; a different source per surface, each warped to its own corners; 'multi-surface mapping', 'multiple quads', 'kantan quads', 'assign a video per surface', 'map several windows', 'quad projection mapping'
routing.geometry_class: N content TOPs -> per-quad cornerpinTOP (extract crop + pin keystone) -> one compositeTOP (over) over a black canvas -> one projector-res image (TOP)
routing.notes: The data-only kantanMapper substitute for 2D multi-surface mapping (distinct from projection_align_and_output's SINGLE global keystone and mesh_freeform_warp's SINGLE remapTOP mesh warp). Per-quad 4-corner pins; on-site corner-drag is the HUMAN step, numbers typed back via set_par.

routing.input_element: camSchnappr, calibrate projector to 3D model, projector calibration, OpenCV calibrateCamera / camera solve, mapamok, align projector to building, projection matrix from survey/solve, load intrinsics extrinsics into camera, projector pose
routing.geometry_class: physical structure + dimensionally-matched 3D twin (point-correspondence calibration)
routing.notes: Use when a REAL solve/survey produced (or will produce) calibration numbers to load. Builds the data-only target cameraCOMP `project` + geo/render/output scaffold + intrinsics/extrinsics intake DATs; the human runs camSchnappr (Python+OpenCV .tox, NOT instantiable) / an OpenCV solve / a survey ONCE on-site, and its two Table DATs (extrinsics pose + intrinsics projection matrix) are typed back via set_par/write_csv or referenced by projmatrixop/xformmatrixop (Vulkan [0,1] matrix). DISTINCT from projector_calibrated_3d, which casts content from a virtual projector set by focal/aperture or a synthetic matrix rather than loading a measured solve. Vendor-file path (viosoTOP/scalabledisplayTOP) covered as a variant.

routing.input_element: a finished/keystoned facade composite that must NOT spill light off the surface -- garbage mask / holdout matte / kill light on ground/sky/neighbors / mask projector sides / hide the rectangular beam edge / soft frame-edge feather / clip content to the building outline
routing.geometry_class: screen-space (post-keystone) holdout matte + soft-edge feather multiplied into the final composite -> masked projector plate
routing.notes: SCREEN-space, applied AFTER cornerpinTOP -- distinct from facade_mask_atlas (UV-space window mask into emitmap); a building can need BOTH. matteTOP is TD's purpose-built 3-input holdout op. Irregular traced silhouette PNG is an upstream HUMAN asset; analytic rectangleTOP/circleTOP/rampTOP unions (variant build_from_shapes) are fully data-only. 256px trap on every mask node.

routing.input_element: a live performer/talent standing in front of the mapped surface who must be held OUT of the projected content so no light washes across their face
routing.geometry_class: chromakeyTOP HSV key on a live videodeviceinTOP/ndiinTOP feed -> alpha holdout composited out of content (compositeTOP operand=outside / matteTOP)
routing.notes: Talent-holdout sub-lane (variant talent_holdout) of the spill/garbage mask recipe. chromakeyTOP huemin/huemax + hsoft/ssoft/vsoft ranges + invert + rgbout=multalpha. Live capture is a WIRE-ONLY input; keying + composite are data-only.

routing.input_element: feed disguise / Resolume / Pixera / MadMapper / Notch / another TouchDesigner LIVE; Spout (same-PC), NDI (networked, groups, alpha), Touch Out (TD<->TD), RenderStream (frustum/schema); live media-server handoff; sender name; low latency
routing.geometry_class: TOP (2D image) -> live per-frame GPU/network send
routing.lane: output / live media-server feed (WIRE-ONLY, active OFF)
routing.notes: The LIVE sibling of output_handoff (which bakes a file). Every send op (syphonspoutoutTOP/ndioutTOP/touchoutTOP/renderstreaminCHOP) DEFAULTS active ON -> built OFF, renamed off defaults. RenderStream: renderstreaminTOP (receive disguise video) + renderstreamoutTOP (send frames back) are NOW in the catalog, so the bidirectional image loop is buildable; the Camera COMP frustum still needs matrix expressions (not default-data-only -> expr lane / human). NDI/Spout/HAP remain fallbacks.

routing.input_element: drive the projector(s) directly from TouchDesigner; perform window; multi-display spanning / edge-to-edge; Direct Display / perfect playback / compositor bypass; front-of-house; genlock / framelock / Quadro Sync
routing.geometry_class: TOP (2D image) -> physical projector output(s)
routing.lane: output / direct-to-projector (WIRE-ONLY; window built-but-closed, Direct Display active OFF)
routing.notes: TD is front-of-house, no media server. windowCOMP multi-display (justifyoffsetto=alldisplays, borders off, blocksleep on) built CLOSED — open is a pulse the operator fires with F1; directdisplayoutTOP 'perfect playback' active DEFAULTS ON -> built OFF and gated to RTX/Quadro + Win11-Enterprise (+Mosaic). Complements projection_align_and_output (keystone) with the Direct Display lane + genlock.

routing.input_element: dark content, black level, black-level mask, black-level uplift, doubled black, overlap band lighter grey, seam grey on black, deep grey, blacklevel
routing.geometry_class: flat facade composite / per-projector blended TOP
routing.notes: Dark-content FOLLOW-ON to multiprojector_edge_blend: overlap band shows a lighter-grey rectangle because two projectors' non-true-black sums; raise black OUTSIDE the overlap to match. constantTOP measured floor x feathered coverage mask -> addTOP onto blended content -> re-point the edge-blend window. Floor (per channel) + feather are HUMAN. Contrast caveat: best 2-proj panoramas.

routing.input_element: projector stacking, stacked projectors, double brightness, brighter image, redundancy, backup projector, convergence, two projectors same area, lumens
routing.geometry_class: full-frame composite (same surface, no tiling)
routing.notes: SAME area, not bigger canvas: identical content -> per-unit cornerpin CONVERGENCE -> optional level trim -> window per display. NO crop / NO blend (the whole difference from edge-blend). differenceTOP = convergence proof. Convergence + trim HUMAN. Doubles black (contrast halves), ~15% perceived brightness, but redundancy. Hybrid: stack pairs then edge-blend halves.

routing.input_element: dome / fulldome / planetarium / fisheye / dome master / 360 / equirectangular / immersive wrap-around room / spherical / stereo-360 VR video
routing.geometry_class: 3D scene -> immersive master image (TOP): fisheye 1:1 or equirectangular 2:1
routing.notes: PREFERRED cubemap path (renderTOP rendermode=cubemap -> projectionTOP input=cubemap output=fisheye, fov 180/210, 1:1); fisheye180 direct = real-time but smears large polys (tessellate); equirect output MUST be 2:1; cubemapods = stereo 360; dualparaboloid is legacy (never an output). Aspect load-bearing; 256px trap on both renderTOP and projectionTOP. Dome projector/lens calibration is HUMAN on-site.

routing.input_element: single wide curved / cylindrical / panoramic / arc screen driven by multiple overlapping projectors; curved-screen warp + soft-edge blend
routing.geometry_class: flat composite (TOP) -> cylindrically warped + blended wide canvas (TOP)
routing.notes: remapTOP bends the flat composite onto the curve (data-only analog of a warp mesh; ramp map = linear stand-in, exact curvature from calibration), then reuse multiprojector_edge_blend (cropTOP slices + rampTOP/levelTOP falloff + layoutTOP). Calibrated path = viosoTOP/scalabledisplayTOP consuming an EXTERNAL calibration file (HUMAN). Sibling of dome_fisheye_master; seam alignment + blend luminance tuned on-site.

routing.input_element: on-site rig-and-focus: need to PROJECT a test pattern / alignment grid / registration grid / focus chart / colour bars / grayscale or gamma chart / convergence crosshatch for stacked projectors / edge-blend overlap markers / a native-resolution 1:1 pixel check / a numbered per-projector ident -- to set up, focus, align and QC projectors BEFORE running show content
routing.geometry_class: pure typed generator ops (2D TOPs + one gridSOP rendered through an orthographic cameraCOMP) -> switchTOP-selected pattern -> wire-only output at projector native res
routing.notes: The setup-time SIBLING of projection_align_and_output (which consumes finished content and applies the keystone) and multiprojector_edge_blend (which builds content-time blend ramps): this one GENERATES the reference imagery the projectionist projects to align/focus/converge/colour-match, then hands the live pattern WIRE-ONLY to a projector/file/media server at NATIVE resolution with no resampling. DATA-ONLY throughout. Honest limits carried in governance: no grid TOP (gridSOP+ortho render), tileTOP not exposed, native Palette:testGrid/checker are GLSL .tox (human/GLSL-lane alternative for a fine checkerboard). Physical focus/aim/convergence and projector-side scaling are HUMAN steps.

routing.input_element: finished video clips / a show built from rendered media; play a movie or clip; a media player; a playlist / clip library / cue list; gapless clip switching; now playing / next; media-server clip layer for a flat or whole-surface projection (not per-section, not generative)
routing.geometry_class: moviefileinTOP deck(s) -> gapless A/B crossTOP or N-clip switchTOP, folder/table cue list, timer auto-advance -> tapped program stream (TOP)
routing.notes: The finished-video content atom for a FLAT/whole-surface canvas -- distinct from segmented_facade_video_* (per-section emit onto a mesh) and generative_texture_fx (procedural fields). Data-only 4K playback (codec/preread/loop/cue/trim/speed) + playlist (folderDAT/tableDAT -> crossTOP/switchTOP, timerCHOP GO via the pulse actuator). WIRE-ONLY out; feeds output_handoff / projection_align_and_output, and is a layer SOURCE for layer_compositor. Palette moviePlaylist/moviePlayer are Python .tox = reference only. 256 trap + N-decoder play-gating are the headline gotchas.

routing.input_element: finished sources you want to STACK/MIX; multi-layer compositing; a VJ / media-server layer stack; per-layer opacity, blend mode, transform; master fade to black / blackout; crossfade / dissolve / luma-wipe between scenes; overlay layers on a flat / whole-surface show
routing.geometry_class: N (source->transformTOP->levelTOP) layers -> layermixTOP stack (per-layer opacity/blend/transform, black bg) + master levelTOP fade + crossTOP/luma-wipe transitions -> composite (TOP)
routing.notes: Invoked as a task ON sources you already have (media_clip_player streams, generative fields, stills, live in). SPATIAL simultaneous stacking -- orthogonal to media_clip_player's TEMPORAL one-of-N selection; a playlist can be one layer of the stack, so keep them separate/composable. layermixTOP operand=opperlayer gives per-layer blend modes (not layoutTOP, which is a grid). Master fade = trailing levelTOP.opacity. Transitions data-only (set_par or bound timer fraction). WIRE-ONLY out; feeds projection_align_and_output / multiprojector_edge_blend / mesh_freeform_warp.

routing.input_element: camera, webcam, IR camera, depth sensor, kinect, orbbec, presence, silhouette, shadow, motion, people, interactive wall, touch-to-reveal, blob, tracking, vision
routing.geometry_class: TOP (live image -> presence/motion mask)
routing.notes: Data-only CORE is a silhouette/motion MASK (camera -> mono -> lumalevel threshold -> blur) used as a matte/displace; frame-difference replaces the ABSENT opticalflowTOP; single-blob centroid gives one XY with no tracker. Depth sensors orbbecTOP/orbbecselectTOP/realsenseTOP/kinectazureTOP(+CHOP) are NOW in the catalog (true fg/bg + XYZ + skeleton when the hardware is present); opticalflowTOP and nvidiabackgroundTOP are still absent; blobtrackTOP's position table needs a Callbacks DAT (code); blobtrackCHOP is data-only but needs a point/depth CHOP feed. No thresholdTOP -- use lumalevelTOP.

routing.input_element: audio, sound, music, FFT, spectrum, bass, kick, snare, beat, onset, band energy, audio-reactive, VJ
routing.geometry_class: CHOP (audio/energy) + TOP (generative image)
routing.notes: GENERATES content from sound (FFT + band energy + onset -> displace/feedback/colour/instancing), deeper than realtime_input_driver which only ROUTES an audio channel onto per-section emit. Rebuilds the palette:audioAnalysis Low/Mid/High/Kick/Snare bundle from typed ops (that palette is a .tox, not an operator). beatCHOP is a tempo clock, not an onset detector -- onset = envelope->logicCHOP->triggerCHOP. Smoothing (lagCHOP) mandatory; one-exporter-per-param when energy drives a parameter.

routing.input_element: project onto a MOVING prop or performer -- a dancer, actor, handheld object, rolling/spinning set piece, moving scenery; dynamic / real-time projection mapping; tracked-surface projection; make content STICK to a moving object; BlackTrax / RTTrPM / PosiStageNet / PSN / OptiTrack / NatNet / Motive driven projection; motion-tracked reprojection; follow the object
routing.geometry_class: live tracking CHOP -> selectCHOP body-pick + axis rename -> filterCHOP oneeuro de-jitter -> bind_chop (Export flag) onto a digital-twin geometryCOMP transform -> renderTOP from the FIXED projector-matched cameraCOMP -> OUT_aligned
routing.notes: Data-only builds the whole tracker->twin->render network + numeric registration; the physical tracking rig, marker/beacon calibration, and projector-to-tracking registration are on-site human steps. Reuses camera_match_facade for the fixed projector camera; tracker channel NAMES are read live off OUT_trackraw, not hard-coded. Camera-tracking receivers freedinCHOP (FreeD), stypeinCHOP (Stype), mosysCHOP (Mo-Sys StarTracker) and ncamCHOP (Ncam) are also in the catalog -- use them for the moving-projector / camera-tracked reprojection variant. No dedicated dynamic-mapping/registration-solver op exists -- assembled from verified primitives.

routing.input_element: typography / text / TITLE content -- show titles, lower-thirds / name supers / name straps / chyron, subtitles/captions, rolling CREDITS, a COUNTDOWN or count-up timer, a live CLOCK, a data-driven readout/scoreboard, kinetic type, 3D extruded titles
routing.geometry_class: textTOP (2D) or geotextCOMP/textSOP+extrudeSOP->renderTOP (3D) -> transformTOP/levelTOP animated by exported CHOP -> compositeTOP over content (TOP image)
routing.notes: ROUTING FIX: 'typography' formerly landed on generative_texture_fx (no text op) -- this is the real text lane. Live counters are code-free (timerCHOP/clockCHOP -> choptoDAT -> textTOP), not expressions. Approved copy + licensed fonts are the human's.

routing.input_element: GPU particle content -- embers, sparks, fire, snow, ash, dust, rain, a fountain, an explosion burst, a vortex/tornado swirl, a flow field; 'make particles', 'particle system', 'sparks flying up the facade'
routing.geometry_class: POP particle sim -> point sprites -> rendered image (TOP)
routing.notes: Newer POP family (particlePOP/forceradialPOP/noisePOP/sprinklePOP verified present); renders NATIVELY inside a geometryCOMP with pointspriteMAT -- no poptoSOP converter exists (catalog gap). Distinct from point_cloud_content (static scan, TOP-instancing) and generative_texture_fx (2D feedback). Classic fallback: particleSOP prtype=pointsprites.

routing.input_element: LED wall / LED video wall / LED screen / pixel map / pixelmap feed to a Novastar or Brompton Tessera or Linsn or Colorlight processor/sender; tile a panel grid; build the exact-size canvas a LED processor ingests; LED output
routing.geometry_class: master content -> per-tile cropTOP+transformTOP carve (or layoutTOP grid-pack) over a black constantTOP -> resolutionTOP pins exact total canvas res -> WIRE-ONLY output TOP
routing.notes: No LED/pixelmap TOP exists -- assembled from primitives; TD delivers a correctly-sized, correctly-tiled canvas only. Physical panel map (positions/gaps/rotation/calibration) lives in the LED processor software (human/on-site). All output TOPs default active=ON -> set OFF (WIRE-ONLY).

routing.input_element: a fully enclosing immersive room / projection space -- 3+ walls plus floor and/or ceiling wrapped with continuous content (Van Gogh room, digital art gallery, 360 room, teamLab-style space, CAVE/cave enclosure, ceiling or floor projection, forced-perspective anamorphic floor)
routing.geometry_class: one shared room-scale geometryCOMP (box interior) -> N calibrated cameraCOMPs (one per surface, numeric pose+lens) -> per-surface renderTOP or shared multi-camera renderTOP fanned by renderselectTOP -> per-projector cornerpinTOP -> windowCOMP(specifydisplay)/ndioutTOP (wire-only)
routing.notes: Single 3D scene viewed from N calibrated cameras so content wraps seamlessly around the enclosure; floor/anamorphic is a dual viewer-eye vs projector-lens camera mode. BOUNDARY/GAP: no immersive-room/CAVE op and no auto-calibration solver -- projector poses and physical edge overlaps are surveyed on site (typed via set_par); overlap feather cross-references multiprojector_edge_blend; outputs built wire-only (winopen not fired, ndiout active=off).

routing.input_element: content that changes automatically by time-of-day / opening hours / day-of-week / date / sunrise-sunset with NO operator present -- dayparting, scheduled playback, unattended kiosk / retail window / museum lobby / architectural facade that runs itself and goes black off-hours; auto on/off, calendar/cron-like content switching
routing.geometry_class: wall clock CHOP -> logic daypart gates -> CHOP-built index exported onto a switchTOP + lagged crossTOP fade over a black constantTOP
routing.notes: Fully data-only build; TD has no cron/scheduler op so the clock+logic graph is the substitute. HUMAN: OS auto-boot + correct wall clock/timezone/DST (and site lat-long for sun gating). Off-hours fails safe to black at switch input0.

routing.input_element: make TouchDesigner FOLLOW an external clock -- chase / slave to timecode, LTC / SMPTE / MTC in, frame lock / frame-accurate playback, sync to a master clock / video server / FOH console / DAW, externally-driven playback, broadcast or festival house sync; the inverse of the master transport
routing.geometry_class: LTC audio -> ltcinCHOP decode (total seconds/frames) -> timecodeCHOP readout + moviefileinTOP frame-lock (playmode=timecodeop or index-export), with logic/lookup cue windows -> switchTOP
routing.notes: Slave counterpart to show_control_timecode (the master). Data-only decode+lock; ltcinCHOP is audio-LTC only (MTC via midiin is coarser), no genlock op. HUMAN: the master timecode feed, its fps/drop-frame, and audio level are patched on site.

routing.input_element: an instant blackout / DBO / kill-to-black / panic button / cut-to-black; a STANDBY holding slide or house-open card between segments; a preview-vs-program safety split -- the every-show safety layer
routing.geometry_class: program TOP bus -> state switchTOP -> DBO switchTOP over an opaque black constantTOP; a control constantCHOP (state/dbo) drives the indices; a 2nd nullTOP preview bus
routing.notes: DATA-ONLY: switch-over-black is the primitive (no blackout/DBO/panic/standby op exists); DBO is an instant switchTOP hard cut via set_par index=1 or a bound console toggle -- crossTOP fade-to-black is a separate variant. The panic-button decision + physical console are HUMAN; output is wire-only via output_handoff.

routing.input_element: a LIVE external video source to project -- an SDI or HDMI feed off a capture card (Blackmagic / AJA / Datapath / Deltacast / Bluefish), an NDI network stream, a SMPTE ST 2110 / 2110 broadcast IP flow, a Syphon or Spout GPU share, or TouchIn from another TouchDesigner; a camera / switcher / media-server / playback-deck feed to remap onto surfaces; live input, live feed, ingest, incoming signal, IMAG
routing.geometry_class: live capture TOP (videodeviceinTOP|ndiinTOP|st2110inTOP|syphonspoutinTOP|touchinTOP) -> stable ingest null -> cornerpinTOP warp -> matteTOP holdout -> OUT_aligned
routing.notes: Ingest twin of the output recipes -- ingests actual VIDEO as content (vs realtime_input_driver which ingests control DATA, and vision_interactive_mask which ingests a camera only to derive a mask). BOUNDARY: capture hardware (card/NIC/cabling) + the physical signal feed are on-site human; no signal-present sensor is readable, so a black frame vs an unplugged cable look identical from the MCP.

routing.input_element: multiple independent output zones / separate screens each showing different content at once (lobby screen + stage projector + bar LED); multi-output multi-zone; one window per display with per-zone content and resolution; per-zone NDI/Spout
routing.geometry_class: per-zone independent content -> per-zone resolutionTOP (own res) -> per-zone nullTOP tap -> own windowCOMP(specifydisplay) and/or per-zone ndiout/spout
routing.notes: N GENUINELY INDEPENDENT zones (different content/res/destination) -- NOT direct_projector_output's ONE spanning window/edge-blend. windowCOMP maxinputs=0: bind via winop param, not a wire; never fire winopen; ndiout/spout active=OFF. Zone-to-physical-display index mapping depends on on-site display topology (human); monitorsDAT lists heads but assignment is a human decision.

routing.input_element: make my projectors MATCH in colour -- white balance / white point / gamma / brightness / luminance match across a multi-projector array, projector colour calibration, grey-scale match, lamp-to-lamp colour, colour uniformity, hot-spot / centre-to-corner / vignette evenness, ASC-CDL or OCIO per-projector trim, the colour step after edge-blend and black-level
routing.geometry_class: per-projector aligned+blended feed -> level (luma) -> channelmix (WB) -> ocio (gamut/CDL) -> ramp uniformity mask -> guard level -> layout match wall
routing.notes: Completes the 3-part array match (geometry via multiprojector_edge_blend, black-level via multiprojector_blacklevel_mask, colour here). Correction VALUES are HUMAN -- a colorimeter/eye on the real surface; MCP builds the chain and types numbers back. No dedicated projector-colour-cal TOP exists; assembled from generic colour primitives.

routing.input_element: project onto a SHEER / see-through surface -- scrim, gauze, bobbinet, HoloGauze, holographic gauze, mesh, net, fog screen, water screen; only-lit-pixels-show black-is-transparent content, rear-projection reveal, front-to-back dissolve, figure-appears-from-nothing, black-crush prep, actor-safe holdout behind a scrim
routing.geometry_class: black constantTOP ground -> crush (level) -> front/back reveal (cross) -> rear mirror (flip) -> steep keystone (cornerpin) -> feather (ramp+blur+multiply) -> composite over black -> null -> reused garbage-mask holdout
routing.notes: KEY GOTCHA baked in: black bg + black-crush are MANDATORY (any non-black hazes the whole sheet). Reveal animates data-only (lfo/keyframe CHOP exported onto crossTOP.cross). Actor holdout REUSES output_spill_garbage_mask. Hanging the sheet + measuring throw/keystone/crush-target = HUMAN on-site. No dedicated sheer/gauze TOP; assembled from primitives.

routing.input_element: COLOR GRADE the output / apply a LUT / deliver in a target colorspace -- a client .cube (.3dl / .clf) 3D LUT, an OCIO / OpenColorIO colorspace transform to Rec709 / sRGB / DCI-P3 / P3 / ACES, a 1D tone curve, an ASC-CDL look, final black-point / white-point / gamma legalize; color management, match the projector/LED color, delivery color
routing.geometry_class: aligned frame -> opencolorioTOP colorspace -> opencolorioTOP .cube file transform -> lookupTOP 1D curve -> levelTOP legalize -> OUT_delivery
routing.notes: The delivery-color stage the library lacked; the only recipe using lookupTOP + opencolorioTOP. CORRECTED FACT: lookupTOP is a 1D/gradient remap, NOT a .cube loader -- the .cube loads via opencolorioTOP File Transform. BOUNDARY: the .cube file + target colorspace + measured black/white/gamma come from the client delivery spec + a meter on the real wall (human asset).

routing.input_element: a live-event / CORPORATE / conference / keynote stage-graphics package -- IMAG (stage-camera magnification) inset or full-frame, speaker lower-thirds, a holding/standby/pre-show slide, a countdown-to-start, sponsor supers
routing.geometry_class: ndiinTOP/videodeviceinTOP IMAG -> transformTOP PiP + reused text_title_content supers + moviefileinTOP holding slide + timerCHOP countdown -> compositeTOP program -> switchTOP program/standby bus (TOP image)
routing.notes: Leans on text_title_content (supers/countdown) + signal_ingest_remap (IMAG ingest) as meta-steps. HUMAN: the live camera + vision switcher are the event's video system; the bridge garnishes their feed, it does not cut the show. Output wire-only.

routing.input_element: animated instance array / instanced motion graphics -- a rippling grid or wall of cubes, a swarm of tiles/cards, a kinetic sculpture, a pulsing block wall, a field of dots; 'grid of moving cubes', 'kinetic array', 'instanced motion graphics'
routing.geometry_class: one shape instanced N times, CHOP-driven transforms -> rendered image (TOP)
routing.notes: geometryCOMP CHOP-instancing (patternCHOP layout + lfoCHOP/noiseCHOP animation), constantMAT per-instance color, keyframeCHOP->cameraCOMP fly-through. Deterministic authored motion -- distinct from facade_3d_render (static mesh) and particle_system_content (stochastic sim). replicatorCOMP usable only bytable with callbacks/tscript LEFT EMPTY (code sinks).

routing.input_element: bake a seamless / perfectly looping generative clip -- 'make this loop', 'seam-free loop', 'endless background loop', 'loopable texture', 'frame N wraps to frame 0', VJ loop
routing.geometry_class: generative TOP -> periodic-phase or head/tail-dissolve loop -> baked file (wire-only)
routing.notes: timerCHOP loop length + periodic patternCHOP/lfoCHOP phase (method A, exact wrap) OR crossTOP head/tail dissolve (method B, for feedback/trail loops). moviefileoutTOP bake is WIRE-ONLY (record OFF; operator fires). Generative analog of media_clip_player loop-crossfade; loop_length x fps MUST be integer frames.

routing.input_element: an operator confidence monitor / multiview / quad-split of program + preview + each projector; a low-res FOLDBACK / downstage-monitor feed; a hot-standby / redundancy / failover tap -- eyes on every feed
routing.geometry_class: N nullTOP feed taps -> textTOP labels -> compositeTOP panes -> one layoutTOP grid; a resolutionTOP downscale -> ndioutTOP foldback; a warm hot-standby nullTOP + an advisory analyzeTOP health flag
routing.notes: DATA-ONLY: layoutTOP IS the multiview (no failover/redundancy/tally/multiview-widget op exists). TD builds the taps + foldback + warm standby + advisory flag; the physical monitors and the FAILOVER DECISION are HUMAN/watchdog. ndioutTOP active OFF (wire-only); never route the multiview to a program output.

routing.input_element: build my own control panel / operator console / on-screen UI / GUI to run the show; custom control surface, front panel, show-control panel, cue buttons + master fader + DBO, a phone/tablet/TouchOSC remote or browser remote to drive parameters
routing.geometry_class: containerCOMP + buttonCOMP/sliderCOMP widgets -> per-widget panelCHOP -> renamed/merged nullCHOP bus -> bind_chop/export onto target params (levelTOP opacity, switchTOP cue index, crossTOP DBO); oscinCHOP mirrors the same targets
routing.notes: Data-only via panel-VALUE reads + bind_chop -- NO callbacks DAT. Human boundary: visual widget layout + remote device pairing. Browser remote (webserverDAT) needs a callbacks DAT = code sink, out of lane; OSC is the data-only remote. Distinct from realtime_input_driver (consumes external control, builds no UI) and confidence_monitor_foldback (monitors, does not control).

routing.input_element: show health / reliability watchdog -- monitor fps, frame time, DROPPED FRAMES, GPU memory / VRAM, GPU temperature; a performance monitor + threshold alarm overlay + numeric readout dashboard so the operator sees the show stuttering / overheating / running out of VRAM / dropping frames BEFORE it fails; perfect-playback discipline, uptime, no dropped frames
routing.geometry_class: performCHOP telemetry -> mathCHOP/logicCHOP threshold -> choptoTOP+textTOP readout + alarm-bound constantTOP -> layoutTOP/compositeTOP dashboard
routing.notes: Data-only for telemetry + alarm + readout; thresholds are operator-set numbers, and auto-recovery + continuous disk-logging are honest gaps (fileoutDAT Write not on the allowlist). Distinct from confidence_monitor_foldback (watches the video FEEDS, not SYSTEM performance).

routing.input_element: naked-eye 3D / glasses-free 3D / anamorphic corner LED / L-shaped or 90-degree corner LED wall where a hero object appears to float, bulge, or pop OUT of the screen (the Seoul 'wave in a box' / Chengdu / d'strict-style out-of-bounds billboard); make a 3D object breach the corner for one design viewpoint; forced-perspective single-viewpoint LED content
routing.geometry_class: to-scale 3D geometryCOMP scene -> ONE off-axis eyepoint cameraCOMP (perspective + winx/winy lens-shift) -> single renderTOP -> cropTOP split at the fold column -> per-face cornerpinTOP homography -> compositeTOP combined LED canvas (or per-face taps)
routing.notes: ONE anamorphic camera at ONE fixed viewer eyepoint ACROSS both faces (single-viewpoint illusion) -- explicitly NOT immersive_room_mapping's anamorphic-FLOOR mode which uses one camera PER surface. Single-render + perspective-cornerpin split is geometrically exact (limited only by how wide the single frustum can span a hard fold -> per-face quad-reproject variant for close/steep corners). Illusion holds ONLY from the design eyepoint. BOUNDARY/GAP: no corner-LED / naked-eye-3D op and no auto-calibration solver -- corner face sizes + pixel dims + true fold angle, the chosen eyepoint, and the LED processor panel/colour map are measured on site (typed via set_par); hands off wire-only to led_wall_pixelmap_feed / ndiout (active OFF); bespoke single-pass fold projection is a gated glsl_opportunity (cameraCOMP customproj).

routing.input_element: interactive floor / interactive wall driven by a 2D laser scanner (lidar) -- Hokuyo UST/URG or Leuze ROD4; presence-reactive projection install; people walking on a projected floor; a pool of light / spotlight that follows you; step-on hotspot zones; large-area footfall / presence tracking without a camera; works in the dark; motion-follows-you; crowd presence over a big area
routing.geometry_class: hardware scanner CHOP (polar/cartesian point fan) -> blobtrackCHOP centroids+velocity -> lag smoothing -> mathCHOP scan-metres-to-canvas-UV calibration -> logicCHOP zone/presence gates -> bind_chop onto reactive content (circleTOP spotlight) / interaction mask
routing.notes: Distinct from vision_interactive_mask (camera/depth-scoped) -- lidar is THE interactive-floor sensor; reuse that recipe's reveal downstream. Sensor is real hardware: no scanner = zero channels (author against a constantCHOP/patternCHOP stand-in). Scanner mount + scan-space->projection-space calibration are human/on-site. Distinct from blacktrax/optitrack 3D beacon tracking (tracked_surface_content).

routing.input_element: animated edge / outline light-lines that TRACE a building's real architecture -- neon-outline facade, edge tracing, contour reveal, running/chasing light along the lines, light streaking along cornices and window frames, only the light moving aligned with the edges, draw-on outline, architectural line-art / edge lighting, festival facade line tracing
routing.geometry_class: traced contour CVs (survey/photo trace -> write_csv/tableDAT/dattoSOP) -> polyspline smooth + resample -> carveSOP chase (patternCHOP phase) -> linethickSOP + lineMAT neon -> geometryCOMP + ortho cameraCOMP + renderTOP -> feedbackTOP trails -> composite over black
routing.notes: Distinct from facade_mask_atlas (masks REGIONS / area fills); this animates LINE-ART along contours (the two combine). Tracing the real architectural lines from a rectified photo/survey is the human boundary. Auto-trace lane via edgeTOP/tracePOP; no live in-viewport line-draw tool exists (write_csv->dattoSOP is the data-only stand-in).

routing.input_element: play the show soundtrack / audio playback / audio out / sound output / play music or a track, route audio to a multichannel or spatial / surround (5.1 / 7.1 / immersive) speaker layout, speaker routing / channel map, keep a movie's own audio synced to its picture (A/V sync), lock audio to the timeline or timecode -- the audio-OUT lane of running the show (distinct from audio-reactive, which consumes audio for visuals)
routing.geometry_class: soundtrack file / movie audio track -> CHOP audio channels -> shuffle/reorder into a physical speaker-order bed -> audiodeviceoutCHOP hardware out, timecode-locked to the show clock
routing.notes: Data-only builds the play+route+sync graph and names every channel; the physical interface, speaker patch/amp gains, and master-clock feed are HUMAN/hardware. audiodeviceoutCHOP.active defaults ON to the SYSTEM DEFAULT device -- set device/driver first. No spatial-panner/Ambisonics/object-audio op in the catalog -- discrete channel routing is the stand-in; true object audio lives in an external engine. Verify with inspect on CHOP channels (no save_top for audio).

routing.input_element: send the show out as SMPTE ST 2110 uncompressed video-over-IP / 2110 output / video over IP / IP video fabric / PTP grandmaster sync / broadcast-grade delivery / Blackmagic-Deltacast-AJA IP card / rec2020 HDR PQ HLG 10-bit 2110 out / the broadcast alternative to NDI/Spout/SDI
routing.geometry_class: finished content nullTOP -> st2110outTOP (active OFF) linked to st2110deviceCHOP (PTP follower) -> wire-only IP essence flow
routing.notes: Cleanest wire-only OUT scaffold: no dynamic params, no missing op. active DEFAULTS ON -> built OFF. HARD BLOCKER (external): needs a 2110-capable NIC + a PTP grandmaster clock + a 2110-aware switch/receiver; arming transmit is the operator's on-site step. No 2110-INPUT here (that is signal_ingest_remap / st2110inTOP).

routing.input_element: plan a projector rig on paper -- throw ratio / lens / lumens / brightness / coverage / image size / overlap planning sheet, projector calculator, throw-distance calculator, lens selection, lumens per square meter, coverage map, projector spec sheet, rigging plan, pre-production planning table, CSV export of a projector plan, frustum coverage preview
routing.geometry_class: write_csv spec sheet -> tableDAT -> constantCHOP/mathCHOP derived columns -> choptoDAT -> write_csv plan; optional cameraCOMP+renderTOP frustum preview
routing.notes: A PLANNING deliverable, not a live show graph -- nothing armed/transmitted. Data-only CHOP-math fallback ships now; the clean per-row-formula version wants evaluateDAT = the GATED expression lane (allow_expr default OFF, surfaced as an expr_opportunity). Source lens/lumens numbers = manufacturer datasheet + on-site measured throw (human). No dedicated projector-calculator op exists -- assembled from primitives.

routing.input_element: play / trigger a Notch .dfx Block (Notch LC generative content) inside TouchDesigner -- load a dfx, pick a layer, run/scrub the transport, hand off the output
routing.geometry_class: notchTOP source (dfx-driven) -> conditioned TOP -> standby-switched playout (wire-only)
routing.notes: LICENSE-GATED SCAFFOLD: the bridge builds the full transport (block/layer/playmode/play toggle/speed/index) + conditioning + standby fallback, but playback needs a Notch Playback/Builder LICENSE, the author-made .dfx asset, and author-defined dynamic Block params that appear only after the Block loads (set via set_par then). Run = play toggle (data-only), not a pulse. Honest limits flagged inline.

routing.input_element: MQTT / IoT / building-automation / smart-facade / smart-building triggers -- occupancy & motion sensors, door contacts, lighting scenes, HVAC/thermostat, a pub/sub message bus, a phone or dashboard publishing state -- driving content and parameters
routing.geometry_class: mqttclientDAT received-message table -> dattoCHOP parse -> selectCHOP/lagCHOP/mathCHOP/logicCHOP condition -> bind_chop/EXPORT onto content & params
routing.notes: The MQTT transport extension of the realtime_input_driver family (OSC/DMX/MIDI/audio). Data-only once the stream flows; the broker + topic schema + the subscribe() callbacks touch are human/gated, and structured-JSON payload parsing wants the gated expr lane (data-only fallback = subscribe to pre-split leaf topics).

routing.input_element: export a model's UV layout / UV atlas / unwrap as a registration template so an external artist paints pixel-registered artwork for the mapped surfaces of a per-section rig
routing.geometry_class: model SOP (uv0) -> geometryCOMP -> renderTOP rendermode=uvunwrap wireframe atlas -> composite -> save_top file
routing.notes: Data-only via renderTOP's NATIVE rendermode=uvunwrap (uvunwrapcoord=uv0) -- no shader/expression needed to flatten to UV. A convenience around per_section_material_rig: the MCP renders the guide, the artist paints externally, the finished map re-imports as the section colormap. Gotchas: delete the geometryCOMP default torus; force atlas res (256 trap); opaque mid-gray bg (white-on-transparent trap); compositeTOP swaporder. Numbered/colored islands need the gated glsl lane.

routing.input_element: generate structured-light / gray-code / phase-shift pattern SEQUENCES for AUTOMATIC projector<->camera calibration and geometry capture (beyond static alignment charts)
routing.geometry_class: rampTOP->mathTOP binary stripes + patternCHOP->choptoTOP sine fringes, timerCHOP-sequenced via switchTOP at native res (wire-only)
routing.notes: DATA-ONLY for PATTERN GENERATION only. Distinct from test_pattern_generator (static grids/crosshatch). Must stay 1:1 native res + nearest filter + no AA/mipmap/scale or stripe edges blur and the decode fails. The synced camera capture and the external gray-code/phase SOLVE are human/external. No dedicated structured-light op exists -- assembled from primitives; pixel-exact version is a gated glsl_opportunity.

routing.input_element: control a PROJECTOR directly -- power it on/off, select its input, open/close its shutter (AV-mute), or read lamp-hours / error / status; PJLink; projector device control; turn the projectors on for the show; projector health / lamp monitoring
routing.geometry_class: device command -> projector over PJLink TCP:4352 (no TOP); async status replies read back from the tcpipDAT
routing.notes: The projector-brain sibling of dmx_artnet_output (DMX fixtures). tcpipDAT client -> device_send CLOSED-ALLOWLIST PJLink tokens (power/input/shutter + read-only queries); CONSENT-GATED behind allow_device_control (default OFF) and needs a REAL projector -- the .send() round-trip is unprovable in authoring. Unauthenticated PJLink Class 1 only. Keywords: projector, PJLink, power on, input select, shutter, AV-mute, lamp hours, error status, device control, device send.

routing.input_element: multiple render machines / a render cluster that must cook the SAME frame in lockstep (distributed rendering, a wall spanning nodes, multi-projector show split across PCs)
routing.geometry_class: multi-machine frame-locked cook
routing.notes: syncoutCHOP master -> syncinCHOP nodes + engineCOMP content; software packet-sync is not genlock (Quadro Sync + house reference is the hardware boundary).

routing.input_element: a disguise (Designer/d3) render node: receive frames + camera/pose over RenderStream and return the rendered TOP
routing.geometry_class: bidirectional RenderStream video+data loop
routing.notes: renderstreaminTOP/CHOP in, renderstreamoutTOP back; camera frustum driven data-only via cameraCOMP xformmatrixop/projmatrixop CHOP refs; needs the disguise stack + a live peer.

routing.input_element: a depth sensor (RealSense / Orbbec / Kinect Azure|Femto) for true-3D presence, a projection-immune depth-slab mask, or per-player skeleton XYZ
routing.geometry_class: depth TOP + body CHOP -> interactive mask / driver
routing.notes: depth gate via lumalevelTOP inlow/inhigh is immune to projected light; skeleton is Azure/Femto-only (Body Tracking SDK + ONNX + GPU); slab + mapping are human-measured.

recipes.title: Building model -> framed, shaded render (the 3D lane)
recipes.summary: Import a building model into a Geometry COMP, set the render flag, assign a MAT, frame it with a Camera, light it, render to a Render TOP, composite over a dark plate, tap with a null. Emits a 2D image (TOP). geometryCOMP(torus)+constantMAT+cameraCOMP+renderTOP+constantTOP(black plate)+overTOP+nullTOP builds, wires, and cooks to the shaded model on a clean black plate at 1280x720. NOTE param naming: set the constantMAT color + plate color via set_par (raw colorr/colorg/colorb) OR the CREATE tool's `color`:[r,g,b] tuplet vector -- passing raw component names (colorr) or a pars{} wrapper TO A CREATE TOOL silently drops them (they are not create-tool params; the tool exposes the `color`/`resolution` tuplets).

steps.note: The container for the model. Its `material` param assigns the MAT for the whole component (set in step 6); the operator inside whose RENDER flag is on is what gets rendered. Renders BLACK with no material assigned.

key_params.render: on (the COMP participates in the render)
key_params.material: set in step 6 to the MAT path
key_params.t/r/s: transform to animate/position the model (drive from a CHOP for motion)

steps.geometry_out: 3D COMP (holds the model network)

verify.pass_if: COMP exists, no cook error

steps.note: Import the model INSIDE the geometryCOMP. VALIDATED: a static .obj mesh renders DIRECTLY from a File In SOP — no soptoPOP bridge needed. File In SOP reads .obj (and .tog); FBX is NOT supported here (use fbxCOMP), .abc uses alembicSOP, .usd uses usdCOMP (see variants).

key_params.file: path to the model (.obj / .tog), confined to the working dir

steps.geometry_out: poly (SOP)

verify.pass_if: File In SOP cooked, prims>0

steps.note: A fresh geometryCOMP ships a DEFAULT child (a torus SOP) carrying the render+display flags. Delete it so your imported File In SOP becomes what renders — the TD analog of Houdini's D2 display-flag gotcha.
steps.geometry_out: (scene edit)

verify.pass_if: default torus gone

steps.note: REQUIRED: turn ON the render (and usually display) flag of the File In SOP. Inside a geometryCOMP the SOP with the RENDER flag is what the Render TOP renders; without this the render is empty.
steps.geometry_out: (flag edit)

verify.pass_if: File In SOP has render flag

steps.note: A MAT is MANDATORY or the geometry renders black. constantMAT = flat, light-independent façade content (the common projection-mapping choice; needs NO light). Use phongMAT/pbrMAT for lit 3D (phong renders black WITHOUT a light).

key_params.colormap: a TOP for a texture (all textures enter as TOPs; no disk-file MAT param)

steps.geometry_out: MAT

verify.pass_if: MAT preview shows the color/texture

steps.note: Assign the MAT to the whole component: set geometryCOMP.material = the MAT path from step 5. The Geometry COMP's `material` param, not a wire.
steps.geometry_out: (param edit)

verify.pass_if: material param set

steps.note: Frame the façade. See recipe camera_match_facade for the ortho-vs-perspective decision; for a flat building face use projection=ortho + orthowidth to frame the front 1:1.

key_params.t/r: position on the façade normal axis; or lookat a null at façade centre

steps.geometry_out: camera COMP

verify.pass_if: model fills the frame through cam

steps.note: Add a light IF using phongMAT/pbrMAT (skip entirely for constantMAT — flat content is light-independent). Optional environmentlightCOMP adds IBL but REQUIRES pbrMAT.
steps.geometry_out: light COMP

verify.pass_if: light exists (lit MATs only)

steps.note: The Render TOP references camera / geometry / lights BY PARAMETER (a path or name-pattern), NOT by wiring them into its inputs — its only real input wiring is downstream compositing. Output is a 2D image.

key_params.camera: path to OUT_cam (a parameter reference, not a wire)
key_params.geometry: path/pattern to the geo COMP (e.g. 'geo*' or the OUT_geo path)
key_params.format: rgba16float if you need HDR headroom before grade

steps.geometry_out: TOP (2D image, TRANSPARENT background)

verify.pass_if: resolution == requested (custom), not the default
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_render_raw

steps.note: The Render TOP output is TRANSPARENT — composite it over a dark constantTOP to get a readable preview (and a solid background for projection content).
steps.geometry_out: TOP (2D image)

verify.pass_if: solid dark plate at render res

steps.note: Composite the render OVER the dark plate (render = input 0, bg = input 1). Wire with `connect`. This is the readable beauty pass.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (2D image)

verify.pass_if: over TOP has both inputs wired

steps.note: Plant the stable output tap. Downstream FX (recipe generative_texture_fx) and the output lane target this null NAME, not a node that may move.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (2D image)

verify.pass_if: the shaded model reads over the dark plate
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_render

recipes.classify: a building / 3D model of a façade — render a shaded, framed 2D image from a 3D mesh (.obj/.abc/.fbx/.usd) for projection content
recipes.governance: A MAT is mandatory (phong needs a light or renders black; constant needs none). The Render TOP references camera/geometry/lights by PARAMETER, not wires. Its output is transparent — composite over a dark constantTOP. Generators/Render TOP need outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h; non-commercial builds cap at 1280. Build to the deliverable's resolution, not the tool ceiling.
tips: Render is black -> no MAT assigned, render flag off on the SOP, or the camera isn't framing the geo. See https://docs.derivative.ca/Why_is_My_Render_Black .
A static .obj mesh renders DIRECTLY from a File In SOP — do NOT insert a soptoPOP bridge for a static model (that's the POP-instancing path; see variants).

recipes.title: Segmented building model -> N addressable per-section emit surfaces (the PM rig)
recipes.summary: Turn a pre-sectioned model (section_00.obj … section_NN.obj) into N independently-addressable Geometry COMPs sec00..secNN, each loading its own OBJ part and carrying its own phong MAT (matNN) whose EMISSION is the projected content — self-illuminated, no scene light. One Render TOP with geometry='sec*' renders all sections in a single pass through one camera; composite over a dark plate and plant a stable preview tap. This is the FOUNDATION every per-section choreography (e.g. height_sweep_choreography) drives. Built from the REAL 15-section building (building_sections/section_00..14.obj) via import_segmented_model -- 15/15 sections load as per-section geometryCOMP + phongMAT with UVs AND normals present (real geometry, up to ~147k pts/section), zero warnings. This is the one-call form of the step-by-step per-section rig.

steps.note: Create ONE geometryCOMP PER SECTION: sec00, sec01, … secNN (N = number of exported OBJ parts). One-material-per-object is MANDATORY in TD — you cannot scope a MAT to part of a merged mesh (no group field on materialSOP; group isolation needs denied code sinks). This per-section split is the whole reason a single merged building.obj fails. Each COMP: render=1; material=matNN (set in step 6). Geometry is already in world coords from the Houdini export, so leave t/r/s at identity.
steps.geometry_out: 3D COMP (one per section)

verify.pass_if: N geometryCOMPs sec00..secNN exist, no cook error

steps.note: INSIDE each secNN, a File In SOP (file1) loads that section's OBJ. A static .obj renders DIRECTLY from a File In SOP — no soptoPOP bridge. Point each file1 at its own part: section_{NN}.obj (UVs + normals intact from the per-meshId export). Files live UNDER the working dir (e.g. assets/sections/section_{NN}.obj).

verify.pass_if: each file1 has render+display on

The MATERIAL'S EMISSION is the projected content — self-illuminated, shows at full brightness with NO scene light (proven: emit renders lit with no light, correct for projection mapping; phong DIFFUSE would render black without a light, but we don't use it). Base state: diffr/g/b=0, specr/g/b=0, emitr/g/b=0 (dark). GOTCHA: emission is THREE scalars emitr/emitg/emitb — there is NO single 'emit level' param, so a WHITE pulse means driving all three. recipes.classify: a segmented / pre-sectioned building model (multiple OBJ parts) — build N independently-addressable per-section emit surfaces + one-pass render, the foundation for per-section projection-mapping animation
recipes.governance: One material PER OBJECT is a hard TD constraint — sections MUST be separate geometryCOMPs (a merged mesh cannot be per-section addressed without denied code sinks). Emission (not diffuse) carries projection content: self-illuminated, needs no light; diffuse/spec set to 0. Emission is 3 scalars emitr/emitg/emitb (no single level). renderTOP references geometry ('sec*' pattern) + camera by PARAMETER, not wires, and its output is transparent — composite over a dark constantTOP. THE 256px TRAP: constantTOP/overTOP default to 256x256 and crush the render — always set outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h. Non-Commercial builds cap output at 1280; build to the deliverable's resolution.
tips: Section renders black -> matNN not assigned, file1 render flag off, default torus not deleted, or the camera isn't framing that section.

Bring-up proof: set each matNN to a DISTINCT flat emit color, save_top @OUT_secrender — you should see the building rebuilt from N addressable parts (the 'all_sections' proof). Then hand emit to a choreography.

This is ~6 tool calls PER SECTION (geometryCOMP + fileinSOP + delete_op + set_flags + phongMAT + set_par); for 15 sections that's ~90 calls. A convenience tool 'import_segmented_model(dir, name_pattern)' that builds sec00..secNN + mat00..matNN + assigns materials in one call would collapse this dramatically (see integration note E).
Textured (not flat-color) per-section content: set matNN.emitmap to a TOP and emitmapcoord=uv0 to sample through the section's UVs (moviefileinTOP loops are the most reliable animated source).
variants: Lit look instead of pure emission: keep diffuse and add a lightCOMP (but emission is the projection-mapping default — no light needed).
PBR content: pbrMAT with emitmap (also self-illuminated).
Per-section video: matNN.emitmap = a moviefileinTOP loop (play follows the timeline), windows = a black-emit material (dark cutout).
Keystone for a real projector: append a cornerpinTOP (numeric pin corners = data-only) after OUT_secfinal.

recipes.title: Animated per-section 'height sweep' — one LFO drives N sections by height (data-only)
recipes.summary: Given a per_section_material_rig (sec00..secNN + mat00..matNN emit surfaces sharing a parent), animate a travelling band of light that sweeps bottom->top and back, brightening each section as the sweep passes its height. Built entirely from typed CHOPs and CHOP-EXPORT — NO expressions, NO code: a single ping-pong LFO, per-section height constants, a distance/brightness math chain, and a rename+merge+export block that drives every matNN:emitr/g/b live. Play the timeline to animate; freeze for deterministic stills. DRIVE MECHANISM FIXED + VERIFIED: CHOP-export drives a parameter ONLY when the exporter's Viewer Active flag is ON and it is force-cooked (the Export flag alone does NOT drive it -- a cook-time side effect per the TD API). bind_chop now does this to drive the target. This recipe's MANUAL export chain must likewise set the exporter (nullCHOP) activeViewer + force a cook, or route the final per-section drive through bind_chop.

steps.note: The single travelling sweep position. wavetype=tri, amp=0.5, offset=0.5 -> a 0..1 ping-pong (bottom<->top). channelname='c[0-14]' is the BROADCAST TRICK: the bracket pattern emits N IDENTICAL channels c0..c14 in one op, so the sweep can be subtracted per-section by index WITHOUT undocumented single-channel-vs-many math. frequency = fps / loopframes (e.g. 0.08 for a slow sweep). play=on to animate.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (N identical sweep channels)

verify.pass_if: N channels c0..cN, all equal, sweeping 0..1

steps.note: Per-section normalized HEIGHT (0=bottom .. 1=top), one channel c0..cN, one value per section. GOTCHA: the constantCHOP tool only exposes const0 at create time — EXPAND to N channels with a follow-up set_par writing const{i}name and const{i}value for i=0..N-1. Quirk: setting the highest index (e.g. const14value) AUTO-EXTENDS the sequence, and the `const` count param may report 0 even though the values apply — verify with inspect, not the count. Use RANK-EQUALIZED centroid-Y heights (ties share a value) so the sweep reveals sections evenly in time instead of bunching where centroids cluster.

key_params.const{i}name/const{i}value: via set_par: c{i} / rank-equalized height of section i, i=0..N-1

steps.note: Phase = height - sweep. chopop='sub', match='index' pairs channel i of input0 (heights) with channel i of input1 (sweep) by INDEX. Wire pm_heights -> input 0, pm_sweep -> input 1. Result per section = h_i - sweepPos (signed distance of the sweep from that section's height).

steps.note: Distance -> brightness bump. fromrange=[0, W], torange=[MAXB, MINB] linearly maps distance 0 (sweep ON the section) to MAXB (full bright) and distance W (band half-width, ~0.18) to MINB (dark). NOTE the tool takes ranges as ARRAYS: fromrange=[a,b], torange=[a,b]. Beyond W it extrapolates past MINB (clamped next step). Wire pm_dist -> input 0.

verify.pass_if: all values within [MINB, MAXB]

Build THREE renameCHOPs (pm_nm_r, pm_nm_g, pm_nm_b), one per emit component, each fed from pm_brightc (input 0). renamefrom='*'; renameto = an EXPLICIT space-separated list 'mat00:emitr mat01:emitr … matNN:emitr' (and :emitg, :emitb for the other two). USE THE EXPLICIT LIST, not a bracket pattern — the explicit list is more reliable for op:par export targets. Driving all three r/g/b with the same brightness = a WHITE pulse.

THE AUTONAME SAME-PARENT RULE: because pm_out and the materials share parent /project1, autoname resolves each channel 'matNN:emitr' to the sibling material's emitr parameter — that parameter switches to Export mode (ParMode.EXPORT) and is driven LIVE by the CHOP. (This is the proven mechanism; the older DAT-table 'datname' export is a DEAD END and the Null CHOP's own renamefrom/renameto are a NO-OP via the API — do NOT use those.) recipes.classify: animate an existing per-section rig — a travelling 'height sweep' of light that reveals building sections bottom->top over time, driven data-only by one LFO + CHOP-export (no code)
recipes.governance: PREREQUISITE: a built per_section_material_rig — pm_out (the export null) and the materials mat00..matNN MUST share a parent for autoname export to resolve. Animation is 100% data-only: typed CHOPs + CHOP-EXPORT (exportmethod=autoname + autoexportroot='..' + the export node flag), NO expressions, NO code. The PROVEN export mechanism is renameCHOP('*' -> explicit 'op:par' list) + autoname + export flag; the DAT-table 'datname' route and the Null CHOP's own rename params are DEAD ENDS — do not use. mathCHOP ranges are ARRAYS: fromrange=[a,b], torange=[a,b]. Emission is 3 scalars (emitr/g/b) — drive all three for a white pulse. Playing the timeline animates; nothing is fired that writes to disk (save_top preview only).
tips: Nothing animates -> confirm pm_sweep play=on AND the timeline is playing; a static sweep = a static image.

A material stays dark / not driven -> inspect matNN.emitr: mode must be EXPORT with source pm_out. If CONSTANT, the autoname target name didn't match (check the renameto 'matNN:emitr' spelling) or pm_out isn't a sibling of the materials.

constantCHOP shows fewer channels than expected -> the tool only creates const0; you must set_par const{i}name/value up to N-1. Don't trust the `const` count param (can read 0); verify channels with inspect.
Bunched reveal (sections pop together) -> use RANK-EQUALIZED centroid-Y heights so the sweep spreads sections evenly in time.
Sharper/softer band -> shrink/grow W (band half-width) in pm_bright's fromrange; brighter/dimmer -> MAXB/MINB in torange + limit.

Driving N params from one CHOP is ~5 nodes here (3 renames + merge + null + export). A convenience 'bind_chop'-style helper that broadcasts one channel set onto N sibling op:par targets in one call would collapse this (see integration note E).
variants: Cue-table choreography (sections activate at authored moments, not by height): replace pm_sweep/pm_heights/pm_phase/pm_dist with a tableDAT of cues -> timerCHOP (channelcolumns, Custom Channel Interpolation = Ease In/Out, On Done = Re-Start) -> the same rename+merge+export block. Smooth, keyframeless.
Continuous per-section pulsing: drive emit from lfoCHOP/patternCHOP/lookupCHOP per section instead of a single sweep.
Colored sweep (not white): drive pm_nm_r/g/b from different brightness chains, or multiply the brightness by a per-section color constant before rename.

Wire-only (touch no parameter): choptoTOP the brightness channels into a small level texture and Multiply/Remap against a section-ID mask atlas feeding the emit maps — the most robust route if export binding is undesirable.

recipes.title: Time-sequenced section choreography (cue table + Timer CHOP, data-only)
recipes.summary: Show-structure layer above the per-section rig: a cue table (tableDAT loaded from a working-dir cues.csv of literal per-section values) feeds a timerCHOP whose Custom Channel Interpolation = Ease In/Out, producing one eased 0..1 control channel per section that steps through cues and loops (On Done = Re-Start). Eased channels applied per section via the PROVEN autoname CHOP-export (renameCHOP->merge->null->set_par exportmethod=autoname/autoexportroot=.. + set_flags export=true) OR wire-only (chopto->multiply vs section masks). Scene arc = top-level crossTOP/switchTOP driven by the Timer segment fraction. Layers on the height-sweep (mult: cue-activation x sweep-motion) and per-section video (cue gates each moviefileinTOP). No expressions/Python/callbacks.

steps.note: CUE TABLE. Rows=cues; cols=Timer segment ctrl (length[,begin,cycle]) + one per-section target col sec00..secNN (literal 0..1). GATEWAY REALITY: tool withholds Fill-page code sinks (cellexpr/fills*expr) and there is NO cell-write param; manual cell edit is Python(banned). ONLY data-only way to get literal cells = the `file` param: write a cues.csv to the working dir, set tableDAT.file, then fire pulse(loadonstartpulse) to load it -- setting file alone does NOT read the CSV mid-session, and loadonstart is project-start only. Keep fill=manual. NOTE: cells are NOT typeable via params.

key_params.load: pulse(loadonstartpulse) after setting file -- reads the CSV now (file alone / loadonstart do NOT load mid-session)

steps.note: DRIVER. segdat=OUT_cuetable. segmethod=serial (ordered arc) | parallel (per-section own begin+length). channelcolumns names the per-section cols -> one output channel per column read from the cue cells. interpolation=easeinouttovalue = auto-eased cue-to-cue, no keyframes/code. ondone=restart loops the show. outseg/outfraction feed scene crossfades.

ROBUSTNESS (verified live): also set cooktype=always on the export null so it COOKS EVERY FRAME -- the autoname export then drives the targets LIVE even in a passive project where nothing downstream pulls the null; without it a stalled exporter can leave the emit values frozen.

recipes.title: Blast VIDEO onto each section's surface (per-section emit-map projection, UV-registered)
recipes.summary: Take the proven per-section rig (sec00..secNN each fileinSOP(section_NN.obj)+phongMAT matNN; one renderTOP geometry='sec*') and drive ACTUAL VIDEO onto each surface. A moviefileinTOP feeds each material's EMIT MAP (emitmap), sampled through that section's UVs (emitmapcoord=uv0); diffuse stays 0 so only the self-illuminated video shows (=projected light). KEY: emitmap is MULTIPLIED by emit color, so the existing brightness-sweep export onto emitr/g/b REVEALS/FADES the video per section over time with ZERO extra nodes. Windows keep blank emitmap + emit 0 (black cutout). Render over dark plate, tap a null, preview. A real moviefileinTOP clip mapped onto the building via emitmap x per-section UVs; emit color = the per-section dimmer/tint that multiplies the video (set emitr/g/b=1 for full-bright, or let the sweep/color export modulate it).

ONE shared content TOP is the DEFAULT (every emitmap points at it, UVs place it); branch to N only where sections need DISTINCT clips. GPU codec (HAP/HAP Q) essential for N decodes.

verify.pass_if: res==requested, frame non-black (decoding)

Emit is added UNLIT = video at full value = projected light. N materials -> N calls (helper candidate).

(b) SWEEP-MODULATED (RECOMMENDED, reuses proven rig): LEAVE emitr/g/b driven by the sweep export (pm_out). The sweep's 0..1 now fades/reveals the VIDEO per section over time — zero extra nodes. recipes.title: Keystone-align the composite and hand it to a projector / file / media server (data-only up to the on-site human calibration)
recipes.summary: Take the finished façade composite (OUT_facade_video / OUT_render / OUT_choreo), apply a data-only 4-corner keystone (cornerpinTOP pin* corners), plant an aligned null, then WIRE the output: a windowCOMP perform window to the real projector (incl. multi-display), or moviefileoutTOP / ndioutTOP / syphonspoutoutTOP. Complements output_handoff by adding the ALIGNMENT stage + the windowCOMP/perform lane. The MCP builds every node + sets every corner numerically; the on-site correspondence (6-point camSchnappr solve or hand-dragged corners) is a HUMAN step whose OUTPUT NUMBERS get typed back via set_par. Nothing is fired by the bridge. OUT_render -> cornerpinTOP -> nullTOP(OUT_aligned) builds and cooks, passing the render through the keystone at 1280x720 (identity pins = pass-through; numeric corner pins = the data-only keystone). On-site projector alignment is the HUMAN boundary; the measured pin numbers are typed back via set_par.

steps.note: Start from the finished composite tap; wire it into the cornerpin with connect.

verify.pass_if: composite tap exists and cooks

steps.note: DATA-ONLY PROJECTOR KEYSTONE. The 4 output corners = the pin* params: pintopleftx/y, pintoprightx/y, pinbotleftx/y, pinbotrightx/y (unit default 'fraction' 0..1). Nudging them warps the frame onto the real surface = numeric keystone. Identity start: TL(0,1) TR(1,1) BL(0,0) BR(1,0). mapping=perspective for a TRUE projective keystone (straight edges stay straight); bilinear bows them. DO NOT confuse with extract* (crops the SOURCE). Wire OUT_render->in0.

Fade-to-black over the dark constantTOP plate = the opacity/fade (emit->0); for TRUE alpha opacity (content crossfade) use a per-section levelTOP.opacity export. recipes.title: Window/feature mask atlas -- keep content OFF the real windows/recesses (punched-out-black-windows)
recipes.summary: Persistent window/feature masking for the per-section rig so content stays BLACK on real windows even when a section is lit. Data-only-BUILDABLE = the compose/load + multiply + assign chain; a hand-painted or Houdini-baked window-cutout PNG for irregular arches is an upstream ASSET (only its loading is buildable).
