recipes.classify: persistent window/feature masking for a per-section facade rig -- keep projected content OFF the real windows/recesses (walls glow, windows stay black) via a UV-space mask atlas multiplied into the emit content, or window-as-section blackout
recipes.governance: Masking is data-only-BUILDABLE (compose shapes / load PNG -> multiply -> assign emitmap). The mask must live in the SAME UV space as the content: combine mask x content in TOP space FIRST, then assign the PRODUCT to emitmap (emitmapcoord=uv0). multiplyTOP is the unambiguous masker; compositeTOP operand=inside/insideluminance is equivalent (content=input1, mask=input2, swaporder off). emitmap is MULTIPLIED by emit color, so a live brightness/color export coexists -- never overwrite exported emit. emitmapextendu/v=hold (no atlas bleed). Match resolutions (256px default trap). set_par_many pattern='mat*' assigns ONE shared mask+sampling to N mats in one call; distinct per-section masks need per-section set_par. UPSTREAM ASSET: a hand-painted/Houdini-baked window PNG for irregular arches -- only its loading is buildable. CROSS-REF (coordinate space): this is UV-SPACE masking (multiplied into emitmap, sampled through each section's UVs, to keep content off windows/recesses ON the surface). For SCREEN-space spill control -- clip ALL content to the surface silhouette so no light hits the ground/sky/neighbors/people, plus a soft projector frame-edge feather -- see output_spill_garbage_mask, applied on the FINAL composite AFTER the cornerpinTOP keystone; a building can need BOTH at once. NC caps 1280.
tips: Windows stay lit -> mask not black there, OR assigned straight to emitmap without multiplying content, OR emitmapextend=repeat wrapping. Multiply mask x content FIRST, assign the product.
Gray fringe at edges -> mask filtered linear; use inputfiltertype=nearest or lumalevelTOP threshold=0.5 for a hard cutout.
Mask misaligned -> the PNG isn't in the model's UV layout. Bake it from Houdini in the SAME UV atlas as content (window group -> UV render / attribute_to_texture).
Shared UV atlas -> one mask, one multiply, one set_par_many. Per-section 0..1 UVs -> one mask + one set_par per section.
Regular window grid -> skip the PNG; composite rectangleTOP shapes (each has its own operand=over) over a black bg, fully data-only.
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_mask(shapes=[{kind:rect|circle,cx,cy,w,h|r,soft}],invert,res) -> a rect/circle chain over black -> a null mask, one call.
variants: build_from_shapes (Route B1, data-only, no asset): constantTOP black bg -> chain rectangleTOP/circleTOP (fillcolor white, size/center placing each WALL panel; each shape's own operand=over stacks them) -> nullTOP OUT_maskatlas. Best for regular grids.
composite_inside (Route C): compositeTOP operand=inside (mask alpha) or insideluminance (mask B/W luminance); content=input1, mask=input2, swaporder off, size=input1.
matte route: matteTOP mattechannel=alpha|luminance -- RGB from content(input1), cut from the mask(input2).
MAT alphamap route: mask -> phongMAT.alphamap (alphamapcoord=uv0) cuts window texels via surface alpha; emit-with-alpha interaction is subtler -- prefer the multiply route.
feathered recesses: rampTOP (radial/vertical) as a soft mask instead of hard shapes.
animated mask reveal: drive shape params or a levelTOP.opacity via the autoname export to open/close cutouts over time.

recipes.title: Split a finished facade composite to N overlapping projectors with an invisible soft-edge blend (data-only stand-in for camSchnappr Auto-Blend / projectorBlend)
recipes.summary: Real building projection almost always uses >=2 overlapping projectors -- this is the DATA-ONLY native equivalent of the camSchnappr Auto-Blend / projectorBlend .tox tools (uninstantiable). From a finished flat composite, build ONE chain PER PROJECTOR: cropTOP (this projector's master slice INCLUDING the shared overlap band) -> cornerpinTOP keystone -> multiply by an edge-blend ramp mask (rampTOP fed by a tableDAT of keyframes: flat 1.0 interior, linear 1->0 across the overlap band at the seam edge) that is gamma-corrected (levelTOP gamma1) so the two projectors' overlapping brightness SUMS to full instead of doubling/dark-seaming -> nullTOP -> windowCOMP to that projector's display. Extends projection_align_and_output (reuses its cornerpin keystone + windowCOMP/WIRE-ONLY handoff). BLEND-UNITY. On-site overlap width, corners, blend gamma are HUMAN-measured and typed back via set_par; the MCP builds the whole ramp/multiply/gamma/window scaffold + numeric defaults. WIRE-ONLY: windows built, not opened.

steps.note: The finished flat composite. Each projector chain crops ITS slice from this same master. Repeat steps 2-9 per projector i (example: N=2, proj0=LEFT, proj1=RIGHT).

verify.pass_if: master composite tap exists and cooks

steps.note: This projector's master slice INCLUDING the shared band (both projectors must carry the band pixels). Rule (axis x, w=1/N, master overlap o): cropleft{i}=max(0,i*w-o/2), cropright{i}=min(1,(i+1)*w+o/2). N=2,o=0.2: LEFT [0,0.6], RIGHT [0.4,1.0]. Horizontal seam (stacked) -> crop Y + vertical ramp. Wire OUT_master->in0. outputresolution=custom (256px trap).

verify.pass_if: slice incl. band; res==projector

steps.note: Per-projector keystone (each projector its OWN corners). pin* unit=fraction, identity TL(0,1)TR(1,1)BL(0,0)BR(1,0); mapping=perspective. HUMAN tunes corners on-site. Variant: use cornerpinTOP extract* corners to fold the crop in.

verify.pass_if: res==projector; identity until human-tuned

steps.note: The blend gradient as ramp KEYFRAMES (rampTOP gradient comes from a DAT, NOT colorN params -- those are picker swatches; position1/2 are radial centers). write_csv a table (cols: pos r g b a; first col=position 0..1 across the PROJECTOR frame) then set tableDAT.file AND fire pulse(loadonstartpulse) to load it -- setting file alone does NOT read the CSV mid-session (the Load File pulse is required). Band fraction f=o/slice_width (N=2: f=0.333). LEFT (band at RIGHT edge, 3 keys): 0,1,1,1,1 / 0.667,1,1,1,1 / 1,0,0,0,1. RIGHT (band at LEFT edge, 3 keys): 0,0,0,0,1 / 0.333,1,1,1,1 / 1,1,1,1,1. MIDDLE (both edges, 4 keys): 0,0,0,0,1 / f,1,1,1,1 / 1-f,1,1,1,1 / 1,0,0,0,1. HUMAN nudges band positions on-site. VERIFY column order live.

steps.geometry_out: DAT (ramp keyframes)

verify.pass_if: 3 (end) or 4 (middle) pos/rgba rows

steps.note: The blend mask. type=horizontal (vertical seam / side-by-side) or vertical (horizontal seam / stacked). dat=OUT_blend_keys{i}. phase=0, period=1, extendleft/right=hold (flat plateaus outside the keyed band). Match projector res.

Start gamma1=2.2 (real 1.8-2.4, HUMAN-measured). blacklevel lifts the toe for a faint edge line. Wire OUT_blend_ramp{i}->in0. Hero: a lookupTOP with a measured curve.

verify.pass_if: interior full-bright; content fades to black across the seam-edge band

The MCP builds the scaffold + defaults; measured numbers typed back via set_par. Native stand-in for camSchnappr Auto-Blend / projectorBlend.

Feed to analyzeTOP op=minimum/maximum: min~=max~=1.0 => 'overlapping brightness sums to full'. Dip below 1 -> raise gamma1 on both; above 1 -> lower. Delete after tuning.

recipes.classify: multi-projector edge blending -- split a finished facade composite to N OVERLAPPING projectors and soft-edge blend the overlap so the seam is invisible (native data-only stand-in for camSchnappr Auto-Blend / projectorBlend). Per projector: cropTOP slice + cornerpinTOP keystone + rampTOP(dat) blend mask + levelTOP gamma + multiplyTOP + windowCOMP; overlap width / corners / gamma are HUMAN-measured on-site
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE like projection_align_and_output. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: per-projector cropTOP+cornerpinTOP keystone + the blend stack (write_csv->tableDAT keyframes -> rampTOP.dat mask -> levelTOP gamma -> multiplyTOP) + windowCOMP, wired with numeric defaults. (2) HUMAN on-site: overlap-band width, per-projector corners, blend gamma/blacklevel measured on the rig and typed back via set_par -- the native equivalent of camSchnappr Auto-Blend / projectorBlend (.tox, not in catalog). BLEND MATH: masks must SUM to 1 across the band; a linear ramp dark-seams under projector gamma, so levelTOP gamma1 (~2.2, measured) re-flattens the sum. WIRE-ONLY: windowCOMP built not opened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF. rampTOP gradient = a DAT (pos,r,g,b,a rows) not colorN. BLEND-CURVE has THREE data-only options -- linear rampTOP (dark-seams), levelTOP gamma1~2.2 (the default), or a lookupTOP S-curve/raised-cosine (softest, practitioner-preferred); dome/curved warp is delegated to viosoTOP/scalabledisplayTOP with the camera-calibration solve as the HUMAN boundary (see dome_fisheye_master / curved_screen_warp_blend). 256px res trap on crop/ramp/multiply (multiply size defaults to input2). NC caps output 1280; topology identical at 1920/3840.
tips: rampTOP gradient = the DAT (rampTOP.dat, rows pos r g b a), NOT color1..4 (picker swatches) -- build the mask as a tableDAT (write_csv the file, set tableDAT.file then pulse(loadonstartpulse) to load it -- file alone does not read mid-session). VERIFY the r/g/b/a column order live.
Masks must SUM to 1: LEFT ramps 1->0 on its right edge, RIGHT ramps 0->1 on its left edge; a middle projector blends BOTH edges (4 keyframes).
Dark seam after wiring -> RAISE levelTOP gamma1 (linear masks always dark-seam under projector gamma; ~2.2 start). Bright seam -> LOWER gamma1. Faint edge line -> nudge blacklevel.
Band fraction is PROJECTOR-frame (f = master overlap o / slice width), not master-frame -- else the ramp lands in the wrong place.
multiplyTOP size defaults to input2 (the mask); set outputresolution=custom + projector res so content isn't resized. Same 256px trap on crop/ramp.

Per-CHANNEL blend match (projector R/G/B brightness drifts independently in the overlap): levelTOP has NO gamma1r/g/b -- use its per-channel INPUT levels lowr/highr/lowg/highg/lowb/highb, OR three per-channel curves via a lookupTOP (channel=independent), OR a channelmixTOP before the multiply. Do NOT set gamma1r/g/b; it does not exist and is silently ignored.
Verify without 2 projectors: show each OUT_proj{i}_final (ramp on the right edge, interior full-bright), then the addTOP+analyzeTOP unity proof (summed masks ~=1.0).
Crops MUST overlap in master space (both projectors carry the band pixels) or there's nothing to blend.
variants: Geometry-correct split (deep/angled facade, live 3D scene present): one cameraCOMP per real projector pose (projection=perspective, tx/tz/rx/ry/fov or winx/winy lens-shift) -> one renderTOP/renderpassTOP each -> the SAME ramp+gamma+multiply per render. Only when parallax across the facade matters; a flat composite uses crop+cornerpin.
Inline crop: skip cropTOP, use cornerpinTOP extract* corners to slice + keystone in one op.
N>2 tiling: end projectors 3-key masks, interior projectors 4-key; crop rule cropleft{i}=max(0,i*w-o/2), cropright{i}=min(1,(i+1)*w+o/2), w=1/N.
Stacked (horizontal seam): axis=y -- crop Y (cropbottom/croptop), rampTOP type=vertical.
Measured blend curve: swap levelTOP for a lookupTOP driven by an on-site-measured 1D curve DAT.

S-curve / raised-cosine blend (softer than pure gamma): keep the linear rampTOP mask, then feed it through a lookupTOP (method=secondinput, channel=independent; in0=OUT_blend_ramp{i} as the index, in1=a 1D rampTOP tracing a raised-cosine/smoothstep 0->1) for the 'slow at edges, fast in center' falloff practitioners prefer over both linear (hard mid-seam) and plain gamma; keep gamma1=2.2 as the simple default. lookupTOP outputresolution=custom + projector res.

Dome / curved surfaces (cornerpin + linear ramp cannot model the warp): replace the per-projector cornerpin+ramp+gamma stack with viosoTOP or scalabledisplayTOP (both in catalog) -- they ingest a camera-based auto-calibration solve (VIOSO / Scalable Display Manager) that produces the warp mesh + blend + black-level for domes/spheres/panoramas. The MCP instantiates + WIRES these (source->op->null->window) but the CALIBRATION SCAN/SOLVE is the HUMAN boundary (external camera + vendor tool) -- do not fake mesh-warp math data-only. See curved_screen_warp_blend / dome_fisheye_master.
Per-projector baked file: moviefileoutTOP (videocodec=hap, record=OFF) off each OUT_proj{i}_final for a media server that ingests per-projector files.

HELPER build_edge_blend(source, projectors=N, overlap=f, axis, projector_res, displays[], gamma, blacklevel): builds the whole per-projector crop+cornerpin+keys+ramp+gamma+multiply+null+window scaffold (~8*N ops) in one call; returns the OUT_proj{i}_final taps + prints the 3 human knobs (corners, band width, gamma).

recipes.title: Real-time input driver -- drive the facade LIVE from OSC / audio / DMX-ArtNet / MIDI (reactive, externally controlled)
recipes.summary: Make the per-section facade REACT to a live external source instead of a baked animation. A live-input CHOP (oscinCHOP, audiodeviceinCHOP+audiospectrumCHOP, dmxinCHOP, or midiinCHOP) produces one channel per section; those channels are renamed to matNN:emitr/g/b and pushed through the SAME rename->merge->null->autoname-export apply-block the height-sweep already uses. Only the signal SOURCE changes -- everything downstream is identical, so audio-reactive, OSC-from-a-console, a DMX lighting desk, and MIDI faders are all the same rig with a different first node. Receiving packets/audio is data-only -- no code path.

steps.note: LIVE SOURCE (OSC route, PROVEN). Binds a UDP port; an external process (lighting console, media server, phone app, or a plain UDP sender) sends OSC messages whose ADDRESS becomes the channel name. Send /s00../s14 -> channels s00..s14, one float per section. active=on, port=<your port>. oscaddressscope filters which addresses are accepted; stripprefixes trims leading /segments for naming. GOTCHA: a channel only EXISTS after its first packet arrives -- send before you inspect. For AUDIO/DMX/MIDI instead, swap this one node (see variants); the rest of the chain is unchanged.

key_params.active: on

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (one live channel per section, e.g. s00..s14)

verify.pass_if: channels s00..s14 present, values track what the sender sends

steps.note: MAP source channels -> parameter-export names, ONE renameCHOP per target component (emitr, emitg, emitb). Use WILDCARD CAPTURE renamefrom='s*' renameto='mat*:emitr' -- the '*' captures the index and substitutes it, so s07->mat07:emitr regardless of channel ORDER (robust for live sources where arrival order is not guaranteed; PREFER this over an explicit space-separated list, which needs a stable order). Three renames (r/g/b) fed from the same source = white brightness per section. For COLOUR, feed a per-section colour PRODUCT first (see per_section_color_choreography) then rename its r/g/b.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (channels matNN:emitr / :emitg / :emitb)

verify.pass_if: channels renamed to mat00:emitr .. mat14:emitr (index preserved)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (45 channels: matNN:emit{r,g,b})

verify.pass_if: 45 channels named matNN:emit{r,g,b}

steps.note: THE APPLY-BLOCK (identical to the sweep/colour rigs). set_par exportmethod=autoname + autoexportroot='..' (resolves matNN:emitr -> ../matNN.emitr), then set_flags export=true. CRITICAL: only ONE CHOP may export to a given parameter at a time -- if the height-sweep / colour rig is also exporting matNN:emit*, DISABLE it first (set_flags export=false on that null) or the two fight (last cook wins). Swapping the exporter flag is how you switch the show between 'baked sweep' and 'live input'.

verify.pass_if: export flag true; mat emit params show Export mode driven by OUT_rtout

verify.pass_if: exactly the externally-addressed sections are lit; changing the source changes the render

recipes.classify: make the per-section facade REACT in real time to a live external source -- OSC from a show-control app / lighting console, audio (music-reactive), a DMX/ArtNet/sACN lighting desk, or MIDI faders/notes -- instead of a pre-baked animation; externally controlled / interactive / reactive facade
recipes.governance: Real-time input is DATA-ONLY: receiving OSC/audio/DMX/MIDI packets is not a code path (no operator here evaluates a string as code). The apply-block is the SAME code-free CHOP-export mechanism as every other choreography recipe (channels named target:par + exportmethod=autoname + autoexportroot + the EXPORT flag). TWO disciplines: (1) EXACTLY ONE CHOP may export to a given parameter -- disable the sweep/colour exporter before enabling the live one (set_flags export=false/true) or they conflict. (2) Channel-name DETERMINISM -- wildcard capture (renamefrom='s*' renameto='mat*:emitr') is order-independent and robust for live sources; an explicit renameto list assumes a stable channel order. Networking: oscinCHOP/dmxinCHOP bind a UDP port -- loopback for a local controller, LAN for a real console; pick a free port and match the sender. NC build caps render resolution at 1280.
tips: A live channel only EXISTS after its first packet/sample -- send a test message before inspecting, or the rename/merge look empty.
Prefer wildcard-capture rename (s*->mat*:emitr) over an explicit name list: it maps by index, not by arrival order, so dropped/reordered packets can't misalign the facade.
Only ONE exporter per parameter. Symptom of two: the facade flickers or ignores the live input -- the other null (pm_out) is still exporting. set_flags export=false on it first.
Jittery live input (audio, cheap consoles) -> insert a lagCHOP or filterCHOP between source and rename to smooth; limitCHOP to clamp 0..1.

AUDIO route: audiodeviceinCHOP (live mic/line, needs a device) or audiofileinCHOP (a track) -> audiospectrumCHOP (fftsize sets bands) -> pick 15 bands (a selectCHOP or math) -> rename to sections. Music-reactive facade.

DMX/ArtNet route: dmxinCHOP interface=artnet|sacn, set net/subnet/universe to match the desk; its channels ARE the fixture values -> rename to sections. A lighting operator now runs the building from a grandMA/console.
MIDI route: midiinCHOP -> faders (control) or notes drive per-section levels; great for a hands-on operator.
Switch the show live: keep the baked sweep AND the live rig built; flipping which null has the export flag (set_flags export) crossfades control between 'automatic' and 'operator' with no rebuild.
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_input_driver(source=osc|audio|dmx|midi, port/universe, sections=15) -> the source + 3 renames + merge + null(autoname) in one call.
variants: audio_reactive (music-driven): audiodeviceinCHOP|audiofileinCHOP -> audiospectrumCHOP (fftsize=1024..8192) -> 15 frequency bands -> rename to matNN:emit -> the building pulses to the music. Add mathCHOP gain + lagCHOP attack/decay for a musical envelope.

dmx_console (ArtNet/sACN): dmxinCHOP interface=artnet or sacn, universe/net/subnet matched to the desk -> 512 channels; map 15 (or 45 for RGB) to the sections. The facade becomes a DMX fixture a lighting operator controls.
midi_operator: midiinCHOP control-change faders or note velocities -> per-section levels; hands-on live performance.
osc_color (not just brightness): send /s00r /s00g /s00b ... (or 3 OSC channels/section) and rename to matNN:emitr/g/b separately -> full live RGB per section from the console.
smoothed: source -> lagCHOP (lag1/lag2 = attack/release) or filterCHOP -> rename; de-jitters noisy real-world input.
trigger/gate: a logicCHOP / triggerCHOP on the source turns a threshold crossing (a beat, a fader past 50%, an OSC button) into a section cue -- reactive + event-driven.

recipes.title: Show control + timecode -- a cue TRANSPORT with GO buttons and timecode lock (run the show)
recipes.summary: The SHOW TRANSPORT layer above the choreography: a timerCHOP is the master clock that walks a list of timed CUES (a segments table), emitting a live 'segment' index + a 0..1 'timer_fraction' + running/done flags. Advance it by TIME (it auto-plays each segment), by a GO button (the `pulse` actuator: start / cuepulse / gotonextseg / gotoprevseg / gotodone -- allowlisted, parameterless, data-only), by EXTERNAL input (an OSC/MIDI button -> a toggle exported onto the timer), or lock it to external TIMECODE (timecodeCHOP reading LTC/MTC/system-time) for festival/broadcast sync. The transport output selects each cue's per-section values (a lookup into the cue table -- reuse facade_cue_choreography) which drive the SAME export apply-block.

steps.note: MASTER SHOW CLOCK. length = total (or per-segment) duration; play=on runs it; cycle=on loops the show; enable the output channels you need -- outseg -> a 'segment' cue-index channel, outsegplusfraction -> a per-cue 0..1 fraction (base output already has timer_fraction / running / done). segmethod=serial walks segments one after another (parallel = overlapping cues). This is the transport everything else hangs off.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (timer_fraction, segment, running, done)

verify.pass_if: channels timer_fraction/running/done (+ segment) present and advancing when play=on

steps.note: AUTHOR THE CUE LIST as the timer's segments table: one ROW per cue with a 'length' column (seconds), optional name/delay/begin columns. write_csv writes a confined .csv/.dat; load it into a tableDAT (set file, then pulse(loadonstartpulse) -- file alone does not read mid-session) and point timerCHOP.segdat at that DAT (segunits=seconds). The 'segment' output channel is then the LIVE cue index -- the spine of the whole show.
steps.geometry_out: tabular file -> tableDAT -> timerCHOP.segdat

verify.pass_if: one row per cue with a length column; timer.segdat points at it

steps.note: GO / TRIGGER -- the actuator (allowlisted, data-only, no code). pulse(timer, start) begins the show; pulse(timer, cuepulse) fires the segment cue; pulse(timer, gotonextseg|gotoprevseg|gotodone|gotoendcycle) jumps cues -- the manual/operator/AI GO button. For an EXTERNAL console GO, route an oscinCHOP/midiinCHOP button channel and EXPORT it onto the timer's 'play'/'cue' TOGGLE (a value, still data-only) or gate it with a triggerCHOP -- a CHOP can't fire a pulse (that would need an expression), so external triggers drive a toggle, while `pulse` covers MCP/operator-driven GO.
steps.geometry_out: (action -- advances the transport)

verify.pass_if: done channel 0->1 (or segment index increments on gotonextseg)

steps.note: BIND transport -> facade. The 'segment' cue index selects that cue's per-section values (a lookupCHOP/selectCHOP into the cue tableDAT from facade_cue_choreography), or 'timer_fraction' drives an interpolation; either way feed the SAME rename->merge->null->autoname-export apply-block. Do NOT rebuild the apply-block -- reuse the rig's. One exporter per param (disable others).
steps.geometry_out: (drives the 15 mats' emit via the shared export)

verify.pass_if: mat emit is Export-driven; changing the cue changes the values

steps.note: TIMECODE LOCK (festival/broadcast SYNC, optional). timecodeCHOP reads an external timecode -- LTC (SMPTE audio) off an audio input, MTC over MIDI, or system time-of-day -- as a running timecode value. Feed it to the timerCHOP external-timecode input (exttcop) or offset the show to wall-clock so the building stays frame-locked to a festival master clock / video playback. Standalone shows skip this (the timer's own clock is the master).
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (running timecode -> timer sync)

verify.pass_if: timecode advances in step with the external source (or system time)

steps.note: MILESTONE -- run the show and prove cues advance. Play the transport (or fire GO pulses), capture OUT_secfinal at 2-3 cue points: the facade must show a DIFFERENT state per cue, and a GO pulse must advance it. Confirms the transport, the cue binding, and the GO actuator end to end.
steps.geometry_out: TOP preview (inline)

verify.cheap: save_top @OUT_secfinal at cue 0, then pulse gotonextseg, save again
verify.pass_if: the render changes between cues; GO advances the show
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_secfinal across 2-3 cues -> distinct facade states; pulse gotonextseg advances the cue

recipes.classify: RUN THE SHOW -- a cue transport / playback timeline for the facade with GO buttons (start/cue/next-cue), external OSC-MIDI triggers, looping, and TIMECODE lock (LTC/MTC/SMPTE) for festival or broadcast sync; show control, playback, sequencing transport, go-cue, timecode
recipes.governance: Transport + GO are DATA-ONLY: a timerCHOP is a clock; the `pulse` actuator fires only parameterless, ALLOWLISTED actions (timerCHOP start/initialize/cuepulse/goto*/exitendcycle -- no code, no evaluated value, same risk class as the export flag; windowCOMP winopen/winclose + any execute/reinit are REFUSED). External triggers from a console reach the timer as a TOGGLE export (oscin/midiin channel -> timer play/cue) or a triggerCHOP -- a CHOP never fires a pulse (that needs an expression), so `pulse` is the MCP/operator GO path and toggles are the external-input path. Cue tables are authored with write_csv (confined). Timecode LOCK needs a real external feed: LTC on an audio input or MTC over MIDI; system time works standalone. One exporter per parameter (disable others before binding a new driver). NC render cap 1280.
tips: Turn ON the timer outputs you actually read: outseg -> a 'segment' cue index, outsegplusfraction -> per-cue 0..1; base output already has timer_fraction/running/done.
GO is the `pulse` tool and it is ALLOWLISTED: start / cuepulse / gotonextseg / gotoprevseg / gotodone / gotoendcycle / exitendcycle -- anything else (reset, execute, window) is refused by design.

A CHOP cannot fire a pulse. For an EXTERNAL console GO, export an oscin/midiin button channel onto the timer's play/cue TOGGLE (a value), or gate it with a triggerCHOP; use `pulse` for operator/AI-driven GO.
Loop an ambient show with cycle=on and no external trigger; run a triggered show with cycle=off and GO per cue.
The 'segment' channel is the cue INDEX -- lookup that row in the cue tableDAT (facade_cue_choreography) to get each cue's per-section values; don't rebuild the apply-block, reuse the rig's.
Timecode lock: timecodeCHOP source=LTC reads SMPTE off an audio input (wire the LTC audio in); MTC reads it over MIDI; tod uses the wall clock. Match rate (25/30 fps) to the master.
Festival/broadcast sync = feed timecodeCHOP into the timer's external-timecode input (exttcop) so the building is frame-locked to the show's master clock.
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_show(cues=[{name,length,cue_id}], loop, timecode=None) -> timerCHOP + segments tableDAT + lookup into the cue table + wiring, in one call.
variants: manual_go: cycle=off, one segment (or GO-gated segments); an operator/AI fires pulse cuepulse/gotonextseg per cue -- a hands-driven show.
timecode_lock: timecodeCHOP (LTC off audio / MTC off MIDI) -> timer exttcop; the facade is frame-locked to a festival master clock or a video server for perfect A/V sync.
looping_ambient: cycle=on, no external trigger -- an unattended looping installation that runs itself.
osc_triggered: an oscinCHOP button (a phone / console) -> exported onto the timer play/cue toggle, or a triggerCHOP -> GO from anywhere on the network.
parallel_cues: segmethod=parallel -- overlapping/crossfading cues instead of strictly serial ones.

recipes.title: Video on a segmented façade in one call: import_segmented_model -> per-section emit-map video -> WIRE-ONLY 4K file
recipes.summary: The end-to-end video-mapping flow. Copy the pre-sectioned building OBJs UNDER the working dir (assets/sections/), then import_segmented_model builds the WHOLE per-section rig (sec00..secNN geometryCOMPs, each with its own File In SOP + phong matNN, materials assigned, one-pass render-ready) in a SINGLE call — collapsing the ~6-calls-per-section hand build of per_section_material_rig. A moviefileinTOP supplies the content clip; set_par_many drives it onto every section's phong EMIT MAP (emitmap) sampled through the section's baked UVs (emitmapcoord=uv0), with emitr/g/b=1 (full-bright) and diffuse=0 so only the self-illuminated video shows (= projected light). One renderTOP (geometry='sec*') through a camera renders all sections in one pass; composite over a dark constantTOP, tap a null, and WIRE (record OFF) a moviefileoutTOP for the 4K HAP deliverable.

steps.tool: (copy the section OBJs into the working dir assets/sections/)
steps.note: CONFINEMENT PREREQUISITE (data-only meta-step; do it however you copy files). The F2 file-path confinement BLANKS any path outside the working dir, so section OBJs that live elsewhere (e.g. the Houdini export dir) load as EMPTY. Copy the pre-sectioned parts (section_00.obj … section_NN.obj, UVs + normals intact) INTO a confined subfolder such as assets/sections/ (gitignored), and import from THAT path. Skipping this is the classic 'building imports blank / loads the defgeo sample box' failure.

key_params.files: section_00.obj … section_NN.obj (UVs + normals from the per-meshId export)

steps.geometry_out: (files on disk, confined)

verify.pass_if: all section_*.obj present under the working dir

steps.note: ONE CALL builds the whole rig: for each section_{NN}.obj it creates a geometryCOMP secNN (default torus deleted, File In SOP render+display on), a phong matNN, and assigns matNN to secNN — the entire per_section_material_rig in a single tool. BUG-FIX BAKED IN: the importer forces the File In SOP `file` param to CONSTANT mode; earlier it left the param in its default EXPRESSION mode, which evaluates to TD's sample box (app.samplesFolder+'/Geo/defgeo.tog') and silently loaded an 80-point default cube instead of the real OBJ. Point `dir` at the CONFINED assets/sections/ from step 0. Sections import WITH their UVs (required for emitmap in step 3).
steps.geometry_out: N geometryCOMPs sec00..secNN + N phong mat00..matNN (materials assigned)

verify.pass_if: sec00..secNN + mat00..matNN exist; each File In SOP cooked prims>0 (NOT the 80-pt defgeo box)

steps.note: The content clip that gets sprayed onto the building. Loops while play=on (movie recycles; no loop param). Set outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h. ONE shared content TOP is the default — the sections' UVs place it across the façade; branch to N only where sections need DISTINCT clips. GPU codec (HAP / HAP Q) is essential when N sections each decode.

key_params.file: .mov HAP / .mp4 / image-seq (confined to the working dir)

steps.geometry_out: TOP (2D image, the content video)

verify.pass_if: res==requested, frame non-black (decoding)

steps.note: CORE, ONE CALL across all sections: assign the video to every section's EMIT MAP and set it full-bright + unlit. For each matNN set emitmap=<OUT_content path>, emitmapcoord=uv0 (samples the section's baked UVs = registers the video ON the surface), emitmapfilter=linear, emitmapextendu/v=hold (no edge bleed); emitr/g/b=1 (emitmap is MULTIPLIED by emit color — 1 = full-bright pass-through); diffr/g/b=0 and specr/g/b=0 (diffuse off — projection content is pure emission, needs no light). WINDOWS/non-content sections: leave emitmap blank + emitr/g/b=0 for a black cutout. set_par_many applies the same param dict to a list/pattern of ops in one round-trip (mat* -> N materials).

key_params.ops: mat* (all section materials; exclude window mats)
key_params.pars: { emitmap: <OUT_content>, emitmapcoord: uv0, emitmapfilter: linear, emitmapextendu: hold, emitmapextendv: hold, emitr: 1, emitg: 1, emitb: 1, diffr: 0, diffg: 0, diffb: 0, specr: 0, specg: 0, specb: 0 }

steps.geometry_out: (param edit across N materials)

verify.pass_if: each matNN.emitmap set, emitmapcoord==uv0, emitr/g/b==1, diffuse==0

steps.note: The projector viewpoint through which all sections render. For a flat façade use projection=ortho + orthowidth to frame the front face 1:1; for a lens/projector match use perspective (see recipe camera_match_facade). Referenced by the Render TOP's `camera` param (a path), not wired.

key_params.t/r: position on the façade normal axis, or lookat a façade-centre null
key_params.near/far: clip planes bracketing the whole model

steps.geometry_out: camera COMP

verify.pass_if: camera exists; model framed

steps.note: ONE render for the whole building: geometry='sec*' (a name-PATTERN matching every section COMP — proven) and camera=OUT_cam, both OP-reference PARAMS, not wires. Each prim draws its own matNN, so N videos light N surfaces in a single pass. No lights param — emission is self-illuminated. REQUIRED: outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h or it stays at the default res. Non-Commercial TD caps output at 1280 (use 1280x720; the graph is identical at 3840x2160 on a commercial licence). Output is a TRANSPARENT 2D image.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (2D image, transparent bg)

verify.pass_if: resolution == requested (custom), not default

steps.note: Dark plate to composite the transparent render over. GOTCHA — THE 256px TRAP: constantTOP DEFAULTS to 256x256 and will crush/mismatch the render. Set outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h to MATCH the render (1280x720).
steps.geometry_out: TOP (2D image)

verify.pass_if: solid black at the render resolution (NOT 256x256)

steps.note: Composite the render OVER the dark plate (render = input 0, bg = input 1; wire with `connect`). GOTCHA — THE 256px TRAP AGAIN: overTOP also defaults to 256x256 — set outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h to match the render. This is the readable beauty plate.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (2D image)

verify.pass_if: over TOP has both inputs wired; res matches render (not 256)

steps.note: Plant the stable output tap the output/hand-off lane targets by NAME. Preview: save_top @OUT_facade_video with the timeline PLAYING returns an inline image, or point the perform window (set_par /perform winop=<the over TOP>, size='fill').
steps.geometry_out: TOP (2D image)

verify.pass_if: video registered per section via UVs; windows black; content reads at target resolution

steps.note: WIRE-ONLY 4K deliverable. Wire OUT_facade_video in and set the codec + path, but leave `record` OFF — the operator fires the record. HAP / HAP Q is the media-server playback default (GPU-decoded, smooth multi-layer 4K); HAP Alpha carries transparency. On a commercial licence render + output at 3840x2160; on Non-Commercial the whole chain is capped at 1280.

key_params.file: output path (confined to the working dir)
key_params.record: leave OFF — the operator's gated action

steps.geometry_out: TOP (terminal output op)

verify.pass_if: wired, record == OFF

output_opportunity.why: Baking the 4K deliverable writes a large file — a heavy, side-effectful action that is the operator's call. The bridge builds and wires the output op but does not fire it.
output_opportunity.propose_via: Offer to WIRE the moviefileoutTOP (codec/path set, record OFF) and hand off; tell the user to press record when ready.
output_opportunity.consent: Enabling record is a human-gated action performed by the operator in TouchDesigner, never by the bridge.

recipes.classify: video on surfaces / project video / spray video onto a building / video mapping — one-call import a segmented building model and blast a content clip onto every façade section (UV-registered), rendered and wired to a 4K file
recipes.governance: CONFINEMENT IS MANDATORY: the segmented models MUST live UNDER the working dir (copy them into assets/sections/ first) — the F2 file-path confinement blanks any path outside it, so external OBJs load empty. import_segmented_model forces the File In SOP to CONSTANT mode so the real OBJ loads (the earlier default-EXPRESSION-mode bug silently loaded TD's defgeo sample box — an 80-point cube — instead of the model). Content maps ONLY if the sections carry UVs (they do, from the per-meshId export) — emitmap requires texture coords, sampled with emitmapcoord=uv0. emitmap is MULTIPLIED by emit color, so emitr/g/b is the per-section dimmer/tint; setting it to 1 = full-bright, or leave it driven by a choreography export to reveal/fade the video over time (see segmented_facade_video_content). Emission is unlit — no light needed; diffuse/spec set to 0. THE 256px TRAP: constantTOP/overTOP default to 256x256 and crush the render — always set outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h. Non-Commercial builds cap output at 1280 (use 1280x720; identical graph at 3840x2160 on commercial). Output is WIRE-ONLY: the moviefileoutTOP is wired with record OFF; enabling record is the operator's gated action.
tips: Building imports blank / a tiny cube -> the OBJs are OUTSIDE the working dir (confinement blanked the path) OR you hit the old defgeo bug. Fix: copy the sections into assets/sections/ and import from there; the current import_segmented_model forces CONSTANT mode so the real mesh loads.

PER-SECTION mapping (this recipe) vs a UNIFIED camera-projected map: here each section samples the shared clip through its OWN baked UVs (emitmap + emitmapcoord=uv0) — precise, UV-registered, and free to modulate per section. For a single image projected across the whole building from a viewpoint (no per-section UVs needed), use a UNIFIED CAMERA PROJECTION instead: projectionPOP / texturemapPOP in perspective mode driven by a cameraCOMP (project the clip along the camera's view), or a lightCOMP acting as a projector via its projector/projmap map. Camera projection ignores surface UVs (projects from the eye), so it fixes bad/missing UVs but distorts on oblique faces; per-section UV mapping is the sharper choice when the export UVs are good.

Windows/recesses must stay black -> exclude their materials from the set_par_many (or set those matNN emitmap blank + emitr/g/b=0) so the glass reads as a punched-out cutout next to the glowing walls.
One shared content TOP is the default (UVs place it); only branch to N moviefileinTOPs where sections need DISTINCT clips — each distinct clip is a GPU decode, so use HAP/HAP Q.

Reveal/fade the video over time for free: leave emitr/g/b driven by the height_sweep_choreography (or facade_cue_choreography) export instead of a static 1 — the sweep's 0..1 multiplies the emitmap, revealing the video per section with zero extra nodes.
Never enable record from the bridge — confirm moviefileoutTOP.record is OFF with read_network before hand-off; the operator fires it.
variants: Unified camera projection (no per-section UVs): projectionPOP / texturemapPOP in perspective mode fed by a cameraCOMP, or a lightCOMP projector (projmap) — one clip projected across the whole building from the eye instead of per-section UV sampling.
Sweep-/cue-modulated reveal: leave emitr/g/b bound to the height_sweep_choreography or facade_cue_choreography export so the content is revealed/faded per section over time (emitmap x emit color).
Distinct clip per section: branch N moviefileinTOPs (one per matNN.emitmap) instead of one shared TOP — N GPU decodes, HAP/HAP Q essential.
Drive an EXISTING hand-built rig instead of one-call import: recipe segmented_facade_video_content applies the same emitmap-video onto a per_section_material_rig you built step by step.
4K commercial delivery: render + moviefileoutTOP at 3840x2160 (UHD) / 4096x2160 (DCI) on a commercial licence — the graph is identical, only the resolution caps differ.
Keystone for a real projector: append a cornerpinTOP (numeric pin corners = data-only) after OUT_facade_video, then the output lane (see projection_align_and_output).

recipes.title: Mesh / freeform UV warp of a composite onto an irregular surface (data-only remapTOP, the analog of kantanMapper)
recipes.summary: Warp a finished facade composite onto a curved / multi-plane / irregular surface with a remapTOP driven by a DATA-ONLY remap map -- the data-only analog of kantanMapper / MadMapper mesh warp. Build an IDENTITY UV field (rampTOP horizontal -> R, rampTOP vertical -> G, packed by a reorderTOP), author a coarse control-grid of per-vertex (du,dv) OFFSETS as a CSV (write_csv -> tableDAT -> dattoCHOP -> choptoTOP -> blurTOP up to full res), ADD the offset field to the identity (compositeTOP operand=add) to get the final map, then remapTOP(in0=content, in1=map, horzsource=red, vertsource=green, resolutionsource=input2) applies the warp. With a zero (or bypassed) offset the map is identity and the remap reproduces the source UNCHANGED; a non-zero control grid visibly bends the content (a smooth central bulge). The interactive per-vertex DRAG (kantanMapper) is a HUMAN step whose measured numbers are typed back by editing the control-grid CSV / set_par -- data-only end to end up to that on-site nudge.

steps.tool: (tap OUT_aligned / OUT_facade_video / OUT_render, or a moviefileinTOP / noiseTOP)
steps.note: Start from the content you want to warp -- a finished composite, a moviefileinTOP of media (file MUST be under the working dir; set the file via set_par with an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path AFTER create -- a relative path is rejected as 'outside working directory'), or (proven here) a colored noiseTOP. Wire it into the remapTOP's FIRST input (in0 = the content to be resampled). This recipe consumes content; it does not make it.

verify.pass_if: content tap exists and cooks

steps.note: HORIZONTAL identity ramp: type=horizontal -> the default black->white gradient whose RED channel rises 0..1 left->right = the source U coordinate for every column. outputresolution=custom, resolutionw/h = the WARP output resolution (projector res). Make a sibling OUT_uvv with type=vertical for the V coordinate.

verify.pass_if: red rises 0->1 left to right

steps.note: VERTICAL identity ramp: type=vertical -> red rises 0..1 bottom->top = the source V coordinate. Same custom resolution as OUT_uvh.

verify.pass_if: red rises 0->1 bottom to top

steps.note: PACK the identity UV map: input0=OUT_uvh, input1=OUT_uvv. outputred=input1 + outputredchan=red (U), outputgreen=input2 + outputgreenchan=red (V), outputbluechan=zero, outputalphachan=one. Result RG = (u,v) in 0..1 -> feeding this alone to remapTOP reproduces the source UNCHANGED (the identity check). This is the base the warp offsets add to. NOTE reorder input1/input2 = the FIRST/SECOND wired input.

verify.pass_if: R=horizontal ramp, G=vertical ramp (red-green gradient)

steps.note: AUTHOR the coarse control grid = the deformable mesh, data-only. An NxM grid (e.g. 5x5) flattened to N*M rows with a du,dv HEADER row, per-vertex UV OFFSETS (0 = no displacement). Path MUST be under the working dir with a .csv/.tsv/.txt/.dat extension. Start all-zeros (identity) and let the on-site human fill measured nudges; a single strong central value gives a visible bulge. This CSV IS the freeform-mesh state; editing a cell moves a control vertex.

verify.pass_if: warp_grid.csv written under the working dir

steps.note: Load the control grid: set tableDAT.file via set_par with an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path (a file passed at create time can normalize to a \\?\ path and not read), THEN fire pulse(loadonstartpulse) to read it. GOTCHA: setting file alone does NOT load the CSV mid-session, and loadonstart is project-start only -- the Load File pulse is what reads it now. After that the 25 (du,dv) rows load. Data-only source of the warp; no expression / code.

key_params.load: pulse(loadonstartpulse) after set file -- reads the CSV now

verify.pass_if: header du,dv + N*M offset rows present

steps.note: Table -> CHOP so it can become pixels: dat=OUT_warptable, output=chanpercol (each COLUMN -> a channel), firstrow=names (header du,dv names the channels), firstcolumn=values (there is NO row-name column -- else du would be eaten as row names). Result: channels 'du','dv', each with N*M samples.

verify.pass_if: channels du,dv carry the control-grid offsets

steps.note: CHOP -> a small NxM TOP: chop=OUT_warpchop, dataformat=rg (du->R, dv->G), layout=rowswrapped, outputresolution=custom, resolutionw/h = the control-grid dims (e.g. 5x5) so the N*M samples fill the grid. LOW-RES offset field (one texel per control vertex). NOTE choptoTOP writes samples into ROW 0 unless resolution matches -- keep res == grid dims here.

verify.pass_if: NxM texels, RG = per-vertex offsets

steps.note: SMOOTH + upscale the coarse grid to full warp resolution: outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h = projector res, size = a moderate blur so the per-vertex offsets interpolate into a continuous displacement field (bilinear-ish mesh). Turns a handful of control points into a smooth freeform surface.

verify.pass_if: smooth RG offset field at full res

steps.note: FINAL MAP = identity + offsets: operand=add, input0=OUT_uvident, input1=OUT_warpoffset, outputresolution=custom at projector res. Where offsets are 0 the map is identity (content unwarped); where the human nudged a vertex the lookup shifts = the warp. This RG map is remapTOP's second input.

verify.pass_if: identity where grid=0, displaced where grid!=0

steps.note: THE WARP. input0=OUT_warpsrc (content), input1=OUT_remapmap (the RG lookup). horzsource=red, vertsource=green (these name the CHANNEL of the SECOND input that supplies the per-pixel lookup coord -- NOT 'input2'; the second input is the map by wiring). resolutionsource=input2 so output matches the map/projector res. extend=zero (off-surface -> black). outputresolution=custom at projector res. Bypass OUT_remapmap (pure identity) and the output equals the source exactly; un-bypass and the content visibly bends. Wire OUT_warped downstream into projection_align_and_output / the output lane.

verify.pass_if: content follows the warp; zero/bypassed offset -> unchanged image

steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === On site the mapper drags control vertices to make content hug the real surface. TD has NO data-only interactive freeform-mesh editor op (kantanMapper / projectorMapper are .tox palette components needing Python + live mouse -- NOT in the catalog). WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds the whole remap network + the control-grid table; the human's measured per-vertex offsets are TYPED BACK by editing warp_grid.csv (re-run write_csv -> tableDAT reloads) or set_par on a pre-offset transform. The interactive DRAG is the human step; the numeric warp is ours -- exactly like the on-site cornerpin drag in projection_align_and_output.

verify.pass_if: grid holds on-site offsets (or zeros for authoring)

recipes.classify: mesh / freeform / irregular-surface WARP for projection mapping -- warp video onto a mesh / freeform warp / bend a finished facade composite onto a curved or multi-plane building surface with a data-only remapTOP UV map (the analog of kantanMapper / MadMapper mesh warp), authored from an identity UV field + a control-grid CSV of per-vertex offsets; the interactive per-vertex drag is a HUMAN step whose numbers are typed back
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE, like projection_align_and_output. (1) DATA-ONLY: the entire remap network + identity UV field + control-grid table are created / wired / parameterized by the bridge; no expression / Python / callback anywhere. (2) HUMAN: the on-site interactive mesh drag (kantanMapper .tox) is NOT a data-only op; the bridge builds the numeric structure and the human's per-vertex offsets are typed back via write_csv / set_par. GOTCHAS: set a moviefileinTOP/tableDAT file via set_par with an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path AFTER create (+ tableDAT loadonstart=on) or the file will not read; remapTOP horzsource/vertsource are CHANNEL tokens (red/green) not 'input2'. NC build caps render at 1280; swap resolutionw/h for 4K, topology identical.
tips: Prove the plumbing first: bypass the compositeTOP (map = pure identity) and confirm remapTOP reproduces the source EXACTLY before authoring any offset -- isolates map wiring from warp authoring.
remapTOP defaults (horzsource=red, vertsource=green) already match an RG identity map; the only must-sets are extend=zero and resolutionsource=input2.
The offset field is ADDED to the identity, so du/dv are FRACTIONS of the full UV range (0.1 ~= a 10% shift). Keep them small; a smooth blur turns a 5x5 grid into a continuous mesh.
For content warp visibility use structured content (a grid/checker/colored noise); a flat field hides the bend.
variants: Analytic warp (no control grid): for a KNOWN curved surface (cylinder, bowed wall) build the offset field with rampTOP / transformTOP / noiseTOP math instead of the write_csv->choptoTOP steps, then the same compositeTOP add + remapTOP.

displaceTOP one-node path: displaceTOP (2 inputs: content + displacement map; horzsource/vertsource pick channels, displaceweightx/y scale) applies the OFFSET field directly without the explicit identity-add -- remapTOP is the absolute-UV path, displaceTOP the relative-offset path.
4K: set every outputresolution custom resolutionw/h to 3840x2160; topology identical (NC render cap 1280 previews downscaled).

recipes.title: DMX / Art-Net / sACN OUTPUT -- drive fixtures / LED / wash lighting FROM TouchDesigner in sync with the facade (data-only, WIRE-ONLY enable)
recipes.summary: Make TD a lighting SOURCE, not just a receiver -- control lights / fixtures / LED / wash / pixel-mapping from TD in sync with the projection. Route A (simple/wash/generic): a CHOP whose samples/channels ARE the DMX slot values (patternCHOP / constantCHOP, or the choreography drivers) -> dmxoutCHOP with interface = Art-Net | sACN | KiNET | Serial + net/subnet/universe -> a universe on the wire. Route B (pixel-mapping LED): a POP with a per-point colour attr -> dmxfixturePOP (per-channel value blocks mapping Cd -> RGB channels) -> dmxoutPOP -> the universe; a dmxmapDAT (POP input only) reads the channel map back for a data-only VERIFY. The SAME choreography drivers feed the lighting, so projected content and physical fixtures move together. WIRE-ONLY: dmxoutCHOP/dmxoutPOP active DEFAULTS ON -- the bridge MUST set active=off; the operator connects the physical Art-Net node/interface + fixtures and enables output. The bridge never puts packets on a live universe.

steps.note: ROUTE A source (patternCHOP; constantCHOP for fixed values). Build a CHOP whose samples = the DMX slot values: e.g. patternCHOP wavetype=ramp length=512 (a full 512-slot universe fade), or per-section emit brightness/colour from per_section_color_choreography, or a cue timer, or the live realtime_input_driver. Order/rename to the fixtures' patch. Plant a nullCHOP OUT_dmxvals as the stable tap. Values 0..1 (dmxoutCHOP scales to 0..255) or raw 0..255 per Format.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (N samples/channels = N DMX slots)

verify.pass_if: values in range, ordered to the patch

steps.note: ROUTE A sink. input0=OUT_dmxvals. interface=artnet (a MENU: serial | enttecusbpro | enttecusbpromk2 | artnet | sacn | kinet -- so no separate sACN op is needed; artnet is the DEFAULT). net/subnet/universe to match the fixtures' patch; format=packetpersample (one CHANNEL, each SAMPLE = a DMX slot) or packetperchan (each CHANNEL = a slot). netaddress for the Art-Net node (or broadcast; multicast=on for sACN). rate = refresh Hz (e.g. 44). *** active=off *** -- ACTIVE DEFAULTS ON, so this MUST be set explicitly (WIRE-ONLY, like ndiout/spout active). Building this node with active=off does NOT emit packets.

verify.pass_if: interface/universe/net/subnet set; active OFF

steps.note: NON-DESTRUCTIVE PROOF (Route A). Confirm the patch WITHOUT any packet leaving: read_network @OUT_dmxsend pars=true shows active=off + universe/net/subnet/interface; inspect @OUT_dmxvals shows the per-slot values. (dmxmapDAT is NOT usable here -- its dmxpop input is POP-only; it belongs to Route B.) This is the wire-only proof the mapping is right before the human goes live.

verify.pass_if: active OFF and universe/channel mapping matches the intended patch

steps.note: ROUTE B (pixel-mapping LED, many fixtures). input0 = a POP with a per-point colour attr (e.g. Cd sampled from the content per LED). Define the fixture's channel blocks (per-channel value source=attribute, name=Cd, comps=3 for RGB) plus net/subnet/universe/channel/changap for the patch layout. Each point becomes a fixture at consecutive DMX addresses -> the classic LED pixel-map. (Confirm the exact per-channel param names against the live node UI.)
steps.geometry_out: POP (points patched to DMX channels)

verify.pass_if: points carry a colour attr mapped to RGB channels

steps.note: ROUTE B sink. Collect the fixture POP(s); interface=artnet|sacn + net/subnet/universe + netaddress. *** active=off *** until hardware is connected + the human enables. Same wire-only posture as Route A (active DEFAULTS ON).

verify.pass_if: fixture POP wired; universe set; active OFF

steps.note: ROUTE B data-only VERIFY. dmxpop = OUT_fixture / OUT_pixsend (a POP -- this input is POP-only, it does NOT read a dmxoutCHOP). netfilter/subnetfilter/universefilter to scope. Prints the universe -> channel -> value MAP as a table you can inspect -- confirms the patch WITHOUT any packet leaving.

verify.pass_if: channel<->value map matches the intended patch

steps.tool: (WIRE-ONLY / HUMAN: go live on a real universe)
steps.note: === WIRE-ONLY BOUNDARY (a physical device is involved). === The bridge builds + patches + verifies the ENTIRE output network with active=off. GOING LIVE is the operator's step: connect the Art-Net/sACN node (or serial DMX interface) + the fixtures, confirm the patch, then set active=on (set_par). Same discipline as opening a windowCOMP or firing a moviefileoutTOP record -- the bridge never enables an output onto real hardware. NOTE: artnetDAT is NOT the output path -- it is a receive/discovery DAT whose `callbacks` param is a universally-denied code-sink; output goes through dmxoutCHOP/dmxoutPOP, which carry NO denied params.

verify.pass_if: active still OFF until the operator flips it

recipes.classify: drive DMX / Art-Net / sACN OUTPUT from TouchDesigner -- TD as a lighting / pixel-mapping SOURCE to control lights / fixtures / LED / wash feeding facade lighting in sync with the projection: Route A CHOP channel-set -> dmxoutCHOP universe (simple/wash), Route B coloured POP -> dmxfixturePOP -> dmxoutPOP (pixel-mapping LED); read_network/inspect (Route A) or dmxmapDAT (Route B) read the patch back; enabling output onto real hardware is a WIRE-ONLY human step (active defaults ON, bridge sets it OFF)
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY + WIRE-ONLY. Building the CHOP/POP source, the dmxout node, the fixture patch, and the read-back is data-only (no code path: producing DMX values from channels/attributes evaluates no string as code). The artnetDAT is deliberately NOT used for output -- it is a receive/discovery DAT whose `callbacks` param is a UNIVERSALLY DENIED code-sink; output goes through dmxoutCHOP/dmxoutPOP, which have NO denied params, so the output capability is fully intact. WIRE-ONLY: dmxoutCHOP/dmxoutPOP active DEFAULTS ON and MUST be set off; the operator connects the physical interface + fixtures and enables output. sACN/KiNET/serial are interface-MENU options on the same ops -- no separate op needed. DMX has no image, so the live proof is inspection of the driving values (a choptoTOP visualization of the universe ramp) + read_network confirming active=off.
tips: dmxoutCHOP.active DEFAULTS ON -- the single most important wire-only set: active=off. Verify with read_network pars=true (a default-on toggle shows as active:false only when you set it).
One op, many protocols: interface = serial | enttecusbpro | enttecusbpromk2 | artnet | sacn | kinet. No separate sACN/KiNET op.
format=packetpersample puts ONE channel's N samples across N DMX slots (great for a strip/universe fade); packetperchan puts each CHANNEL on one slot (great for named per-fixture channels).
A full DMX universe is 512 slots -- a patternCHOP length=512 ramp is a clean, sane, inspectable universe to prove the mapping.
Visualize the driving CHOP with a choptoTOP -- but it writes samples into ROW 0 (make it 1px tall, then upscale) and dataformat=r leaves alpha 0 (set the extra alpha to 1).
variants: Route B pixel-mapping: dmxfixturePOP (Cd -> RGB channel blocks) -> dmxoutPOP for per-LED mapping of many fixtures; dmxmapDAT (POP input) reads the patch back.
sACN / KiNET / serial: same dmxoutCHOP/dmxoutPOP, just switch the interface menu (multicast=on for sACN).

Loopback self-test (operator step, never in a design session): interface=artnet, netaddress=127.0.0.1, active=on, and read it back with a dmxinCHOP -- a send->receive proof that never leaves the machine.

recipes.title: Calibrated-projector spatial projection onto 3D geometry (cast content FROM a virtual projector whose lens+placement match the real one onto a building mesh -- the true 3D projection-mapping path, NOT a 2D warp or a camera match)
recipes.summary: Project a content TOP onto 3D geometry from a VIRTUAL PROJECTOR calibrated to the real projector's lens + physical placement, so the image lands on the surface exactly as the hardware would -- distinct from mesh_freeform_warp (2D remapTOP) and camera_match_facade (viewpoint registration). PRIMARY route (GPU-standard): a lightCOMP AS the projector -- lighttype=cone, projmap=<content TOP>, projmapmode=useview (cast along the light's OWN frustum = calibrated; simplehorzfov is the quick-and-dirty alternative), projection=perspective with viewanglemethod=focalaperture + focal/aperture set to the real lens (or projmatrixop referencing a CHOP/DAT of the measured 4x4 intrinsics for exact calibration); aim + place the light (tx/ty/tz + lookat, or rx/ry/rz) at the surveyed projector position; projmapextendu/v=zero so outside the frustum stays black. A phongMAT on the geo makes the surface RECEIVE the projected light (a constantMAT ignores lights and would show nothing). Render through a SEPARATE viewer cameraCOMP (audience/inspection POV, never the projector) so you can see the mapped result. ALTERNATIVE route (bake the projector's view into UVs): projectionPOP(camera=<projector cameraCOMP>, fromcoordsys=cartesian, tocoordsys=screenspace, outputattrscope=Tex) writes per-point UVs from the projector's viewpoint, then texturemapPOP samples the content by those UVs -> render; use it when you want the texture 'pinned' as the projector sees it (survives re-lighting) rather than modulating a light. The on-site keystone residual is removed data-only by editing the projector transform / projmatrixop via set_par, or a trailing cornerpinTOP on the output.

steps.tool: (tap OUT_geo/OUT_model from facade_3d_render, OUT_secrig from import_segmented_model, import_scan; else geometryCOMP + fileinSOP)
steps.note: The 3D surface to project onto -- a renderable geometryCOMP holding the building mesh (model file MUST live under the working dir). This recipe LIGHTS existing geometry; it does not build the mesh. Surface UVs are NOT required for the primary (projector-light) route -- the projector casts from its own eye, not the surface's UVs (that is exactly what fixes bad/missing UVs). The alternative UV-bake route DOES write UVs (Tex) onto the points.

verify.pass_if: a renderable geometryCOMP with geometry inside exists

steps.note: The image the projector casts. Tap a finished composite (OUT_facade_video), a moviefileinTOP of media (file under the working dir; set the path via set_par with an ABSOLUTE forward-slash value AFTER create -- a relative path is rejected as outside the working dir), or (proven here) a noiseTOP. This is wired into the projector's projmap (primary) or sampled by texturemapPOP (alternative).

verify.pass_if: content TOP cooks with a non-zero resolution

steps.note: Assign to the surface via the geometryCOMP's material par (set_par geo.material=<this>). The material MUST be lit -- phongMAT, NOT constantMAT (constant ignores lights, so the projected cone would never appear). Keep diffuse mid and specular low so the projected image reads cleanly; drop ambient in the scene so ONLY the projector lights the surface (a pure projection look).

verify.pass_if: the geometryCOMP's material points at OUT_projmat

steps.note: THE calibrated projector. lighttype=cone; projmap=<OUT_projcontent> (the Projector Map); projmapmode=useview so the map is cast along the light's own projection frustum (calibrated) rather than a naive horizontal FOV; projection=perspective; viewanglemethod=focalaperture with focal+aperture matched to the real projector lens (or set projmatrixop to a CHOP/DAT carrying the measured 4x4 intrinsics for exact calibration -- this is the projection-MATRIX injection point, a legit data DAT, not a shader). coneangle/conedelta bound the beam; projmapextendu/v=zero keeps everything outside the frustum black. Position + aim (tx/ty/tz + lookat the surface, or rx/ry/rz) at the SURVEYED physical projector placement.

verify.pass_if: lighttype=cone and projmap resolves to OUT_projcontent

steps.note: The VIEWER camera -- the audience / inspection viewpoint from which you judge the mapped result. It is DISTINCT from the projector (the projector is the lightCOMP above); do not render through the projector. Place/aim it where you evaluate the projection (often near the real audience sightline).

verify.pass_if: a cameraCOMP aimed at the surface exists

steps.note: Render the lit surface: geometry=<OUT_projsurface>, camera=<OUT_viewcam>, lights=<OUT_projector>. Set outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h to the projector/delivery resolution -- do NOT leave the 256px default (the 256px trap). Non-Commercial builds cap output at 1280 (use 1280x720; the identical graph runs 3840x2160 on a commercial licence).

verify.pass_if: renderTOP cooks at the set resolution with the projected pattern on the surface

steps.note: Composite the render over a constantTOP black plate (outputresolution=custom to match) so the un-projected area is a clean, premultiplied black for the media server. Keeps the deliverable a full-frame image the downstream warp/blend can consume.

verify.pass_if: composite cooks at delivery resolution

steps.note: The stable OUT tap for the output/handoff lane (see output_handoff / projection_align_and_output). WIRE-ONLY: any downstream moviefileoutTOP/NDI is wired with record/active OFF -- the operator fires it.

verify.pass_if: OUT tap cooks and is ready for the output lane

steps.note: UV-BAKE route instead of the projector light: projectionPOP(camera=<a cameraCOMP set up AS the projector with the same focal/aperture>, fromcoordsys=cartesian, tocoordsys=screenspace, outputattrscope=Tex, fov matched) writes per-point UVs from the projector's viewpoint onto the surface points; texturemapPOP then samples OUT_projcontent by those baked UVs; render as above through the viewer camera. Choose this when you want the texture PINNED as the projector sees it (independent of scene lighting) rather than modulating a cone light. Both routes are data-only.

The physical alignment loop, data-only: measure the real projector's position + lens and type them into the projector's tx/ty/tz + rx/ry/rz + focal/aperture via set_par (or feed a measured 4x4 into projmatrixop). Residual keystone from imperfect placement is removed by a trailing cornerpinTOP (numeric corner pins) on OUT_projection -- matching projection_align_and_output. Everything up to the surveyed numbers is data-only; the survey itself is the human step.

recipes.governance: WIRE-ONLY output by design (any moviefileoutTOP/NDI downstream is left with record/active OFF; the operator fires it). The surface material MUST be a phongMAT (lit) -- a constantMAT ignores lights and the projected cone would not appear. Avoid the 256px trap: set outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h on the renderTOP AND the constantTOP/overTOP plate. Non-Commercial builds cap output at 1280 (1280x720; the graph is identical at 3840x2160 on commercial). projmatrixop / projection matrices are legit projection-MATRIX data DATs (core to projection mapping), not shader code.
tips: Nothing on the surface -> the material is a constantMAT (unlit). Switch to phongMAT and assign it via the geometryCOMP's material par; drop scene ambient so only the projector lights it.

Projected image is soft/low-detail on oblique faces -> that is correct projector foreshortening (the eye projects, not the surface UVs). For sharp per-face registration where the export UVs are GOOD, prefer per-section UV mapping (segmented_facade_video_projection) instead; the projector route is the fix for bad/missing UVs.

Calibrate the lens, not just the pose: set viewanglemethod=focalaperture + focal/aperture to the real projector's throw, or inject the measured 4x4 via projmatrixop -- pose (tx/ty/tz+rot) alone will not match a real lens.

Two or more projectors on one building -> one lightCOMP projector each (each with its own projmap slice + calibration), rendered together; edge-blend the overlaps downstream (multiprojector_edge_blend) or on the media server.
Keep the projector and the viewer camera separate -- rendering through the projector shows the content flat (the projector's own view), not how it lands on the building.
variants: UV-bake (texture pinned to the surface): projectionPOP -> texturemapPOP fed by a projector cameraCOMP, instead of the cone-light projmap -- survives scene re-lighting.
Exact intrinsics: drive the projector's projmatrixop from a CHOP/DAT of the measured 4x4 projection matrix (from a calibration solve) rather than focal/aperture.
Keystone finish: append a cornerpinTOP (numeric pins = data-only) after OUT_projection, then the output lane (projection_align_and_output).
4K commercial delivery: render + output at 3840x2160 (UHD) / 4096x2160 (DCI) on a commercial licence -- identical graph, only the resolution caps differ.

recipes.title: Data-only multi-quad 2D projection mapper (N sources -> per-quad cornerpinTOP -> one compositeTOP over black -> OUT_aligned) -- the plain-operator kantanMapper substitute
recipes.summary: Map N independent flat/quad surfaces (shop windows, stage flats, sign faces, building faces treated as quads) the way kantanMapper does, but entirely data-only. Per surface: a content TOP -> a cornerpinTOP that CROPS the source sub-region (Extract page: extracttl/tr/bl/br) and PLACES+keystones the quad onto the projector canvas (Pin page: pintopleft/pintopright/pinbotleft/pinbotright as fraction 0..1 of the canvas, mapping=perspective, extend=zero so outside the quad is transparent, outputresolution=custom at projector res, bgcolor alpha 0). All N cornerpins wire into ONE compositeTOP (maxinputs=9999, tops multi-input, operand=over) stacked over a black constantTOP canvas, then a nullTOP(OUT_aligned) hands off WIRE-ONLY to the output lane. kantanMapper itself is a Python .tox that draws shapes by live mouse -- NOT buildable here; this recipe is its typed-operator equivalent and the on-site corner-drag is the HUMAN step whose measured numbers are typed back via set_par on the pin* params. KEY GOTCHA: cornerpinTOP defaults outputresolution=useinput and pin/extract are DIFFERENT pages -- extract* crops the SOURCE, pin* warps the QUAD; leave res at useinput or swap the two and quads composite at wrong size/place.

steps.note: BLACK PROJECTOR CANVAS = the base layer every quad composites over (kantanMapper's black project background). color black, alpha 0 so it stays a transparent-but-sized ground; outputresolution=custom at the PROJECTOR resolution (256px trap: leave it and the canvas is 256x256). This defines the composite size and aspect. Wire it as the FIRST input of the final compositeTOP.
steps.geometry_out: black RGBA canvas at projector resolution

verify.pass_if: resolution == projector res, all pixels black/alpha 0

steps.note: SOURCE for quad 0 (repeat this + the cornerpin per surface). Set the file via set_par with an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path UNDER the working dir AFTER create -- a relative or external path is blanked by the F2 path confinement. Any content TOP works (moviefileinTOP / constantTOP / a generative composite tap / a still). N distinct clips = N GPU decodes; prefer one shared content TOP placed differently per quad where the design allows.
steps.geometry_out: content image for one surface

verify.pass_if: clip resolution reported, not the default sample

steps.note: THE QUAD: crop + place + keystone for surface 0. EXTRACT page (extracttl/tr/bl/br, unit fraction 0..1) crops the sub-region of the SOURCE to use (kantanMapper Texture Editor analog; identity = full frame TL(0,1) TR(1,1) BL(0,0) BR(1,1)). PIN page (pintopleft/pintopright/pinbotleft/pinbotright, unit fraction of the CANVAS) is where the quad lands + its 4-corner keystone -- this is the surface's position on the projector. mapping=perspective for a true keystone (straight edges stay straight; bilinear bows them). extend=zero + bgcolor alpha 0 so everything outside the pinned quad is transparent for clean compositing. outputresolution=custom at PROJECTOR res (NOT useinput -- else the quad composites at the clip's size). Wire OUT_src0 -> in0 (maxinputs=1). Duplicate this whole source+cornerpin pair for quad1..quadN.
steps.geometry_out: one keystoned quad placed on a transparent projector-res canvas

verify.pass_if: content occupies only the pinned quad region; rest transparent
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_quad0 -- the source lands inside the four pin corners and is transparent everywhere else

steps.note: OPTIONAL PER-QUAD SOFT-EDGE / FEATHER (kantanMapper Softedge analog) -- build in SOURCE space, BEFORE the cornerpin, so the pin warps the already-feathered alpha into place. A white rectangle mask with soft borders: fillcolor white, fillalpha 1, bgalpha 0, softness > 0 (fraction of frame) to fade the alpha at the edges, size slightly inset. outputresolution=custom to match the source. Then multiply it into the source alpha (next step) and feed that into the cornerpin instead of the raw source. Skip the step entirely for hard-edged quads.
steps.geometry_out: white-on-transparent soft-edged alpha mask

verify.pass_if: white center fading to alpha 0 at the borders

steps.note: OPTIONAL (pairs with the feather step): multiply the soft mask into the source so its alpha is feathered. in0 = OUT_src0, in1 = OUT_feather0 (maxinputs=2). The product's alpha fades at the edges; wire THIS into the cornerpin's in0 instead of the raw source. Use compositeTOP operand=multiply if you prefer; multiplyTOP is the 2-input node. Omit when not feathering.
steps.geometry_out: source with feathered (soft-edged) alpha

verify.pass_if: source alpha falls off softly at the borders

steps.note: STACK ALL QUADS OVER BLACK = the single composited output (replaces kantanMapper's whole shape-render). operand=over, tops multi-input (maxinputs=9999): wire OUT_canvas FIRST, then OUT_quad0, OUT_quad1 ... OUT_quadN in draw order (later inputs draw on top -- mirrors the Shapes Tree order). outputresolution=custom at PROJECTOR res. Because each quad is transparent outside its pin region, over-compositing lays each surface exactly where its pins put it. This one node is the N-quad mapper's heart.

key_params.tops: OUT_canvas, OUT_quad0, OUT_quad1, ... (draw order; last on top)

steps.geometry_out: all quads composited into one projector-res image

verify.pass_if: every quad appears at its pinned location over black
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_mapped -- the full multi-surface map reads as one image at projector resolution

steps.note: STABLE ALIGNED TAP. Every downstream output op targets this NAME so the physical output can be swapped without rewiring. Wire OUT_mapped -> this. Hand off to projection_align_and_output / output_handoff (windowCOMP to the projector, or moviefileoutTOP HAP / ndioutTOP / syphonspoutoutTOP) -- all WIRE-ONLY, trigger/record/active OFF. A global cornerpinTOP keystone AFTER this null can correct the whole projector frame at once (distinct from the per-quad pins here).
steps.geometry_out: final multi-quad map, projector res, ready for wire-only output

verify.pass_if: composited multi-quad map at projector res
verify.milestone_check: OUT_aligned holds the deliverable frame the projector will show

steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === On site the projectionist judges where each quad's four corners land on the real surface and DRAGS them (kantanMapper, or the cornerpinTOP viewer). The MCP cannot see the building or drive the mouse. WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds every source+cornerpin+the compositor and sets every extract*/pin* corner numerically (identity or a first estimate). The human's MEASURED corner numbers are typed back via set_par on each cornerpin's pin* components (raw names pintopleftx/pintoplefty/.../pinbotrighty). kantanMapper / kantanUVHelper are Python .tox palette components (live mouse) and are NOT in the catalog -- this typed-operator network is their data-only stand-in.
steps.geometry_out: quads landing on the real surfaces once measured numbers are typed in

verify.pass_if: pin* hold on-site values (or identity/estimate for authoring)

recipes.classify: map video/images onto MULTIPLE flat or quad surfaces (shop windows, stage flats, sign faces, building faces as quads), a different source per surface, each corner-warped -> this recipe (the data-only kantanMapper multi-quad workflow)
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the whole N-quad network -- black canvas, per-quad source + cornerpinTOP (extract crop + pin place/keystone), optional feather (rectangleTOP -> multiplyTOP), the over-compositor, the aligned null -- is created / wired / parameterized by the bridge. No script/execute/cplusplus op, no parameter expressions, no callbacks DAT anywhere; every corner is a literal number set via the create tool or set_par. (2) HUMAN / ON-SITE: kantanMapper's actual value is drawing shapes and DRAGGING corners against the live projection -- that judgement + mouse drag cannot be emitted; the human's measured corner numbers are typed back via set_par on each cornerpin's pin* components. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: nothing here fires; downstream terminal ops (windowCOMP not opened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF; ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active DEFAULT ON -> MUST set OFF) are wired via projection_align_and_output / output_handoff. HONEST GAPS: kantanMapper and kantanUVHelper are Python .tox palette components (live mouse) -- ABSENT from the catalog and deliberately NOT used; this is their plain-operator substitute. True bezier/freeform (non-quad) shapes and per-quad INNER-mesh (finer than 4 corners) warp are NOT covered by cornerpinTOP (4-corner only) -- escalate to mesh_freeform_warp (remapTOP) applied per quad. NC build caps live render at 1280; swap resolutionw/h for 4K, topology identical.
tips: REFERENCE-STILL UNDERLAY: capture a photo of the lit surface (a moviefileinTOP of a still, or a videodeviceinTOP frame saved to the working dir) and wire it as an extra LOW input of the compositor (just above OUT_canvas, dimmed) so the human aligns each quad's pins against the real features -- kantanMapper's Bg Mask analog. Remove/disable it before delivery.
extract* crops the SOURCE sub-region; pin* places + keystones the QUAD on the canvas -- never swap the two pages. Identity extract = full frame; identity pin = the quad fills the whole canvas.
mapping=perspective on both extract and pin for flat surfaces (straight edges stay straight); bilinear visibly bows long edges -- the classic 'why is my window frame curved' bug.
Force outputresolution=custom at projector res on the canvas, EVERY cornerpin, and the compositor. Any node left at useinput/256 composites at the wrong size or the 256px default.
Draw order = compositor input order: wire OUT_canvas first, then quads bottom-to-top of the intended stack; later inputs draw on top (the Shapes Tree ordering).

Feather in SOURCE space before the pin (rectangleTOP softness -> multiplyTOP into source alpha) so the keystone warps the soft edge with the content; a canvas-space rectangle will not follow the warped quad.
Keep each cornerpin's extend=zero and bgcolor alpha 0 -- without transparent outside-the-quad pixels the quads paint black over each other instead of stacking cleanly with over.
variants: Per-quad soft-edge (feather): insert the rectangleTOP -> multiplyTOP pair per surface (steps 4-5) to fade each quad's alpha; omit for hard-edged quads. For a seam between two abutting quads, feather both facing edges so the overlaps sum visually.

Global keystone after the map: add one cornerpinTOP AFTER OUT_aligned (pin* corners, mapping=perspective) to correct the entire projector frame at once -- this is projection_align_and_output stacked on top of the per-quad pins.

Per-quad INNER-mesh / curved surface: cornerpinTOP is 4-corner only; for a bowed or multi-plane face route that one quad's source through mesh_freeform_warp (remapTOP identity-UV + control-grid offset) before its cornerpin, then composite as usual.

SOP-based freeform (closest to kantan internals, heavier): for true bezier/non-quad shapes, texture a gridSOP per shape (materialSOP UVs), warp its points (transformSOP / lattice / CSV-driven), and renderTOP all shapes through one orthographic cameraCOMP into OUT_mapped -- many more nodes than the cornerpin compositor; reserve for genuine freeform.
4K delivery: set every outputresolution=custom resolution to [3840,2160]; topology identical (NC render cap 1280 previews downscaled).

recipes.title: Projector-calibration target camera + numeric intake (build the data-only cameraCOMP/geo/render/output SCAFFOLD that on-site camSchnappr, an OpenCV solve, or a survey calibrates INTO -- then type the solved intrinsics/extrinsics straight back; NOT a virtual projector set from focal/aperture like projector_calibrated_3d)
recipes.summary: Stand up the exact rig a real projector gets calibrated INTO, plus the numeric ports the calibration result plugs into -- all data-only. camSchnappr is a Python + OpenCV .tox (interactive point-pick windows + cv2.calibrateCamera); it CANNOT be instantiated by this surface, so this recipe builds what it needs and where its output lands: (1) a renderable geometryCOMP holding the DIMENSIONALLY-ACCURATE virtual twin of the physical structure (the correspondence reference -- model accuracy is the ceiling on alignment; file under the working dir); (2) a target cameraCOMP named `project` -- the camera camSchnappr writes into, armed on the focal/aperture pose path as a valid fallback; (3) two tableDATs pre-wired as the calibration intake -- an INTRINSICS 4x4 projection matrix -> cameraCOMP.projmatrixop (with projection=custommatrix) and an EXTRINSICS 4x4 pose matrix -> cameraCOMP.xformmatrixop (or set tx/ty/tz + rx/ry/rz directly). On-site a human runs camSchnappr / an OpenCV solve / a total-station survey ONCE; it emits two Table DATs (extrinsics pose + intrinsics projection matrix) -- those numbers are typed back into the intake via set_par / write_csv, or projmatrixop is pointed straight at the solver's own output DAT. GOTCHA: a projmatrixop 4x4 must be in Vulkan depth-clip range [0,1], not OpenGL [-1,1] -- an OpenGL-convention matrix (older camSchnappr/other-DCC exports) clips wrong; sign flips and +/-0.5 principal-point offsets are common when importing a foreign matrix. Render the twin through the calibrated `project` camera and hand off WIRE-ONLY. This is the SCAFFOLD+INTAKE for MEASURED calibration output; projector_calibrated_3d instead casts content from a virtual projector set by focal/aperture or a synthetic matrix -- use this when a real solve/survey produced numbers to load.

steps.tool: (tap OUT_projsurface/OUT_geo/OUT_model from projector_calibrated_3d, import_segmented_model, import_scan, facade_3d_render; else geometryCOMP + fileinSOP)
steps.note: The virtual twin -- a renderable geometryCOMP holding the 3D model that MATCHES the physical structure. This is the correspondence reference camSchnappr/OpenCV/survey solves against; its dimensional accuracy is the hard ceiling on final alignment (a wrong model cannot be calibrated away).
