Model file MUST live under the working dir. UVs are NOT required -- the calibrated camera projects from its own eye. This recipe does not build the mesh.

verify.pass_if: a renderable geometryCOMP with geometry inside exists

steps.note: THE calibration target -- name it `project` (this is exactly the Camera COMP camSchnappr expects dropped on its Project parameter, and what a survey/OpenCV solve writes into). Arm it on the parametric pose path as a valid fallback: viewanglemethod=focalaperture with focal/aperture pre-set to the real projector lens, near/far bounding the scene depth. Leave projection=perspective FOR NOW so it renders a sane image before calibration (an empty custommatrix would blank). The set_par intake step below flips it to custommatrix once measured numbers arrive. HUMAN/on-site: the intrinsics+extrinsics that make this camera match the real projector come from a solve/survey -- this surface builds the bare target, it does NOT run camSchnappr (Python+OpenCV .tox, not instantiable).

verify.pass_if: a cameraCOMP named project exists on the focalaperture path

steps.note: INTRINSICS intake -- a 4 row x 4 col table that will hold the measured PROJECTION MATRIX (camSchnappr/OpenCV emit this as their intrinsics Table DAT; a survey/other DCC can supply one too). Empty/identity until calibrated. On-site, type the solver's 4x4 in via set_par or write_csv, OR skip this table and point the camera's projmatrixop directly at the solver's own output DAT. GOTCHA: the matrix MUST be in Vulkan depth-clip range [0,1], not OpenGL [-1,1] -- an OpenGL-convention matrix clips/depth-inverts; foreign matrices often need a sign flip and a +/-0.5 principal-point offset (FOV also normalizes by render width, e.g. fov/(resw/aperture)).

verify.pass_if: a 4x4 tableDAT exists ready to receive the projection matrix

steps.note: EXTRINSICS intake -- a 4 row x 4 col table holding the measured POSE (projector translate+rotate as a 4x4; camSchnappr/OpenCV emit this as their extrinsics Table DAT). Wired into the camera's xformmatrixop below. ALTERNATIVE (simpler, no table): read the pose numbers and set the camera's tx/ty/tz + rx/ry/rz directly via set_par -- order-sensitive, match the cameraCOMP xord/rord. Empty until the on-site solve/survey fills it.

verify.pass_if: a 4x4 tableDAT exists ready to receive the pose matrix

steps.note: WIRE the intake into the target camera -- do this AFTER the measured numbers are in the tables (before that, leave the camera on the focalaperture fallback so it still renders). Set OUT_project projection=custommatrix, projmatrixop=<OUT_projintrinsics path>, xformmatrixop=<OUT_projextrinsics path>. projmatrixop/xformmatrixop are matrix-reference params (accept a CHOP/DAT/tdu.Matrix) -- a Table DAT of the 4x4 resolves directly; these are legit projection-MATRIX data DATs, not shader code. If using the parametric fallback instead, set tx/ty/tz + rx/ry/rz + focal/aperture here and leave projection=perspective.

verify.pass_if: projection=custommatrix and projmatrixop/xformmatrixop resolve to the two intake DATs

steps.note: The content the calibrated projector casts. Tap a finished composite, a moviefileinTOP of media (file under the working dir; set the path via set_par with an ABSOLUTE forward-slash value AFTER create), or a noiseTOP for a test pattern. Sampled by the renderTOP through the calibrated camera.
steps.geometry_out: image

verify.pass_if: content TOP cooks with a non-zero resolution

steps.note: Render the twin THROUGH the calibrated `project` camera -- geometry=<OUT_calibgeo>, camera=<OUT_project>. This is the payoff: with the measured 4x4 loaded, the rendered image lands on the virtual model exactly as the real projector will on the physical structure. Set outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h to the PROJECTOR resolution -- do NOT leave the 256px default. Non-Commercial builds cap at 1280 (use 1280x720; identical graph runs 3840x2160/4096x2160 on commercial).
steps.geometry_out: image
steps.milestone_check: renderTOP through OUT_project cooks at the projector resolution and the model fills the frame as the calibrated projector's eye sees it (pre-calibration it shows the focalaperture fallback view; post-intake it matches the measured projector pose+lens)

verify.pass_if: renderTOP cooks at the set resolution through OUT_project

steps.note: Stable OUT tap for the output/handoff lane (projection_align_and_output / output_handoff) and the projector window. WIRE-ONLY: any downstream windowCOMP / videodeviceoutTOP / moviefileoutTOP / NDI is wired with record/active/output OFF -- the operator fires it on-site.
steps.geometry_out: image

verify.pass_if: OUT tap cooks and is ready for the output lane

steps.tool: (on-site HUMAN step: run camSchnappr / OpenCV solve / survey, then set_par / write_csv the two Table DATs back)
steps.note: THE calibration itself -- irreducibly human + code, done ONCE on-site. Physically rig/aim/focus the projector and ZERO all its digital transforms (keystone, digital zoom/shift -- any in-projector warp poisons the intrinsics). Then EITHER drag camSchnappr from Palette>Mapping and point its Project par at OUT_project + Geo SOP at the twin, pick >=6 non-coplanar correspondence points in its live windows, and let cv2.calibrateCamera solve (watch Calibration Error); OR run any OpenCV calibrateCamera / total-station survey. The solve emits an extrinsics Table DAT (pose) + an intrinsics Table DAT (projection matrix). Type those numbers into OUT_projextrinsics/OUT_projintrinsics via set_par/write_csv (or repoint projmatrixop/xformmatrixop at the solver's own output DATs). NONE of camSchnappr's point-pick UI or OpenCV solve is buildable by this surface -- only the target + intake it fills.

steps.tool: (alternative intake: viosoTOP / scalabledisplayTOP fed a vendor calibration file)
steps.note: If calibration comes from vendor auto-align software instead of an OpenCV solve, skip the camera-matrix intake and warp the rendered content with a viosoTOP (configfile=<VIOSO .vwf>) or scalabledisplayTOP (configfile=<Scalable .ol>) placed after OUT_calibrender; reloadpulse to load, projectorindex to pick the projector. The vendor file is produced by that external software = the human/external step; the TOP + file path is data-only. This is a distinct calibration source (image-space warp file) from the camera-matrix path above.

key_params.configfile: <absolute forward-slash path to vendor calibration file>

recipes.classify: I have a real projector aimed at a physical structure + a matching 3D model, and I ran (or will run) camSchnappr / an OpenCV solve / a survey to calibrate it -> build the data-only target camera + intrinsics/extrinsics intake to load the result -> camera_calibration_intake
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY: builds only typed operators + matrix/pose DATs; no script/execute/cplusplus, no expressions, no callbacks. camSchnappr is a Python+OpenCV .tox (interactive point-pick windows + cv2.calibrateCamera) and is NOT instantiable by this surface -- this recipe builds the bare cameraCOMP target it writes into plus the numeric intake, never camSchnappr itself. projmatrixop/xformmatrixop reference legit 4x4 projection/pose MATRIX data DATs (core projection-mapping data), not shader code. HUMAN/on-site split: the projector rig/aim/keystone-zero, the >=6-point correspondence pick, and the OpenCV/survey solve are the human step; its two output Table DATs (extrinsics pose + intrinsics projection matrix) are the ONLY thing crossing back, typed in via set_par/write_csv or referenced directly. WIRE-ONLY output by design: downstream windowCOMP/videodeviceoutTOP/moviefileoutTOP/NDI left with record/active/output OFF; the operator fires it. HONEST GAPS: distinct from projector_calibrated_3d (that sets a virtual projector from focal/aperture or a SYNTHETIC matrix; this loads a MEASURED solve). Vulkan projmatrix depth-clip [0,1] (not OpenGL [-1,1]) or the depth inverts. Pre-calibration the camera shows only the focalaperture fallback, not a real match. No live tool verifies the solve numerically -- correctness is judged on the physical structure by the human.
tips: projmatrixop matrix MUST be Vulkan depth-clip [0,1], not OpenGL [-1,1] -- an OpenGL-convention 4x4 (older camSchnappr exports / other DCCs) clips wrong or inverts depth; sign-flip and offset the principal point by +/-0.5 when importing a foreign matrix.
Zero the projector's keystone / digital zoom / lens-shift BEFORE calibrating -- any in-projector warp is baked into the intrinsics and cannot be undone in TD.
Model accuracy caps alignment: the virtual twin must match the physical structure dimensionally; a survey/LiDAR/CAD twin beats an eyeballed box.

Two intake paths, pick one: the exact 4x4 (projmatrixop+xformmatrixop, projection=custommatrix) OR the parametric fallback (focal/aperture + tx/ty/tz+rx/ry/rz, projection=perspective). Pose-only will not match a real lens -- load the intrinsics too.
Extrinsics via tx/ty/tz+rx/ry/rz are xord/rord-order-sensitive -- match the cameraCOMP transform order when typing surveyed numbers, or use the xformmatrixop 4x4 to sidestep order entirely.

camSchnappr's Geo SOP must not sit on a branch with a Material SOP (it breaks its blend) -- keep the twin's texture on the Color Map path, mirrored here by feeding content via the renderTOP, not a MAT on the geo.
variants: Quad reprojection (LED walls / XR stage, pixel-perfect): set OUT_project quadreprojsop=<a SOP holding the screen quad> and quadreprojpts1..4 to the quad's bottom-left, bottom-right, top-left, top-right point indices (as seen from the camera) -- blows that quad up to fill the render; the data-only counterpart to sweetSpot for flat pixel arrays.

sweetSpot / trompe-l'oeil: render the scene from the OBSERVER'S position (place OUT_project at the surveyed sweet-spot / tracked-viewer location) and project onto the surface so it reads perspective-correct from that spot -- same rig, camera placed at the eye rather than the projector.

Vendor calibration file: skip the camera-matrix intake and warp OUT_calibrender with a viosoTOP (configfile=<VIOSO .vwf>) or scalabledisplayTOP (configfile=<Scalable .ol>), reloadpulse to load -- for installs calibrated by VIOSO/Scalable auto-align software instead of an OpenCV solve.

Parametric-only (no measured matrix): drive OUT_project purely by focal/aperture + tx/ty/tz+rx/ry/rz from a survey, projection=perspective -- this collapses toward projector_calibrated_3d's lens/pose path; use it when there is no solved 4x4.

Multi-projector: one target cameraCOMP + intake per projector, each fed its own solved 4x4, rendered together; edge-blend the overlaps downstream (the on-site camSchnappr Auto-Blend mask is a live-COMP feature, not built here).

recipes.title: Screen-space spill/garbage mask + soft frame-edge feather -- clip ALL content to the surface, kill light on ground/sky/neighbors
recipes.summary: The projectionist's holdout matte, in PROJECTOR/SCREEN space (applied AFTER the cornerpinTOP keystone, not in UV space): a silhouette mask (surface=white/1, everything-else=black/0) clips the finished keystoned composite so ZERO light spills onto the ground, sky, neighboring windows, or people beside the building; then a soft frame-edge feather (radial rampTOP or a high-softness rectangleTOP) fades the projector's rectangular beam edge to black so it disappears. moviefileinTOP(traced silhouette PNG)->lumalevelTOP(harden 0/1)->matteTOP(content over black plate using mask, TD's purpose-built holdout op)->rampTOP feather->multiplyTOP->nullTOP builds, wires, and cooks to the clipped+feathered projector plate at OUT_spillmasked. DATA-ONLY-BUILDABLE = the load/harden + matte/multiply + feather + apply chain; the irregular hand-traced silhouette PNG for a real building outline is an upstream HUMAN asset (only its load+apply is buildable). ANALYTIC silhouettes (rectangleTOP/circleTOP/rampTOP unions) are FULLY data-only (variant build_from_shapes). Distinct from facade_mask_atlas (UV-space window mask multiplied into emitmap); this is the screen-space complement, applied on the final composite. WIRE-ONLY: hands OUT_spillmasked to the projector/file/media-server output stage; nothing is fired.

steps.note: MASK SOURCE (Route A, pre-authored asset). Load the surface silhouette: the mapped surface WHITE(1), everything the beam must NOT touch BLACK(0), in PROJECTOR/OUTPUT space (matches the keystoned frame, NOT UV space). Reads stills/PNG + image sequences. outputresolution=custom + resolution to MATCH the projector output (256px default trap). ASSET FLAG: for an irregular real building outline this traced PNG is an UPSTREAM HUMAN asset (hand-painted in Photoshop, or projected-and-traced on-site); only loading is data-only. For a REGULAR/analytic silhouette (rectangular or round surface, tidy window grid) SKIP this and build from shapes -- see variant build_from_shapes (fully data-only, no human asset).

key_params.file: surface_silhouette.png (surface white, off-surface black; projector/screen space)

steps.geometry_out: TOP (grayscale silhouette, screen space)

verify.pass_if: surface region ~white, off-surface ~black, at projector res

steps.note: HARDEN to a clean 0/1 cutout. threshold + inlow/inhigh (or clamplow/clamphigh) crush grays to crisp black/white; invert=1 if the PNG has the surface black. HARD vs SOFT is a deliberate choice: set inputfiltertype=nearest here for a crisp architectural clip; for a SOFT holdout edge skip the crush and feather instead (softness on a shape mask, or the radial rampTOP in the feather step). 256px trap: outputresolution=custom + resolution == silhouette.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (clean 0..1 holdout matte)

verify.pass_if: surface==1, off-surface==0, crisp edge

steps.note: PIPELINE-POSITION ANCHOR. The garbage mask lives in PROJECTOR/SCREEN space, so it must be applied AFTER the keystone. REUSE the keystone recipe's OUT_aligned (projector_output_handoff) as the content input if already built -- DON'T duplicate; this step is here to make the 'after keystone' position explicit. If not built, keystone the finished composite here: extractmapping=perspective, pinp1..pinp4 = the four corner positions. Identity pins = pass-through. HUMAN boundary: the on-site 4-corner/6-point calibration is a HUMAN step whose measured corner numbers are typed back via set_par. 256px trap: outputresolution=custom + resolution.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (keystoned content, screen space)

verify.pass_if: content at projector res, in screen space

steps.note: BLACK PLATE for the matte's input2 (what shows through where the mask is black = the killed spill regions). color=[0,0,0], alpha=1. 256px TRAP: constantTOP DEFAULTS to 256x256 and will mis-scale the matte -- set outputresolution=custom + resolution == the keystoned content.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (solid black plate)

verify.pass_if: pure black at projector res

steps.note: CORE HOLDOUT (recommended) -- TD's PURPOSE-BUILT matte op. matteTOP is 3-INPUT: it composites input1 OVER input2 USING input3 as the matte. Wire OUT_aligned->input1 (content), OUT_blackplate->input2 (shows in killed regions), OUT_holdout->input3 (the mask). mattechannel=luminance (white in input3 draws content, black shows the black plate = spill BLACKED OUT). switchinputs if the matte reads inverted. 256px trap: outputresolution=custom + resolution. ALT (same result): multiplyTOP -- OUT_aligned x OUT_holdout (content x mask, unambiguous). ALT: compositeTOP operand=inside (input1.rgba*clamp(input2.a)) clips content to the mask; operand=outside (input1.rgba*(1-input2.a)) is the INVERSE holdout (kill inside the shape). Use insideluminance/outsideluminance to key off the mask's luminance instead of alpha.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (content clipped to surface -- black off-surface)

verify.pass_if: content only on the surface; pure black everywhere off-surface

steps.note: SOFT FRAME-EDGE FEATHER. Fade the projector's rectangular beam edge to black so the hard frame disappears. type=radial (or circular), position=[0.5,0.5], with a black OUTER key and white INNER key so edges->0; dither=on to kill banding. ALT (rectangular inset feather): a rectangleTOP with fillcolor=[1,1,1], fillalpha=1, high softness (blends its black background inward) gives a clean feathered rectangle matte -- use when the surface fills most of the frame. 256px trap: outputresolution=custom + resolution == content. NOTE: master soft-edge only reads correctly head-on; under strong perspective feather AFTER the keystone, in the space where it must appear.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (soft-edge feather field, 0..1)

verify.pass_if: white center falling smoothly to black at the frame edge

steps.note: APPLY the feather into the garbage-masked composite. OUT_clipped->input0, OUT_feather->input1 -> beam edges fall to black while the surface stays lit. This is the same feather mechanism projector_blend uses for multi-projector seams (masks sum to 1) -- for a single beam it just kills the outer frame. 256px trap: outputresolution=custom + resolution. MILESTONE: content clipped to the surface silhouette AND the rectangular beam edge feathered away.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (clipped + frame-feathered projector plate)

verify.pass_if: light only on the surface, beam edge soft to black
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_spillfeathered -- content confined to the surface silhouette, no hard rectangular beam edge, pure black elsewhere

steps.note: STABLE TAP. Plant OUT_spillmasked and WIRE it to the output stage (projector_output_handoff: windowCOMP perform window / moviefileoutTOP / ndioutTOP / syphonspoutoutTOP). WIRE-ONLY: window not opened, record OFF -- nothing is fired by the bridge.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (final masked projector plate)

verify.pass_if: matches OUT_spillfeathered; ready to hand to the projector

recipes.classify: screen-space (post-keystone) spill/garbage masking for projection mapping -- clip ALL content to the mapped surface silhouette so no light spills on the ground/sky/neighbors/people (holdout matte via matteTOP/multiplyTOP/compositeTOP inside-outside) + a soft frame-edge feather (radial rampTOP / high-softness rectangleTOP) to hide the projector's rectangular beam edge; talent-holdout (chromakeyTOP) and animated reveal-wipe sub-lanes; the irregular traced silhouette PNG is an upstream HUMAN asset, analytic shape-unions are fully data-only
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY: no script/expression/callback ops -- shape synthesis, PNG load, harden, matte/multiply/composite holdout, feather, chroma/luma key, and CHOP-driven animated wipe are all typed tools. COORDINATE SPACE is the #1 trap: this mask lives in PROJECTOR/SCREEN space and is applied AFTER the cornerpinTOP keystone -- it is NOT the UV-space window atlas (facade_mask_atlas), which multiplies into emitmap sampled through section UVs. A building can need BOTH at once (windows dark via the UV atlas, ground/sky/neighbors dark via this screen mask). matteTOP is 3-INPUT (input1 over input2 using input3) -- easy to mis-wire vs the 2-input multiply; match mattechannel to the mask's channel. 256px TRAP on EVERY mask node (moviefileinTOP/lumalevelTOP/constantTOP/matteTOP/rampTOP/rectangleTOP/multiplyTOP default to 256x256) -- set outputresolution=custom + resolution to the projector output. Apply the mask on the FINAL composite (post-render/post-keystone) or animated content crawls under a static edge. HUMAN boundary: the irregular hand-traced silhouette PNG is an upstream asset (Photoshop paint / on-site trace); the on-site registration offset is a HUMAN step whose numbers are typed back via set_par. HONEST GAP: analytic silhouettes (rectangleTOP/circleTOP/rampTOP unions) are fully data-only; only the irregular traced PNG needs a human. WIRE-ONLY output.
tips: COORDINATE-SPACE CHECK: if content mis-registers to the physical edge, you are masking in the wrong space -- the garbage mask is screen space AFTER keystone; the window atlas is UV space into emitmap.

HARD vs SOFT edge: inputfiltertype=nearest + a hard lumalevel threshold = crisp architectural clip (may alias on a dark facade); linear + softness/radial-ramp = soft edge that hides the beam frame. Choose per surface.

matteTOP wiring: input1=content, input2=black constantTOP, input3=mask; mattechannel=luminance for a grayscale mask, alpha for an alpha matte. Wrong order or wrong channel = inverted holdout -- flip with switchinputs.
Feather AFTER the keystone, in the space where it must read -- a pre-keystone feather stretches unevenly under perspective. Master soft-edge only works head-on.
Verify across time: save_top @OUT_spillmasked at 2-3 frames with content animating -- the mask edge must not crawl and no spill must appear as content moves.
Multi-projector seam blend is the SAME feather mechanism -- reference projector_blend (per-projector ramp masks summing to 1) rather than rebuilding it here.

variants.when: regular/analytic surface silhouette (rectangular or round surface, tidy window grid) -- NO human-traced PNG
variants.how: Skip moviefileinTOP. Synthesize the silhouette from rectangleTOP/circleTOP (fillcolor=[1,1,1], fillalpha=1, softness for a feathered edge, cornerradius/borderwidth) and UNION multiple shapes with compositeTOP (operand=add or over, top='shape*'). Feed the union into lumalevelTOP (step 2) and continue. FULLY DATA-ONLY -- no upstream asset, no human boundary except final on-site registration.

variants.when: a live performer/talent stands in front of the surface and must be held OUT of projected content (no light washing across their face)
variants.how: chromakeyTOP on a live videodeviceinTOP/ndiinTOP feed keys the performer to alpha: set huemin/huemax (+ hsoftlow/hsofthigh, satmin/satmax, valmin/valmax soft ranges) around the key color, invert to select the person, rgbout=multalpha. Then compositeTOP operand=outside (content x (1-talent.a)) OR matteTOP punches the talent silhouette out of the content before the garbage mask. 256px trap on the key + composite.

variants.when: a moving reveal/wipe transition instead of a static holdout (content wipes onto the surface)
variants.how: DATA-ONLY, no expressions: drive a rampTOP position (or a transformTOP tx/ty sliding a hard-edged rectangleTOP mask) from an lfoCHOP or timerCHOP via bind_chop / CHOP-export -> the mask edge sweeps across the surface. Multiply the animated mask into the content (step 7 mechanism). Keep the garbage mask (step 5) in the chain so the wipe still can't spill off the surface.

recipes.title: Feed a media server / another TD LIVE (Spout / NDI / Touch Out / RenderStream) — WIRE-ONLY, active OFF
recipes.summary: Hand the finished content to a downstream media server or render engine as a LIVE per-frame stream, distinct from the file-bake output_handoff. Four lanes off one stable tap: syphonspoutoutTOP (same-PC zero-latency GPU share -> Resolume/MadMapper/Notch/OBS), ndioutTOP (networked, compressed -> disguise/Pixera/another machine; groups + alpha), touchoutTOP (TD<->TD over TCP/IP, HAP Q), and the RenderStream network (renderstreaminCHOP + a schema tableDAT so disguise drives the frustum/params). EVERY live-out op DEFAULTS active=ON and would start broadcasting the instant it is created — the bridge builds them all with active OFF and unique sender names; the OPERATOR flips active on when the show is live. RenderStream is now mostly wireable: the two image TOPs (renderstreaminTOP/renderstreamoutTOP) are present, so the frame loop builds data-only; only its Camera COMP frustum still needs matrix EXPRESSIONS (not default-data-only). A nullTOP OUT_feed_tap feeding syphonspoutoutTOP(active OFF)/ndioutTOP(active OFF)/touchoutTOP(active OFF) plus a renderstreaminCHOP(active OFF)+schema tableDAT; verified every send op is built inactive and renamed off its default.

steps.note: Start from the finished content tap (output_handoff OUT_final, projection_align_and_output OUT_aligned, or facade_3d_render OUT_render). Meta-step: it already exists; wire it into the feed tap below with `connect`. This recipe is the LIVE sibling of output_handoff (which bakes a file) — same source, different terminal ops.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (2D image)

verify.pass_if: the content tap exists and cooks

steps.note: Stable feed tap. Every live-send op targets this NAME so you can add/remove Spout/NDI/Touch/RenderStream lanes without rewiring the content. Wire OUT_final -> this.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (2D image)

verify.pass_if: wired to the content tap; cooks

steps.note: SAME-PC lane (Spout on Windows / Syphon on macOS): zero-latency shared-memory GPU texture to Resolume/MadMapper/Notch/OBS on THIS machine — never across a network (use NDI/Touch Out for that). active DEFAULTS TRUE (ON) -> MUST set OFF (WIRE-ONLY; creating it live-shares immediately). sendername DEFAULTS to 'TDSyphonSpoutOut' -> RENAME to a unique show string (the receiver picks the sender by this exact name; two shows sharing the default collide). GOTCHAS: Windows Spout is capped at 10 senders (registry-tunable), Nvidia/AMD only (Intel unsupported); Spout carries up to 32-bit float RGBA, Syphon only 8-bit RGBA. Wire OUT_feed_tap -> in0.

key_params.active: off — WIRE-ONLY; the operator turns it on (DEFAULT ON)
key_params.format: rgba16float / rgba32float for HDR content (Spout only; Syphon=8-bit)

steps.geometry_out: TOP (terminal send op)

verify.pass_if: wired; active == OFF; sendername != default

steps.note: NDI GROUPS table (data-only): a table with a single column header 'groups', one group name per row. Feeds ndioutTOP.grouptable so only receivers in those groups discover this source (show partitioning on a shared LAN). Optional — skip for an ungrouped public source. Pure data, no code.

key_params.table content: col header 'groups'; one NDI group name per row

recipes.title: Black-level uplift mask: raise black OUTSIDE the overlap to match the doubled-black seam band on dark content (data-only follow-on to multiprojector_edge_blend)
recipes.summary: Projectors can't project true black -- they emit deep grey. Where two edge-blended projectors OVERLAP, both greys sum, so on dark content the overlap band is a visibly LIGHTER grey rectangle while the single-coverage regions stay darker. This recipe raises the black floor EVERYWHERE EXCEPT the overlap so the whole wall matches the doubled-black band. Per projector, AFTER the blend multiply (OUT_blend_mult{i} from multiprojector_edge_blend): constantTOP holding the measured per-channel black-floor value -> multiply by a feathered COVERAGE/COMPLEMENT mask (rampTOP: 1.0 in this projector's sole-coverage interior, feathering to 0 across the shared band) -> addTOP that lift field onto the blended content -> null -> the SAME windowCOMP (re-point winop). 100% data-only (constant+ramp+blur+multiply+add); the floor VALUE (per channel) and the feather width are HUMAN-measured on the wall. Caveat: uplift trades contrast for uniformity -- best on 2-projector panoramas, degrades with grid overlaps. WIRE-ONLY handoff.

steps.note: The blended per-projector content from multiprojector_edge_blend (post crop+cornerpin+ramp+gamma+multiply). Insert this black-level chain BETWEEN OUT_blend_mult{i} and the null->window; the window's winop just re-points to the new final tap. Repeat per projector i.

This is the only per-channel knob most rigs need.

This is its OWN DAT (not the blend keys) so the feather can be softer/wider than the blend curve and carries NO gamma pre-distort. Band fraction is PROJECTOR-frame (f=overlap o / slice width). LEFT (band at RIGHT edge): pos,r,g,b,a = 0,1,1,1,1 / 1-f,1,1,1,1 / 1,0,0,0,1. RIGHT (band at LEFT edge): 0,0,0,0,1 / f,1,1,1,1 / 1,1,1,1,1. recipes.classify: black-level uplift / black-level masking -- on DARK content the edge-blend overlap band shows a lighter-grey rectangle because two projectors' non-true-black sums; raise the black floor OUTSIDE the overlap to match. Data-only content-side stand-in for VIOSO/Watchout Black Level Uplift. Per projector, after the blend multiply: constantTOP measured floor x feathered coverage/complement mask (rampTOP) -> addTOP onto content -> null -> re-point the edge-blend window. Floor value (per channel) + feather are HUMAN-measured on the wall.
recipes.governance: FOLLOW-ON to multiprojector_edge_blend (inserts between OUT_blend_mult{i} and the null->window; re-points the SAME windowCOMP winop -- no new output lane). 100% DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: constantTOP floor + coverage rampTOP (write_csv->tableDAT->rampTOP) + blurTOP feather + multiplyTOP + addTOP, wired with numeric defaults. HUMAN on-site: the per-channel black-floor VALUE and the feather width, measured on a black frame on the wall and typed back via set_par. PER-CHANNEL is native here -- constantTOP colorr/g/b set the floor independently (projector black is tinted). CONTRAST CAVEAT: uplift raises the whole floor, so it TRADES dynamic range for uniformity -- best on 2-projector panoramas, worsens with each additional overlap (grids); make it defeatable (floor=0 == off) and never lift beyond the measured band delta or the image greys out. Physical alternative (optical douser / shaped blend mask in front of the lens) preserves contrast but is out of MCP scope (hardware). WIRE-ONLY: window built not opened. TRAPS: 256px default on constant/ramp/multiply/add; multiplyTOP AND addTOP both default size=input2 -> set outputresolution=custom + projector res so content isn't resized to the mask; constantTOP premultrgbbyalpha defaults ON (turn off for a raw floor).
tips: The uplift mask is the projector's COVERAGE map (1 in sole-coverage, 0 in the shared band) -- shaped like the blend plateau but its OWN DAT with a softer feather and NO gamma. Reusing the blend gamma mask would double-distort the floor.
constantTOP colorr/g/b is the per-channel knob: set R/G/B floors independently to neutralize a tinted projector black -- no per-channel level op needed on the floor itself.
premultrgbbyalpha on constantTOP defaults ON; leave it OFF here or the RGB floor gets scaled by alpha before the add.
BOTH multiplyTOP and addTOP default size=input2 -> outputresolution=custom + projector res on each, or the projector content silently resizes to the mask.

Lift edge visible on the wall -> widen OUT_bl_mask{i} blur or the OUT_bl_keys{i} feather; band still lighter than interior -> raise OUT_bl_floor{i}; interior now lighter than band -> lower it (overshoot).
Only apply on content that shows the band (dark scenes). On bright content the doubled black is invisible; a static full-time lift just costs contrast -- gate it or set floor 0.
Verify without 2 projectors: push a BLACK master through and read analyzeTOP max-min on OUT_proj{i}_bl_final -- flat == matched.
variants: Reuse the blend mask: instead of a second DAT, take OUT_blend_ramp{i} through a levelTOP (invert to get the complement, soften) -- fewer nodes but the feather is locked to the blend curve.
N>2 / grid: each projector's coverage mask is 1 only where it is the SOLE cover; interior tiles are 0 on all four bands. Contrast loss compounds -- prefer physical dousers for big grids.
Stacked seam (horizontal): rampTOP type=vertical, band on croptop/cropbottom axis.
Measured curve floor: swap the flat constantTOP for a lookupTOP/rampTOP gradient if the wall black is non-uniform across the panel (vignette).

HELPER build_blacklevel_uplift(blended_tap, projectors=N, overlap=f, axis, projector_res, floor_rgb[], feather): builds the whole per-projector floor+coverage-ramp+blur+multiply+add scaffold (~6*N ops), re-points the edge-blend windows, and prints the 2 human knobs (floor per channel, feather).

recipes.title: Stacked projectors: 2+ units on the SAME area for double brightness / redundancy -- identical content, per-projector convergence keystone, NO crop and NO blend (data-only)
recipes.summary: STACKING is fundamentally different from edge-blend: both projectors show the SAME full frame on the SAME surface to add brightness (and give redundancy -- lose one, the image dims instead of going black), NOT to enlarge the canvas. So there is NO crop and NO summed blend mask (the entire difference from multiprojector_edge_blend). Per unit: the shared master -> cornerpinTOP with its OWN convergence corners (near-identity, sub-pixel nudges to register onto the other unit's pixels) -> optional levelTOP luminance/color trim so the units match -> null -> windowCOMP to that projector's display. A scratch differenceTOP of the two units' outputs (or their test grids) is the data-only convergence check: converged == near-black diff, mis-converged == doubled ghost edges. Brightness reality: doubling projectors is only ~15% perceived brightness AND doubles black so contrast halves -- pros stack for redundancy/lumens-vs-ambient, or hybrid: stack pairs for brightness then edge-blend the halves. Convergence + trim are HUMAN, typed via set_par. WIRE-ONLY.

steps.note: The finished FULL-FRAME composite. Every stacked unit shows this SAME frame in full -- no cropTOP, no slicing. Repeat steps 2-5 per stacked unit i (example: 2 units, proj0 + proj1 on one surface).

verify.pass_if: master composite tap exists and cooks

steps.note: Per-unit CONVERGENCE keystone -- each stacked unit gets its OWN corners to register its pixels ONTO the other unit's on the wall. mapping=perspective; pins start at identity TL(0,1)TR(1,1)BL(0,0)BR(1,0). Unlike edge-blend keystone (large per-projector geometry), stacking corners are near-identity SUB-PIXEL nudges. Projector res, outputresolution=custom (256px trap). HUMAN converges on-site; drift from humidity/wind/floor-settling is worse than blend, so this is re-checked often.

Leave identity for a pure redundancy stack. HUMAN tunes on-site. Wire OUT_stack_key{i}->in0.

Chain analyzeTOP op=maximum: max->0 == converged. GOTCHA: differenceTOP size defaults to input2 -> set outputresolution=custom + projector res. Scratch node; delete after converging. recipes.classify: projector STACKING -- 2+ projectors on the SAME surface for double brightness and/or redundancy (not canvas size). Identical full-frame content -> per-unit cornerpinTOP CONVERGENCE keystone -> optional levelTOP luminance/color trim -> null -> windowCOMP per display. NO crop, NO summed blend masks (the whole difference from multiprojector_edge_blend). differenceTOP of the two units' grids = the convergence proof. Convergence corners + trim are HUMAN. Contrast halves (doubled black), perceived brightness gain ~15% not 2x, but redundancy: lose one unit -> dimmer not dark.
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: identical content fan-out + per-unit cornerpinTOP + optional levelTOP trim + null + windowCOMP + a scratch differenceTOP/analyzeTOP convergence check, all with numeric defaults. HUMAN on-site: convergence corners (sub-pixel registration, drifts with environment -- re-checked often) and per-unit luminance/color trim, measured on the wall and typed via set_par. THE DEFINING CONTRAST vs multiprojector_edge_blend: NO cropTOP (no slicing -- every unit shows the full frame) and NO ramp/gamma/multiply blend chain and NO summed-to-1 masks (stacking co-locates identical pixels; it does not tile). BRIGHTNESS/CONTRAST REALITY (author honestly): stacking ~doubles lumens but perceived brightness rises only ~15%, and it doubles the black floor so contrast HALVES -- often the wrong trade for mapping against ambient light; its real wins are redundancy (a unit can die mid-show, audience loses half brightness not the image) and raw lumens on bright surfaces. HYBRID: on big shows stack PAIRS for brightness on each half, then edge-blend the halves at the center (feed each pair's content through multiprojector_edge_blend crops). WIRE-ONLY: windows built not opened. TRAPS: 256px default on cornerpin/level/difference; differenceTOP (and compositeTOP) default size=input2 -> set outputresolution=custom + projector res.
tips: The whole point: SAME content, DIFFERENT per-unit convergence. If you find yourself adding a cropTOP or a blend ramp, you're building edge-blend, not a stack.

Convergence needs pixel-perfect registration and drifts with humidity/wind/floor settling -- keep OUT_stack_converge_check in the network for quick re-checks, don't delete it on a long-running install.
Redundancy framing for the client: a stacked pair means one projector failing = half brightness, never black -- worth the contrast hit on shows that cannot go dark.
levelTOP has NO per-channel gamma; match a color-cast between lamps with the per-channel INPUT levels lowr/highr/lowg/highg/lowb/highb (or brightness1/gamma1 for overall).

Convergence test source: push a fine checker/grid (constantTOP checker or a rendered gridSOP) through BOTH cornerpins into the differenceTOP -- edges reveal sub-pixel offset far better than photographic content.
differenceTOP defaults size=input2 -> custom + projector res, or one unit silently resizes to the other before diffing and the check lies.
Pure redundancy stack (no brightness match needed) -> skip the levelTOP trim; convergence still matters.
variants: N-stack (3+ units) for extreme lumens: same pattern, compositeTOP operand=difference across all N for the convergence check.

Hybrid stack+blend: stack pairs for brightness, then run each pair's content through multiprojector_edge_blend (crop+cornerpin+ramp+gamma+multiply) so the stacked halves edge-blend at the seam -- brightness AND canvas size.
Redundancy-only: identical content, no trim, corners converged -- lose-one-stay-lit insurance for shows that can't go dark.
Per-unit baked file: moviefileoutTOP (videocodec=hap, record=OFF) off each OUT_stack{i}_final for a media server that ingests per-projector files.
Test-pattern lane: constantTOP checker or a rendered grid as a switchable convergence source feeding both cornerpins.

HELPER build_projector_stack(source, units=N, projector_res, displays[], trim=[]): builds identical-content fan-out + per-unit cornerpin + optional trim + null + window + the differenceTOP/analyzeTOP check (~4*N+2 ops); returns OUT_stack{i}_final taps + prints the 2 human knobs (convergence corners, per-unit trim).

recipes.title: Immersive dome/360 master -> fisheye or equirectangular (cubemap-reprojection path, the fulldome lane)
recipes.summary: Render a scene as an immersive master for a dome / planetarium / 360 room. PREFERRED path: renderTOP rendermode=cubemap (6 clean 90-degree perspective faces, no line-smearing) -> projectionTOP input=cubemap output=fisheye fov=180 (or 210 for tilted domes) at a 1:1 square 'dome master' -> null -> WIRE-ONLY movie/file. geometryCOMP(well-tessellated content)+constantMAT+cameraCOMP(at dome center)+renderTOP(cubemap)+projectionTOP(cubemap->fisheye)+nullTOP+moviefileoutTOP. ASPECT IS LOAD-BEARING: fisheye/dome master MUST be 1:1, equirectangular MUST be 2:1 (e.g. 4096x2048) or the sphere/dome mapping distorts. renderTOP AND projectionTOP default to the 256px trap -- set resolution explicitly (2048x2048+). rendermode=dualparaboloid is legacy (nothing in TD consumes it) -- do NOT use it as an output. Variants: direct rendermode=fisheye180 real-time lane (fast but smears large polys -> tessellate), equirectangular 2:1 for 360/immersive rooms, cubemapods stereo pair for stereo-360 video. Dome projector calibration + fisheye-lens fit is HUMAN on-site.

In the cubemap path each face is a clean perspective render, so tessellation matters far less, but keep it healthy.

recipes.classify: dome, fulldome, planetarium, fisheye, dome master, domemaster, immersive, 360, equirectangular, wrap-around room, spherical, cubemap render, stereo 360, VR video, hemisphere, zenith
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY: builds/wires operators, no script/expression/callback path. Output is WIRE-ONLY -- the movie/file export node is built but the USER fires the write. Content authoring (fisheye/equirect/cubemap master, aspect, FOV, axis rotation) is fully data-only. HUMAN on-site: physical dome projector alignment, fisheye-lens focus, dome-edge registration, multi-projector radial seam blend, and final luminance/gamma to the dome gain. vioso/scalable calibration files (if used to drive a domed multi-projector array) are produced by external human calibration software; TD only consumes them. HONEST GAPS: rendermode=dualparaboloid exists but is legacy/unconsumed (excluded); cubemapods stereo needs Pascal/Polaris+ GPU for single-pass; reprojecting an EXISTING 2D asset (vertical-cross/equirect) into a dome uses the cubemapTOP as the input assembler (see variant), not a live 3D render.
tips: Cubemap-first beats direct fisheye180 for quality: each cube face is a clean perspective render, so straight lines/tessellation artifacts vanish; reserve fisheye180 for real-time/interactive where a single warped pass is worth the smearing.
ASPECT is the #1 failure: fisheye/dome master = 1:1 square; equirectangular = 2:1 (e.g. 4096x2048). Wrong aspect distorts the dome/sphere mapping even when every node cooks clean.
Beat the 256px trap TWICE -- both the renderTOP (per-face) and the projectionTOP (master) default to 256; set both to 2048x2048+ explicitly.
fov=180 is a true hemisphere; bump to 210 only for tilted/over-the-horizon domes -- wrong fov leaves a black ring at the dome edge or spills content off it.
Aim the dome axis with projectionTOP `r` (rx/ry/rz) rather than re-rigging the camera -- rx=-90 lifts a Y-up scene's zenith overhead; rz aligns north.
Use rgba16float through the render->projection chain for reprojection headroom, then convert at the file-out.
variants: DIRECT FISHEYE (real-time lane): skip the cubemap+projectionTOP; set renderTOP rendermode=fisheye180 and a 1:1 resolution -- single warped pass, fast for live/interactive, but large flat polys SMEAR so tessellate heavily (raise sphereSOP rows/cols). Camera fov still ignored.

360 / EQUIRECTANGULAR (immersive room / 360 video / sphere): renderTOP rendermode=cubemap -> projectionTOP input=cubemap output=equirectangular, outputresolution=custom at 2:1 (4096x2048). u-v = longitude-latitude, ready to map onto a sphereSOP with lat/long UVs for a wrap-around room.

STEREO 360 (VR video): renderTOP rendermode=cubemapods renders a stereo pair (two eyes); cameraCOMP IPD Shift offsets each eye; recover the 2nd eye with a renderSelectTOP cameraindex=1, then run each eye through its own projectionTOP to equirect 2:1. Needs multi-camera-capable GPU.

REPROJECT AN EXISTING ASSET (no live 3D): assemble a cubemap from a vertical-cross image or 6 side images with a cubemapTOP, then feed projectionTOP input=cubemap -> output=fisheye/equirectangular. Converts pre-made 360/cube content into a dome master without rendering a scene.
HEMISPHERE OPTIMIZATION: for a 180 dome, turn OFF the unused cube face(s) via renderTOP negside/posside (e.g. the downward face) to save render cost before the projectionTOP.

recipes.title: Single wide CURVED screen -> cylindrical warp + multi-projector soft-edge blend (data-only, the curved-screen lane)
recipes.summary: Take a finished flat composite and fit it to one wide curved/cylindrical screen driven by N overlapping projectors. remapTOP bends the flat image onto the curvature via a remap/UV map, then reuse the multiprojector_edge_blend machinery: per-projector cropTOP slices + rampTOP/levelTOP luminance falloff in the overlap, laid out with layoutTOP, tapped WIRE-ONLY. nullTOP(composite in)+remapTOP(cylindrical warp)+cropTOP(N slices)+rampTOP(blend ramp)+levelTOP(falloff)+layoutTOP+nullTOP+moviefileoutTOP. The remapTOP is the data-only analog of a physical warp mesh; the EXACT curvature map + seam alignment comes from on-site calibration (Stoner/camSchnappr by hand, or a viosoTOP/scalabledisplayTOP consuming an external calibration file = HUMAN). Cross-links: reuse multiprojector_edge_blend for the blend, dome_fisheye_master for the immersive/360 sibling. 256px trap applies on every TOP.

steps.note: The flat finished composite entering the warp/blend stage (fed from generative_texture_fx, facade_3d_render, or any content lane). Fixed tap so the curved-screen stage has a stable input address. Set an explicit high resolution -- beat the 256px trap.

A plain ramp is a LINEAR stand-in (approximate cylindrical stretch); the TRUE curvature map is authored per-screen or comes from calibration (honest gap -- exact curvature is not a pure ramp). Use 32-bit float for clean sampling. Aspect must match the physical screen's unrolled arc.

key_params.type: horizontal/radial ramp encoding the horizontal sample coordinate

verify.pass_if: 32-bit float map at target res; no cook error

Input 0 = the flat composite (OUT_flat), input 1 = the warp map (OUT_warpmap). horzsource/vertsource pick which map channels drive the horizontal/vertical sample position, remapping the flat image onto the cylindrical screen shape. This is the data-only analog of a Stoner/kantanMapper warp MESH -- the geometry of the curve lives entirely in the map. interp=linear (or mipmap) to keep the stretch smooth.

key_params.horzsource: map channel supplying the horizontal coordinate (e.g. r)
key_params.vertsource: map channel supplying the vertical coordinate (e.g. g)

This is the same split as multiprojector_edge_blend, applied AFTER the curvature warp so each projector gets its curved sub-region.

Mirror the ramp direction per neighbour. Radial ramp variant for a curved seam. Same principle as the facade edge-blend lane.

key_params.position1/position2: align the falloff to the overlap band

verify.pass_if: overlap edge fades smoothly; no hard seam
