recipes.classify: curved screen, cylindrical screen, curved-screen warp, wraparound screen, panoramic screen, multi-projector blend on a curve, softedge blend curved, immersive wall, arc screen, projection warp
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY: builds/wires operators only, no script/expression/callback path. Output is WIRE-ONLY -- the file/output node is built, the USER fires it. Warp geometry and blend live entirely in data (remap map + ramps + level), so authoring is data-only. HUMAN on-site: measuring the real screen curvature, aligning projector seams, and dialing final blend luminance/gamma to the physical surface -- the exact curvature/seam map is a calibration artifact. vioso/scalable calibrated warp+blend consume EXTERNAL calibration files (configfile) generated by their own on-site software -- TD only reads them (human boundary). HONEST GAPS: a plain rampTOP warp map is a LINEAR approximation of cylindrical curvature -- a production-exact map is authored per-screen or comes from calibration; TD has no data-only tool that measures the physical curve. Cross-link: reuse multiprojector_edge_blend for the blend stage and dome_fisheye_master for the fisheye/360 immersive sibling.
tips: Warp FIRST, then slice+blend: bend the whole composite onto the curve with the remapTOP, then split into per-projector overlapping slices -- slicing before warping mis-registers the seams.

The curvature lives in the remap MAP, not in geometry -- this is the data-only analog of a Stoner/kantanMapper warp mesh; a ramp is only a linear stand-in, swap in an authored/calibration map for production accuracy.
Keep the warp map and remap chain in 32-bit float -- 8-bit remap coords band and tear the stretched image.
Overlap bands must be equal width on both neighbours and the blend ramps mirrored, or the summed seam shows a bright or dark line.
Beat the 256px trap on every TOP in the chain (in null, ramp map, remap, layout) -- one defaulted 256 node silently caps the whole curved output.
For a genuinely curved seam use a radial rampTOP for the blend rather than a linear one.

For a fully calibrated pipeline, replace the manual warp+blend with a single viosoTOP or scalabledisplayTOP fed the on-site .vwf/scalable mesh file -- that file is a HUMAN calibration output, not something TD authors.
variants: CALIBRATED WARP+BLEND (production): drop the remap/crop/ramp/level/layout chain and route OUT_flat through a viosoTOP (configfile = VIOSO calibration file, projectorindex per output) or a scalabledisplayTOP (configfile = Scalable mesh, eyepoint set) -- one node does measured warp+blend across the array. The calibration file is generated on-site by external software (HUMAN); TD consumes it read-only.
PER-PROJECTOR OUTPUTS: instead of one wide layoutTOP canvas, tap each OUT_blended slice to its own nullTOP/output for N discrete projector feeds (multi-window/multi-GPU setups).

SHARED BLEND MACHINERY: for the pure flat multi-projector case (no curvature), skip the remapTOP and use multiprojector_edge_blend directly -- this recipe = that blend lane + a curvature warp in front.

DOME SIBLING: for a full dome/360 immersive surface rather than a single curved screen, use dome_fisheye_master (fisheye/equirect master), optionally slicing the fisheye into per-projector radial wedges with cropTOP + a radial rampTOP blend.

recipes.title: Rig-and-focus test-pattern / alignment-grid generator (data-only QC patterns a projectionist projects on-site to align, focus, verify 1:1 native pixels, converge stacks, set blend overlaps, and match colour -- WIRE-ONLY output at projector native res)
recipes.summary: The setup-time companion to projection_align_and_output: builds the reference imagery the projectionist PROJECTS during rig-and-focus (registration grid, edge-of-frame + safe-area border, centre crosshair + centre target, grayscale/gamma ramp, SMPTE colour bars, high-frequency focus/uniformity field, per-projector number+resolution label, convergence crosshatch, edge-blend overlap markers), lets them flip between patterns with one switchTOP index, and hands the live pattern to a projector/NDI/Spout/file WIRE-ONLY. Purely typed generator ops -- NO script, NO expressions, NO callbacks. The whole point is native-pixel accuracy: every generator's outputresolution=custom at the projector's native pixels, resmult OFF, and NOT ONE fitTOP/resample anywhere in the chain, so a 1px grid or fine field is a true 1:1 test -- if it shimmers, a scaler is in the path. HONEST LIMITS: TouchDesigner has NO grid TOP (grid lines come from a gridSOP rendered through an ORTHOGRAPHIC cameraCOMP), NO tileTOP is exposed on this surface, and TD's own Palette:testGrid / Palette:checker are GLSL/scripted .tox COMPs -- so a FINE checkerboard is out of the data-only lane (see governance). Labels/numbers are pure textTOP, no render pass.

steps.note: The native-resolution CANVAS and the convention anchor for the whole recipe: a flat black field at the projector's native pixels. Set outputresolution=custom + resolution=[native_w,native_h] and turn resmult OFF (the global res multiplier must never shrink a test pattern). EVERY generator below copies these three settings -- that, plus never inserting a fitTOP/resampling op, is the entire native-pixel guarantee. Human boundary: the projectionist supplies the exact native res per projector (e.g. 1920x1080 or 3840x2160).
steps.geometry_out: flat black TOP at projector native resolution

verify.pass_if: resolution == projector native (e.g. 1920x1080) and resmult reads off

steps.note: The registration-grid GEOMETRY -- there is NO grid TOP, so grid lines are real polylines: type=poly + surftype=rowcol gives row+column open lines (no filled quads). Use an ODD rows/cols count so a line lands exactly on centre (17 -> 16 cells + centreline). orient=xy so it faces the ortho camera; size=[2,2] to match the camera's ortho width. Convergence-crosshatch and focus-grid variants reuse this same SOP at different divisions.
steps.geometry_out: SOP: 17x17 grid of row+column polylines centred on origin, facing +Z

verify.pass_if: gridSOP present, type=poly, surftype=rowcol, odd rows/cols

steps.note: White, unlit line material for the grid (and, tinted, for the convergence crosshatch). constantMAT ignores lights so line brightness is exact. Keep color=[1,1,1] for the master grid; the convergence variant sets color=[1,0,0] on projector A and [0,1,1] on projector B so the two stacks' lines are distinguishable when overlaid by eye. Line width is 1px by default (ideal for the native-pixel test) -- thicken via a linethickSOP before the geometryCOMP only if the surface needs it.
steps.geometry_out: MAT: flat white line shader (per-projector tint for convergence)

verify.pass_if: constantMAT exists with color white, alpha 1

steps.note: Hosts the grid SOP and carries the line material. Wire OUT_tpg_grid_geo into it; set material to OUT_tpg_line_mat and leave render=on. No transform needed -- the SOP is already centred and sized to the ortho frame.
steps.geometry_out: renderable object: grid lines with white constant material

verify.pass_if: geometryCOMP references the grid SOP and the constantMAT

steps.note: ORTHOGRAPHIC camera -- this is load-bearing: a perspective camera would taper the grid toward the edges and ruin it as a registration reference. projection=ortho, orthowidth=2 to exactly frame the size-2 grid; pull back on +Z (tz=5) looking down -Z (default forward). Shared by every rendered-SOP pattern (grid, crosshatch, focus-grid).
steps.geometry_out: orthographic camera framing the unit grid edge-to-edge

verify.pass_if: cameraCOMP projection=ortho, orthowidth=2

steps.note: MILESTONE: renders the registration grid to a native-resolution TOP. camera=OUT_tpg_ortho_cam, geometry=OUT_tpg_grid_obj, outputresolution=custom at native, transparent background (bgcolor alpha 0). CRITICAL gotcha: set antialias=aa1 (OFF) -- multisampling softens 1px grid lines and would fake a blurry image on a perfectly-focused projector, defeating the sharpness/native-pixel test. This render is the on-site geometry/keystone reference; the numeric keystone correction itself is applied downstream in projection_align_and_output, not here.
steps.geometry_out: registration-grid TOP at projector native res, crisp 1px lines, alpha outside lines
steps.milestone_check: top_info on OUT_tpg_grid reports native resolution with resmult off and antialias aa1; non-zero (white) pixels present on grid lines -- a clean, unscaled, pixel-exact registration grid.

verify.cheap: top_info on OUT_tpg_grid; find_errors on the render chain
verify.pass_if: resolution == native, no cook errors, grid visible

steps.note: Edge-of-frame border + safe-area/aspect guide, pure 2D. Full-frame outline: size=[1,1] fraction, fillalpha=0 (no fill), border on via borderwidth in PIXELS (2px) so the outline is exactly at the frame edge. Add a second rectangleTOP at size=[0.9,0.9] for a safe-area guide, and letterbox marks as further rects. Native res as always.
steps.geometry_out: white frame-edge outline (+ optional safe-area rect) on transparent

verify.pass_if: native res, border pixels only at frame edge, interior transparent

steps.note: Centre crosshair -- vertical bar. A single rectangleTOP can't draw a cross, so the crosshair is TWO thin rects composited: this one is the vertical stroke, size=[~2px,1] centred at origin. Pair with the horizontal bar (next step). Centre marks let the projectionist set lens shift and find true centre for stacking.
steps.geometry_out: thin white vertical centre stroke on transparent

verify.pass_if: native res, single thin vertical white line at x-centre

steps.note: Centre crosshair -- horizontal bar (the second half of the cross). size=[1,~2px] centred at origin, white fill. Composited with the vertical bar (step 8) and the centre target (step 10) into the alignment pattern.
steps.geometry_out: thin white horizontal centre stroke on transparent

verify.pass_if: native res, single thin horizontal white line at y-centre

steps.note: Centre target ring -- a hollow circle at frame centre (fillalpha=0, border on 2px white) so distortion reads instantly (the ring goes oval if aspect/keystone is off). radius in fractionaspect keeps it round regardless of frame aspect. Corner registration circles are the same circleTOP re-used with center at the four corners and composited (or drop small circleTOPs via transform + the composite in step 11).
steps.geometry_out: hollow white centre-target ring on transparent

verify.pass_if: native res, round hollow ring centred

steps.note: Assembles the full ALIGNMENT pattern: wire OUT_tpg_grid, OUT_tpg_frame, OUT_tpg_cross_v, OUT_tpg_cross_h, OUT_tpg_center_target as inputs, operand=over (stack), and Fixed Layer size=input1 so the composite locks to the native-res grid and never resizes. This one TOP is what the projectionist projects to aim, keystone, and confirm the frame lands on the surface.
steps.geometry_out: composite alignment pattern: grid + frame + crosshair + centre target, native res

verify.pass_if: resolution == native, all elements visible over black

steps.note: Grayscale ramp for brightness/black-level/white-clip matching between projectors. type=horizontal, native res. GAMMA-CHART variant: set interpnotches=step and drive a multi-key ramp from a tableDAT for a stepped grey wedge, or follow with a levelTOP gamma. Colour caveat: keep NO stray levelTOP/opencolorioTOP elsewhere in the chain or the grayscale reads false.
steps.geometry_out: horizontal black-to-white grayscale ramp at native res

verify.pass_if: native res, monotonic 0->1 luminance across width

steps.note: One SMPTE colour-bar patch (representative). Build SEVEN of these -- white, yellow, cyan, green, magenta, red, blue -- each a constantTOP at native res with its colour; they feed the layoutTOP in the next step. Grayscale-step variant: make N grey constantTOPs instead. (This is where a fine repeating pattern would want the tileTOP -- which is NOT exposed on this surface -- so colour bars are done as discrete patches, not tiled.)
steps.geometry_out: one solid SMPTE colour patch (build 7 total)

verify.pass_if: constantTOP set to the intended SMPTE colour at native res

steps.note: SMPTE colour bars: wire the 7 colour-patch constantTOPs as inputs, align=horizlr, fit=fill so each bar takes an equal vertical stripe; native res. For a colour+grayscale QC card use align=gridcols/gridrows to tile bars over a grey-step row. This is the between-projector colour/brightness match pattern.
steps.geometry_out: vertical SMPTE colour-bar array at native res

verify.pass_if: native res, N equal-width colour stripes

steps.note: Focus / uniformity / moire field: a high-frequency monochrome noise field the projectionist walks the focus ring against and eyeballs for hotspotting, vignetting, dead pixels and screen-door/moire. Native res, resmult off (a scaled noise field would itself moire and mislead). Choose a fine, monochrome noise on the live UI; keep it 1:1.
steps.geometry_out: high-frequency monochrome detail field at native res

verify.pass_if: native res, dense per-pixel detail present

steps.note: Per-projector identity + native-res readout, e.g. 'PJ-01  1920x1080@60'. Pure textTOP -- fully data-only, NO render pass needed. font/size/colour typed directly; centred; transparent background (bgalpha=0) so it can overlay any pattern. One per projector so a multi-projector rig is self-identifying ('which feed is on PJ-3?'). Change the text per output via set_par.
steps.geometry_out: projector-number + resolution label, white on transparent, native res

verify.pass_if: native res, legible label rendered

steps.note: Edge-blend OVERLAP markers: vertical boundary bars at the two edges of the overlap band plus a semi-opaque fill for the band, so the projectionist can physically place adjacent projectors to a target overlap (~15% of frame width is common practice). Size/centre define the band. CONVERGENCE crosshatch for stacked projectors is NOT a new op -- it is OUT_tpg_grid rendered with OUT_tpg_line_mat tinted per projector (color=[1,0,0] vs [0,1,1]); the projectionist overlays the two stacks and nudges until the coloured lines coincide (any blur = imperfect convergence).
steps.geometry_out: overlap-band markers (boundary lines + faint fill) at native res

verify.pass_if: native res, band edges marked at the intended overlap width

steps.note: The pattern SELECTOR the projectionist drives during rig: wire the pattern outputs as inputs in order -- OUT_tpg_align, OUT_tpg_grayramp, OUT_tpg_colorbars, OUT_tpg_detail, OUT_tpg_label, OUT_tpg_overlap (and a convergence-tinted grid) -- and change index to flip the live pattern. blend OFF (hard cut), extend=clamp. index is a plain parameter set via set_par (data-only, no expression).
steps.geometry_out: single selected test pattern at native res

verify.cheap: top_info on OUT_tpg_select; set_par index and re-read
verify.pass_if: output equals the input named by index; resolution stays native

steps.note: Planted output landmark -- the stable hand-off point every downstream output op reads (per recipe convention, keeps the network re-wireable without touching the switch).
steps.geometry_out: the live selected pattern, native res, at the output null

verify.pass_if: resolution == native, matches the selected pattern

steps.note: WIRE-ONLY output to the real projector: winop=OUT_tpg, Opening Size=custom with winw/winh at native, justifyoffsetto=specifydisplay + display=<projector's monitor index>, borders OFF so nothing steals a pixel, DPI Scaling=native so Windows can't rescale. DO NOT pulse setperform/winopen/performance -- the bridge only WIRES the window; the projectionist opens it. Native-pixel integrity depends on no scaling here AND on disabling projector-side overscan/aspect/EDID scaling (a human step). Alternatives, all wire-only: moviefileoutTOP (record OFF) for a native-res pattern file, ndioutTOP / syphonspoutoutTOP (active OFF) for a live feed to a media server.
steps.geometry_out: configured (unopened) perform window mapping OUT_tpg to the projector display, 1:1

verify.pass_if: winop=OUT_tpg, size=custom at native, display set, setperform NOT fired (window closed)

recipes.classify: on-site rig-and-focus QC + alignment tooling for projection mapping -- generate DATA-ONLY test patterns (registration grid via gridSOP->ortho cameraCOMP->renderTOP; frame/safe-area + crosshair + centre target via rectangleTOP/circleTOP+compositeTOP; grayscale/gamma via rampTOP; SMPTE colour bars via layoutTOP of constantTOPs; focus/uniformity field via noiseTOP; per-projector number+res via textTOP; convergence crosshatch = tinted grid; edge-blend overlap markers via rectangleTOP), select with switchTOP, expose WIRE-ONLY to a projector (windowCOMP) / file (moviefileoutTOP) / media server (ndioutTOP/syphonspoutoutTOP) at projector NATIVE resolution with no resampling in the chain; the physical focus/aim/converge and projector-side scaling settings are HUMAN steps
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY: pure typed generator ops -- no script/execute op, no expressions, no callbacks DATs; the switchTOP index and every parameter are set literally via set_par. HONEST CATALOG LIMITS (do not paper over): (1) TouchDesigner has NO grid TOP -- grid lines are gridSOP polylines rendered through an ORTHOGRAPHIC cameraCOMP; a perspective cam tapers the grid and is wrong. (2) tileTOP is NOT exposed on this surface, so repeating/tiled references and a FINE checkerboard cannot be built cheaply here; colour bars are discrete constantTOP patches via layoutTOP, not tiled. (3) TD's own Palette:testGrid and Palette:checker are the ideal ready-made patterns but are GLSL/SDF, scripted .tox COMPs -- OUTSIDE the data-only, typed-tool lane; a fine checkerboard is therefore either the owner-gated validated GLSL lane, or a HUMAN step (the projectionist drops Palette:testGrid/checker in by hand). NATIVE-RESOLUTION is the core contract: every generator outputresolution=custom at projector native, resmult OFF, and NO fitTOP/resampling op anywhere -- a 1px line or fine field is then a true 1:1 pixel test. Output is WIRE-ONLY: windowCOMP is configured but NOT opened (setperform/winopen never pulsed), moviefileoutTOP record OFF, ndioutTOP/syphonspoutoutTOP active OFF; the operator fires them. Minimal HUMAN boundary: physical focus/aim/stacking/convergence-by-eye, colour match by eye, disabling projector-side overscan/aspect/EDID scaling, and supplying each projector's native resolution. This recipe ENDS at the reference pixels; the numeric keystone correction belongs to projection_align_and_output.
tips: Turn multisampling OFF (renderTOP antialias=aa1) for the grid and any 1px pattern -- AA softens thin lines and fakes a blurry image on a sharply-focused projector, defeating the focus/native-pixel test.
resmult=off on EVERY generator: the global res multiplier will otherwise silently shrink a pattern and invalidate the 1:1 check.

The 1px grid IS the trap and the test: if it shimmers/moires, a scaler is resampling -- first confirm it isn't your own chain (no fitTOP, no mid-chain resolution change), then suspect projector overscan/aspect/EDID scaling.
Use ODD grid divisions (17, 33) so a line falls exactly on centre and lines up with the crosshair.

Convergence for stacked projectors: reuse OUT_tpg_grid with the constantMAT tinted red on stack A and cyan on stack B; overlay by eye and nudge until the coloured lines coincide (blur = misconvergence).
Per-projector labels: duplicate OUT_tpg_label and set_par text 'PJ-02...', 'PJ-03...' so each output self-identifies on a multi-projector rig.
Keep the colour chain linear: no stray levelTOP/opencolorioTOP anywhere or the grayscale/colour-bar match reads false.
Thicker grid lines for a rough surface: insert a linethickSOP before the geometryCOMP -- do NOT rely on AA (see tip 1).
variants: Gamma / step-wedge chart: rampTOP interpnotches=step driven by a tableDAT of grey keys (data-only), or a levelTOP gamma after the grayscale ramp, for mid-tone matching between projectors.

Coarse checkerboard (data-only, low division count): a layoutTOP align=gridcols/gridrows fed by alternating black/white constantTOPs -- acceptable for a few cells; a FINE checker needs the absent tileTOP or the GLSL lane, or Palette:checker by hand.
Multi-projector patch view: layoutTOP align=gridcols of each projector's OUT_tpg feeds to eyeball the whole rig at once on one preview surface.

File hand-off: swap the windowCOMP for a moviefileoutTOP (record OFF) to bake a native-res pattern still/loop the media server can hold; or ndioutTOP/syphonspoutoutTOP (active OFF) to send the live pattern to Pixera/disguise.
Focus-grid: reuse the gridSOP->ortho->render path at high divisions (65+) as a dense fine-detail focus chart instead of the noiseTOP field.

recipes.title: Robust 4K clip playback + playlist (moviefilein deck, gapless A/B, folder/table cue list, data-only)
recipes.summary: The media-server CLIP layer for FLAT/whole-surface shows built from finished video (not generative, not per-section emit). A moviefileinTOP is the playback atom -- codec-aware 4K (HAP/HAP Q/NotchLC via High Performance Read; H.264/H.265 via Hardware Decode), pre-read into memory, loop (textend=cycle) or ping-pong (mirror) with a gapless seam dissolve (loopcrossfade), cue (cuepoint+cuepulse), trim (tstart/tend), and speed. A folderDAT of a media directory (or a tableDAT loaded from a write_csv playlist.csv) is the cue list. Two decks (deckA/deckB) feed a crossTOP for GAPLESS switching: preload the idle deck's file while the other plays, then sweep cross 0->1 -- the data-only substitute for the Python preload()/isFullyPreRead handshake (observe readiness with an infoCHOP instead). A timerCHOP (one segment per clip, outseg on) auto-advances by binding its segment channel to the selector; GO/next/prev is the allowlisted pulse actuator (timer gotonextseg/gotoprevseg/start, or moviefilein cuepulse/reloadpulse). A switchTOP is the alternative N-clip bank selector -- but all N decks decode every cooked frame, so gate each deck's play=(index==i) via a logic/math CHOP to avoid N simultaneous 4K decodes. Now/next is a nullDAT tap off the playlist. WIRE-ONLY: feeds output_handoff/projection_align_and_output; the bridge never fires the show. 256px trap is REAL -- moviefileinTOP defaults 256x256; set outputresolution=custom + 3840x2160 for 4K delivery.

steps.tool: (asset) copy clips under the working dir
steps.note: The F2 path confinement blanks external file paths -- stage the show media under the working dir (assets/media/) before referencing it. Transcoding sources to HAP/HAP Q/NotchLC is an UPSTREAM human step (external encoder); only loading the finished file is in-scope.
steps.geometry_out: clips staged on disk under the working dir

verify.pass_if: working dir contains the media folder

steps.note: The data-only cue list: point rootfolder at assets/media/, movieextensions=true, pathcol=true so each row is a playable clip path. VARIANT: author an ordered/annotated show list as playlist.csv via write_csv -> a tableDAT (gives explicit order, in/out, per-clip trim columns a raw folder listing lacks). callbacks MUST stay empty (denied code-sink).
steps.geometry_out: a table (DAT) of clip paths = the cue list

verify.pass_if: row count == number of staged clips; a 'path' column resolves to files

steps.note: DECK A -- the robust 4K playback atom. 256 TRAP: outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h=3840/2160 or the whole chain inherits 256. CODEC: for 4K HAP/HAP Q/NotchLC set highperfread=on (very high SSD read rates); for H.264/H.265 keep hwdecode=on (GPU decode, but seeks/cues poorly). PRELOAD (data-only, substitutes Python preload()): prereadframes raised (e.g. 20) + alwaysloadinitial=on keeps a hot first frame. LOOP: textendleft/textendright=cycle (loop) or mirror (ping-pong); loopcrossfade>0 (fraction) dissolves the loop seam for gapless. CUE: cue + cuepoint + cuepointunit=seconds, fired by the cuepulse actuator. TRIM: trim=on + tstart/tend (+ units). SPEED: speed. AUDIO is a SEPARATE audiomovieCHOP on the same file (the TOP carries no audio). callbacks MUST stay empty (denied code-sink).
steps.geometry_out: a decoded 4K clip (TOP), looping

verify.pass_if: resolution==3840x2160 and the TOP is valid/non-black

steps.note: DECK B -- the idle preload deck for GAPLESS switching. Same 4K/codec/preread params as deckA; its file is set (via set_par from the NEXT playlist row) and preread (alwaysloadinitial=on) WHILE deckA plays, so its first frame is hot before the cut. Set play=off (or gate it) until it becomes the live deck to save a decode.
steps.geometry_out: the next clip, preloaded (TOP)

verify.pass_if: resolution==3840x2160; first frame present with play off (alwaysloadinitial worked)

steps.note: GAPLESS double-buffer selector: deckA -> in1, deckB -> in2, cross 0..1 dissolves between them (cross=0 shows deckA, 1 shows deckB). On a cut: sweep cross 0->1 (bound to the transport, or a hard set_par for an instant cut), then repoint the now-idle deck's file to the following clip and preload it. This is the data-only stand-in for the moviePlayer .tox's frame-drop-free switch. VARIANT (many short clips): a switchTOP with index selecting an N-deck bank and blend=on for the crossfade -- but see the N-decoder gotcha in tips.
steps.geometry_out: the live program stream (TOP)

verify.pass_if: cross=0 image==deckA, cross=1 image==deckB

steps.note: AUTO-ADVANCE transport (reuses show_control_timecode). One SEGMENT per clip (a segdat table -- a DATA table of durations, NOT code), outseg=on emits the current segment index, outsegplusfraction/outfraction gives 0..1 within-clip progress (drive crossTOP.cross for an eased scene change; set interpolation=easeinouttovalue). ondone=restart loops the playlist. GO/NEXT/PREV = the allowlisted pulse actuator: start, gotonextseg, gotoprevseg. active=running. callbacks MUST stay empty (denied code-sink); segdat/segments is a data table, allowed.

key_params.active: running

steps.geometry_out: a transport: segment index + 0..1 fraction (CHOP)

verify.pass_if: a 'segment' channel exists and increments when gotonextseg is pulsed

steps.note: DRIVE selection data-only: bind OUT_transport 'segment' -> switchTOP.index (N-clip bank), or 'timer_fraction' -> crossTOP.cross (2-deck eased cut). bind_chop is the proven cook-time drive (sets exporter activeViewer + force-cook per the CHOP-export gotcha). Manual GO without the timer = a plain set_par on cross/index. NO expressions, NO callbacks.
steps.geometry_out: the selector param now follows the transport

verify.pass_if: OUT_now changes clip when the transport advances

steps.note: READINESS/now-playing observation -- the data-only substitute for Python isFullyPreRead. op=OUT_deckB reads the preload/index/length state (e.g. current index vs total frames, decode timing) so you can VERIFY the idle deck is hot before sweeping the cross. Read-only; drives nothing. Pair with a nullDAT tap off OUT_playlist for the 'now / next' clip names.
steps.geometry_out: deck state channels (CHOP)

verify.pass_if: index/length channels present and non-zero for the preloaded deck

steps.note: Stable program tap. Everything downstream references OUT_clip_player, never the decks/cross directly, so deck rewiring never breaks consumers. WIRE-ONLY handoff: feeds output_handoff (moviefileoutTOP record OFF / NDI / Spout) or projection_align_and_output; a single clip player is also one LAYER SOURCE for layer_compositor.
steps.geometry_out: the finished, tapped program stream (TOP)

verify.pass_if: shows the live clip at full 4K res

recipes.classify: play a video / movie / clip; media player; playlist; clip library; cue list; now playing / next; gapless playback; switch clips; crossfade between clips; 4K HAP / HAP Q / NotchLC / ProRes / H264 / H265 playback; loop / cue / trim / speed / deinterlace a movie; folder of clips; media-server clip layer for a flat / whole-surface show
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY: typed operators + literal set_par + bind_chop (cook-time CHOP drive) + the allowlisted pulse actuators (moviefilein cuepulse/reloadpulse; timer start/gotonextseg/gotoprevseg -- parameterless, carry no code). NO expressions, NO script/execute, NO callbacks -- every moviefileinTOP.callbacks / folderDAT.callbacks / timerCHOP.callbacks MUST stay empty (denied code-sinks). The Python preload()/isFullyPreRead ready-handshake is NOT data-only and is NOT used -- substituted by prereadframes + alwaysloadinitial + an infoCHOP that OBSERVES readiness plus a bounded A/B preroll. The stock Palette moviePlaylist / moviePlayer are Python .tox components (embedded extensions/callbacks) -- REFERENCE DESIGN ONLY, they are NOT buildable by this typed surface and must not be instantiated. Output is WIRE-ONLY: this recipe builds and taps the program stream; the operator/media server fires playback and record. NEW DOMAIN 'media' is warranted: this is finished-video content assembly for a flat / whole-surface canvas -- distinct from projection-mapping (per-section emit), texture (generative fields), and output (hand-off). HONEST GAPS: (1) truly frame-perfect gapless equals the .tox's scripted ready-gate -- the data-only A/B preroll is robust but relies on adequate prereadframes/SSD headroom, not a guaranteed handshake; (2) an N-deck switchTOP bank decodes ALL N clips per cooked frame (see play-gating tip) -- prefer the 2-deck crossTOP for 4K; (3) audio sync is a parallel audiomovieCHOP path, not automatic from the TOP.
tips: 256 TRAP: moviefileinTOP defaults 256x256 -- set outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h=3840x2160 (or useinput) on EVERY deck for 4K.
CODEC = the #1 reliability lever: HAP/HAP Q/NotchLC + highperfread for smooth 4K; ProRes for master quality; H.264/H.265 only for low-bitrate/preview (heavy decode, poor scrub/cue) with hwdecode=on.

N-DECODER GOTCHA: a switchTOP of N moviefileinTOPs decodes ALL N every cooked frame = N simultaneous 4K decodes. FIX: gate each deck's play=(index==i) via a logicCHOP/mathCHOP channel bound to moviefileinTOP.play, so only the live (and the next-preloading) deck decodes. The 2-deck crossTOP path already does this by design.

GAPLESS pattern: play deckA; set deckB.file = next clip + alwaysloadinitial=on to preload; sweep crossTOP.cross 0->1; then repoint the now-idle deck to the following clip. Confirm deckB is hot via the infoCHOP before the sweep.
SINGLE-OP variant (infrequent scene changes): one moviefileinTOP, set_par file=next row, fire reloadpulse -- one light decoder, but the swap is a visible reload gap, not gapless.
loopcrossfade dissolves the loop seam for a clean repeat; textendright=mirror gives ping-pong; trim (tstart/tend) plays a sub-range; cuepoint+cuepulse jumps to an in-point live.
variants: N-clip bank: folderDAT -> N moviefileinTOPs -> switchTOP (index bound to the transport 'segment', blend=on for crossfade, extend=loop) with per-deck play-gating -- for many short/low-res clips.
Show-list from CSV: write_csv playlist.csv (order, in, out, dur) -> tableDAT instead of a raw folderDAT -- explicit ordering, trims, and cue annotations.
Timecode-locked playback: moviefileinTOP playmode=timecodeop + a timecodeCHOP (LTC/MTC) for festival/broadcast sync (reuse show_control_timecode).
Audio-synced: add an audiomovieCHOP on the same file -> audiodeviceoutCHOP for lip-synced sound (WIRE-ONLY out).

recipes.title: Media-server layer stack: N source->transform->opacity/grade layers into layermixTOP, master fade-to-black + scene transitions (data-only)
recipes.summary: The VJ/media-server LAYER STACK for a flat/whole-surface show: N layers, each source (a media_clip_player OUT_clip_player, or any TOP) -> transformTOP (position/scale/rotate) -> levelTOP (opacity dimmer + brightness/gamma grade), composited top-to-bottom in ONE layermixTOP (maxinputs 9999) with per-layer opacity, per-layer blend mode (operand=opperlayer), per-layer transform, comporder=backtofront, and a black constant background (background=constlayer, bgcolor 0). A master fade-to-black is a trailing levelTOP.opacity 1->0 (or a crossTOP against a black constantTOP). SCENE TRANSITIONS between two whole looks: a crossTOP (cross 0..1 dissolve) or a data-only LUMA-WIPE (rampTOP gradient -> levelTOP threshold-window swept to a moving soft edge = a matte, applied by compositeTOP: multiply the incoming look by the matte, then composite over the outgoing look). Every transition/opacity scalar is driven data-only -- set_par (manual) or a bound CHOP/timer fraction (auto, eased), NO expressions, NO callbacks. Consumes media_clip_player as a layer source; the OUT_composite tap feeds projection_align_and_output / multiprojector_edge_blend / mesh_freeform_warp downstream. 256 trap applies to the constantTOP/rampTOP generators.

steps.note: Each LAYER is a TOP -- typically a media_clip_player OUT_clip_player (finished clip), but also a generative_texture_fx OUT_facade_tex field, a text/still, or a live NDI/Spout in. Build 2-8 layers; the stack composites them simultaneously (spatial), distinct from the playlist's temporal one-of-N selection.
steps.geometry_out: N program TOPs = the layer sources

verify.pass_if: each layer source shows its content at delivery res

steps.note: Per-layer PLACEMENT: tx/ty (tunit=fraction), sx/sy scale, rotate -- position/resize a layer within the canvas (a lower-third, a corner inset, a full-bleed bg). extend=zero keeps outside-frame transparent. One transformTOP per layer that needs moving; skip for full-bleed layers.
steps.geometry_out: the layer, positioned/scaled (TOP)

verify.pass_if: layer sits at the intended position/scale

steps.note: Per-layer OPACITY + GRADE: opacity is the layer's dimmer/fade (1->0), brightness1/gamma1/blacklevel for a quick grade so mismatched clips sit together. Bind opacity to a fader/timer for a live layer crossfade. NOTE: layermixTOP has its own per-layer opacity (enableopac) -- use this upstream levelTOP when you also want grade, or lean on layermix's built-in opacity for a lighter graph.
steps.geometry_out: the layer, faded/graded (TOP)

verify.pass_if: layer visibly dims with opacity

steps.note: THE layer stack (one node = a media-server stack; maxinputs 9999). Wire layers bottom-first; comporder=backtofront composites input1 (back) up to inputN (front). PER-LAYER controls: enableopac (+opacity), enablebright, enablelevels, enablet/enabler/scalemode (transform), and operand=opperlayer to give EACH layer its own blend mode (over/add/screen/multiply/difference/overlay/softlight/lightercolor...). BLACK CANVAS: background=constlayer + bgcolor 0,0,0,1 (or 0 alpha) so the stack always sits on black. size=outputres + set 4K output res.
steps.geometry_out: the composited layer stack (TOP)

verify.pass_if: all layers composite top-to-bottom over black; per-layer blend modes read correctly

steps.note: The black canvas / master-fade target. Set color 0,0,0 and MATCH the 4K delivery res (256 trap: outputresolution=custom + 3840x2160) so the master fade and any crossTOP against it are full-frame.
steps.geometry_out: a 4K black frame (TOP)

verify.pass_if: resolution==3840x2160, pixels black

steps.note: MASTER fade-to-black: a trailing levelTOP on OUT_stack with opacity 1->0 blacks out the WHOLE show (the media-server grand-master). opacity driven data-only by set_par (manual) or a bound CHOP/timer fraction (timed blackout). Equivalent alternative: crossTOP(OUT_stack in1, OUT_black in2) with cross=master 0..1.
steps.geometry_out: the stack under a master dimmer (TOP)

verify.pass_if: opacity 0 => full black; opacity 1 => full stack

steps.note: SCENE TRANSITION (dissolve): to cut between two whole looks (e.g. two layer stacks, or stack vs an incoming clip), feed lookA->in1, lookB->in2, sweep cross 0->1 for a linear dissolve. Drive cross by set_par (manual GO) or a bound timer fraction (eased, via interpolation=easeinouttovalue). For a LUMA-WIPE instead, see the next two steps.
steps.geometry_out: the transition between two looks (TOP)

verify.pass_if: 0=lookA, 1=lookB, 0.5=blend

steps.note: LUMA-WIPE matte (step 1 of 2): a gradient (horizontal/radial). Set 4K res (256 trap). A levelTOP downstream sweeps a narrow inlow/inhigh threshold window (+ soften for a soft edge) across this ramp to make a MOVING soft-edged matte M (0=old, 1=new). Sweep the threshold via set_par/bound CHOP = the wipe progress.
steps.geometry_out: a gradient (TOP) to be thresholded into a wipe matte

verify.pass_if: resolution==3840x2160; a smooth 0..1 gradient

As the level threshold sweeps, the new look is revealed behind a soft moving edge. All-verified ops (no matte-only node needed). For a plain dissolve use the crossTOP step instead.
steps.geometry_out: the luma-wiped transition (TOP)

verify.pass_if: a soft-edged wipe reveals the new look; ends fully on the new look

steps.note: Final composite tap. Downstream references OUT_composite only. WIRE-ONLY handoff: feeds projection_align_and_output (cornerpin keystone + windowCOMP/moviefileout/NDI/Spout, record OFF), multiprojector_edge_blend, or mesh_freeform_warp. The bridge builds and taps; the operator/media server delivers.

recipes.classify: layer stack; multi-layer compositing; composite video layers; VJ / media-server layers; blend modes; per-layer opacity / transform; master fade to black; blackout; crossfade / dissolve / luma-wipe between scenes; mix finished clips onto a flat / whole-surface canvas; overlay a lower-third / bug / background layer
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY: typed compositing operators + literal set_par + bind_chop for animated scalars (opacity, cross, wipe threshold). NO expressions, NO script/execute, NO callbacks. Every transition/fade is a parameter sweep, never code. The stock Palette moviePlaylist/moviePlayer are Python .tox = REFERENCE ONLY (not used here); this recipe consumes media_clip_player, which is itself fully data-only. Output is WIRE-ONLY: builds and taps the composite; the operator/media server keystones and delivers it (via projection_align_and_output etc.). NEW DOMAIN 'media' (shared with media_clip_player): finished-video assembly for a flat/whole-surface canvas -- orthogonal to projection-mapping's per-section emit rig. SEPARATION rationale: playlist (media_clip_player) = TEMPORAL one-of-N clip selection over time; layer_compositor = SPATIAL simultaneous stacking of many sources -- a projectionist mixes both (a playlist can be one layer of a stack), so they are distinct, composable recipes not one node. HONEST GAPS: (1) layermixTOP composites simultaneous layers but is NOT a timeline -- sequencing/cueing layers over time is the timerCHOP transport (facade_cue_choreography / show_control_timecode) driving the opacity/cross scalars; (2) the luma-wipe is a ramp+level+composite build (no dedicated matte-wipe node), robust but hand-wired; (3) heavy stacks of 4K layers are GPU-bound -- layer count is a performance budget the operator validates on the show machine.
tips: layermixTOP operand=opperlayer is the key to a real media-server stack -- EACH layer gets its own blend mode; a single compositeTOP forces ONE blend mode across the whole stack (use compositeTOP only for uniform add/screen).
layoutTOP is NOT a compositor -- it arranges TOPs in a grid/row (monitor wall / preview multiview). For stacked comping use layermixTOP (or chained overTOP for pairwise control).
Master fade-to-black: a trailing levelTOP.opacity on the whole stack is the grand-master; drive it and each layer's opacity from a bound CHOP/timer for live faders.
256 TRAP on the generators: constantTOP (black canvas) and rampTOP (wipe matte) default 256x256 -- set them to the 4K delivery res or the master fade/wipe won't be full-frame.

Per-layer opacity twice: layermixTOP's enableopac gives built-in per-layer opacity (lighter graph); the upstream levelTOP is for when you ALSO need brightness/gamma grade -- don't double-apply the same fade.
Drive every transition scalar data-only: set_par for manual GO, or bind_chop a timer 'fraction' (interpolation=easeinouttovalue) for an eased auto crossfade/wipe -- no expressions, no callbacks.
variants: Pairwise control: chain overTOP (premultiplied A-over-B) per layer instead of one layermixTOP -- more nodes, maximum per-pair control.
Uniform-blend stack: a single compositeTOP (multi-input tops, one operand=add/screen) when all layers share one blend mode -- lighter than layermix.
Timeline-sequenced layers: drive per-layer opacity from facade_cue_choreography's eased cue channels / show_control_timecode transport for a cued show (reveal/hide layers over time).
Dissolve vs luma-wipe: crossTOP for a plain scene dissolve; the rampTOP->levelTOP->compositeTOP matte chain for a shaped soft-edge wipe.

recipes.title: Vision-interactive content -- a live camera drives a silhouette / presence / motion MASK that reveals or displaces generative content (data-only)
recipes.summary: Make the wall REACT to people from a plain camera, no code and no depth SDK. videodeviceinTOP -> monochromeTOP -> lumalevelTOP(threshold) -> blurTOP builds a soft PRESENCE MASK (a person's outline), which a matteTOP/multiplyTOP uses to reveal generative_texture_fx content through the silhouette (touch-to-reveal, shadow-play, presence bloom). Two data-only extensions live in variants: a MOTION-ENERGY field (cacheTOP/feedbackTOP holds the previous frame -> differenceTOP -> lumalevel = where movement happened; this REPLACES the absent opticalflowTOP) and the single-blob CENTROID trick (mask x rampTOP -> analyzeTOP average -> toptoCHOP = one moving subject's XY, no tracker). HONEST LIMITS: depth sensors orbbecTOP/orbbecselectTOP/realsenseTOP/kinectazureTOP(+CHOP) are NOW in this catalog -- with the hardware present they give true fg/bg, XYZ, and (Azure) skeletal tracking as a cleaner presence source than a plain camera; opticalflowTOP and the NVIDIA AI-segmentation TOP are still absent; blobtrackTOP's per-blob TABLE is delivered through a Callbacks DAT = code, out of surface; blobtrackCHOP is data-only but needs a point/depth CHOP feed. The plain-camera silhouette/motion MASK below stays the no-hardware data-only CORE. 256px trap is real -- set outputresolution=custom on the camera and every stage.

steps.note: LIVE camera -- the interactive source. HUMAN/HARDWARE BOUNDARY: the user physically mounts and aims the camera, provides lighting (an IR illuminator + IR-pass camera is the field-standard fix for lighting-robust silhouettes), installs the capture driver, and selects the device; you only build the node. Set driver to match the hardware (directshow/mediafoundation for USB webcams, blackmagic/aja for SDI), pick device, active=on. CRITICAL 256px trap: outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h (e.g. 1280/720 for tracking, it need not be 4K). format=mono8fixed if the camera is already IR/greyscale.

key_params.active: on

steps.geometry_out: TOP (live camera image)

verify.pass_if: resolution == custom, image is live (not 256 default, not black)

steps.note: Desaturate to a single luminance channel so the threshold has one clean value to work on. Defaults are correct: rgb=luminance, mono=1. (You can skip this and let lumalevelTOP's source=luminance do it in one node -- kept explicit here for readability.)
steps.geometry_out: TOP (mono image)

verify.pass_if: single-channel luminance, no cook error

steps.note: THRESHOLD the mono image into a hard silhouette -- this is where presence becomes a mask. NOTE: there is NO thresholdTOP in TouchDesigner; lumalevelTOP IS the threshold op. source=luminance, raise `threshold` until only the person (or only the moving foreground) is white, `soften` to feather the cut, `invert` if your subject is darker than the background. blacklevel/gamma1/contrast further shape it. GOTCHA: a fixed threshold is lighting-fragile -- IR lighting (human) is the real fix, not a param.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (silhouette mask, white=presence)

verify.pass_if: person reads as a clean white shape on black
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_silhouette

steps.note: Soften the hard silhouette into a PRESENCE FIELD -- soft edges read better as a reveal/bloom and make a better displacement source than a binary edge. `size` sets the falloff radius. Keep outputresolution=custom to hold delivery res.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (soft presence mask)

verify.pass_if: mask is soft-edged, no hard aliasing

steps.note: REVEAL generative content through the silhouette. Wire your content (e.g. generative_texture_fx OUT_facade_tex) to input0 and OUT_mask to input1; mattechannel=luminance (the mask is mono, so luminance is the matte, NOT the default alpha). switchinputs flips fg/bg. This is the 'touch-to-reveal on a wall' move: content only appears where a person is. ALT: multiplyTOP (content x mask) for a plain gate, or displaceTOP with OUT_mask as the displace map for a push-away-on-presence look (see variants).
steps.geometry_out: TOP (content revealed by presence)

verify.pass_if: content shows only inside the silhouette
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_masked

recipes.classify: camera / webcam / IR camera / depth sensor -> reactive content; make projection respond to people, presence, silhouette, shadow, motion, touch-to-reveal, interactive wall; kinect/orbbec/blob tracking questions land here (with honest limits)
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY CORE: the silhouette mask, the frame-difference motion-energy field, and the single-blob centroid trick are 100% typed TOP/CHOP tools -- no script, no expression, no callbacks. DOMAIN: filed under a new 'interactive' lane (not 'texture') because the defining intent is 'react to a live external sensor', a distinct content-source axis from static texture-FX; this is the vision sibling of audio_reactive_content, and the reactive-source framing (not the TOP plumbing) is what a user searches for. HUMAN/HARDWARE BOUNDARY: mounting/aiming the camera, IR illumination, installing the capture driver, selecting the device, and firing every cook/render are the user's -- data-only means you build the graph, the user runs it. CATALOG UPDATE: depth sensors orbbecTOP/orbbecselectTOP/realsenseTOP/kinectazureTOP/kinectazureCHOP are NOW in the catalog (509-op) -- with the hardware attached they deliver clean fg/bg, true XYZ, and (Azure) multi-person skeletal tracking as a superior presence source; still ABSENT: kinectTOP (v1/v2), opticalflowTOP, and nvidiabackgroundTOP (AI green-screen segmentation) -- say so rather than fake them. There is NO thresholdTOP -- thresholding is lumalevelTOP/levelTOP/monochromeTOP. blobtrackTOP's per-blob TABLE (id/x/y/w/h) is delivered through a Callbacks DAT (Python) = a code boundary, out of surface; the drawn-blob TOP image itself is data-only but not a usable position feed. blobtrackCHOP IS data-only (Kalman centroid/velocity) but its input is a CHOP of POINTS, so without a depth-sensor CHOP there is no data-only camera->points path to feed it -- flagged, not hidden. WIRE-ONLY output.
tips: 256px trap: set outputresolution=custom on videodeviceinTOP AND every downstream stage or the chain silently inherits the 256 default.
Lighting beats parameters: a threshold tuned in daylight fails at night. IR illuminator + IR-pass filter (human hardware) is how field installs stay robust -- do not try to fix it with gamma alone.
matteTOP mattechannel MUST be luminance here (the mask is mono); the default 'alpha' will read an empty alpha and reveal nothing.

Camera adds latency; if you ever composite a delayed key (e.g. a future AI-seg TOP) against the live frame, delay the source with a cacheTOP negative Output Index to re-sync -- the standard fix from the NVIDIA Background TOP docs.
ONE-EXPORTER rule: if the centroid variant drives an instance/geo parameter, only one CHOP may export to that param at a time -- disable any competing exporter first (last cook wins).
variants: MOTION-ENERGY field (replaces the absent opticalflowTOP, data-only): videodeviceinTOP -> monochromeTOP -> cacheTOP (or feedbackTOP with top=self) to hold the PREVIOUS frame -> differenceTOP(current input1, previous input2) -> lumalevelTOP (raise threshold, invert off) -> blurTOP = a mask that is bright only where movement happened. Feed it as an emit mask or as the displaceTOP map so content erupts around moving bodies.

BACKGROUND SUBTRACTION (data-only): capture an empty-scene plate into a cacheTOP once (user pulses it), then differenceTOP(live, plate) -> lumalevel -> a clean presence mask that ignores static set dressing -- more robust than a raw luminance threshold.

SINGLE-BLOB CENTROID as position (data-only, one subject, no tracker): OUT_silhouette x a horizontal rampTOP(u) via multiplyTOP -> analyzeTOP(op=average, analyzechannel=luminance) -> toptoCHOP(crop=pixel, read r) = sum(u*mask); divide by the mask's own analyzeTOP average (mathCHOP) = centroid_x in 0..1; repeat with a vertical ramp for centroid_y. Export that CHOP to a geometryCOMP instance translate or a light position for spotlight-follow.

MULTI-BLOB tracking (partial): blobtrackCHOP gives Kalman-tracked per-blob centroid (outputcentroid=on) + velocity (outputvelocity=on), maxblobs, predicttype=kalman -- fully data-only, BUT it consumes a CHOP of points, so it needs a depth-sensor CHOP or a point source (absent here). blobtrackTOP finds blobs from the camera image but its position TABLE requires a Callbacks DAT = out of surface.
DISPLACE-ON-PRESENCE: use OUT_mask as displaceTOP input1 (horzsource=red, vertsource=green, displaceweightx/y) to push/warp content away from where people stand instead of revealing it.

depth_sensor (hardware present): orbbecTOP/orbbecselectTOP or realsenseTOP give a true DEPTH image (clean fg/bg in any light, real XYZ) and kinectazureTOP + kinectazureCHOP add multi-person SKELETON channels -- a far cleaner presence/mask source than the plain-camera silhouette when the sensor is attached; feed the depth/IR TOP into the same threshold->blur mask chain, or the skeleton CHOP straight into bind_chop. (opticalflowTOP / nvidiabackgroundTOP / kinectTOP are still absent.)

recipes.title: Audio-reactive content GENERATION -- build the generative image FROM the music (FFT + band energy + onset), not just route audio to per-section emit (data-only)
recipes.summary: The generative counterpart to realtime_input_driver: instead of renaming an audio channel onto matNN:emit exports, this GENERATES and warps the content itself from sound. audiodeviceinCHOP/audiofileinCHOP -> audiospectrumCHOP (FFT) forks two ways: (1) a spectrum TEXTURE via choptoTOP that drives displaceTOP / feedback trails / lookupTOP colour; (2) BAND ENERGY -- audiofilterCHOP (low/mid/high) -> analyzeCHOP(rmspower) -> lagCHOP smoothing -> values that scale displacement weight, feedback gain, instance energy. ONSET/KICK is reconstructed from primitives: a band envelope -> logicCHOP(gt threshold) -> triggerCHOP (attack/decay envelope) fires bursts and cuts. This REBUILDS the palette:audioAnalysis Low/Mid/High/Kick/Snare bundle from typed ops (that palette is a .tox COMP, not a catalog operator). Everything is data-only. 256px trap applies to choptoTOP/noiseTOP/displaceTOP; smoothing via lagCHOP/filterCHOP is mandatory or the visuals strobe; normalize because venue levels vary; one-exporter-per-param when an energy channel drives a TOP parameter.

steps.note: LIVE audio in -- the reactive source. HUMAN/HARDWARE BOUNDARY: the user selects the audio interface / input device and handles routing (a loopback/virtual cable to capture the show's playback, or a line/mic in for a live room); receiving audio is data-only, no code. Swap to audiofileinCHOP to react to a fixed track (file param, play). GOTCHA: pick the right device -- the default may be a silent input; verify samples are non-zero before building downstream.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (audio waveform, 1-2 channels)

verify.pass_if: waveform present, values move with sound (not flat zero)

steps.note: FFT -> magnitude spectrum, the analysis core. fftsize 4096-8192 (bigger = finer bins, more latency), outputmenu=setmanually + outlength to fix the bin count you want as a texture, frequencylog>0 to spread the perceptually-important lows across more bins (raw linear bins bunch all the musical energy into the bottom few). This one node feeds BOTH the spectrum-texture branch and, optionally, per-bin analysis.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (N-sample magnitude spectrum)

verify.pass_if: N samples, magnitudes rise/fall with the music

steps.note: BAND SPLIT -- isolate a frequency band from the raw audio (input0 = OUT_audio). filter=lowpass for BASS/kick body, bandpass for MIDS, highpass for HI/sparkle; units=frequency + cutofffrequency (e.g. lowpass ~150Hz, bandpass ~1kHz, highpass ~5kHz), resonance/rolloff shape the skirt. Instantiate THREE (low/mid/high) -- this trio is the data-only rebuild of the audioAnalysis Low/Mid/High bundle (the palette:audioAnalysis is a .tox COMP, NOT a typed op, so it is reconstructed here from primitives).
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (one band-limited waveform)

verify.pass_if: only the target band's energy remains

steps.note: Reduce each band to ONE energy value. function=rmspower gives a perceptual loudness of the band-limited signal (function=maximum for a peakier response). One analyzeCHOP per band = the raw Low/Mid/High scalars. For SNARE, band-limit ~150-250Hz-plus-noise and rms it; for a broadband KICK use the low band. (analyzeCHOP is the honest envelope extractor; the dynamics-processing audiodynamicsCHOP is a compressor/limiter you can insert BEFORE this to even out venue-to-venue level, not an energy follower.)
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (1 sample: band energy)

verify.pass_if: single value tracks that band's loudness

steps.note: SMOOTH the energy -- MANDATORY. Raw band energy is jittery and will strobe the visuals; lag1 (attack) small and lag2 (release) larger gives a snappy-rise / graceful-fall envelope that reads musically. filterCHOP is the alternative. Also normalize here if needed (a mathCHOP range, or divide by a running max) because absolute levels vary by venue -- otherwise the show is too dim or blown out.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (smoothed band energy)

verify.pass_if: value rises fast, falls smooth, no per-frame jitter

steps.note: ONSET GATE step 1 -- turn a band envelope into a clean 0/1 hit. convert=gt with boundmin as the trigger level, so the channel is 1 only while the band is above threshold. This + the triggerCHOP below is the data-only rebuild of the audioAnalysis Kick/Snare detectors. IMPORTANT: beatCHOP is a TEMPO CLOCK (it emits ramps/pulses at a set or tapped BPM), NOT an onset/transient detector -- for content that fires on the actual kick you MUST build envelope->logic->trigger, not reach for beatCHOP.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (0/1 gate on the hit)

verify.pass_if: channel pulses to 1 on each kick, 0 between

steps.note: ONSET GATE step 2 -- shape each 0/1 hit into a musical envelope for bursts/flashes/cuts. threshup fires on the gate rising, then attack/peak/decay/sustain/release draw the pulse; retrigger sets a minimum re-fire gap so one kick = one burst. Drive a particle emission, a feedback flash, or a scene cut from OUT_kick.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (attack/decay burst envelope)

verify.pass_if: clean envelope per kick, no double-fires

steps.note: Turn the SPECTRUM into a TEXTURE -- the generative seed. chop=OUT_spectrum, dataformat=r (or rgb to pack three bands), layout=square (wrap N bins into a 2D tile) or rowscropped (a 1D strip). CRITICAL 256px trap: outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h so the texture is delivery-scaled, not 256. This live spectrum image is what you displace and colour by.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (live spectrum texture)

verify.pass_if: texture ripples with the spectrum, res == custom
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_spectex

steps.note: GENERATE the reactive image -- warp a content field by the spectrum/energy. Wire your base (a noiseTOP or generative_texture_fx output) to input0 and OUT_spectex to input1; horzsource=red, vertsource=green pick the displace channels, displaceweightx/y set the push. To make BASS pump the warp, export OUT_smooth_low to displaceweightx via a nullCHOP apply-block (exportmethod=autoname/datname + export flag) -- ONE-EXPORTER rule: only one CHOP may drive that param, disable competitors first. extend=mirror avoids edge tearing.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (audio-warped content)

verify.pass_if: image warps in time with the bass
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_displaced

glsl_opportunity.why: bespoke audio-reactive fields the fixed displace/feedback chain cannot express -- per-pixel spectral bars mapped to a facade, radial FFT rings, domain-warped noise whose frequency is band energy, reaction-diffusion pumped by the kick. A glslTOP reading the spectrum texture + energy uniforms is the real tool for signature content.
glsl_opportunity.propose_via: glsl_reference topic=patterns (also topic=environment for the glslTOP contract, topic=functions)
glsl_opportunity.consent: run via set_glsl ONLY if the user enabled allow_glsl (explicit consent); otherwise PROPOSE the GLSL text via glsl_reference for the user to paste into a Text DAT wired to the glslTOP's pixeldat, and EXPLAIN what it does and why (a teaching moment, not just an action).

steps.note: ENERGY-DRIVEN TRAILS -- the generative_texture_fx feedback spine, now audio-driven. Point top at the loop's compositeTOP output and cycle OUT_displaced back through a transformTOP (scale/rotate) + levelTOP (opacity<1 to fade); export a smoothed band energy to the transform scale or level opacity so trails bloom and swirl on the music. resetpulse clears the buffer. Keep resolution custom throughout the loop.

key_params.(loop): transformTOP scale/rotate + levelTOP opacity<1, driven by energy

steps.geometry_out: TOP (reactive feedback trails)

verify.pass_if: trails build on loud passages, fade in quiet ones

steps.note: Blend the layers -- spectrum texture, displaced field, trails, and a lookupTOP-coloured pass (map a rampTOP/palette by band energy for on-beat colour shifts) into one image. operand=add/screen for energy, over for stacked layers.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (composited reactive content)

verify.pass_if: layers read as one coherent audio-reactive image

steps.note: WIRE-ONLY hand-off tap. Plant OUT_audio_content as the stable name the projection/output lane reads; the USER fires the cook/render. This is the generative sibling of realtime_input_driver's export block -- here the audio BUILDS the image rather than just setting emit brightness.
steps.geometry_out: TOP (final audio-reactive content)

verify.pass_if: resolution == delivery, cooks clean

recipes.classify: audio / sound / music -> GENERATE reactive content; audio-reactive visuals, FFT/spectrum, bass/kick/snare/beat-driven, band energy to displacement/feedback/colour/instancing; deeper than routing audio to per-section emit (that is realtime_input_driver)
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY CORE: the entire lane -- FFT, band split, energy analysis, smoothing, onset gate, spectrum-to-texture, displacement, feedback, colour lookup, and reactive instancing -- is built from typed CHOP/TOP tools; no script, no expression, no callbacks. DOMAIN: filed under the new 'interactive' lane alongside vision_interactive_mask because the intent is 'react to a live external source', a distinct content-source axis from static generative_texture_fx and from realtime_input_driver (which only ROUTES an audio channel onto matNN:emit exports; this recipe GENERATES the content). HUMAN/HARDWARE BOUNDARY: choosing the audio interface, routing a loopback/virtual-cable to capture show playback, tapping BPM if beatCHOP is used for sequencing, and firing every cook/render are the user's. HONEST LIMITS: palette:audioAnalysis (Low/Mid/High/Kick/Snare/Rhythm/Spectral-Centroid) is a .tox COMP, NOT a catalog operator -- this recipe REBUILDS that bundle from primitives (audiofilter x3 -> analyzeCHOP rmspower -> lagCHOP; logicCHOP -> triggerCHOP for kick/snare). beatCHOP is a TEMPO CLOCK, not an onset detector -- there is no FFT auto-tempo/transient op in the catalog, so onset is the envelope->logic->trigger build. 256px trap on choptoTOP/noiseTOP/displaceTOP. Smoothing (lagCHOP/filterCHOP) is not optional -- unsmoothed energy strobes. ONE-EXPORTER-per-param: when an energy channel drives a TOP parameter via a nullCHOP export block, disable any competing exporter (e.g. realtime_input_driver's emit rig) first or the last cook wins. WIRE-ONLY output.
tips: frequencylog on audiospectrumCHOP is the difference between a useful spectrum and one where all the musical energy is jammed into the bottom 5 bins -- raise it.
Smooth BEFORE you drive anything: an unsmoothed rms value at 60fps looks like a seizure on a 4K wall. lag1 fast / lag2 slow is the musical default.
Normalize for the venue: divide band energy by a slow running max (mathCHOP) so the same patch works at soundcheck volume and at peak -- absolute dB varies wildly.
beatCHOP is NOT onset detection -- it is a clock. Use it to SEQUENCE on-beat events (it needs a BPM/tap), and use envelope->logicCHOP->triggerCHOP to fire on the actual transient.

ONE-EXPORTER rule: audio energy and a baked sweep cannot both export to the same matNN/param -- swapping which nullCHOP has its export flag on is how you switch the show between 'baked' and 'audio-reactive'.
audiodynamicsCHOP (compressor) BEFORE the analysis tames loud/quiet swings so your thresholds stay valid across a set -- optional but pro.
variants: REACTIVE INSTANCING: feed OUT_spectrum (or the per-band energy CHOP) into a geometryCOMP instance setup -- per-instance scale/tx/colour from the CHOP channels via the instance page, so a wall of instanced shapes pulses per frequency bin (an audio-reactive facade of bars/particles), fully data-only param wiring.
COLOUR BY BAND: energy CHOP -> a rampTOP phase or lookupTOP index so the palette shifts on the beat; composite over the displaced field.
3-BAND PACK: pack low/mid/high energies into R/G/B of a single choptoTOP (dataformat=rgb) to make one texture that carries all three bands for a shader or displace map.

audiobandeqCHOP alternative: instead of three audiofilterCHOPs, a single audiobandeqCHOP gives multiple graphic-EQ bands in one node -- analyze each band's output. Cleaner node count, same data-only result.
FILE-DRIVEN rehearsal: swap audiodeviceinCHOP for audiofileinCHOP to design the whole reactive look against a known track before the live input exists.

recipes.title: Dynamic projection mapping onto a MOVING prop/performer (tracking CHOP -> select/oneeuro-filter -> bind onto a digital-twin geometryCOMP -> renderTOP from the FIXED projector camera -> OUT_aligned) -- content that sticks to a moving surface
recipes.summary: Project mapped content onto something that MOVES -- a dancer, a handheld object, a rolling set piece, a spinning prop -- instead of a static facade. The technique is 'move the digital twin, keep the projector camera fixed': a live tracking receiver CHOP (blacktraxCHOP / posistagenetCHOP / optitrackinCHOP) reports the real object's position (and orientation) each frame; a selectCHOP picks the one tracked rigid-body/beacon's channels; a filterCHOP in oneeuro mode de-jitters them; and those smoothed channels DRIVE the transform of a geometryCOMP that holds a matched DIGITAL TWIN of the prop -- all code-free, via bind_chop / the CHOP Export flag (never an expression). A renderTOP then renders that moving, content-textured twin from a cameraCOMP whose numeric pose + lens are matched to the REAL projector (reuse camera_match_facade). Because the twin tracks the real object and the camera equals the real projector, the rendered frame -- when projected -- lands the content on the object as it moves. KEY GOTCHA: the tracking system reports in ITS OWN coordinate frame (its origin, its units mm-vs-m, its handedness/up-axis); the twin will fly off unless that tracking-to-world REGISTRATION (scale + axis swap + offset) is reconciled -- done numerically in the geometryCOMP pre-transform (pxform on, ptx/pt.., pr.., pscale) or by renaming axis channels on the selectCHOP, both data-only, with the measured numbers coming from on-site calibration. DATA-ONLY: every drive is a CHOP channel bound onto a parameter via the Export flag; no callbacks, no expressions, no code. HUMAN/HARDWARE: the physical tracker rig, marker/beacon placement + calibration, and the projector-to-tracking-space registration are on-site measured-by-a-person steps -- the MCP builds the entire tracking->twin->render network and sets every numeric offset.

steps.note: LIVE TRACKING INPUT (pick the receiver that matches the on-site system; this step shows blacktraxCHOP, swap for posistagenetCHOP or optitrackinCHOP). blacktraxCHOP receives BlackTrax RTTrPM over UDP: set port (default 24002) + protocol (msging / multicastmsging) + netaddress to match the tracking server, centroid=on for per-trackable position, and velocity/acceleration off unless needed; a mappingtable DAT renames beacons to friendly channels. posistagenetCHOP (PSN) has pos=on + ori=on for position + orientation per tracked object (port 56565); optitrackinCHOP (NatNet/Motive) has rigidbodies=on giving tx/ty/tz + a quaternion per rigid body (dataport 1511, commandport 1510). active is default ON (this is an INPUT receiver, not a wire-only OUTPUT -- leaving it on is correct). CHANNEL NAMES VARY by tracker + config, so DO NOT guess them: after create, inspect the node to read the exact channel names, then select by those in the next step. This receiver is the whole spine -- the real object's live pose enters here.

key_params.port: 24002 (match the BlackTrax server; PSN 56565; OptiTrack dataport 1511)
key_params.netaddress: the tracking server / multicast group address
key_params.centroid: on (per-trackable position; PSN pos=on+ori=on; OptiTrack rigidbodies=on)
key_params.active: on (live receiver -- an INPUT, not a wire-only output)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP: live per-trackable position (+orientation) channels from the tracking server

verify.pass_if: live channels present and updating when a tracked object moves (channel names read off here, not guessed)

steps.note: PICK THE ONE TRACKED BODY. The receiver may carry many beacons/rigid-bodies; selectCHOP.channames (a space/pattern list of the exact names you read off OUT_trackraw) narrows to the single prop/performer you are mapping, and renamefrom/renameto normalizes them to clean tx ty tz (rx ry rz for orientation) so downstream nodes and the bind are tidy. This rename is ALSO the code-free AXIS-SWAP lever: if the tracker is Z-up and TD is Y-up, rename the incoming z channel to ty and y to tz here (a handedness flip may also need a sign, handled numerically in the pre-transform later). Keep it to the channels you will actually drive -- fewer channels = cleaner bind.

key_params.channames: the exact tracked-body channel names read off OUT_trackraw (e.g. 'prop1/pos/*' or 'RigidBody03:*')
key_params.renameto: tx ty tz rx ry rz (also usable to swap axes, e.g. z->ty for Z-up trackers)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP: just the chosen body's position/orientation, renamed tx/ty/tz (rx/ry/rz)

verify.pass_if: only the target body's channels remain, named tx/ty/tz(/rx/ry/rz)

steps.note: DE-JITTER THE TRACKING (the make-or-break step). Raw tracker data has high-frequency jitter that reads as the projected content 'buzzing' on the surface; naive heavy smoothing kills jitter but adds lag so fast moves smear off the object. filterCHOP type=oneeuro is the tracking-industry 1-Euro adaptive low-pass: cutoff sets the baseline smoothing (LOW when the object is still = no jitter), speedcoeff raises the cutoff as the object speeds up (= low lag when moving fast), slopecutoff smooths the derivative. Tune cutoff down / speedcoeff up until still-jitter is gone without visible lag on quick moves. A nullCHOP at the end gives a stable named tap to bind FROM. (Alternative: a lagCHOP -- constant lag1/lag2 in seconds, overshoot for a spring feel -- when you want fixed, predictable smoothing rather than adaptive.)
steps.geometry_out: CHOP: smooth, low-lag tx/ty/tz(/rx/ry/rz) ready to drive a transform

verify.pass_if: channels are smooth when the object is still yet track quick moves without obvious lag
verify.milestone_check: inspect @OUT_smoothed while jiggling then quickly moving the tracked object -- still = no buzz, fast = keeps up

steps.note: THE DIGITAL TWIN = a matched mesh of the real moving prop, textured with the CONTENT, that the projector camera will render. Build the twin SOP inside: for a real object use import_scan / a fileinSOP of the prop's mesh (must live UNDER the working dir, absolute forward-slash path -- external paths are blanked by path confinement); a boxSOP (texture=boxinside for UVs) is a fast stand-in for a box-like prop. CRITICAL: a fresh geometryCOMP renders its own default torus1, NOT your SOP -- delete the torus and set_flags render=true (display=true) on the REAL twin SOP or you will map onto a doughnut. Texture it with a constantMAT (UNLIT -- we are pasting content, not relighting) whose colormap is the content moviefileinTOP, and set the geo's material param to it. THE REGISTRATION LIVES HERE: turn pxform=on and set the pre-transform (ptx/pty/ptz, prx/pry/prz, pscale) to the numeric tracking-to-world offset + unit-scale + axis alignment (from on-site cal) so the tracked position lands the twin where the real object is. The LIVE pose goes on the MAIN transform (next step) -- pre-transform = static registration, main transform = live tracking.

key_params.pscale: unit scale (e.g. 0.001 if tracker is mm and TD is m)

steps.geometry_out: COMP: content-textured twin of the prop, registration baked into its pre-transform

verify.pass_if: the real twin SOP has the render flag (default torus deleted), material=constantMAT, pxform on with registration values

expr_opportunity.why: a tracker whose handedness/up-axis differs from TD (Z-up + left-handed, say) sometimes wants a small basis-change matrix on the incoming pose rather than per-axis numeric juggling
expr_opportunity.propose_via: expr_reference then set_expr on the pre-transform / a matrix parameter
expr_opportunity.consent: needs allow_expr (default OFF); DATA-ONLY fallback = swap axis channels by rename on the selectCHOP (step 2) + numeric ptx/pr../pscale on this geo's pre-transform -- no expression required

steps.note: DRIVE THE TWIN FROM THE TRACKER -- code-free. bind_chop wires the smoothed CHOP channels onto the twin's MAIN transform parameters via TouchDesigner's Export flag (Channel Name is Path:Parameter autoname) -- a DATA binding, never an expression. Bind OUT_smoothed tx->OUT_twin.tx, ty->ty, tz->tz (and rx/ry/rz if you tracked orientation). Now as the real object moves, its live pose flows tracker -> select -> oneeuro -> bind -> twin transform, and the twin moves with it (registration from the pre-transform keeps it aligned). ONE exporter per parameter -- do not double-bind a param. (Full-6DOF variant: feed a single matrix/quaternion CHOP into the twin's xformmatrixop param instead of six scalar binds -- best for OptiTrack quaternions; see variants.)

key_params.chop: OUT_smoothed (a nullCHOP tap at the chain end)
key_params.par: tx/ty/tz (repeat per channel; add rx/ry/rz for orientation)

steps.geometry_out: COMP: the twin now MOVES live with the tracked object (Export-driven, no code)

verify.pass_if: tx/ty/tz are Export-driven; moving the tracked object moves the twin
verify.milestone_check: read_network @OUT_twin pars=true -- transform params show Export mode and follow OUT_smoothed

steps.note: REPROJECT: render the moving, content-textured twin from the FIXED projector camera. camera = a cameraCOMP whose translate/rotate + lens (viewanglemethod/fov or focalaperture, near/far) are numerically matched to the REAL projector's position and optics (this is exactly camera_match_facade / projection_align_and_output -- reuse it, do not re-derive). geometry = OUT_twin, lights left default (constantMAT is unlit so lighting is irrelevant). bgcolora=0 so everything outside the prop silhouette is transparent (clean over black / clean handoff). 256px TRAP: renderTOP resolution defaults to 256 -- force outputresolution=custom and resolution to the PROJECTOR resolution or the map is a 256x256 postage stamp. Because the twin follows the real object and the camera equals the real projector, this rendered frame IS the map that makes the content stick to the moving surface. (White-on-transparent content can look blank over a white preview -- judge over black.)
steps.geometry_out: TOP: content reprojected onto the moving twin as the real projector sees it

verify.pass_if: content lands on the twin's silhouette and that silhouette moves as the tracked object moves; rest transparent
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_reproj at two tracked positions -- the lit region tracks the object's moving silhouette

steps.note: STABLE ALIGNED TAP. Every downstream output op targets this NAME so the projector output can be swapped without rewiring. Wire OUT_reproj -> this. Hand off WIRE-ONLY to output_handoff / projection_align_and_output (windowCOMP to the projector, or ndioutTOP / syphonspoutoutTOP to a media server) -- all terminal ops stay unactuated: windowCOMP not opened, moviefileoutTOP.record OFF, ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active DEFAULT ON so you MUST set them OFF. A global cornerpinTOP keystone can sit AFTER this null to fine-correct the whole projected frame at once.
steps.geometry_out: TOP: final tracked-surface map at projector res, ready for wire-only output

verify.pass_if: projector-res frame; content tracks the moving object
verify.milestone_check: OUT_aligned holds the deliverable frame the projector shows onto the moving surface

steps.note: REUSE the projector camera. The renderTOP above needs a cameraCOMP whose numeric pose (tx/ty/tz, rx/ry/rz) and lens (fov / focal+aperture, near/far, winx/winy lens-shift) equal the REAL projector -- that calibration IS camera_match_facade / projection_align_and_output. Do NOT rebuild it; build that camera once and point this recipe's renderTOP.camera at it. The tracked-surface network is that camera plus the moving twin: fixed projector camera + live-driven twin = dynamic map.

key_params.reuse: camera_match_facade cameraCOMP as renderTOP.camera (fixed projector pose + lens)

steps.geometry_out: (the fixed projector-matched camera the reprojection renders from)

verify.pass_if: camera pose + lens match the real projector; renderTOP.camera points at it

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: tracker rig, marker/beacon calibration, and projector-to-tracking registration)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === What a PERSON must do ON SITE: (1) rig and calibrate the physical tracking system -- mount the BlackTrax/PSN/OptiTrack cameras or bases, place the beacons/markers on the real prop or performer, and run the tracker's own wand/marker calibration so it reports accurate poses (the MCP cannot see the room or the markers); (2) measure/verify the tracking-to-world REGISTRATION -- physically relate the tracker's origin/units/up-axis to the projector's world so the twin sits ON the real object; (3) physically aim + focus the projector and confirm its numeric camera match (camera_match_facade). WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds the entire tracker-receiver -> select -> oneeuro -> bind -> twin -> render -> null network and sets every numeric value -- the registration pre-transform (ptx/pt.., pr.., pscale), the filter tuning, the projector camera pose. The human's MEASURED registration numbers are typed back via set_par on OUT_twin's pre-transform components (ptx/pty/ptz, prx/pry/prz, pscale) and any axis rename on OUT_bodysel. Live rehearsal (walk the prop through its range, watch the projected content stick) is the on-site tuning loop; the MCP re-sets the numbers it is told.

key_params.set_par (after human measures): op=OUT_twin, pars={pxform:'on', ptx:<meas>, pty:<meas>, ptz:<meas>, prx:<meas>, pry:<meas>, prz:<meas>, pscale:<meas>}

steps.geometry_out: content locked to the real moving object once the physical rig + registration are calibrated

verify.pass_if: pre-transform holds on-site registration values (or a first estimate for authoring)

recipes.classify: project mapped content onto a MOVING object -- a dancer, performer, handheld prop, rolling or spinning set piece, moving scenery, an actor's costume; dynamic / real-time projection mapping; tracked-surface projection; make content STICK to a moving surface; BlackTrax / RTTrPM / PosiStageNet / PSN / OptiTrack / NatNet / Motive driven projection; motion-tracked projection, camera-matched reprojection onto a live-tracked digital twin; moving-target mapping, follow-spot content
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the entire dynamic-mapping network -- the live tracking receiver (blacktraxCHOP / posistagenetCHOP / optitrackinCHOP), the selectCHOP body-pick + axis rename, the filterCHOP oneeuro de-jitter (or lagCHOP), the nullCHOP tap, the geometryCOMP digital twin with its content constantMAT and registration pre-transform, the bind_chop drive of the twin transform via the Export flag, the projector-matched cameraCOMP, the renderTOP reprojection, and the aligned nullTOP -- is created, wired, and parameterized by the bridge. Every drive is a CHOP CHANNEL bound onto a parameter (Export flag / bind_chop): NO callbacks DAT, NO parameter expressions, NO script/execute/cplusplus anywhere. The tracker's active receiver is an INPUT (correctly left on), not a wire-only output. (2) HUMAN / ON-SITE / HARDWARE: the physical tracking rig + its own marker/wand calibration, the beacon/marker placement on the real prop or performer, the tracking-to-world REGISTRATION measurement, and the physical projector aim/focus are measured-by-a-person steps the MCP cannot emit; their numbers are typed back via set_par on the twin's pre-transform. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: nothing here is actuated -- hand off via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output with windowCOMP unopened, moviefileoutTOP.record OFF, ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active set OFF (they DEFAULT ON). HONEST CATALOG GAPS: there is NO dedicated 'dynamic mapping' / camera-tracker / registration-solver operator -- this recipe assembles the standard technique from real primitives; the tracker receivers exist (verified) -- beacon/rigid-body trackers blacktraxCHOP/posistagenetCHOP/optitrackinCHOP AND camera-pose trackers freedinCHOP(FreeD)/stypeinCHOP(Stype)/mosysCHOP(Mo-Sys)/ncamCHOP(Ncam) for the moving-projector / virtual-production reprojection variant -- but their channel NAMES depend on the tracker config + mapping table, so names are read live off OUT_trackraw, never hard-coded. Quaternion->euler and tracker-handedness basis changes have no dedicated code-free converter beyond feeding a matrix/quaternion CHOP into xformmatrixop or renaming/sign-flipping axis channels -- an exact arbitrary basis change is surfaced as an expr_opportunity (default OFF), not baked in. NC build renders cap at 1280; swap resolutionw/h for 4K, topology identical.
tips: Read channel names LIVE, never guess: inspect @OUT_trackraw and select by the exact names -- BlackTrax/PSN/OptiTrack name channels by beacon/rigid-body + a mapping table, and they differ per install.

oneeuro is the right de-jitter: filterCHOP type=oneeuro gives low jitter when the object is still AND low lag when it moves fast -- tune cutoff down / speedcoeff up. A plain lagCHOP trades one for the other.
