Registration is a pre-transform, tracking is the main transform: put the static tracking-to-world offset/scale/axis in the geo pre-transform (pxform on, ptx/pr../pscale); bind the LIVE pose onto tx/ty/tz -- keep the two separate or you cannot re-calibrate without breaking the drive.
Unit scale bites first: BlackTrax/OptiTrack often report millimetres while TD world is metres -- if the twin flies far off-screen, set pscale ~0.001 before anything else.
Delete the default torus: a fresh geometryCOMP renders torus1, not your twin -- delete it and set_flags render=true on the real twin SOP, or you map onto a doughnut.

Match the projector camera FIRST (camera_match_facade): if the cameraCOMP pose/lens is wrong the content will never sit right no matter how good the tracking -- calibrate the fixed camera, then add the moving twin.
bgcolora=0 on the renderTOP and force outputresolution=custom at projector res -- transparent outside the silhouette for a clean handoff, and dodge the 256px stamp.
HELPER CANDIDATE: track_prop(tracker='blacktrax'|'psn'|'optitrack', body, twin_sop, projector_cam, res) -> receiver + select + oneeuro + null + twin geo + bind + renderTOP + null, wired in one call.
variants: full_6dof_matrix: instead of six scalar binds, feed a single matrix (or quaternion) CHOP into the twin's xformmatrixop param -- best for OptiTrack rigid bodies that report a quaternion; the whole pose drives in one op with no euler conversion.
position_only: track only translation (bind tx/ty/tz, skip rotation) for a prop that stays upright -- fewer channels, rock-solid, good for a rolling cart or a lifted panel.

moving_projector (handheld / robotic): keep the object's twin FIXED and instead drive the cameraCOMP's transform from the tracker (bind onto the camera, or its xformmatrixop) -- for a projector on a moving yoke/robot/handheld rig tracking a static surface.

lag_smoothing: swap the oneeuro filterCHOP for a lagCHOP (lag1/lag2 seconds, overshoot for spring) when you want fixed, predictable smoothing or a deliberate trailing feel rather than adaptive tracking.

registration_by_objectCHOP: compute the tracking-to-world offset with an objectCHOP (compute=mat, reference=a placed origin null, target=the tracker-origin null) to derive the pre-transform matrix numerically instead of hand-typing ptx/pr.., then feed it to xformmatrixop.

multi_prop: duplicate the select -> oneeuro -> twin -> bind chain per tracked body and render all twins through the ONE projector camera into a single renderTOP -- several moving objects mapped from one projector.

camera_tracked (virtual production): for a TRACKED CAMERA/PROJECTOR rig, freedinCHOP (FreeD), stypeinCHOP (Stype), mosysCHOP (Mo-Sys StarTracker) or ncamCHOP (Ncam) report live camera pose (+lens for ncam) -- bind those channels onto the projector cameraCOMP (or its xformmatrixop) instead of the twin, exactly like the moving_projector variant; the channel names are read live off OUT_trackraw as with the beacon trackers.

recipes.title: Data-only titling / lower-thirds / credits / countdown content (textTOP text+font+fontsizex/y+align+fontcolor -> transformTOP/levelTOP animated by lfoCHOP/keyframeCHOP EXPORT -> compositeTOP over content; geotextCOMP or textSOP+extrudeSOP -> renderTOP for 3D titles) -- the operator-native title generator
recipes.summary: Make TYPOGRAPHY content -- show titles, name/lower-third supers, rolling credits, a live clock or a countdown-to-start, and data-driven readouts -- entirely data-only. The 2D spine is a textTOP: set text/font/typeface/fontsizex+fontsizey/alignx+aligny/fontcolor(r/g/b)+fontalpha, bgalpha 0 so the type is transparent-backed for compositing, outputresolution=custom at canvas res. For a STATIC super you type the string into the textTOP 'text' param. For a LIVE counter/clock/countdown there is a code-free path (NO parameter expression): a timerCHOP (or clockCHOP) emits the value, a choptoDAT turns that CHOP value into a DAT cell, and the textTOP reads it via its dat/rowindex/colindex source (or via the textTOP 'chop' input with chopvaluereplace on for %-token substitution, plus the built-in valuetouse/totaldigits/decimaldigits/posttext numeric formatter) -- so the digits update every frame with zero script. Motion (slide-in, hold, slide-out, opacity fade, credit scroll) is code-free too: an lfoCHOP or keyframeCHOP is EXPORTED (set_flags export=true, exportmethod=autoname) onto a transformTOP's tx/ty and a levelTOP's opacity that the title passes through. A compositeTOP (operand=over) lays the title -- optionally on a constantTOP/rectangleTOP lower-third bar -- over the underlying content, and a nullTOP(OUT_titleout) is the stable hand-off. 3D EXTRUDED titles use geotextCOMP (a renderable 3D-text object; set mode=text, text, font, fontsize, fontcolor, assign a constantMAT) OR textSOP(extrude=on, extrudedepth) / textSOP+extrudeSOP(depthscale) inside a geometryCOMP, rendered through an orthographic cameraCOMP + renderTOP to a TOP that re-enters the same transform/composite chain. KEY GOTCHA: textTOP uses fontsizex AND fontsizey (two params, keepfontratio on to lock them) -- not a single 'fontsize'; and bgalpha defaults 0 (good) but fontcolor defaults white, so white type over a white preview page reads as blank -- composite over the actual dark content or a bar to see it. ROUTING NOTE: 'typography' historically mis-routed to generative_texture_fx (which owns no text operator); this recipe is the real text lane -- its routing row claims typography/titles/text/lower-third/credits/countdown so the router re-points here.

steps.note: THE 2D TITLE SPINE. Create the textTOP and set the copy + look: text (the string, e.g. a show title or a name super), font + typeface (Regular/Bold/Italic/Bold Italic) or a fontfile path under the working dir for a licensed brand face, fontsizex AND fontsizey (TWO params -- keepfontratio=on ties them so you size once; fontsizexunit=points or pixels), alignx (left/center/right) + aligny (top/center/bottom) for lower-third vs centred-title placement, fontcolor(r/g/b) + fontalpha for the type colour, bgalpha=0 so the background stays transparent for clean over-compositing (bgcolor only matters if you want a solid card). outputresolution=custom at the delivery/canvas res (256px trap: leave it default and the title renders 256x256 and pixelates when scaled up). For a STATIC super, the 'text' param IS the content and you are done here; for a LIVE counter leave 'text' to be driven by the dat/chop path built in steps 2-3.

key_params.fontcolorr: 1.0 (raw comps via set_par; fontcolor=[r,g,b] on create)

steps.geometry_out: white-on-transparent (or coloured) title image at canvas res

verify.pass_if: the typed string renders sharp at the set size/colour with a transparent background
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_title -- the title reads correctly (composite over dark content if white type looks blank over a white page)

steps.note: LIVE COUNTDOWN / CLOCK DRIVER (skip for a purely static title). A timerCHOP is the data-only source of a changing number: for a COUNTDOWN-TO-START set length = the countdown seconds, play=on, cycle=off -- it counts down and emits a running fraction plus running/done flags (the 'seconds remaining' / fraction channels the choptoDAT will read next). Start/reset it with the allowlisted parameterless `pulse` (start / cuepulse) -- never an expression. For a WALL CLOCK / time-of-day super use a clockCHOP instead (hour/minute/second channels). This CHOP is only the value; it never touches the textTOP directly (that would need an expression) -- the choptoDAT in the next step is the code-free bridge.

key_params.outseg: off (single countdown; on only for multi-segment)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (countdown fraction / seconds-remaining, running, done)

verify.pass_if: a channel advances/decrements when play=on; pulse start restarts it

steps.note: CODE-FREE LIVE-TEXT BRIDGE (the data-only alternative to a parameter expression). Set its 'chop' to OUT_countclock (or a mathCHOP that has already converted the raw value to whole seconds / MM:SS); output=colperchan, names off. The choptoDAT writes the current CHOP value into a DAT cell; point the textTOP's dat parameter at THIS DAT with rowindex/colindex on the cell so the title string becomes the live number -- updating every cook with no script. ALTERNATIVE inline path: skip the DAT and wire OUT_countclock straight into the textTOP's 'chop' input with chopvaluereplace=on, putting a %-token in the textTOP 'text' and using the built-in numeric formatter (valuetouse/appendvalue/totaldigits/decimaldigits/leadingzero/posttext) for zero-padded 'MM:SS' style digits. Either way the counter is pure data flow. For a folder-of-slides CREDIT source, use a folderDAT (rootfolder under the working dir, type=files, namecol on) as the row source instead of a timer.

key_params.(textTOP side): SET textTOP.text='' FIRST (the textTOP 'text' param DEFAULTS to the placeholder 'derivative', which otherwise PREPENDS the live cell value), then dat=<this DAT>, rowindex/colindex on the cell -- OR textTOP.chop + chopvaluereplace=on with a %-token in 'text'

steps.geometry_out: DAT cell holding the live value -> textTOP text source

verify.pass_if: the DAT cell shows the current number and the textTOP updates as the timer runs

steps.note: PLACE + ANIMATE THE TITLE ON THE CANVAS. Pass OUT_title through a transformTOP to position it (tx/ty, tunit=fraction so 0..1 of the canvas), scale it (sx/sy), or SCROLL it (animate ty upward for a credit roll). This node is the animation TARGET whose tx/ty the exporter drives in the next step (a slide-in from off-canvas, a settle, a scroll). Keep outputresolution=custom at canvas res; extend=zero + bgcolor alpha 0 so off-canvas is transparent. For a lower-third that sits bottom-left, set tx/ty to park it there and let only opacity animate.
steps.geometry_out: title placed/animated on a transparent canvas-res frame

verify.pass_if: the title sits where tx/ty put it, transparent elsewhere

steps.note: CODE-FREE ANIMATOR (the data-only motion path). Build an lfoCHOP (wavetype=ramp for a one-way slide/scroll, sin for a gentle pulse, tri for in-out; frequency = 1/duration, amp/bias to hit the start+end values) and EXPORT it onto the title's animated params: set_flags export=true with exportmethod=autoname (autoexportroot pointing at the transformTOP) so the LFO channel drives transformTOP.tx (slide/scroll) and a levelTOP.opacity (fade in/out). Build a levelTOP after the transform (opacity 0..1, brightness1) as the fade node and export onto its opacity too. ONE exporter per parameter -- disable any other driver on that param first. For an AUTHORED slide-in/hold/slide-out with precise timing, use a keyframeCHOP instead (it reads an animationCOMP's keyed channels; same autoname export) -- lfoCHOP for cyclic/looping motion, keyframeCHOP for a scripted cue-timed move.

key_params.(export): set_flags export=true onto transformTOP.tx and levelTOP.opacity (one exporter per param)
key_params.(levelTOP): opacity 0..1 fade node after the transform

steps.geometry_out: CHOP animation exported onto the title's transform + opacity (data-only)

verify.pass_if: tx (and the levelTOP opacity) show Export-driven values that change over time

expr_opportunity.why: an ease-curve slide (cubic/elastic) or a data-bound counter formatted with arithmetic (e.g. remaining = ceil(length - elapsed) as MM:SS) is most concisely a parameter expression
expr_opportunity.consent: needs allow_expr (default OFF); data-only fallback = an lfoCHOP/keyframeCHOP shaped ramp for easing, and a mathCHOP + choptoDAT for the formatted counter (this recipe uses the fallback)

steps.note: LAY THE TITLE OVER CONTENT (+ optional lower-third bar). operand=over, swaporder=on -- compositeTOP's over draws INPUT 0 ON TOP, so swaporder=on makes input 0 the BOTTOM layer and the LAST input the top, matching the draw order described here (verified live: an opaque bg on input 0 without swaporder hides everything above). tops multi-input: wire the UNDERLYING content first (a moviefileinTOP / a generative_texture_fx tap / a black constantTOP), then -- for a lower-third -- a constantTOP or rectangleTOP BAR (a dimmed rounded/soft strip via rectangleTOP softness), then OUT_titlefade (the animated title) on top. outputresolution=custom at canvas res. Because the title's bgalpha is 0 it drops cleanly onto the content; the bar gives legibility over busy footage. For a full-frame CREDIT ROLL there is no bar -- just the scrolling title over black or content. This is where 'white type looks blank' resolves: over real content the super is finally visible.

key_params.swaporder: on (input 0 = BOTTOM layer; without it compositeTOP over draws input 0 on TOP)
key_params.tops: content, [lower-third bar], OUT_titlefade (draw order; title last/on top)

steps.geometry_out: title/lower-third/credits composited over the content

verify.pass_if: the title reads clearly over the content, on its bar if used
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_titlecomp -- the legible super/lower-third/credit sits correctly over the underlying content

steps.note: 3D EXTRUDED TITLE (optional alternate spine for depth/bevel/lighting). geotextCOMP is a renderable 3D-text OBJECT: set mode=text, text=the string, font, fontsize (single float here, unlike textTOP's X/Y), fontcolor(r/g/b)+fontalpha, transform t/r/s to orient it, assign a material (a constantMAT color for flat 3D, or a lit MAT), render=on. Point a renderTOP at it (camera=an orthographic or perspective cameraCOMP, geometry=the geotextCOMP, lights=* or a lightCOMP), outputresolution=custom at canvas res, bgcolor alpha 0. The renderTOP image re-enters the SAME transformTOP/levelTOP/compositeTOP chain above. HEAVIER SOP VARIANT: a textSOP (extrude=on + extrudedepth, output=triangles) OR textSOP -> extrudeSOP (depthscale for depth, thickscale) inside a geometryCOMP (assign constantMAT, render=on, delete the COMP's default torus + set_flags render/display on the real SOP) -- use this when you need true bevels/side-face control the geotextCOMP does not expose.

key_params.(renderTOP): camera=ortho cameraCOMP, geometry=this geotextCOMP, lights=*, outputresolution=custom, bgcolor alpha 0

steps.geometry_out: 3D extruded title rendered to a canvas-res TOP

verify.pass_if: the 3D/extruded title renders (not the geometryCOMP default torus) with depth/lighting
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_title3d -- extruded type appears; if blank, the cameraCOMP framing or the render/display flags on the real geo are wrong

steps.note: STABLE TITLE TAP + HAND-OFF. Wire OUT_titlecomp (or OUT_title3d routed through the composite) into a nullTOP that every downstream layer targets by NAME, so the title layer can be re-plumbed without rewiring consumers. This TOP is the deliverable title layer: it feeds a projection map (a cornerpinTOP in multi_quad_mapper), a media-server layer, or a file/stream via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output (WIRE-ONLY -- windowCOMP not opened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF; ndioutTOP.active/syphonspoutoutTOP.active DEFAULT ON -> set OFF). For a lower-third used as an overlay ON a live feed, this null is the alpha-keyable super the switcher/media server composites.
steps.geometry_out: final title/lower-third/credit layer, canvas res, ready for wire-only output

verify.pass_if: the finished title layer at canvas res, transparent where there is no type
verify.milestone_check: OUT_titleout holds the deliverable title/super the map or media server will use

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: copy approval, font licensing, live data feed)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === The MCP builds the whole title network and sets every string/font/size/colour/position/animation numerically. A PERSON must supply and sign off the things the bridge cannot invent or verify: the exact approved COPY (names spelled right, titles, sponsor supers, legal credit order), the LICENSED font file (a menu font is safe; a brand face is a fontfile the human places under the working dir -- licensing is theirs), and any EXTERNAL live data the counter shows (a real countdown target time, a scoreboard/stats feed, a time-of-day source). For a broadcast lower-third the SWITCHER/graphics operator decides when each super is keyed live -- the MCP builds the alpha-keyable layer; the on-air GO is theirs. WHAT THE MCP DOES: set_par the approved strings into textTOP.text (or wire the approved data DAT), point fontfile at the placed font, and expose the countdown target as a param the human sets.

key_params.set_par (after approval): op=OUT_title, pars={text:'<approved copy>', fontfile:'<licensed font under working dir>'}

steps.geometry_out: titles carrying approved copy, licensed type, and the real live-data feed

verify.pass_if: text holds the approved copy and fontfile points at the licensed face (or a safe menu font)

recipes.classify: TYPOGRAPHY and TEXT content -- show titles, main titles, lower-thirds, name supers/name straps, chyron, subtitles/captions, rolling or crawling CREDITS, a COUNTDOWN / countdown-to-start / count-up timer, a live CLOCK / time-of-day, a scoreboard or data-driven readout, text-on-screen, kinetic type, 3D extruded titles -> this recipe (the data-only text/title generator; textTOP + geotextCOMP). Keywords: typography, type, text, title, titling, lower third, caption, subtitle, credits, countdown, timer, clock, chyron, name super, message, ticker.
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY: the entire title network is created, wired and parameterized by the bridge with literal values -- strings via textTOP.text, look via font/size/colour params, motion via an lfoCHOP/keyframeCHOP EXPORTED (set_flags export, exportmethod=autoname) onto a transformTOP/levelTOP, and a LIVE counter/clock via the code-free timerCHOP/clockCHOP -> choptoDAT -> textTOP.dat (or textTOP.chop + chopvaluereplace) path. NO parameter expression, no DAT callback/script, no evaluateDAT, no code sink anywhere; the only actuator is the allowlisted parameterless `pulse` (timerCHOP start/cuepulse; tableDAT loadonstartpulse if a CSV of supers is loaded via write_csv -> tableDAT.file -> pulse(loadonstartpulse)). An ease-curve or an arithmetic-formatted counter is the one place an expression would be tidier -- surfaced as an expr_opportunity, never baked in. HUMAN / OFF-BRIDGE: approved copy, licensed font files, the real external data feed, and the on-air keying decision for a broadcast super. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: the title layer hands off through output_handoff / projection_align_and_output (terminal ops built inactive). HONEST GAPS: there is no dedicated 'lower-third' or 'credits' template operator -- this recipe assembles them from textTOP + transform + composite primitives (a helper build_lower_third(text, bar, position) is a candidate). geotextCOMP covers 3D text without a SOP; the textSOP/extrudeSOP path is for bevel/side-face control it lacks. NC build caps live render at 1280; swap resolution for 1920/3840, topology identical. ROUTING FIX: 'typography' formerly landed on generative_texture_fx (no text op) -- this recipe is the correct text lane and its routing row claims that vocabulary.
tips: textTOP has fontsizex AND fontsizey (two params) -- set keepfontratio=on and size once, or the type stretches; there is no single 'fontsize' on the TOP (geotextCOMP does use a single 'fontsize').

bgalpha defaults 0 (transparent, correct for compositing) but fontcolor defaults white -- a white title over the white preview page looks blank; always judge it composited over the real dark content or a lower-third bar.

LIVE counter without an expression: timerCHOP/clockCHOP -> choptoDAT -> textTOP dat/rowindex/colindex; OR wire the CHOP into textTOP.chop with chopvaluereplace=on and a %-token, using valuetouse/totaldigits/decimaldigits/leadingzero/posttext for zero-padded MM:SS. When using the dat source, SET textTOP.text='' first -- its default is the placeholder 'derivative', which otherwise prepends the live value.

compositeTOP's over draws INPUT 0 ON TOP (verified live): to stack a title over an OPAQUE background, either set swaporder=on (then input 0 is the bottom and the last input is on top) or wire the background as the LAST input -- an opaque bg on input 0 without swaporder hides everything above it.

Animate code-free: lfoCHOP (ramp=slide/scroll, sin=pulse) or keyframeCHOP (authored cue timing) EXPORTED with exportmethod=autoname onto transformTOP.tx and levelTOP.opacity -- one exporter per parameter, disable any other driver first.
Force outputresolution=custom at delivery res on the textTOP, every transform, and the compositor -- a title left at 256 default is soft the instant it scales onto a 4K canvas.

3D title: geotextCOMP is the quick path (mode=text, assign a constantMAT, render=on, point a renderTOP at it); if you build the textSOP/extrudeSOP route inside a geometryCOMP, delete the COMP's default torus and set_flags render/display on the real SOP or the renderTOP shows the torus or nothing.

Credits from a folder: a folderDAT (rootfolder under the working dir, type=files, namecol on) gives one row per name -- drive the textTOP row index with a timerCHOP for a paced credit sequence, no script.

Lower-third bar: a rectangleTOP (softness>0 for a soft strip) or a dimmed constantTOP wired UNDER the title in the compositor gives legibility over busy footage; feather the bar rather than a hard box.
variants: static_super: type the string straight into textTOP.text, skip the timer/choptoDAT -- a fixed title/lower-third with only an lfoCHOP opacity fade for on/off.
live_countdown: timerCHOP(length=countdown, cycle off) -> choptoDAT -> textTOP -- a count-to-zero clock (count-up = a clockCHOP or a mathCHOP negating the timer); pulse start restarts it.
rolling_credits: a folderDAT/tableDAT of names -> textTOP (word-wrapped, aligny top) -> transformTOP ty animated upward by a ramp lfoCHOP for a smooth full-frame credit scroll over black or content.
extruded_3d_title: geotextCOMP (or textSOP extrude / textSOP+extrudeSOP in a geometryCOMP) + orthographic cameraCOMP + renderTOP -> a bevelled/lit dimensional title re-entering the composite chain.
data_readout: a mathCHOP-shaped external value (score, temperature, stat) -> choptoDAT -> textTOP with the numeric formatter -- a live on-screen number that updates every frame with no expression.

recipes.title: GPU particle content -- embers / sparks / snow / flow (spherePOP or boxSOP emitter -> sprinklePOP birth points -> particlePOP sim + forceradialPOP forces + noisePOP turbulence -> nullPOP -> pointspriteMAT on a geometryCOMP -> renderTOP -> OUT_particlerender)
recipes.summary: Author a live GPU particle system as projection content -- rising embers, drifting snow, spark bursts, a flow field -- entirely from typed operators, no VEX and no expressions. The spine is the NEWER POP particle family: an emitter shell (spherePOP or a boxSOP) feeds sprinklePOP, which scatters the BIRTH points; particlePOP is the actual simulation (birthrate / life / initial velocity / mass / drag / max particles); forceradialPOP adds the force field (gravity via globforce, wind via windspeed, a radial burst or a spiral); noisePOP curls or jitters the motion for organic turbulence. A terminal nullPOP (OUT_pop) is the stable particle tap. The particles RENDER as point sprites: assign pointspriteMAT (additive blending for glowing embers/sparks) to a geometryCOMP that holds the POP chain, frame it with a cameraCOMP, and renderTOP bakes the image (bgcolor alpha 0, outputresolution=custom). KEY GOTCHA #1: a fresh geometryCOMP renders its default torus1, NOT your particles -- delete torus1 and set_flags render/display on the terminal nullPOP inside the geo. KEY GOTCHA #2: this is DISTINCT from point_cloud_content (a STATIC scan rendered by TOP-instancing) and from generative_texture_fx (a 2D feedback texture with no 3D sim) -- this recipe is a live deterministic-ish 3D simulation. HONEST STATE: the POP particle path is real and shipped but NEW (2023+); there is NO poptoSOP converter in the catalog, so the POP renders NATIVELY inside the geometryCOMP -- if that path is unavailable on a given build, fall back to the classic particleSOP (prtype=pointsprites) inside the same geo, or to copySOP/TOP-instancing (see variants). Look approval against the real surface, and the wire-only output, are the human/hardware boundary.

steps.note: EMITTER SHELL -- the surface/volume the particles are born from (a fountain nozzle, a snow ceiling, a spark line). spherePOP gives a rounded emitter; swap for boxSOP (a ceiling plane for snow) or a linePOP (a spark edge) as the shape demands. Keep the poly count modest (freq/rows/cols low) -- it is only a birth surface, never rendered. Position it in world space with t (tuplet t=[x,y,z]) where the emission should originate. This POP is the INPUT to sprinklePOP; it is not itself the content.

key_params.radx: 0.5 (radx/rady/radz as rad vector for an ellipsoid nozzle)

steps.geometry_out: a low-res emitter shell (birth surface)

verify.pass_if: a small POP surface exists at the intended emission origin

steps.note: BIRTH POINTS -- scatter the seed points that particlePOP will emit from. Wire OUT_emitter -> sprinklePOP (maxinputs=1). numpoints controls how many candidate birth sites; method=perprim scatters per face of the shell, method=vol fills the volume (embers boiling out of a fire body), seed randomizes the pattern. sprinklePOP turns the smooth shell into a point cloud of emission sites -- particlePOP births along these each frame. Use noisePOP here too if you want the birth density to breathe (optional). This is the emit source the brief calls for.
steps.geometry_out: scattered birth points on the emitter

verify.pass_if: a point cloud of ~numpoints birth sites exists

steps.note: THE SIMULATION -- the heart of the system. Wire OUT_birthsrc -> particlePOP as the birth source (maxinputs=1, emissionmode=rate births from the input points at birthrate per second). Set life (seconds a particle lives) + lifevariance (fraction, so not every ember dies at once); initvelocity (tuplet initvelocity=[x,y,z]) is the launch velocity -- +y for rising embers/sparks, small for drifting snow; initmass + initdrag govern how forces and air resistance act; maxparticles caps the live count (GPU budget); damping bleeds velocity. play=on runs it; speed scales sim time. This node alone produces a moving particle stream; forces and noise refine it. Because particlePOP feeds a solve, keep maxparticles within the GPU/NC budget.
steps.geometry_out: a live particle stream (points with velocity)

verify.pass_if: point count rises then stabilizes near birthrate*life; particles move each cook
verify.milestone_check: read_network @OUT_particles across two cooks -- the live particle count grows toward birthrate*life and positions change (the sim is running)

steps.note: THE FORCE FIELD -- shape the motion. Wire the particle stream through forceradialPOP (maxinputs=1) to add forces to velocity: globforce (tuplet globforce=[x,y,z], default -0.1 in y) is GRAVITY -- negative y for snow/ash falling, positive for embers rising; windspeed (tuplet) is a constant WIND drift; enable radial (radial=on, radialstrength) for an outward BURST from pos (a spark explosion, a shockwave); enable spiral (spiral=on) for a vortex/tornado swirl; falloffradius + falloff shape how force decays with distance from pos. Stack multiple forceradialPOPs for layered behavior (gravity + wind + a pulsing burst). This is where 'embers' vs 'snow' vs 'flow' is decided.
steps.geometry_out: particle stream with forces applied

verify.pass_if: particle trajectories bend under gravity/wind/burst as configured

steps.note: TURBULENCE -- the organic wobble that sells fire/smoke/snow. Wire OUT_forced -> noisePOP. Two modes: (a) enable curl3d (curl3doutputattrscope=curlnoise) and combine it into velocity for a divergence-free swirling flow (the classic curl-noise look -- flames licking, snow eddies); (b) set outputattrscope=P with a small amp to jitter positions directly. type=simplex4d animates over time (the 4th dimension is time -> use t4d or let it evolve), period sets the feature size, amp the strength, harmon/gain add detail octaves. Keep amp modest -- too much and embers scatter into static. Optional but almost always worth it.
steps.geometry_out: particle stream with turbulent motion

verify.pass_if: motion gains organic swirl without particles exploding apart

steps.note: THE SPRITE MATERIAL -- how each particle is drawn. pointspriteMAT renders each point as a camera-facing sprite. For glowing embers/sparks set blending=on + blendop=add + srcblend=one + destblend=one so overlapping sprites SUM to bright hot cores (additive glow); for snow use normal alpha blending (blending=on, srcblend=sas, destblend=omsa) with a soft round colormap. colormap = a soft dot/glow TOP (a rampTOP radial or a circleTOP with soft edge) drives the sprite shape; pointsize (or pointscaleattrib='PointScale' reading a per-particle scale attribute) sets size; sizingmodel=perspective makes near particles bigger. color/alpha tint the whole system. First terminate the POP chain in a nullPOP (OUT_pop) as the stable tap.
steps.geometry_out: additive/alpha point-sprite material

verify.pass_if: blending on with the intended add/alpha blend factors

glsl_opportunity.why: a bespoke sprite shader (soft falloff, per-particle color ramp by age/velocity, texture-atlas frames) exceeds pointspriteMAT's fixed lighting
glsl_opportunity.propose_via: glsl_reference then set_glsl on a glslMAT assigned to the geometryCOMP in place of pointspriteMAT
glsl_opportunity.consent: needs allow_glsl (default OFF); data-only fallback = pointspriteMAT additive blend + a colormap TOP, which covers embers/sparks/snow well

steps.note: RENDER THE PARTICLES. Put the POP chain INSIDE a geometryCOMP (or reference it) and assign OUT_spritemat via the geo's material param; CRITICAL GOTCHA -- a fresh geometryCOMP renders its default torus1, so delete_op torus1 and set_flags render=true/display=true on the terminal nullPOP so the particles are what renders. Add a cameraCOMP (projection=perspective, tz back so the whole system is in frame, fov ~45, set near/far to bracket the particles) and wire geo + camera into renderTOP. Force outputresolution=custom at delivery res (256px trap otherwise); bgcolora=0 so the particles land on TRANSPARENT for compositing over the map (white-on-transparent looks blank over a white preview -- judge over black). antialias=aa8 for clean sprite edges. This is the deliverable content frame.
steps.geometry_out: rendered particle image, delivery res, transparent bg

verify.pass_if: particles render as sprites over transparent; motion visible across frames
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_particlerender at two times -- the particle system reads as intended (embers/snow/flow) and has clearly moved

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: on-surface look approval + WIRE-ONLY handoff)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN + HARDWARE SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds the whole POP sim, the sprite material, the geo+camera+render, and sets every numeric param. WHAT A PERSON DOES: judges the look ON the real surface at real scale and brightness (ember size vs building height, additive glow vs ambient light, density vs projector lumens) and calls the measured tweaks back via set_par on birthrate / initvelocity / pointsize / globforce -- the MCP cannot see the wall. HANDOFF is WIRE-ONLY: OUT_particlerender feeds the map/output lane (multi_quad_mapper / projection_align_and_output / output_handoff); terminal output ops are BUILT but never fired here -- windowCOMP not opened, moviefileoutTOP.record OFF, ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active set OFF. To BAKE a fixed-length particle loop instead of running live, hand to seamless_loop_authoring.
steps.geometry_out: approved particle content, wired to the output lane (not actuated)

verify.pass_if: content tap exists and downstream output ops are OFF (record/active=off)

recipes.classify: GPU particle system content -- embers, sparks, fire, snow, ash, dust, rain, bubbles, a flow field, a fountain, an explosion burst, a vortex/tornado swirl; live 3D particle simulation as projection content; particlePOP birthrate life velocity forces, forceradialPOP gravity wind radial spiral, noisePOP curl turbulence, sprinklePOP emit, pointspriteMAT additive sprites rendered through a camera; NOT a static point-cloud scan and NOT a 2D feedback texture
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY: the entire POP particle system -- emitter, birth scatter, the particlePOP sim, forces, turbulence noise, the sprite material, the geo/camera/render -- is created, wired and parameterized by the bridge with literal numbers via create tools and set_par. No script/execute/cplusplus/callbacks DAT and no parameter expressions anywhere; motion is the GPU sim itself (deterministic given seed + params), which is inherently code-free. HUMAN / HARDWARE: look approval at real scale/brightness on the surface, and the physical output, are off-MCP; the wire-only terminal ops are BUILT but not fired (windowCOMP not opened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF; ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active default ON -> MUST set OFF) and handed to the output lane. HONEST CATALOG GAPS: (1) the POP particle family (particlePOP, forceradialPOP, noisePOP, sprinklePOP) IS present and verified in the catalog, but it is the NEWER (2023+) path and this library historically treated POPs as forward-looking (see point_cloud_content, which uses TOP-instancing as its documented path). (2) There is NO poptoSOP converter in the catalog (verified absent) -- so POP particles must render NATIVELY inside a geometryCOMP with the render/display flags on a nullPOP, rather than being converted to a SOP first; if native POP rendering is unavailable on a given build, use the classic particleSOP (SOP family, prtype=pointsprites) inside the geo, or copySOP/TOP-instancing (variants) -- both fully data-only. (3) pointspriteMAT is a real MAT and verified. NC render cap is 1280: build/preview at <=1280, swap resolution to 1920/3840 for delivery -- topology identical.
tips: A fresh geometryCOMP renders its default torus1, not your particles -- delete_op torus1 and set_flags render=true/display=true on the terminal nullPOP inside the geo, then assign pointspriteMAT via the geo's material param.

Additive glow (embers/sparks): pointspriteMAT blending=on, blendop=add, srcblend=one, destblend=one -- overlapping sprites SUM to hot bright cores. Snow/dust: normal alpha (srcblend=sas, destblend=omsa) with a soft round colormap.
Judge particle content over BLACK, never over the white preview page -- additive sprites and low-alpha snow look blank on white but read correctly over a dark map.
lifevariance>0 staggers particle deaths so the system doesn't pulse; without it every ember born together dies together (a visible strobe).
curl3d noise (divergence-free) gives fire/smoke swirl without particles piling up or tearing apart; plain P-jitter noise scatters them -- prefer curl for flow looks.
maxparticles is the GPU budget: birthrate*life must stay under it or the oldest particles are recycled early (a hard cutoff). Size it to the look, not the max.
Forces are additive POP nodes: stack forceradialPOP for gravity + a second for wind + a third pulsing radial burst; each modifies velocity in the chain.
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_particles(look='embers'|'snow'|'sparks'|'flow', origin, rate, life) -> emitter+sprinkle+particlePOP+forces+noise+sprite+geo+camera+render preset in one call.
variants: embers_sparks: initvelocity +y, globforce slight +y then gravity, additive blend (add/one/one), warm colormap, short life + high birthrate -- rising fire embers or a spark shower (radial=on burst for pyro).
snow_ash_fall: boxSOP ceiling emitter, initvelocity ~0, globforce small -y, gentle windspeed drift, curl noise low amp, normal alpha blend with a soft dot colormap -- drifting snow or falling ash.
vortex_flow: forceradialPOP spiral=on + axial=on around a pos, curl noise, long life -- a tornado / flow-field / magic swirl.

particleSOP_fallback (fully classic, no POP path): a particleSOP (prtype=pointsprites, behave=psystem) inside the geometryCOMP with a source SOP into input, forces via its external/wind/turb params, rendered with pointspriteMAT -- the pre-POP data-only route if native POP rendering is unavailable.

instanced_geo_particles: instead of point sprites, instance a small quad/sphere SOP per particle via geometryCOMP instancing reading the particle P/scale/color -- heavier but gives shaded 3D confetti/leaves (bridges toward instanced_kinetic_content).

recipes.title: LED wall / pixel-map canvas feed (content -> cropTOP+transformTOP per-tile carve OR layoutTOP grid-pack over a black constantTOP -> resolutionTOP pins the EXACT total canvas res -> ndiout/st2110out/videodeviceout/directdisplayout, active OFF) -- the data-only feed for a Novastar/Brompton/Linsn processor; NO LED/pixelmap TOP exists
recipes.summary: Deliver a single, correctly-sized, correctly-tiled video canvas to an external LED processor (Novastar / Brompton / Linsn / Colorlight), which does the actual physical pixel-map (which panel sits where in the rig). TouchDesigner's job is ONLY to produce the master canvas the processor ingests: content assembled at the EXACT total pixel resolution the processor is configured to receive, with each source region landing where the processor expects it. There is NO dedicated LED/pixelmap panel-map TOP in the catalog (tileTOP tiles/repeats/mirrors ONE input into a grid -- great for a REPEATED motif across identical panels or test patterns, but not per-panel-unique carving) -- so you ASSEMBLE from primitives: a black constantTOP base at the total canvas res, then per-panel content carved with cropTOP (which slice of the source feeds this tile) + transformTOP (place that slice at its exact pixel position on the canvas, extend=zero) composited over black; OR, for a uniform rectangular tile grid, a single layoutTOP grid-packs N equal tile TOPs (align=gridrows/gridcols, numrows/numcols); OR, for a repeated identical motif, a single tileTOP (repeatx/repeaty). A resolutionTOP then PINS the exact total canvas resolution the processor demands -- this is the make-or-break step: a Novastar sender configured for e.g. 3840x1080 will corrupt/offset the whole wall if fed 1920x1080. The finished canvas hands off WIRE-ONLY to whichever transport the processor takes (ndioutTOP over IP, st2110outTOP for 2110 plants, videodeviceoutTOP for an SDI/DisplayPort feed board, or directdisplayoutTOP when the processor is an EDID display) -- every one of those output TOPs has active DEFAULT ON, so the recipe MUST set active OFF (WIRE-ONLY). KEY GOTCHA: the 256px default-resolution trap bites every node here (force outputresolution=custom on the canvas, every crop/transform, and the resolutionTOP), and transformTOP translate is in FRACTION units by default -- set tunit=pixels to place a tile at an exact pixel offset. HUMAN BOUNDARY: the physical map (panel A is top-left, panel B is 256px right, this tile is rotated) lives in the LED processor's own software and is measured/entered on site by a person; TD only guarantees the canvas is the right size with the right content in the right canvas regions.

steps.note: BLACK MASTER CANVAS = the base every tile composites over, sized to the EXACT total pixel-map resolution the LED processor ingests (sum of all panel columns wide x all panel rows tall, e.g. a 8x2 array of 128x128 tiles = 1024x256). color black, alpha 1 (LED walls are opaque -- unlike projection there is no transparent surface behind, so a solid black ground is correct and off-panels read as black). outputresolution=custom at the total canvas res (256px trap: leave it and the whole feed is 256x256 and the processor mis-maps every panel). This node defines the canvas size/aspect that resolutionTOP will later pin. Wire it FIRST into the final compositeTOP.

key_params.resolution: [1024,256] (TOTAL processor canvas res; set to your sender's configured input res)

steps.geometry_out: black opaque canvas at the total pixel-map resolution

verify.pass_if: resolution == the processor's configured total canvas res, all pixels black

steps.note: MASTER CONTENT SOURCE. Set file via set_par with an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path UNDER the working dir AFTER create (a relative or external path is blanked by path confinement). This is the whole-show content that gets sliced across the wall; any content TOP works (moviefileinTOP / a generative composite tap / a still). Because a physical LED wall almost always has a non-16:9 pixel-map aspect, author or letterbox your content to the total-canvas aspect so the carve steps sample it cleanly.
steps.geometry_out: master content image feeding the wall

verify.pass_if: clip resolution reported, not the default sample

steps.note: PER-TILE SOURCE CARVE (repeat this + the transform per panel/tile for an IRREGULAR wall). cropleft/cropright/cropbottom/croptop select the sub-region of OUT_content that this physical panel should show (default fraction units: left 0, right 1, bottom 0, top 1 = full frame). Use this when the processor's panels do NOT form a simple contiguous grid -- e.g. scattered set-piece tiles, a wall plus a separate DJ-booth strip fed on the same canvas, or content that must be re-ordered to match the processor's panel numbering. extend=zero so anything outside the crop is transparent/black. outputresolution=custom at THIS tile's exact pixel size (e.g. 128x128) so the carved slice is already at panel resolution before placement.

key_params.cropleft: 0.0 (fraction, or set cropleftunit=pixels for exact px)

steps.geometry_out: one panel's worth of content at that panel's resolution

verify.pass_if: the intended source sub-region, at the panel's pixel size

steps.note: PLACE THE CARVED TILE at its exact pixel position on the master canvas (pairs with the cropTOP; repeat per tile). t = translate; SET tunit=pixels (default is fraction -- the classic 'my tile is a hair off' bug) then tx/ty are the tile's pixel offset from center on the canvas. extend=zero + a transparent/black background so only the tile's rectangle is painted. outputresolution=custom at the TOTAL canvas res (NOT useinput -- else the tile composites at its own 128px size and lands wrong). rotate is available for the occasional physically-rotated panel. Wire OUT_tile0crop -> in0. Duplicate the crop+transform pair for tile1..tileN, each with its own crop region and pixel offset.

key_params.tx: -448 (pixel offset to this tile's canvas slot; requires tunit=pixels)
key_params.rotate: 0 (nonzero only for a physically rotated panel)

steps.geometry_out: the tile placed at its exact canvas pixel coordinates over transparency

verify.pass_if: the tile occupies only its target rectangle; rest black/transparent

steps.note: FAST PATH for a UNIFORM contiguous tile grid (use INSTEAD of the crop+transform pairs when every panel is the same size and packs edge-to-edge). Wire the N equal tile TOPs into layoutTOP's multi-input (tops, maxinputs 9999) and let it auto-arrange: align=gridrows or gridcols with numrows/numcols set to the physical panel grid, fit=nativeres (or fill) + scaleres so each tile keeps its exact pixel size. outputresolution=custom at the total canvas res. This one node replaces the whole per-tile carve when the wall really is a plain grid; the crop+transform route is for anything irregular. Draw/pack order follows input order -- match it to the processor's panel numbering.

key_params.tops: OUT_tile0crop, OUT_tile1crop, ... (equal-size tiles, in processor panel order)

steps.geometry_out: the uniform tile grid packed into one canvas

verify.pass_if: tiles pack into the numrows x numcols grid at their native pixel size

steps.note: ASSEMBLE ALL PLACED TILES over the black canvas (skip this and use OUT_gridpack directly if you took the layoutTOP fast path). operand=over, tops multi-input (maxinputs 9999): wire OUT_canvas FIRST, then OUT_tile0placed, OUT_tile1placed ... OUT_tileNplaced. Because each placed tile is transparent outside its rectangle, over-compositing lays every panel exactly where its transform put it, on the opaque black ground. outputresolution=custom at the total canvas res. This is the assembled pixel-map canvas, one frame before the resolution pin. SWAPORDER: set swaporder=on -- compositeTOP's `over` draws INPUT 0 ON TOP, so swaporder=on makes input 0 the BOTTOM layer and the LAST input the top, matching the draw order described here (verified live: an opaque background on input 0 without swaporder hides everything above it).

key_params.swaporder: on (input 0 = BOTTOM layer; without it compositeTOP over draws input 0 on TOP)

steps.geometry_out: all panels assembled into one canvas over black

verify.pass_if: every panel appears at its mapped canvas position over black
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_assembled -- the full wall reads as one canvas with each tile in its slot

steps.note: PIN THE EXACT TOTAL CANVAS RESOLUTION the processor expects -- the make-or-break node. LED senders (Novastar MCTRL/COEX, Brompton Tessera, Linsn) are configured for one specific input resolution; feed a different size and the wall tears, offsets, or shows a corner crop. resolutionTOP outputresolution=custom, resolution=[exact W, exact H] the sender is set to. Keeping this as an explicit dedicated node (rather than trusting upstream res) is the single most reliable guard against a mis-sized feed on show day -- it also documents the target res for the next operator. highqualresize=on only if the canvas res differs from content res and you actually need resampling; normally the canvas is already exact and this is a pass-through pin.
steps.geometry_out: the canvas pinned to the processor's exact input resolution

verify.pass_if: resolution == the sender's configured input res EXACTLY
verify.milestone_check: top_info @OUT_pixelmap -- width/height match the LED processor's configured input resolution to the pixel

steps.note: === WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT SPLIT. Everything above is buildable + parameterizable; the terminal transport is BUILT but NEVER actuated by us. === Wire OUT_pixelmap into ONE output TOP matching how the processor is fed, and SET active OFF on it (all four default active ON -- leaving it on starts streaming/claims the device unbidden): ndioutTOP (active off, name='LEDwall', includealpha off) for an IP/NDI-input processor; st2110outTOP (active off, device/videodestip/signalformat) for a SMPTE 2110 plant; videodeviceoutTOP (active off, driver=blackmagic|aja|deltacast, device, signalformat) for an SDI/DisplayPort feed card into the sender; directdisplayoutTOP (active off, display) when the processor presents as an EDID display on a GPU head. The projectionist enables active + selects the real device on site. Hand off downstream via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output. Note videodeviceoutTOP has customresolution (customresolutionw/h) for non-standard signal formats -- match the sender's SDI/DP timing.

key_params.videodeviceoutTOP: active=off, driver, device, signalformat (customresolution for odd sizes)

steps.geometry_out: canvas wired to a WIRE-ONLY transport, dormant until the operator enables it on site

verify.pass_if: output TOP wired to OUT_pixelmap with active=off

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: physical pixel-map lives in the LED processor)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. === The actual pixel-map -- which physical panel occupies which region of the incoming canvas, panel gaps, rotated cabinets, receiving-card ordering, brightness/gamma/refresh -- is configured in the LED PROCESSOR'S OWN software (NovaLCT / Brompton Tessera / LEDVISION) by a technician measuring the real rig, and is entirely OUTSIDE TouchDesigner. There is NO LED/pixelmap TOP in the catalog -- TD cannot and does not describe the physical wall; it only guarantees the CANVAS is the exact size the processor expects with content in the correct canvas REGIONS. WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds the black canvas, the per-tile crop+transform carve (or the layoutTOP grid-pack), the compositor, the resolutionTOP pin, and the dormant output TOP -- and sets every crop region / pixel offset / total resolution numerically. WHAT THE HUMAN DOES: builds the physical map in the processor and, if the canvas layout must mirror the processor's panel numbering, feeds the measured region coordinates back which are typed via set_par onto each transformTOP tx/ty and cropTOP crop* params.

key_params.set_par (after tech maps the wall): op=OUT_tile0placed, pars={tx:<measured px>, ty:<measured px>}; op=OUT_tile0crop, pars={cropleft:<>, cropright:<>}

steps.geometry_out: canvas regions aligned to the processor's physical panel map once measured numbers are typed in

verify.pass_if: transform/crop params hold on-site values (or an authoring estimate)

recipes.classify: feed an LED wall / LED screen / LED video wall / pixel map / pixelmap to a Novastar or Brompton Tessera or Linsn or Colorlight processor/sender; build the master canvas at the exact total resolution, carve content into per-tile/per-panel regions, tile a panel grid, output over NDI/SDI/2110/DisplayPort to an LED processor; LED is half of projection/AV work -- send the correctly sized tiled canvas the sender ingests (physical panel map is done in the processor)
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the entire canvas-assembly network -- black constantTOP base at the total pixel-map res, per-panel cropTOP source carve + transformTOP pixel placement (or a layoutTOP grid-pack for uniform walls), the over-compositor, the resolutionTOP that pins the exact sender input resolution, and the aligned tap -- is created/wired/parameterized by the bridge. No script/execute/cplusplus op, no parameter expressions, no callbacks DAT; every crop fraction, pixel offset and resolution is a literal number set via the create tool or set_par. (2) HUMAN / ON-SITE: the PHYSICAL PIXEL-MAP (panel positions, gaps, rotation, receiving-card order, brightness/gamma) is configured in the LED processor's own software by a technician against the real rig and is outside TouchDesigner entirely. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: the terminal transport is built but never actuated -- ndioutTOP / st2110outTOP / videodeviceoutTOP / directdisplayoutTOP all default active=ON, so the recipe MUST set active=OFF; the operator enables the real device on site (hand off via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output). CATALOG NOTE: there is NO dedicated LED/pixelmap/panel-map TOP in the 509-op catalog; tileTOP (now present) tiles/repeats/mirrors ONE input into a grid -- the clean path for a REPEATED motif across identical panels or a test pattern, but NOT for per-panel-unique content -- so per-panel carving is still the plain-operator build (crop + transform + layout + resolution + tileTOP for repeats). It also does NOT model or drive the LED processor, its receiving cards, or panel calibration data -- that hardware layer is unreachable by design. LED is now roughly half of modern projection/AV work and was entirely absent from the library; this fills the TD-side feed only. NC build caps live render at 1280 -- swap resolution vectors for the real (often wider-than-1080) wall canvas; topology identical.
tips: resolutionTOP is the safety pin: LED senders are configured for ONE input resolution -- feed a different size and the wall tears or offsets. Keep an explicit resolutionTOP at the exact sender res as the last node before output; do not trust upstream res to stay correct.
transformTOP translate defaults to FRACTION units -- set tunit=pixels before typing tx/ty or your tile lands a fraction-of-canvas away from its slot.
Force outputresolution=custom on the canvas, EVERY crop/transform, the compositor, and the resolutionTOP. Any node left at useinput/256 poisons the whole feed with the 256px default.
LED walls are OPAQUE: use a black alpha=1 canvas (not the alpha-0 transparent ground projection uses); off-panels and gaps should read as solid black.

Uniform grid wall -> use the layoutTOP fast path (align=gridrows/gridcols, numrows/numcols, fit=nativeres, scaleres=on). Irregular/scattered panels -> use the cropTOP+transformTOP pair per tile. Don't mix approaches on one wall.

Match compositor/layout INPUT ORDER to the processor's panel numbering so tile N of your canvas maps to physical panel N; a mis-ordered pack looks 'shuffled' on the wall even when every tile is correct.

All four output TOPs default active=ON -- ndiout/spout/2110 will start streaming and videodeviceout/directdisplayout will claim the device the moment they exist. Set active=OFF immediately; the operator flips it on site.
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_pixelmap(total_res=[w,h], tiles=[{crop,pos,res}], transport='ndi'|'sdi'|'2110'|'display') -> canvas + per-tile carve + resolution pin + dormant output, in one call.
variants: uniform_grid (layoutTOP fast path): equal panels packing edge-to-edge -> one layoutTOP grid-pack of N equal tiles (numrows x numcols, fit=nativeres) instead of per-tile crop+transform; the simplest and most common regular-wall case.

irregular_map (crop+transform per tile): scattered set-piece tiles, mixed panel sizes, or content re-ordered to match processor panel numbering -> a cropTOP+transformTOP pair per panel composited over black; the flexible case for anything non-grid.

contiguous_single_rect: a plain rectangular wall the processor treats as one image -> skip the carve entirely; content -> resolutionTOP (exact wall res) -> output. The minimal path when no per-tile mapping is needed.

transport_swap: same OUT_pixelmap, different terminal -- ndioutTOP (IP/NDI sender), st2110outTOP (2110 plant), videodeviceoutTOP (SDI/DP feed card, customresolution for odd timings), or directdisplayoutTOP (processor as EDID display); all built active=OFF.

wide_canvas_4K_plus: LED canvases are often far wider than 1080 (e.g. 5760x1080, 3840x2560) -- set every custom resolution vector to the real wall size; topology identical (NC render cap 1280 previews downscaled).

repeated_motif (tileTOP): when every panel shows the SAME motif (or you need a built-in test pattern), a single tileTOP (repeatx/repeaty, flipx/flipy/flop, crop*) tiles ONE input across the canvas -- simpler than per-tile crop+transform; it does NOT carve unique content per panel (use the crop+transform or layoutTOP routes for that).

recipes.title: Immersive enclosing-room mapping (ONE shared room-scale geometryCOMP -> N calibrated cameraCOMPs, one per physical surface with numeric pose+lens -> renderTOP per surface or a shared multi-camera render fanned by renderselectTOP -> per-projector cornerpinTOP -> windowCOMP(specifydisplay)/ndioutTOP, WIRE-ONLY) -- the Van-Gogh / immersive-projection-space builder
recipes.summary: Wrap continuous content around a fully enclosing room -- 3+ walls plus floor and/or ceiling (the immersive 'Van Gogh room' / projection-space type) -- by building ONE shared 3D scene and viewing it from N calibrated cameras, one per physical projector surface. A room-scale geometryCOMP holds the box INTERIOR as textured surfaces (boxSOP with texture=boxinside so UVs land on the inside faces); a single 3D content scene is authored ONCE in that room's metric coordinates. Then ONE cameraCOMP per surface is given a NUMERIC pose (tx/ty/tz = that projector's real position in room coordinates, rx/ry/rz = its aim) and lens (projection=perspective + fov or focal/aperture matching the real projector throw, winx/winy lens shift for off-axis mounts, near/far clipped to the room) so each camera sees exactly the slab of the shared scene that lands on its wall. Each camera drives a renderTOP at that projector's resolution -- OR, to render the scene once, ONE renderTOP is given ALL the cameras (Camera(s) param is multi-camera, multicamerahint) and a renderselectTOP per surface pulls out camera N by cameraindex. Each surface's render then passes a per-projector cornerpinTOP (fine keystone/warp for the physical mount) and hands off WIRE-ONLY to a windowCOMP(justifyoffsetto=specifydisplay, one display index per projector) or an ndioutTOP (active OFF). Because every camera views the SAME scene from its own calibrated viewpoint, a pan or effect authored once flows continuously across the walls, floor and ceiling without a seam. KEY GOTCHA: the illusion is entirely in the camera CALIBRATION -- each cameraCOMP's transform must match the real projector's position/orientation and its lens must match the real throw/shift, or content slides off the corners; also a fresh geometryCOMP renders its default torus1 (delete it + set_flags render/display on the room SOP) and every render/cornerpin left at outputresolution=useinput lands at 256px. FLOOR/ANAMORPHIC is a dual-camera MODE: a VIEWER-eye cameraCOMP at the audience sweet-spot defines the anamorphic look, while a PROJECTOR-lens cameraCOMP at the real projector pose (optionally via the built-in quadreprojsop/quadreprojpts quad-reproject) defines what is actually output. HUMAN/HARDWARE BOUNDARY: measuring each projector's real-world position, orientation and lens, and the physical edge-overlap between adjacent surfaces, is an on-site job -- the MCP builds the multi-camera render graph and sets the numeric camera transforms + cornerpin corners from those measured numbers.

steps.note: THE ROOM SHELL as interior surfaces. A boxSOP is the enclosing room: set size to the real room dimensions in a consistent metric unit (sizex=width, sizey=height, sizez=depth) and center it so the origin sits where you want room-coordinate zero (e.g. floor-center: ty = height/2). CRUCIAL: texture=boxinside (or faceinside) so texture coordinates are generated on the INSIDE faces -- default boxinside vs boxoutside decides whether content maps to the interior (what you want for a room the audience stands inside) or the exterior. Turn dodivs on with a few divs per axis if a downstream warp/displace needs interior tessellation; a plain 6-face box is enough for flat walls. normals on. For a room that is NOT a clean box (an alcove, a curved wall, a dome segment) substitute a gridSOP per wall or an imported model -- the multi-camera principle is identical. This SOP is the shared surface every camera renders.

key_params.ty: height/2 (lift so the floor is at y=0) or 0 for centered

steps.geometry_out: room-interior box with inside-face UVs at real-world scale

verify.pass_if: box SOP at room dimensions, texture=boxinside, normals present

steps.note: THE ONE SHARED 3D SCENE. A single room-scale geometryCOMP holds OUT_roomshell (object-merge or parent the SOP inside) and carries the content material (a pbrMAT/constantMAT whose colormap/emitmap is the wrapping content TOP, so the image lands on the interior UVs). instancing OFF. GOTCHA (bake this in): a freshly created geometryCOMP renders its built-in torus1, NOT your SOP -- delete the default torus and set_flags render=true, display=true on the real room SOP, or every camera renders a doughnut. Everything downstream -- all N cameras -- renders THIS one comp; that shared-scene-single-source is exactly what makes content wrap continuously around walls, floor and ceiling. Keep the scene authored in the room's metric coordinates so camera poses (next step) are literal projector positions.

key_params.material: the content MAT (emitmap/colormap = the wrapping content TOP)

steps.geometry_out: shared textured room scene, one source for all cameras

verify.pass_if: geo renders the room SOP (not torus1); render/display flags on the real SOP
verify.milestone_check: read_network @OUT_room -- the room interior (not the default torus) is the rendered/displayed geometry

steps.note: ONE CALIBRATED CAMERA PER PHYSICAL SURFACE -- the heart of the technique. Create one cameraCOMP per projector/wall and give it the NUMERIC pose of that real projector: tx/ty/tz = the projector's position in the SAME room coordinates as the box, rx/ry/rz = its orientation (aim). LENS: projection=perspective; set the throw with viewanglemethod=horzfov + fov, OR viewanglemethod=focalaperture + focal/aperture to match the real lens; use winx/winy (Window X/Y) + winsize + winroll to model an off-axis projector's LENS SHIFT (real projectors almost never sit on the surface's optical center -- winy is your vertical-shift knob). near/far clip to the room bounds. Because all cameras look at the SAME OUT_room, each one frames exactly the slab of the shared scene that falls on its wall; a pan authored once slides across every camera's view in register. Duplicate this per surface: OUT_cam_wallN, OUT_cam_floor, OUT_cam_ceiling. The numbers here ARE the calibration -- they come from the on-site survey (human boundary step).

key_params.fov: match projector horizontal FOV (or set focal/aperture)
key_params.winy: vertical lens shift for off-axis mount

steps.geometry_out: one calibrated view matching one projector's real pose+lens

glsl_opportunity.why: an exotic projector lens (fisheye, heavy distortion, non-pinhole) can need a custom projection matrix beyond perspective+lens-shift
glsl_opportunity.propose_via: glsl_reference then set_glsl into the cameraCOMP customproj GLSL DAT
glsl_opportunity.consent: needs allow_glsl (default OFF); data-only fallback = projection=custommatrix with projmatrixop pointing at a 16-value CHOP matrix, or perspective + winx/winy lens shift set numerically

verify.pass_if: t/r hold the projector pose, projection=perspective, lens (fov/focal) set

steps.note: RENDER EACH SURFACE'S VIEW. Simplest topology: ONE renderTOP per camera -- camera=OUT_cam_wall_a, geometry=OUT_room, outputresolution=custom at THAT projector's native resolution (256px trap: leave it useinput/default and you render a 256x256 thumbnail). bgcolor alpha 0 (transparent) if you will composite this surface over others; opaque black if it is the whole wall. antialias aa4+ for clean edges on the room geometry. Repeat per surface (OUT_render_wall_a, OUT_render_floor, ...). This is the per-surface path; for many surfaces the shared-render fan-out (next step) renders the scene ONCE instead of N times. This is where the shared 3D scene becomes each projector's 2D image.
steps.geometry_out: one projector's rendered image of the shared room

verify.pass_if: resolution == projector native (not 256), the wall's content visible

steps.note: SHARED-RENDER FAN-OUT (alternative to N separate renderTOPs -- render the scene ONCE). Give a SINGLE renderTOP ALL the cameras at once: its Camera(s) param (camera) accepts a multi-camera list and multicamerahint=automatic renders every camera in one pass into a texture array. Then ONE renderselectTOP per surface pulls that surface's image out by cameraindex (top = the multi-camera renderTOP, cameraindex = 0,1,2... one per projector, outputresolution=custom at the projector res). This is the efficient path for a room with many projectors -- the shared scene is rasterized once and sliced N ways, guaranteeing every surface is perfectly in register. renderpassTOP is the related tool when a surface needs EXTRA geometry passes layered over the shared render without clearing (renderinput = the base render, clearcolor off). Use per-camera renderTOPs (previous step) for a few surfaces; use this fan-out for many.
steps.geometry_out: one surface's slice out of the single shared multi-camera render

verify.pass_if: cameraindex N yields wall N's view at projector res; all indices share one render

steps.note: PER-PROJECTOR GEOMETRIC CORRECTION. Even with a calibrated camera the physical mount is never perfect -- a per-projector cornerpinTOP corrects the residual keystone/edge misalignment on THIS surface's output. Feed it the surface render (OUT_render_wall_a or OUT_sel_wall_a); set the four pin* corners (pintopleft/pintopright/pinbotleft/pinbotright, fraction of the canvas) to the measured on-site correction, mapping=perspective (straight edges stay straight; bilinear bows them), outputresolution=custom at projector res, extend=zero + bgcolor alpha 0 so outside-the-frame is transparent. The extract* page can crop the source sub-region if this projector only covers part of the render. This is the fine-tune knob the projectionist drags on site; the MCP sets it numerically. For the physical EDGE-BLEND overlap between adjacent surfaces, do NOT hand-roll gradients here -- cross-reference multiprojector_edge_blend, which builds the feathered blend masks for the overlap zones.
steps.geometry_out: one projector's render corrected for its physical mount

verify.pass_if: the wall's content is keystone-corrected and frames the surface
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_pin_wall_a -- the corrected per-projector frame fills its surface with straight edges

steps.note: STABLE PER-PROJECTOR TAP + WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT. Plant one nullTOP per surface (OUT_wall_a_out) as the fixed hand-off name so the physical output op can be swapped without rewiring the render graph. Then the terminal output is BUILT BUT NEVER ACTUATED: a windowCOMP per projector with justifyoffsetto=specifydisplay + display=<that projector's display index> (winw/winh at the projector res, size=custom) drives a dedicated head -- but do NOT fire winopen (WIRE-ONLY; the operator opens the window on site). OR an ndioutTOP per surface for a media-server/processor hand-off -- ndioutTOP.active DEFAULTS ON, so you MUST set active=off. For N surfaces you get N windowCOMPs (one display each) or N NDI streams. Hand the whole set off via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output. Never open, never stream from the bridge.
steps.geometry_out: per-projector deliverable tapped at a stable null, output built but idle

verify.pass_if: windowCOMP specifydisplay+display set and winopen NOT fired; any ndioutTOP active=off

steps.note: FLOOR / ANAMORPHIC MODE (dual-camera) -- the variant for a floor illusion or forced-perspective anamorph. Build TWO cameraCOMPs for the floor surface. (1) the VIEWER-eye camera: pose it at the audience sweet-spot (where people stand/sit) looking down at the floor -- its view DEFINES the anamorphic look the audience should perceive (the content is authored to look correct from here). (2) the PROJECTOR-lens camera: pose it at the real projector's position/lens over the floor -- it defines what is ACTUALLY output. The data-only bridge: render the shared scene from the VIEWER camera, project THAT image onto the floor SOP as its texture (a projected UV / decal on the floor face), then re-render the floor from the PROJECTOR camera so the projector emits the pre-distorted image that resolves to the correct look at the sweet-spot. TouchDesigner's built-in quad-reproject can do this in one camera: set the projector camera's quadreprojsop to the floor quad and quadreprojpts1..4 to the four floor corner point numbers, reprojecting the viewer image through the known floor rectangle -- all numeric, no code. Same pattern maps ceilings or forced-perspective wall anamorphs.

key_params.proj_cam.quadreprojpts1..4: the four floor corner point indices (numeric)

steps.geometry_out: floor/anamorphic surface: viewer-eye look pre-distorted to the projector lens

verify.pass_if: two cameras (eye + projector) present; projector cam holds the reproject quad/points or the two-pass texture path is wired

steps.note: MILESTONE -- prove the room wraps and every surface is in register. Capture each surface's OUT_*_out (or the pre-output cornerpin) and confirm: (a) each projector frame is at its native resolution, not 256; (b) content authored ONCE in the shared scene appears continuously across adjacent surfaces (a horizontal line or a moving element crosses a wall/floor seam without a jump); (c) the floor/anamorph reads correctly from the viewer camera. Grab 2-3 surfaces around a corner to prove continuity. This confirms the shared-scene + multi-camera calibration end to end.
steps.geometry_out: TOP previews (inline) of each surface

verify.pass_if: both at projector res; shared content lines up continuously across the shared corner
verify.milestone_check: save_top across two adjacent surfaces -- a feature authored once in OUT_room crosses the corner without a seam or scale jump

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: on-site projector survey + physical edge overlaps)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === What the MCP builds: the shared room geometryCOMP, one cameraCOMP per surface, the per-surface renderTOP or shared multi-camera render + renderselectTOP fan-out, per-projector cornerpinTOP, and the wire-only outputs -- and it sets every camera transform/lens and every cornerpin corner NUMERICALLY. What a PERSON must do on site: measure each projector's real-world position, orientation and lens (throw + shift) and hand back those numbers (typed into each cameraCOMP's t/r/fov/focal/winx/winy via set_par), survey the physical EDGE OVERLAP between adjacent surfaces where two projectors meet (fed to multiprojector_edge_blend for the feather masks), judge the floor/anamorphic sweet-spot, and open the windows / start the NDI streams on the show machine. The MCP cannot see the room, cannot drive a mouse across the live projection, and cannot measure the overlaps -- it emits the render graph and consumes the surveyed numbers. Room-scanning tools (import_scan) can seed approximate geometry, but the projector poses come from the survey.

key_params.set_par (after survey): op=OUT_cam_wall_a, pars={tx,ty,tz,rx,ry,rz,fov | focal, winx,winy} = measured; repeat per surface; cornerpin pin* = measured corners

steps.geometry_out: content landing correctly on the real room once surveyed numbers are typed in

verify.pass_if: camera poses/lenses hold surveyed values (or estimates for authoring); cornerpins hold measured corners

recipes.classify: map projections onto a FULLY ENCLOSING ROOM / immersive projection space -- 3+ walls plus floor and/or ceiling wrapped with continuous content (the Van Gogh immersive room, digital art gallery, projection dome-room, 360 room, cave/CAVE-style enclosure, teamLab-style space); ONE shared 3D scene viewed from N calibrated cameras (one projector per surface), each camera's numeric pose+lens matching a real projector; floor projection and forced-perspective ANAMORPHIC illusions via a dual viewer-eye vs projector-lens camera; multi-wall multi-projector interior mapping, room-scale immersive content, enclosure mapping, ceiling mapping
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the entire multi-camera render graph -- the shared room geometryCOMP (box interior surfaces with inside-face UVs, content material), ONE cameraCOMP per physical surface with numeric pose+lens, the per-surface renderTOP OR the shared multi-camera renderTOP fanned by renderselectTOP (with renderpassTOP for extra layered passes), the per-projector cornerpinTOP, the stable per-surface null, and the terminal output ops -- is created, wired and parameterized by the bridge. No script/execute/cplusplus op, no parameter expressions, no callback DAT anywhere; every camera transform, lens value and cornerpin corner is a literal number set via the create tool or set_par. (2) HUMAN / ON-SITE: the projector SURVEY (each projector's measured position, orientation, throw and lens shift) and the physical EDGE OVERLAPS between adjacent surfaces are measured by a person and typed back; the floor/anamorphic sweet-spot is a human judgement. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: nothing here is actuated -- windowCOMP is built with justifyoffsetto=specifydisplay + a per-projector display index but winopen is NOT pulsed; ndioutTOP.active DEFAULTS ON and MUST be set OFF; hand the set off via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output. CROSS-RECIPE: the feathered overlap between two projectors that cover adjoining surfaces is multiprojector_edge_blend's job (build the blend masks there), not hand-rolled here; per-quad flat-surface mapping without a 3D scene is multi_quad_mapper. HONEST GAPS: there is NO single 'immersive room' or 'CAVE' operator -- this is assembled from primitives (boxSOP + N cameraCOMPs + renderselectTOP). The catalog has no automatic projector-to-surface auto-calibration / structured-light solver (products like a camera-based auto-align are external) -- the poses are surveyed by hand. import_scan can seed approximate room geometry but not the projector poses. A non-box room (curved walls, dome segments, alcoves) needs a gridSOP/imported-model surface per wall instead of the single boxSOP; the multi-camera principle is unchanged. NC build caps live render at 1280 -- swap each render/renderselect/cornerpin resolutionw/h for 4K per projector at show time; topology identical.
tips: The illusion lives in the camera CALIBRATION: each cameraCOMP's t/r must be the real projector's position/aim in the SAME room coordinates as the box, and its lens (fov or focal/aperture + winx/winy shift) must match the real throw -- get these wrong and content slides off the corners no matter how clean the render.

Author the shared scene ONCE in room-metric coordinates. Every camera renders the same OUT_room, so a pan/effect made once wraps continuously across walls, floor and ceiling in register -- that single-source-N-views is the whole point.
Fresh geometryCOMP renders its default torus1: delete the torus and set_flags render/display on the actual room SOP, or every projector shows a doughnut.
boxSOP texture=boxinside puts UVs on the INTERIOR faces (audience inside); boxoutside maps the exterior -- the classic 'my content is on the wrong side of the wall' bug.
Force outputresolution=custom at each projector's native res on every renderTOP, renderselectTOP and cornerpinTOP; anything left at useinput/256 renders a thumbnail.

For many surfaces, render the scene ONCE: give one renderTOP all cameras (Camera(s) is multi-camera) and slice per surface with renderselectTOP cameraindex -- cheaper and guarantees every surface shares one rasterization.

Floor/anamorph is TWO cameras: the viewer-eye camera defines the look, the projector-lens camera defines the output; the built-in quadreprojsop/quadreprojpts reprojects the viewer image through the four floor corners with pure numbers.
Do NOT hand-roll the overlap feather where two projectors meet on adjoining surfaces -- build those blend masks in multiprojector_edge_blend and keep this recipe to the render/camera graph.
variants: floor_anamorphic_mode: dual-camera forced-perspective -- a viewer-eye cameraCOMP at the audience sweet-spot defines the anamorphic look and a projector-lens cameraCOMP (optionally via quadreprojsop/quadreprojpts) defines the pre-distorted output; renders correct only from the sweet-spot. Same pattern for ceiling anamorphs and wall trompe-l'oeil.

shared_render_fanout: render the scene ONCE -- one renderTOP with ALL cameras (multicamerahint) + one renderselectTOP per surface (cameraindex). Best for 4+ projectors; every surface is a slice of one rasterization.
per_surface_render: one renderTOP per cameraCOMP -- simplest wiring, ideal for 2-3 surfaces or when each surface needs its own render settings (different AA, background, override material).

non_box_enclosure: for curved walls, dome segments, alcoves or an irregular room, replace the single boxSOP with a gridSOP/imported model per wall (or import_scan-seeded geometry); keep one calibrated cameraCOMP per surface -- the multi-camera method is identical.

corner_overlap_blend: two projectors cover an inside corner with a shared overlap -- keep the per-surface cornerpins here and route the overlap zones to multiprojector_edge_blend for the feathered blend masks so the seam disappears.

cave_walls_floor: a 4-wall + floor CAVE-style cube (no ceiling) -- five cameraCOMPs, five renders/selects, five outputs; the shared scene wraps the participant on five sides for a fully immersive standing space.

recipes.title: Unattended dayparting scheduler (clockCHOP wall-time -> logicCHOP daypart gates -> CHOP-built index EXPORTED onto switchTOP -> crossTOP fade over a black constantTOP) -- content that changes by time-of-day / day-of-week / date / sunrise-sunset with NO operator present
recipes.summary: The self-running venue primitive: a retail window, museum lobby, or architectural facade that plays MORNING content, switches to DAYTIME content, an EVENING look after dark, and goes BLACK off-hours -- entirely on its own, code-free. A clockCHOP reads the machine wall clock and emits numeric hour / wday (day-of-week) / day / month / sunrise / sunset channels; one logicCHOP per daypart thresholds those into 0/1 gates (convert=bound gives an inclusive time WINDOW, e.g. hour in [9,17]; chanop=and combines conditions like hour-window AND weekday); a mathCHOP folds the mutually-exclusive gates into a SINGLE daypart index (sum of gate_i * i). That index is EXPORTED (set_flags export=true, exportmethod=autoname -- data-only, no expression) onto a switchTOP that selects the matching content chain, with input0 = a BLACK constantTOP so any unmatched hour goes dark rather than showing stale content. A crossTOP (or a lagCHOP-smoothed open-gate on switchTOP.blend) dissolves the open/close transitions so the venue fades up at opening and down at close instead of hard-cutting. KEY GOTCHA: TD has NO scheduler / cron / calendar operator -- the clock+logic+index graph IS the scheduler, and it only fires at the RIGHT REAL TIME if the machine's wall clock, timezone and DST are correct (and, for sunrise/sunset, the site latitude/longitude). clockCHOP channels are named by their STRING params (default 'hour','wday','day','month','sunrise','sunset'); note it is 'sec' not 'second', and sunrise/sunset are DECIMAL HOURS derived from lat/long, not a stored time. The whole graph is MCP-buildable; auto-booting the project and keeping the OS clock correct is the human/hardware boundary.

steps.note: THE WALL-CLOCK SOURCE = the scheduler's heartbeat. clockCHOP reads the machine's real time and emits one channel per enabled field; the channel NAMES are the string param values (default 'hour','wday' day-of-week 0..6, 'day' day-of-month, 'month', 'sunrise','sunset', plus msec/'sec'/min/ampm/yday/week/year). Set output=units for raw NUMBERS (fractions/countdown are the other modes), hourformat=24 so hour is 0..23, timezone=local. For sunrise/sunset gating fill latitude/longitude (create-tool tuplets latitude=[deg,min], longitude=[deg,min]) + northsouth/eastwest -- those two channels are DECIMAL HOURS of local dawn/dusk computed from the site coords, NOT a stored clock. Enable only the fields you actually threshold. This is the single source every daypart gate reads.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (hour, wday, day, month, sunrise, sunset -- numeric, live wall time)

verify.pass_if: hour matches the real local hour and advances; wday/day/month present; sunrise/sunset are plausible decimal hours for the site

steps.note: THRESHOLD the clock into daypart GATES (one per daypart, or one logicCHOP with several output channels). convert=bound turns each input channel into 1 when it lies inside [boundmin,boundmax] and 0 outside -- an inclusive time WINDOW (e.g. hour bound [9,17] = 'open hours', hour bound [17,23] = 'evening'). For open-ended edges use convert=ge/lt instead. To AND conditions (hour-window AND a weekday), feed BOTH channels (hour + wday) and set chanop=and so the gate is 1 only when every channel passes; chanop=or for either. Build the windows so dayparts DO NOT OVERLAP -- the index-fold in the next step sums the gates, so two simultaneously-true gates would corrupt the index. Each gate is a clean 0/1 data value, no expression.

key_params.chanop: and (combine hour AND wday) | or | off
