steps.geometry_out: CHOP (0/1 gate per daypart)

verify.pass_if: each gate reads 1 exactly during its window and 0 otherwise; no two gates are 1 at once

steps.note: FOLD the mutually-exclusive gates into ONE switch index. Because at most one daypart gate is 1 at a time, scale each gate by its intended switch input number and SUM them: gate_morning*1 + gate_day*2 + gate_evening*3 (off-hours = all zero = index 0 = the black input). Do it with a per-channel gain then Combine CHOPs=add (or a small mergeCHOP + math). The result is a single 'daypart_index' channel = which content chain is live right now. Keep it integer-valued (a hard cut); a fractional/ramped index is only wanted when you deliberately want switchTOP.blend to crossfade (see crossTOP step / variants). Pure CHOP arithmetic -- data-only.

key_params.chanop: (per-channel gain to weight each gate by its input index)
key_params.combinechops: add (sum the weighted gates into one index)
key_params.integer: on/round so the index lands on an exact input number

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (single daypart_index, 0=off-hours black)

verify.pass_if: index equals the intended input number for the current daypart; 0 when no window matches

steps.note: SELECT the content chain by daypart. maxinputs=9999: wire in0 = the BLACK off-hours constantTOP (next step), in1 = morning content chain, in2 = daytime, in3 = evening, etc. DRIVE the switch by EXPORTING OUT_daypartindex onto the switchTOP 'index' parameter -- set_flags export=true, exportmethod=autoname on a nullCHOP carrying the single index channel renamed to 'index' (the export-flag path; a CHOP driving a param with NO expression = data-only). blend=off for a hard cut at each boundary (let the crossTOP handle fades); blend=on turns a FRACTIONAL index into an internal crossfade. Force outputresolution=custom at the canvas/projector resolution (256px trap). This node is the scheduler's output stage.

key_params.index: EXPORT-DRIVEN by OUT_daypartindex (do not type a literal; bind via export flag)

steps.geometry_out: the content chain matching the current daypart, at canvas res

verify.pass_if: the frame shown corresponds to the current daypart; forcing the index changes the content
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_scheduled -- at three test indices the switch shows the three distinct daypart chains (black at index 0)

steps.note: THE BLACK OFF-HOURS FRAME = switch input0 (index 0 when no daypart window matches). color [0,0,0], alpha 1 (opaque black -- a dark venue, not transparent), outputresolution=custom at the canvas resolution so it matches every content chain (256px trap: leave it and it is 256x256 and the switch resamples). Wiring black to input0 makes 'no schedule match' fail SAFE to darkness rather than freezing on whatever clip was last live. This is also the fade target for the crossTOP close transition.
steps.geometry_out: opaque black canvas-res frame (off-hours / fade target)

verify.pass_if: resolution == canvas res, fully black, alpha 1, wired to switchTOP in0

steps.note: SOFT OPEN/CLOSE TRANSITIONS = fade the venue up at opening and down at close instead of a jarring cut. in0 = OUT_offhours (black), in1 = OUT_scheduled (the live daypart content); the 'cross' param 0..1 blends black<->content. Drive 'cross' by a lagCHOP-SMOOTHED 'venue open' gate (a logicCHOP channel that is 1 whenever ANY daypart is active, run through a lagCHOP with a several-second lag) EXPORTED onto cross -- the lag turns the 0->1 step at open into a ramp = an automatic fade-in, and the 1->0 step at close into a fade-out. No keyframing, no expression. For daypart-to-daypart dissolves instead, prefer switchTOP.blend=on with a lag on the index. outputresolution=custom at canvas res.
steps.geometry_out: scheduled content faded up from / down to black at open/close

verify.pass_if: at a boundary the image ramps between black and content over the lag time rather than cutting

steps.note: STABLE SCHEDULED TAP. Every downstream output op targets THIS name so the physical output can be swapped without rewiring the scheduler. Wire OUT_dayfaded -> this. Hand off WIRE-ONLY to output_handoff / projection_align_and_output (windowCOMP to the display, or ndioutTOP / moviefileoutTOP) -- all terminal ops stay unactuated: windowCOMP not opened, moviefileoutTOP.record OFF, ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active DEFAULT ON so set them OFF. The scheduler drives the CONTENT; the mapping/warp lives after this null.
steps.geometry_out: final scheduled+faded frame, canvas res, ready for wire-only output

verify.pass_if: holds the current daypart's frame (or black off-hours) at canvas res
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_aligned across simulated dayparts -> distinct content per window, black off-hours

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: auto-boot the project + correct wall clock / timezone)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === An unattended venue only runs itself if a PERSON sets up the machine: the OS must auto-login, AUTO-LAUNCH the .toe, and start in Perform mode; power-loss auto-restart and a UPS are recommended so it recovers after an outage. Crucially the schedule fires at the correct REAL time ONLY if the machine's wall clock, TIMEZONE and DST are right (enable NTP time sync), and -- for sunrise/sunset gating -- the site LATITUDE/LONGITUDE typed into clockCHOP match the actual location. The MCP cannot set the OS clock, configure auto-boot, verify the venue's true local time, or watch the wall at dusk. WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds the entire clock->logic->index->switch->cross->null graph and sets every threshold numerically; the human owns boot reliability and clock accuracy.

key_params.human_owns: OS auto-login + .toe auto-launch + Perform mode; NTP time sync; correct timezone/DST; UPS/auto-restart; correct lat/long for sun gating

steps.geometry_out: a venue that boots and runs the schedule unattended once the machine is configured

verify.pass_if: clock params (timezone/hourformat/lat-long) are set; OS-level auto-boot + time sync are a documented human handoff

recipes.classify: content that changes BY TIME automatically with NO operator -- dayparting, scheduled playback, time-of-day / opening-hours / business-hours content, day-of-week (weekday vs weekend), date-specific (holiday) takeover, sunrise/sunset (dusk/dawn, after-dark) triggering, unattended venue, kiosk, retail window, museum lobby, architectural facade that runs itself, turns black off-hours, auto on/off schedule, calendar/cron-like content switching
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY: clockCHOP is a numeric wall-time source; logicCHOP thresholds it into 0/1 daypart gates; mathCHOP/mergeCHOP fold the gates into one index; that index reaches switchTOP.index and the lagged open-gate reaches crossTOP.cross via the EXPORT FLAG (a CHOP driving a parameter with NO expression -- same risk class as any export, no callbacks DAT, no evaluateDAT, no script). Every threshold, bound and input index is a literal number. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: nothing here is actuated -- downstream windowCOMP (not opened), moviefileoutTOP.record (OFF), ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active (DEFAULT ON -> set OFF) are handed off via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output. HUMAN / HARDWARE: the machine must AUTO-BOOT and auto-launch the project in Perform mode and keep running unattended, and its wall clock / timezone / DST (and site lat-long for sun gating) must be CORRECT -- the MCP cannot set the OS clock, guarantee boot, or verify real local time. HONEST GAPS: TouchDesigner has NO scheduler / cron / calendar / 'is-holiday' operator -- this clock+logic+index graph is the substitute; for specific calendar DATES author a tableDAT of date rows (write_csv -> tableDAT loadonstartpulse) and match day/month with logicCHOP eq, since there is no holiday-feed op. Sunrise/sunset are computed from lat/long, not a network almanac. NC build cap renders live preview at 1280; swap resolutionw/h for 4K, topology identical.
tips: clockCHOP channels are named by their STRING params (default hour/wday/day/month/sunrise/sunset) -- it is 'sec' not 'second'; enable only the fields you threshold to keep the CHOP tidy.
output=units for numeric channels you can threshold; fractions/countdown are display modes, not gate inputs.
sunrise/sunset are DECIMAL HOURS derived from latitude/longitude + timezone -- wrong coords or timezone = the facade lights at the wrong dusk.
logicCHOP convert=bound is an INCLUSIVE window [boundmin,boundmax]; chanop=and to require hour AND weekday (feed both channels), or/off for other combinations.
Make daypart windows MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE -- the index is a SUM of weighted gates, so two simultaneously-true gates corrupt it; leave no overlap and no gap you don't intend.
Wire the BLACK constantTOP to switchTOP input0 so an unmatched hour (index 0) goes dark and fails safe, instead of freezing on the last clip.
Export the single index channel onto switchTOP.index (set_flags export=true, exportmethod=autoname) -- one exporter per parameter; rename the channel to 'index' first.
A lagCHOP on the 'venue open' gate turns the open/close step into an automatic fade-in/out on crossTOP.cross -- no keyframes, no expression.

HELPER CANDIDATE: build_daypart_schedule(windows=[{name,start,end,days,content_op}], lat, long, fade_sec) -> clockCHOP + per-window logicCHOP + index math + switchTOP + lagged crossTOP wired in one call.
variants: sunrise_sunset_astronomical: gate an architectural/lighting look to actual dusk -- logicCHOP compares hour against clockCHOP 'sunset' (content on after sunset) and 'sunrise' (off after dawn); needs correct lat/long + timezone; self-adjusts across the year.
weekday_weekend: add the wday channel (0..6) with chanop=and so business-hours content runs Mon-Fri and a different chain (or black) runs weekends -- one extra logicCHOP condition.

date_specific_takeover: match day + month with logicCHOP convert=eq (or a tableDAT of date rows -> dattoCHOP compared per row) to force a holiday / event content chain on a specific calendar date, overriding the normal daypart via a higher switch input.
hard_cut_vs_dissolve: switchTOP.blend=off + integer index = instant daypart cut; switchTOP.blend=on + a lagged fractional index (or the crossTOP-to-black fade) = a smooth dissolve at boundaries.

countdown_to_open: before opening hours show a holding graphic / 'doors open in HH:MM' -- clockCHOP output=countdown or a timerCHOP counting to the open time drives a text/holding chain on the off-hours switch input instead of pure black.

recipes.title: Timecode chase / slave (audiodeviceinCHOP LTC audio -> ltcinCHOP SMPTE decode -> timecodeCHOP readout + moviefileinTOP frame-lock via playmode=timecodeop, with lookupCHOP/logicCHOP cue windows -> switchTOP) -- TD FOLLOWS an external master clock, the inverse of show_control_timecode
recipes.summary: The SLAVE half of show control: instead of TD generating the timecode (that is show_control_timecode, the master transport with GO buttons), here TD CHASES an external SMPTE/LTC or MTC master so playback is frame-locked to a video server, FOH console, DAW, or festival master clock. LTC arrives as an AUDIO signal, so an audiodeviceinCHOP captures the line/embedded-audio channel carrying LTC and feeds an ltcinCHOP, which DECODES SMPTE into a monotonic 'total seconds' (and 'total frames') chase value plus discrete hour/minute/second/frame channels. inputrate on ltcinCHOP MUST equal the master's frame rate (30 / 25 / 24 / 29.97 drop-frame) or the decode drifts. A timecodeCHOP (mode=chop, reading the decoded CHOP) conforms it to a clean HH:MM:SS:FF operator READOUT -- note timecodeCHOP is a converter/display, NOT the audio decoder. Playback frame-locks two data-only ways: (a) moviefileinTOP playmode=timecodeop with its timecodeop input pointed at the incoming-timecode CHOP -- the movie picks the frame that matches the code (true frame lock); or (b) playmode=specify with the decoded total-seconds EXPORTED onto the movie 'index' (indexunit=seconds). For multi-clip shows, logicCHOP convert=bound windows (or a lookupCHOP cue table) on the total-seconds pick a cue index EXPORTED onto a switchTOP to swap clips at each timecode boundary. KEY GOTCHA: ltcinCHOP reads audio-LTC only (feed it an audiodeviceinCHOP), it is not a MIDI reader; MTC arrives via midiinCHOP/midiinDAT and is coarser. The decode+lock graph is MCP-buildable; the master timecode feed itself -- the physical LTC audio / MTC MIDI line and its correct fps -- is patched and generated by a person, the human/hardware boundary.

steps.note: THE LTC AUDIO SOURCE. SMPTE-LTC is a raw AUDIO waveform on a line input (or embedded in an SDI/HDMI audio channel via driver=blackmagic/aja/deltacast), so capture it as audio first. active=on, pick driver (default/asio for a soundcard line-in, blackmagic/aja for capture-card embedded audio), format=mono, and select the exact input channel carrying LTC (inputselect byname/byindex). Level matters: LTC that clips or is too quiet will not decode cleanly. This CHOP's audio channel feeds the ltcinCHOP decoder next. (For MTC instead of audio-LTC, skip this and use a midiinCHOP -- see variants.)

key_params.active: on

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (raw LTC audio waveform, one channel)

verify.pass_if: an audio channel is present and moving on the input carrying LTC (not silent / not clipped)

steps.note: DECODE SMPTE-LTC -> the chase value. Wire OUT_ltcaudio -> ltcinCHOP in0 (maxinputs=1). inputrate MUST equal the incoming SMPTE frame rate (30 / 25 / 24 / 29.97) -- a mismatch makes the decoded time drift against the master. Enable the outputs you need: totalsec (default ON) = continuous seconds since 00:00:00 = the monotonic CHASE number; totalframes = exact frame count for frame-accurate lock; discrete (default ON) = separate hour/minute/second/frame channels. If the LTC feed stops, the last decoded value simply HOLDS (there is no hardware freewheel here). This decoded CHOP is what everything downstream chases.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (total seconds + total frames + h/m/s/frame, locked to the master)

verify.pass_if: total seconds advances in step with the master and holds when the feed stops; discrete h/m/s/frame read the master's timecode

steps.note: HUMAN-READABLE READOUT / conform (operator display). timecodeCHOP is a CONVERTER, not the decoder -- set mode=chop and point its 'chop' param at OUT_incode so it interprets the decoded frames/seconds as a timecode and emits clean hour/minute/second/frame channels (hourchan/minutechan/secondchan/framechan default ON) plus optional totalseconds/totalframes/fps. Set rate to the master fps and dropframe to match (29.97DF). Use this as the confidence HH:MM:SS:FF display and as a normalized timecode you can also feed to moviefileinTOP.timecodeop. It decodes NOTHING from audio -- ltcinCHOP already did that.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (clean HH:MM:SS:FF readout matching the master)

verify.pass_if: hour/minute/second/frame read the same timecode as the master clock; frame count wraps at the master fps

steps.note: FRAME-LOCKED PLAYBACK = the chase payload. Set file to an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path UNDER the working dir (external/relative paths are blanked by path confinement), play=on. TWO data-only lock mechanisms: (a) PREFERRED -- playmode=timecodeop, timecodemode=absolute, and set timecodeop = the incoming-timecode CHOP (OUT_tcdisplay or OUT_incode); the movie then serves the exact frame matching the incoming code = true frame lock. (b) FALLBACK -- playmode=specify, indexunit=seconds, and EXPORT the decoded 'total seconds' channel (from OUT_incode via a nullCHOP renamed to 'index') onto the movie 'index' param with set_flags export=true, exportmethod=autoname. Both are data-only: timecodeop is a CHOP REFERENCE, the index-export is the EXPORT FLAG -- neither is an expression. outputresolution=custom at canvas res (256px trap).
steps.geometry_out: clip frame that matches the incoming master timecode

verify.pass_if: the displayed frame corresponds to the incoming timecode; jogging the master jogs the clip in lock
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_lockedplayback at two distinct master timecodes -> the clip shows the two matching frames (frame-locked, not free-running)

steps.note: CUE SELECTION by timecode (optional -- multi-clip / multi-segment shows). Build cue boundaries on the monotonic 'total seconds': either logicCHOP convert=bound windows (cue N active while seconds in [in,out]) folded into a cue index, OR a lookupCHOP whose input0 is the total-seconds and input1 is a cue-boundary table (write_csv -> tableDAT loadonstartpulse -> dattoCHOP) mapping seconds -> cue index. EXPORT that cue index onto switchTOP.index (set_flags export=true, exportmethod=autoname) to swap which clip/chain is live at each timecode window; wire in0..inN as the per-cue chains. blend=off for hard cue cuts, on for a crossfade. Reuse the cue-table pattern from show_control_timecode rather than rebuilding it. outputresolution=custom at canvas res.

key_params.index: EXPORT-DRIVEN by the timecode cue index (logicCHOP windows or lookupCHOP table)

steps.geometry_out: the per-cue chain selected by the current master timecode window

verify.pass_if: crossing a cue boundary in the incoming timecode swaps the live chain

steps.note: STABLE CHASED TAP. Downstream output targets THIS name so the physical output swaps without rewiring the chase graph. Wire OUT_lockedplayback (single clip) or OUT_cueswitched (multi-cue) -> this. Hand off WIRE-ONLY to output_handoff / projection_align_and_output -- terminal ops stay unactuated: windowCOMP not opened, moviefileoutTOP.record OFF, ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active DEFAULT ON so set OFF. The chase drives the CONTENT/transport; mapping and warp live after this null.
steps.geometry_out: frame-locked show frame, canvas res, ready for wire-only output

verify.pass_if: holds the frame-locked show frame at canvas res
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_aligned while the master runs -> the frame tracks the incoming timecode end to end

steps.note: CROSS-REFERENCE -- the MASTER counterpart. show_control_timecode is the MASTER TRANSPORT: a timerCHOP GENERATES the show timeline, fires GO/cue pulses, and can emit timecode for others to follow. THIS recipe is the SLAVE/CHASE side: TD consumes an external master's timecode and locks to it, so there are NO GO buttons here -- the incoming code IS the transport. They share the same cue-table + apply-block philosophy (write_csv -> tableDAT -> lookup a cue row); do NOT rebuild that block, reuse the master recipe's. Choose master when TD runs the show, this slave recipe when a video server / console / DAW runs it and TD must follow.

key_params.relationship: show_control_timecode = master (generates/GO); timecode_chase_slave = slave (follows external code)

steps.geometry_out: (reference -- reuse the cue-table + apply-block from the master transport)

verify.pass_if: master vs slave roles are clear; the cue table is shared, not duplicated

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: the external master timecode feed)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === The master timecode itself comes from HARDWARE a person owns: an LTC/SMPTE generator, the FOH console, a video server, or a DAW, carried as LTC audio (a physical line or SDI-embedded audio channel) or as MTC over MIDI. A human PATCHES the cable into the machine, chooses the master frame rate and drop-frame, sets the audio input level so LTC decodes, and confirms the signal is live on site. The MCP cannot patch cables, generate the master code, set the physical audio level, or verify the incoming feed. WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds the audioin -> ltcin -> timecode -> movie frame-lock (+ cue switch) graph and sets inputrate/rate to the declared master fps; the human owns the feed and its correctness.

key_params.human_owns: the LTC audio / MTC MIDI cable + level; the master fps + drop-frame; a live, correctly-patched feed on site

steps.geometry_out: frame-locked playback once the real master timecode is patched in at the correct rate

verify.pass_if: ltcinCHOP inputrate matches the declared master fps; the physical feed/level is a documented human handoff

recipes.classify: make TouchDesigner FOLLOW an external clock -- chase / slave / follow timecode, LTC / SMPTE / MTC in, frame lock / frame-accurate / lock playback to timecode, sync to master clock / video server / FOH console / DAW, externally-driven playback, broadcast or festival master-clock sync, timecode input, slave to house sync; the inverse of the master transport (show_control_timecode)
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY: ltcinCHOP DECODES audio-LTC into numeric time; timecodeCHOP (mode=chop) CONFORMS it to a readout; frame lock is achieved with moviefileinTOP playmode=timecodeop (a CHOP REFERENCE on the timecodeop input) or by EXPORTING the decoded seconds onto the movie 'index' (the export flag) -- neither is an expression, no callbacks DAT, no evaluateDAT, no script. Cue windows come from logicCHOP/lookupCHOP on the decoded seconds; a cue table is authored with write_csv (confined) -> tableDAT (set file then pulse(loadonstartpulse) -- file alone does not load mid-session) -> dattoCHOP. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: nothing is actuated -- windowCOMP not opened, moviefileoutTOP.record OFF, ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active (DEFAULT ON -> set OFF), handed off via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output. HUMAN / HARDWARE: the master timecode feed (LTC audio, SDI-embedded audio, or MTC MIDI) is generated and patched by a person, who also sets the master fps + drop-frame and the audio level; TD only chases. HONEST GAPS: ltcinCHOP is AUDIO-LTC ONLY -- there is NO equally-clean MTC decode CHOP; MTC arrives via midiinCHOP/midiinDAT and is coarser (quarter-frame). There is NO genlock / blackburst / house-sync operator -- lock is software-level and can show sub-frame jitter; true hardware genlock is a GPU/SDI-card + OS concern (human). NC build cap renders live preview at 1280; swap resolutionw/h for 4K, topology identical.
tips: ltcinCHOP decodes AUDIO-LTC -- feed it an audiodeviceinCHOP (soundcard line-in or SDI-embedded audio via driver=blackmagic/aja). It is NOT a MIDI reader.
ltcinCHOP inputrate MUST equal the master frame rate (30/25/24/29.97) -- a mismatch drifts the chase; match drop-frame for 29.97DF over long runs.
totalsec = the monotonic chase value to drive index/cues; totalframes = exact frame; discrete = HH/MM/SS/FF -- enable only what you use.
timecodeCHOP is a converter/DISPLAY (mode=chop reads the decoded CHOP), not the decoder -- do not expect it to read audio itself.

moviefileinTOP playmode=timecodeop (timecodeop = the incoming-timecode CHOP) is the purpose-built frame lock; playmode=specify + an index-EXPORT of the decoded seconds is the generic data-only fallback.
LTC audio level / routing is the #1 failure -- clipped or too-quiet LTC will not decode; check OUT_ltcaudio first, before blaming the lock.
If the master feed drops the last decoded value HOLDS -- add a logicCHOP 'signal present' gate on the audio level to fall back to a standby clip (reuse emergency_blackout_and_standby).
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_timecode_chase(fps, source=LTC|MTC, clip, cues=[{tc_in,tc_out,clip}]) -> audioin + ltcin + timecode + movie frame-lock + cue switch in one call.
variants: ltc_audio_framelock (primary): audiodeviceinCHOP -> ltcinCHOP -> moviefileinTOP playmode=timecodeop; frame-accurate lock to an LTC master.

mtc_midi: the master sends MIDI Time Code instead of audio-LTC -- capture it with a midiinCHOP/midiinDAT (quarter-frame, coarser than LTC) and export the reconstructed seconds onto the movie index; no audio path.
cue_switch_by_timecode: logicCHOP convert=bound windows (or a lookupCHOP cue table) on total-seconds pick a cue index -> switchTOP swaps clips at each timecode boundary for a multi-segment show.
index_export_fallback: playmode=specify + indexunit=seconds, decoded total-seconds EXPORTED onto moviefileinTOP 'index' -- use when timecodeop lock is unavailable or you want a scalar-driven scrub.
signal_loss_standby: a logicCHOP on LTC presence -> switchTOP to a standby/hold clip when the master feed drops, so a lost feed fails to a safe graphic rather than a frozen frame.
embedded_sdi_ltc: audiodeviceinCHOP driver=blackmagic/aja to decode LTC embedded in an SDI/HDMI audio channel from a capture card, instead of a separate soundcard line-in.

recipes.title: Emergency blackout + standby + preview/program safety layer (program null -> state switchTOP -> DBO switchTOP over black constantTOP, standby textTOP/moviefileinTOP, 2nd nullTOP preview bus) -- the every-show kill-to-black
recipes.summary: The operational SAFETY LAYER every live show needs but no single op provides: an instant, reliable DBO ('dead black out') kill-to-black, a STANDBY/holding state to sit on between segments, and a preview-vs-program split so the operator watches what is queued without putting it on the audience. Spine: the live program bus enters a nullTOP (OUT_program) where any content/render/media recipe hands off; a STATE switchTOP picks program vs a standby graphic (a textTOP 'STANDBY' or a moviefileinTOP holding loop); a second DBO switchTOP stacks on top with in0=state-output and in1=an opaque black constantTOP, so index 0->1 is an INSTANT hard cut to black regardless of what state is live. DBO is driven code-free two ways: the fastest/most reliable is set_par index=1 on the DBO switch (immediate, no cook chain); a hardware panic button reaches it as a bound TOGGLE (oscinCHOP/midiinCHOP or a constantCHOP channel -> bind_chop onto the index). A separate nullTOP taps the STATE output as a preview bus so the operator sees the pending/held source while program may be blacked. KEY GOTCHA: use switchTOP (hard cut) NOT crossTOP for the DBO -- a DBO must be an instant, deterministic jump to black, never a dissolve; and keep blend=off on the DBO switch so index=1 is a full-frame black, not a partial mix. The 256px trap applies: force outputresolution=custom at program res on the black canvas, both switches, and the standby graphic or the black layer composites at the wrong size. Wire-only downstream: the program bus hands off to output_handoff / projection_align_and_output with the terminal op's active/record OFF; the physical panic button and the DECISION to kill are the human's.

steps.note: THE BLACK KILL LAYER -- an OPAQUE black frame the DBO switch cuts to. color [0,0,0], alpha 1.0 (opaque: a DBO must fully replace the program with black, not a transparent overlay that lets content show through). outputresolution=custom at the PROGRAM/projector resolution (256px trap: leave it and the kill layer is 256x256 and the switch mismatches size). This is the single most important node in the recipe -- it is what the audience sees the instant someone hits panic, so it must always be present, always black, and never depend on any upstream cook. Wire it as in1 of the DBO switchTOP.
steps.geometry_out: opaque black RGBA frame at program resolution

verify.pass_if: resolution == program res, every pixel black, alpha 1

steps.note: THE LIVE PROGRAM BUS = the stable tap every content chain hands off into, and the input the safety layer protects. Any upstream recipe (generative_texture_fx, facade_3d_render, media_clip_player, a mapped composite, signal_ingest_remap) wires its final aligned frame into THIS null so the blackout/standby rig sits downstream of all content. Naming the tap means the whole show can be re-sourced without rewiring the safety layer. outputresolution=useinput (it inherits program res from whatever feeds it) -- but confirm the feed is at program res so the switches downstream stay size-matched. This null is 'program IN'; the DBO switch output is 'program OUT'.
steps.geometry_out: the live program image entering the safety layer

verify.pass_if: carries the live program at program res (not the 256 default)

steps.note: THE STANDBY / HOLDING GRAPHIC -- what sits on the state switch between segments (house-open holding card, 'STANDBY', 'PLEASE WAIT', an event logo slate). text='STANDBY'; fontcolor near-white, fontsizex large (e.g. 120 points), alignx=center/aligny=center; bgcolorr/g/b [0,0,0] with bgalpha 1.0 so the card is a full opaque black slate with text (a projector must never receive white-on-transparent -- it reads as a blank/checkerboard over a light preview). outputresolution=custom at program res. For a MOVING holding loop (idle animation, slow logo) substitute a moviefileinTOP (see variant) -- it loops by default (textendleft/right=cycle). Wire as in1 of the STATE switchTOP.
steps.geometry_out: opaque STANDBY holding slate at program res

verify.pass_if: readable STANDBY text on solid black at program res

steps.note: THE CONTROL CHANNELS -- data-only state, no code. Author TWO channels on one constantCHOP: 'state' (0 = program, 1 = standby) selects what is queued, and 'dbo' (0 = pass, 1 = black) is the kill toggle. Set const0name='state'/const0value and const1name='dbo'/const1value via set_par (add the second channel by raising the const sequence). These channels are the operator/AI-writable truth of the show: flip 'dbo' 0->1 to black out, flip 'state' to swap the held graphic. They drive the switch indices either by bind_chop (next-but-one step) or are read as the values an operator types. Data-only: a constant is just a number; no expression, no callback.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (state, dbo) -- the writable show-state

verify.pass_if: two channels state/dbo present with the set values

steps.note: STATE SELECT (program vs standby) -- the 'what is queued' cut. maxinputs=9999 but here in0=OUT_program, in1=OUT_standby; index selects (0=program, 1=standby). blend=off for a hard, deterministic cut between the two (a soft state change is a variant: blend=on + a bound ramp). outputresolution=custom at program res so a size mismatch between a full-res program and the standby card cannot resize the output. This node is what you leave sitting on 'standby' during a hold and flip to 'program' when the segment starts. Its output is ALSO the preview bus source (the operator previews the pending state here, before the DBO stage).
steps.geometry_out: the selected state (program or standby) at program res

verify.pass_if: shows program at index 0, the STANDBY slate at index 1

steps.note: THE DBO KILL -- the instant blackout, stacked on top of the state stage. in0=OUT_stateout, in1=OUT_black; index driven by 'dbo' (0 = pass the state through, 1 = INSTANT full-frame black). blend=off is MANDATORY here -- a DBO is a deterministic jump to black, never a dissolve; blend=on would leave the audience on a half-lit frame mid-panic. This switch's output IS the program bus that the audience receives, so it must cut to black no matter what the state stage is doing. The fastest, most reliable kill is a DIRECT set_par index=1 on THIS node (no cook chain, no dependency); a hardware panic button reaches it as a bound toggle (next step). Because switchTOP replaces (does not composite), index=1 gives clean opaque black with zero content bleed. outputresolution=custom at program res.
steps.geometry_out: the program-out bus: live content OR instant black

verify.pass_if: index 0 = the live/standby content, index 1 = full opaque black
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_program_bus at dbo=0 then set_par index=1 -- the frame goes fully black instantly and cleanly

steps.note: DATA-ONLY DRIVE for a HARDWARE / external panic path (optional -- the direct set_par index=1 is the primary instant kill). bind_chop binds the constantCHOP's 'dbo' channel to the DBO switchTOP's index param and 'state' to the STATE switchTOP's index, so an external source flips them without any expression. For a real panic BUTTON or hold switch on a console, feed an oscinCHOP / midiinCHOP button channel into (or in place of) the constantCHOP and bind THAT channel to the DBO index -- a physical button then blacks the show. A CHOP toggle bound to a parameter is pure data (same risk class as the export flag); no code, no callback. Keep exactly ONE driver per parameter (a bind and a manual set_par fight -- pick the console-bound path for a manned show, the direct set_par for AI/operator-in-the-loop).

key_params.chan -> par: OUT_ctrlchan 'dbo' -> DBO switchTOP index ; OUT_ctrlchan 'state' -> STATE switchTOP index
key_params.external button: oscinCHOP/midiinCHOP button channel -> bind onto the DBO index for a physical panic button

steps.geometry_out: (binding -- channels now drive the switch indices)

verify.pass_if: the DBO switch index shows as bound/exported (or held at a literal for the set_par path)

steps.note: THE PREVIEW BUS -- the second output tap that makes this a preview-vs-program rig. Wire OUT_stateout (the PRE-DBO state) into this null so the operator can watch the queued/held source on a preview monitor even while the program bus is blacked out -- the classic 'what's next' vs 'what's live' split. Downstream this null feeds a preview monitor (a windowCOMP on the operator display, or an ndioutTOP to a preview screen, active OFF, wire-only) -- the physical preview monitor is the human's. Keep it tapping OUT_stateout so a DBO on program does NOT blank the preview (the operator must still see the pending content to decide when to restore). A fuller design gives the preview its own switch to cue a source independently of program (variant).
steps.geometry_out: the preview image (pending/held content), independent of the DBO

verify.pass_if: shows the queued/held content even when program is blacked out

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: the panic button + the decision to kill)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === The MCP builds and wires the entire safety layer -- black canvas, standby graphic, state + DBO switches, control channels, preview bus -- and can itself fire the kill (set_par index=1) or bind a console button to it. What it CANNOT do: decide WHEN to black out (a performer falls, wrong content loads, a rights-holder pulls a cue) -- that judgement is the operator's -- and it cannot press a physical panic button or plug in the OSC/MIDI console; those are on-site hardware. WHAT THE MCP DOES on cue: set_par index=1 on the DBO switch for an instant kill, index=0 to restore, and set the 'state' channel to sit on standby between segments. Downstream is WIRE-ONLY: OUT_program_bus and OUT_preview hand off via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output to their windowCOMP (not opened) / moviefileoutTOP (record OFF) / ndioutTOP (active OFF) -- the operator actuates the physical output. There is no dedicated 'blackout'/'DBO'/'panic' op in the catalog; this switch-over-black network IS the data-only primitive.
steps.geometry_out: the show blacks out / restores / holds on the operator's cue

verify.pass_if: DBO index flips 0<->1 on command; standby state selectable

recipes.classify: instant BLACKOUT / DBO / dead black out / kill to black / cut to black / panic button / emergency stop the show / STANDBY holding slide / hold state / house-open holding card / preview vs program / preview bus / program bus / go-to-black safety layer / operator safety / redundancy hold -- the every-show kill-to-black and standby rig
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY, no code path. The safety layer is a switch-over-black network: an opaque black constantTOP, a program nullTOP tap, a standby textTOP/moviefileinTOP, a state switchTOP, a DBO switchTOP, a control constantCHOP, and a preview nullTOP -- all created / wired / parameterized by the bridge. The DBO is fired the fastest way by a literal set_par index=1 (no cook dependency), or by binding a constantCHOP / oscinCHOP / midiinCHOP toggle channel to the index via bind_chop (pure data, same risk class as the export flag -- no expression, no callback, no script). HUMAN / ON-SITE: the DECISION to kill and the physical panic button / console are the operator's; the MCP can only execute the cut it is told to. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: OUT_program_bus and OUT_preview terminate in a windowCOMP (not opened), moviefileoutTOP (record OFF), or ndioutTOP/syphonspoutoutTOP (active DEFAULT ON -> MUST set OFF) via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output; nothing here actuates a physical output. HONEST GAPS: TouchDesigner has NO dedicated blackout / DBO / panic / standby operator -- this typed switch-over-black rig IS the primitive, and a helper build_blackout(program, standby, res) is the natural wrapper. Use switchTOP (hard cut) for the DBO, not crossTOP; a crossTOP fade-to-black is a distinct softer variant, never the emergency path. NC render cap 1280 for previews; swap resolutionw/h for 1080/4K delivery -- topology identical.
tips: Use switchTOP with blend=off for the DBO -- it is an INSTANT hard cut to black; crossTOP dissolves and must never be the panic path (offer it only as a deliberate fade-to-black cue).
Fastest, most reliable kill = a direct set_par index=1 on the DBO switch: no CHOP cook, no bind, no dependency chain that could stall. Bind a console button only for a manned show.
The black constantTOP must be OPAQUE (alpha 1.0) -- a DBO replaces the program, it does not overlay it; a transparent black lets content bleed through on a compositing downstream.
Force outputresolution=custom at program res on the black canvas, both switches, and the standby card -- a 256px black layer resizes the switch output and the kill looks wrong.
Tap OUT_stateout (pre-DBO) for the preview bus so a program blackout does NOT blank the preview -- the operator must keep seeing the pending content to know when to restore.

Keep exactly ONE driver per switch index -- a bind_chop and a manual set_par on the same param fight; choose the console-bound toggle for a manned desk, the direct set_par for AI/operator-in-the-loop.
The standby card must be a full opaque slate (bgalpha 1.0), never white-on-transparent -- a projector receiving unpremultiplied white reads as a blank or checkerboard.
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_blackout(program_tap, standby='STANDBY'|clip, res) -> black canvas + standby + state switch + DBO switch + control CHOP + preview null, wired, in one call.
variants: moving_standby: swap the STANDBY textTOP for a moviefileinTOP holding loop (idle animation / slow logo) as in1 of the state switch -- it loops by default (textendleft/right=cycle); cue it with pulse(cuepulse) if you want it to restart on entry.

fade_to_black: replace the DBO switchTOP with a crossTOP (in0=state, in1=black) driven by a bound 0..1 ramp for a soft, timed fade-to-black cue -- a SEPARATE, non-emergency transition; keep the hard switchTOP DBO alongside it for the actual panic.

independent_preview: give the preview bus its OWN switchTOP so the operator can cue any source to preview (program, standby, an incoming clip) independently of what program is showing -- true preview/program isolation like a broadcast M/E.

console_panic_button: wire an oscinCHOP or midiinCHOP button channel and bind_chop it onto the DBO switch index so a physical panic button / console GPI blacks the show; a hold switch drives the state index the same way.

multi_bus_safety: duplicate the DBO switch per output bus (per projector / per zone) fed from one shared black constantTOP so a single 'dbo' channel blacks every output at once, or per-bus channels black them independently.

recipes.title: Ingest a LIVE external source (SDI/HDMI capture card / NDI / ST 2110 / Syphon-Spout / TouchIn) and remap it onto projection surfaces (videodeviceinTOP|ndiinTOP|st2110inTOP -> nullTOP tap -> cornerpinTOP warp -> matteTOP holdout -> OUT_aligned) -- the INGEST twin of the output recipes
recipes.summary: The content-source mirror of the OUT recipes: instead of playing a file, CAPTURE a live external video signal and warp it onto the mapped surfaces. A capture op brings the signal into a TOP -- videodeviceinTOP for an SDI/HDMI card (Blackmagic / AJA / Datapath / Deltacast; set driver + device, deinterlace an interlaced feed, pick signalformat), or ndiinTOP for a network NDI source, st2110inTOP for a broadcast SMPTE 2110 IP flow (needs an st2110deviceCHOP + an SDP or NMOS setup), syphonspoutinTOP for a same-machine Syphon/Spout share, or touchinTOP for another TouchDesigner instance over the network. That live feed is tapped through a nullTOP (OUT_source) so the physical source can be swapped without rewiring, then it enters the SAME warp/mask chain the file-based mappers use: a cornerpinTOP crops the live sub-region (Extract page) and keystones it onto the surface (Pin page, extend=zero + bgcolor alpha 0 so outside the quad is transparent), and a matteTOP confines it to a surface holdout / knocks out spill using a mask on its input. A final nullTOP (OUT_aligned) hands off WIRE-ONLY to the output lane. KEY GOTCHA: capture ops default outputresolution=useinput -- a card negotiating 1080i or an odd signalformat will drive the whole chain at the wrong size or field order; force the field handling (deinterlace) at the capture op and set the chain to the projector canvas res downstream. CONTRAST: realtime_input_driver ingests control DATA (a CHOP of numbers) and vision_interactive_mask ingests a camera only to derive a MASK -- this recipe ingests the actual VIDEO as the projected content. HUMAN/HARDWARE BOUNDARY: the capture hardware (card, NIC, cabling) and the physical signal feed (a switcher, media server, camera, or playback deck upstream) are on-site and cannot be emitted -- the MCP builds the ingest+warp network and sets every param, but a person plugs in and confirms the signal.

steps.note: PRIMARY CAPTURE = an SDI/HDMI signal off a capture card. Set driver to the card's SDK (blackmagic / aja / datapath / deltacast -- the four pro capture families; also bluefish444), then pick the device from that driver's enumerated list (refreshdevices pulse repopulates it). For an INTERLACED feed (1080i59.94, PAL/NTSC SD) set deinterlace to bob (motion-adaptive per-field) or even/odd (weave a single field) -- leaving it off on interlaced source combs on motion. signalformat is a device-populated menu: leave blank to auto-negotiate or pin it to the exact format the upstream deck outputs (e.g. '1080p5994') so a re-plug does not renegotiate to the wrong mode. quadlink=on for 4x 3G-SDI 4K; inputbitdepth fixed10 for 10-bit SDI. active=on keeps it capturing. This op has NO inputs (maxinputs 0) -- it is a generator.

key_params.active: on

steps.geometry_out: live captured video frame from the SDI/HDMI card

verify.pass_if: resolution/format reported matches the feed (not the 256 default); frame updates
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_capture -- the live card image appears (a person must have the signal plugged in for this to be non-black)

steps.note: NETWORK / IP INGEST ALTERNATIVES (use ONE of these as the spine instead of the card). ndiinTOP receives a network NDI source: set name to the discovered sender (a device-populated menu), bandwidth=high for full quality (low = proxy), hwdecode=on to offload to the GPU. SIBLING INGEST OPS (same role, different transport, all real ops -- swap the create tool): st2110inTOP for a broadcast SMPTE ST 2110 IP flow (wire an st2110deviceCHOP carrying the NIC/PTP config into st2110devicechop, then either paste the stream's SDP into videosdp with setupmode=sdpparameters, or use setupmode=nmos; deinterlace as needed); syphonspoutinTOP for a SAME-MACHINE GPU share from another app (Spout on Windows / Syphon on macOS -- set sendername or usespoutactivesender=on); touchinTOP for video from another TouchDesigner instance over TCP (set address + port, active=on). Pick the transport the venue actually feeds; the rest of the chain is identical.
steps.geometry_out: live captured video frame from the network/IP/share source

verify.pass_if: sender resolved and a frame is arriving (non-black once the upstream is live)

steps.note: STABLE INGEST TAP. Wire whichever capture op you chose (OUT_capture or OUT_ndisrc / the 2110 / spout / touchin op) into this null; every downstream node targets this NAME so the physical source can be swapped card<->NDI<->2110 without rewiring the warp chain. If the show needs LIVE source-switching between two feeds, insert a switchTOP BEFORE this null (index driven by a data channel -- a constantCHOP/keyframeCHOP exported onto switchTOP.index, data-only) and tap the switch here instead. Force outputresolution=custom at the projector/canvas res here so a card negotiating a smaller frame is scaled to the working size once, cleanly.
steps.geometry_out: the chosen live source on one stable, correctly-sized tap

verify.pass_if: fed by exactly one active capture op; resolution == working res

steps.note: WARP THE LIVE FEED ONTO THE SURFACE. Same 2-page model as the quad mapper: EXTRACT page (extracttl/tr/bl/br, unit fraction) crops the sub-region of the LIVE frame to use (identity = full frame TL(0,1) TR(1,1) BL(0,0) BR(1,0)); PIN page (pintopleft/pintopright/pinbotleft/pinbotright, fraction of the canvas) places + keystones the feed onto the surface. mapping=perspective for a true flat keystone (bilinear bows long edges). extend=zero and bgcolor alpha 0 so everything outside the pinned quad is transparent for clean downstream compositing. outputresolution=custom at canvas res (NOT useinput -- else the warp runs at the card's frame size). Wire OUT_source -> in0. For a live feed the extract crop is how you frame a camera/switcher output onto the exact surface region.
steps.geometry_out: the live feed keystoned onto its surface region, transparent elsewhere

verify.pass_if: live content lands inside the four pin corners; rest transparent

steps.note: CONFINE / HOLDOUT. matteTOP takes the warped feed on one input and a MASK on another (maxinputs 3: input to be matted + matte-source) and cuts the content to the mask using mattechannel (alpha / luminance / a specific channel). Use it to knock out spill past the real surface edge or to hold out an actor/architectural feature: feed a white-on-black surface mask (a rectangleTOP, a rampTOP feather, or output_spill_garbage_mask's alpha) as the matte source with mattechannel=alpha (or luminance for a grayscale mask). switchinputs swaps which input is content vs matte if wired backwards. For a simple rectangular surface with no spill you can SKIP this step and go straight to the aligned null. Wire OUT_warped as the content input.
steps.geometry_out: the warped live feed confined to the surface holdout mask

verify.pass_if: content appears only inside the mask; spill/holdout regions are transparent

steps.note: STABLE ALIGNED TAP -- the deliverable frame for this ingested surface. Wire OUT_masked (or OUT_warped if no matte) into this. Every downstream output op targets this NAME so the physical output can be swapped without rewiring. Hand off WIRE-ONLY to the output lane (output_handoff / projection_align_and_output). For MULTIPLE surfaces each fed by the same or different live sources, duplicate the cornerpin(+matte) pair per surface and composite them over black exactly as multi_quad_mapper does -- this recipe is the per-surface ingest branch that feeds that compositor.
steps.geometry_out: final ingested + warped + masked frame, canvas res, ready for wire-only output

verify.pass_if: live source correctly placed on its surface region at canvas res
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_aligned -- the live external signal reads as mapped content on the surface

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: capture hardware + the physical signal feed)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === The MCP builds the capture op + the whole warp/mask chain and sets every param (driver, device, deinterlace, signalformat, all extract*/pin* corners). What it CANNOT do: install/route the capture card, plug the SDI/HDMI cable, configure the NIC/PTP for a 2110 flow, start the upstream switcher/media-server/camera, or SEE that a real signal is present -- until a person connects the feed the capture op reads black. It also cannot judge where the pinned quad lands on the real surface; the projectionist measures that on site and the MEASURED corner numbers are typed back via set_par on the cornerpin's raw pin* components (pintopleftx/pintoplefty/.../pinbotrighty). Signal format, field order (interlaced vs progressive), and cabling are physical facts the operator confirms.
steps.geometry_out: a real live signal, correctly framed, once hardware is connected and corners measured

verify.pass_if: capture op reports a real signal format and a live (non-black) frame

steps.note: WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT HAND-OFF. Route OUT_aligned to the physical output via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output -- do NOT rebuild the output stage here. All terminal ops are BUILT but never actuated by us: windowCOMP not opened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF; ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active DEFAULT ON -> set OFF; st2110outTOP active default ON -> OFF. A global cornerpinTOP keystone AFTER OUT_aligned can correct the whole projector frame at once (distinct from the per-surface warp here).
steps.geometry_out: (reference -- the output lane consumes OUT_aligned)

verify.pass_if: OUT_aligned is the single tap the output lane reads

recipes.classify: CAPTURE a live external video source and project it -- SDI / HDMI / capture card (Blackmagic / AJA / Datapath / Deltacast / Bluefish), NDI network video, SMPTE ST 2110 / 2110 broadcast IP, Syphon / Spout GPU share, TouchIn from another TouchDesigner; live input, live feed, ingest, incoming signal, camera/switcher/media-server/playback-deck feed, IMAG, remap a live source onto surfaces, warp/keystone a live camera; the ingest twin of the output recipes
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the capture op (videodeviceinTOP / ndiinTOP / st2110inTOP / syphonspoutinTOP / touchinTOP), the stable ingest null, the cornerpinTOP warp, the matteTOP holdout, and the aligned null -- all created / wired / parameterized by the bridge. No script/execute/cplusplus op, no parameter expressions, no callbacks DAT anywhere; every corner + every capture setting is a literal value via the create tool or set_par. Live source-switching is data-only (a switchTOP.index driven by an exported CHOP value), never an expression. (2) HUMAN / HARDWARE: the capture card / NIC / cabling and the physical signal feed (switcher, media server, camera, playback deck) are on-site -- the MCP cannot install hardware, route cables, or start the upstream source, and until a person connects the feed the capture op reads black; the on-site corner alignment is also human, its measured numbers typed back via set_par on the cornerpin pin* components. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: nothing here fires; downstream terminal ops (windowCOMP not opened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF; ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active DEFAULT ON -> MUST set OFF; st2110outTOP active default ON -> OFF) are handled by output_handoff / projection_align_and_output. HONEST GAPS: there is NO capture-card auto-detect or signal-present sensor the MCP can read to prove a feed is live -- top_info shows the negotiated format but a black frame vs a disconnected cable look identical from here; the operator confirms signal. st2110inTOP additionally needs an st2110deviceCHOP configured with the venue's NIC + PTP + SDP, which describes physical network infrastructure a person provisions. Color legalization / grade of the ingested signal is out of scope here -- route OUT_aligned through color_grade_lut_delivery for LUT/OCIO delivery color. NC build caps live render at 1280; swap resolutionw/h for 4K, topology identical.
tips: Force deinterlace at the CAPTURE op for any interlaced feed (1080i, SD) -- bob for motion, even/odd to weave one field; leaving it off combs on every motion frame and no downstream node fixes it cleanly.
signalformat is device-populated: leave blank to auto-negotiate, or PIN the exact upstream mode so a cable re-plug does not renegotiate to a wrong resolution/rate mid-show.

Capture ops default outputresolution=useinput -- set the ingest null to custom canvas res so a card negotiating a smaller/odd frame is scaled once, cleanly, instead of propagating the wrong size through the warp.
extract* crops the LIVE source sub-region; pin* places + keystones the quad on the canvas -- never swap the two pages (same trap as the quad mapper).
Keep the cornerpin extend=zero and bgcolor alpha 0 so outside-the-quad pixels are transparent -- required for clean over-compositing when several ingested surfaces stack.

For live A/B source switching insert a switchTOP before the ingest null and drive its index with an EXPORTED CHOP value (constant/keyframe) -- data-only; a CHOP cannot fire a pulse but it can set an index.
st2110inTOP is not standalone: wire an st2110deviceCHOP (NIC/PTP) and paste the stream SDP (setupmode=sdpparameters) or use NMOS -- without the device CHOP it has nothing to receive.
HELPER CANDIDATE: ingest_source(kind='card'|'ndi'|'2110'|'spout'|'touchin', target_res=[w,h]) -> the right capture op + a stable custom-res null in one call.
variants: card_sdi: videodeviceinTOP, driver=blackmagic/aja/datapath/deltacast, deinterlace=bob for 1080i, signalformat pinned -- the standard broadcast/stage capture-card path.
ndi_network: ndiinTOP from a media server or a second machine on the LAN (bandwidth=high, hwdecode=on) -- no capture card needed, just the network.
st2110_broadcast: st2110inTOP + st2110deviceCHOP (NIC/PTP) + SDP/NMOS -- SMPTE 2110 IP video for broadcast/large-venue infrastructure.
spout_syphon_share: syphonspoutinTOP from another GPU app on the same machine (a game engine, a VJ app) -- zero-copy local share, no cabling.
live_source_switch: a switchTOP before the ingest null, index driven by an exported data channel, to cut between two live feeds (e.g. camera A / camera B) inside the same warp chain.

depth_camera_source: a depth sensor's colour/IR/depth stream (orbbecTOP / realsenseTOP / kinectazureTOP, all now in-catalog) is a live capture source too -- tap it through OUT_source and run the same cornerpin/matte warp chain to remap a live depth/IR feed onto surfaces (distinct from vision_interactive_mask, which derives a MASK rather than projecting the feed).

recipes.title: N genuinely independent output zones (per-zone content chain -> per-zone resolutionTOP -> per-zone nullTOP tap -> its own windowCOMP(justifyoffsetto=specifydisplay) and/or per-zone ndiout/spout, all WIRE-ONLY) -- distinct from direct_projector_output's ONE spanning window
recipes.summary: Drive N INDEPENDENT output zones from one TouchDesigner instance, where each zone has its OWN content, its OWN resolution, and its OWN physical destination -- e.g. a lobby screen, a stage-left projector, and a bar-area LED feed all running different material at once. This is explicitly NOT direct_projector_output / projection_align_and_output, which build ONE large spanning window across several displays that together show a single canvas (a video wall / edge-blend). Here each zone is a self-contained chain: an independent content/cue source -> a resolutionTOP pinning THAT zone's native resolution -> a stable nullTOP tap (OUT_zoneN) -> its own terminal. The terminal is per zone and independent: a dedicated windowCOMP whose justifyoffsetto=specifydisplay + display index sends it to one physical monitor/projector output, and/or a per-zone ndioutTOP / syphonspoutoutTOP for a network/inter-app destination. The nullTOP-per-zone convention is the spine: every terminal targets a zone's null by NAME so a destination can be reassigned without rewiring the content. KEY GOTCHA: windowCOMP has maxinputs=0 -- you do NOT wire a TOP into it; you set its winop parameter to the zone null's path (e.g. winop='OUT_zone0'). And WIRE-ONLY holds throughout: windowCOMP is never opened (winopen is a pulse we never fire), ndiout/spout default active ON so each MUST be set active OFF. The human/hardware split is mapping each windowCOMP's display index to the correct physical GPU head / projector, which depends on the on-site display topology (EDID order) and is verified by a person.

steps.note: ZONE 0 INDEPENDENT CONTENT (repeat this whole zone chain per zone). Each zone has its OWN source -- a distinct clip, generative composite, still, or the tail of another recipe (media_clip_player, a cue transport, signal_ingest_remap). This is what makes the zones independent: unlike direct_projector_output where every output shows a slice of ONE shared canvas, here each zone's content is unrelated to the others'. Set file via set_par with an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path UNDER the working dir after create. For a cue-driven zone, drive this source's selection from a per-zone timer/lookup rather than sharing a global transport.

This also guards each zone against the 256px default trap individually. Contrast direct_projector_output, where a single canvas res spans all outputs; here the per-zone resolutionTOP is what lets zones differ.

Wire OUT_zone0 -> this. Give each zone a DISTINCT source name (name='zone0_lobby') so downstream receivers can tell the zones apart on the network. For an inter-app local destination use syphonspoutoutTOP (active off, distinct sendername per zone) instead. This is the per-zone twin of the single-feed output ops -- N independent senders, one per zone.

Reach for THAT recipe when your outputs are tiles of one big picture (a video wall, a wide edge-blend). Reach for THIS recipe when your outputs are genuinely independent zones showing different material. If a show mixes both -- say two independent zones where one zone is itself a 2-projector blend -- build the blended zone via direct_projector_output and treat its final null as one OUT_zoneN in this recipe's zone bus.

For each zone's chosen terminal, reuse output_handoff / projection_align_and_output for the actual WIRE-ONLY hand-off conventions rather than re-deriving them here: windowCOMP left unopened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF if a zone is recorded; ndiout/syphonspoutout/st2110out active OFF. output_handoff also covers per-zone color/level finishing before the terminal. Apply it once per OUT_zoneN so every zone terminates consistently. Do NOT rebuild the hand-off logic per zone -- reference the shared recipe.

steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === Which windowCOMP display INDEX lands on which physical monitor/projector depends on the on-site DISPLAY TOPOLOGY -- the GPU head order, EDID/enumeration order, and how the Windows display arrangement is set -- which the MCP cannot see. On site the projectionist confirms display index N shows on the intended output (open each window, or check the Window Placement dialog) and, if the enumeration differs from the authoring guess, the corrected display indices are typed back via set_par onto each windowCOMP display param. The MCP builds every zone chain, sets every winop / justifyoffsetto=specifydisplay / display index / per-zone name numerically, and leaves each terminal dormant; the human validates the physical mapping and enables each terminal (open window / set active on) at showtime. Auto-detecting the display topology is a real GAP -- monitorsDAT can LIST displays but the intended-zone-to-head assignment is a human decision.

key_params.set_par (after operator confirms head or: op=OUT_z0window, pars={display:<confirmed head index>}; repeat per zone window

steps.geometry_out: each zone window landing on its intended physical output once head indices are confirmed

recipes.classify: drive MULTIPLE independent output zones / separate screens / different displays each showing DIFFERENT content at once from one TouchDesigner -- lobby screen plus stage projector plus bar LED, multi-output, multi-zone, per-zone content and resolution, one window per display, per-zone NDI/Spout; NOT one big spanning canvas or edge-blend (that is direct_projector_output) -- these are N genuinely independent zones
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: N independent zone chains -- per-zone content source, per-zone resolutionTOP (each zone its own resolution), per-zone nullTOP tap, and per-zone terminal (windowCOMP with winop set to the zone null + justifyoffsetto=specifydisplay + display index, and/or ndioutTOP/syphonspoutoutTOP with a distinct name) -- all created/wired/parameterized by the bridge. No script/execute/cplusplus, no parameter expressions, no callbacks DAT; every display index, resolution, and source name is a literal set via the create tool or set_par. windowCOMP has maxinputs=0: the zone TOP is bound through the winop PARAMETER (a path string), not a wired input -- a wire attempt is meaningless here. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT throughout: windowCOMP is never opened (winopen/setperform are pulses we never fire); ndioutTOP / syphonspoutoutTOP default active=ON so each MUST be set active=OFF; the operator opens windows and enables senders on site. HUMAN / ON-SITE: mapping each zone's display index to the correct physical GPU head/projector depends on the display topology (EDID/enumeration order, Windows arrangement) which the MCP cannot see -- monitorsDAT can LIST attached displays but the intended zone-to-head assignment is a human decision typed back via set_par. RELATIONSHIP: this is the deliberate complement to direct_projector_output / projection_align_and_output (ONE spanning window / edge-blend across displays); a mixed show can nest a blended zone as one OUT_zoneN. NC render cap 1280 -- swap per-zone resolution vectors for real device resolutions; topology identical.
tips: windowCOMP takes NO wired input (maxinputs=0) -- bind the zone by setting winop='OUT_zoneN' (a path), not by connecting a TOP. A dangling window with an empty winop shows nothing.

One windowCOMP per zone, each with justifyoffsetto=specifydisplay and its OWN display index -- this is the independent-zones pattern; direct_projector_output instead uses ONE window spanning displays for a shared canvas.
Per-zone resolutionTOP is what lets zones differ -- a 1080 monitor, a 1280x800 projector, a 512 LED strip can coexist because each chain pins its own res. There is no shared canvas res here.
Give each ndiout/spout a DISTINCT name/sendername (zone0_lobby, zone1_stage) or network receivers cannot tell the zones apart -- duplicate names collide.
WIRE-ONLY: never fire winopen; set every ndiout/spout active=OFF. The operator opens windows and enables senders on site -- leaving them hot claims devices/streams unbidden.
The OUT_zoneN nulls ARE the zone bus: name terminals against the null so a destination can be reassigned without rewiring content -- the same discipline as OUT_aligned but one per zone.
monitorsDAT lists attached displays (index, resolution, position) -- read it to sanity-check how many heads exist, but the zone-to-head assignment is still a human decision confirmed on site.
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_zones(zones=[{content, res, display?, ndi_name?}]) -> per-zone content+resolution+null+terminal chains, all dormant, in one call.
variants: windows_only: every zone terminates in its own windowCOMP on a distinct GPU head (specifydisplay + display index) -- the classic multi-monitor/multi-projector independent-output rig, no network.
network_only: every zone terminates in a distinct-named ndioutTOP (or syphonspoutoutTOP) feeding separate media servers / apps -- no GPU-attached windows; all active=OFF until enabled.
hybrid_terminals: some zones drive a physical windowCOMP while others drive a network sender -- mix per zone off the same OUT_zoneN bus.
nested_blend_zone: one zone is itself a multi-projector edge-blend -- build that zone via direct_projector_output and feed its final null in as a single OUT_zoneN, the rest independent.
mixed_resolution_zones: zones at different native resolutions (1080 monitor + 1280x800 projector + 512 LED) -- each per-zone resolutionTOP pins its own; the whole point of independent chains.

recipes.title: Per-output white-point / gamma / luminance MATCH across a projector array (per-projector levelTOP luma trim -> channelmixTOP white balance -> opencolorioTOP gamut/CDL -> feathered rampTOP uniformity mask -> layoutTOP side-by-side match wall -> OUT_uniform) -- the color-uniformity step BEYOND black-level and edge-blend
recipes.summary: When N projectors light one continuous surface, geometry (multi_quad_mapper / multiprojector_edge_blend) and black-level (multiprojector_blacklevel_mask) are only two of the three matches -- the third is COLOR: every lamp ages differently, so one projector reads warm/green/bright and its neighbor cool/magenta/dim and the seam shows as a colour step even when the pixels line up. This recipe builds a per-output correction CHAIN that sits on each projector's already-aligned, already-blended feed: a levelTOP trims black-point / white-point / gamma (luminance + contrast match), a channelmixTOP scales the R->R / G->G / B->B gains for per-channel WHITE BALANCE, an opencolorioTOP normalizes the delivery gamut/transfer (Rec709 / sRGB / DCI-P3) and optionally applies an ASC-CDL slope/offset/power trim, and a radial feathered rampTOP multiplies a UNIFORMITY / vignette-compensation mask to even out a hot centre or dark corners within a single projector. All N corrected feeds tile into ONE layoutTOP so the operator sees every output side by side and matches them by eye. DATA-ONLY mechanism: every correction is a literal parameter number set via the create tool or set_par -- no expressions, no callbacks, no shader. KEY GOTCHA: the correction VALUES are meaningless without a real measurement -- a colorimeter reading off the actual surface (or the projectionist's trained eye comparing lamps on the wall) is the HUMAN input; the MCP builds the whole chain and types the measured numbers back. Order matters: luma trim (level) BEFORE white balance (channelmix) BEFORE gamut (ocio) BEFORE the uniformity mask, or a later stage undoes an earlier one.

steps.note: PER-OUTPUT TAP = the stable input handle for ONE projector's already-aligned + edge-blended feed (the OUT_aligned / OUT_blended null from projection_align_and_output or multiprojector_edge_blend for projector 0). Every correction node below hangs off THIS name so the physical routing can change without rewiring the correction chain, and so the same chain is duplicated identically per projector (OUT_projfeed0, OUT_projfeed1 ...). Wire the upstream aligned feed -> this null. Do NOT correct BEFORE the blend -- colour trims belong on the final per-projector image the lamp actually throws, downstream of geometry and edge-blend, upstream of the wire-only output op.

key_params.(wire): upstream OUT_aligned / OUT_blended for projector 0 -> in0

steps.geometry_out: one projector's aligned+blended feed, tapped

verify.pass_if: resolution == that projector's canvas res; image is the aligned/blended feed, not a default sample

steps.note: LUMINANCE + CONTRAST MATCH (do this FIRST). blacklevel lifts/lowers the floor so every projector's darkest pixel reads the same; brightness1 + outhigh trim the white-point / peak so a dimmer aged lamp is pulled down to match (never push a weak lamp UP past 1.0 -- match DOWN to the dimmest projector so all can reach it); gamma1 matches the mid-tone curve (the usual culprit when blacks and whites align but mids look muddy on one unit); contrast fine-tunes. inlow/inhigh + outlow/outhigh give an explicit input->output remap if you prefer ranges over black/gamma. Leave the per-channel low*/high* at default here -- white balance is the next node's job (keeping luma and WB on separate nodes makes each measurable independently). The measured target comes from the colorimeter / eye step; here you build the node and set an identity or first estimate.

key_params.blacklevel: raise to match the darkest projector's floor (0 = identity)
key_params.brightness1: <=1.0 to pull a hot lamp down to the dimmest unit
key_params.gamma1: match mid-tone curve (1.0 = identity; ~0.9-1.1 typical trim)
key_params.outhigh: <1.0 to cap peak white to the dimmest projector

steps.geometry_out: projector feed with matched black/white/gamma

verify.pass_if: black floor and peak white visually match the reference projector's trim

steps.note: PER-CHANNEL WHITE BALANCE = correct a warm/cool/tinted lamp. channelmixTOP maps each output channel from a weighted sum of the inputs; for a straight white-balance GAIN you scale the diagonal: red1 (R->R), green2 (G->G), blue3 (B->B) -- e.g. a projector reading green gets green2 < 1 and/or red1/blue3 > 1 to rebalance to neutral white. The off-diagonal terms (red2, red3, green1 ...) stay 0 for pure WB but exist for a full 3x3 colour-matrix correction (cross-channel, e.g. matching a projector with an odd primary/colour-wheel). constant1..4 add a lift per channel if needed. Keep this AFTER the luma trim so gains act on already-matched levels. Measure the WB target on the real surface (a grey card + colorimeter, or eye) -- the values are the human's, the node is the MCP's.

key_params.green2: G gain (1.0 identity; <1 kills a green cast)
key_params.red2/red3/green1/blue1: 0 for pure WB; non-zero only for a full colour-matrix

steps.geometry_out: white-balanced projector feed

verify.pass_if: a white patch reads neutral and matches the reference projector's white
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_wb0 next to the reference projector's OUT_wb -- their white patches read as the same neutral

expr_opportunity.why: per-projector WB gains are often derived from a measured target-white / measured-white ratio, which reads naturally as a small parameter expression (target_r/measured_r ...) rather than a hand-typed constant
expr_opportunity.propose_via: expr_reference then set_expr on channelmixTOP red1/green2/blue3
expr_opportunity.consent: needs allow_expr (default OFF); data-only fallback (the actual step) = compute the ratio outside and set_par literal gains, or drive them from a constantCHOP the operator tweaks

steps.note: DELIVERY GAMUT / TRANSFER NORMALIZE + optional ASC-CDL trim. Point config at the OCIO config and use srccs -> display/view (useoutput=on) to land every projector in the SAME target colour space (Rec709 / sRGB / DCI-P3 for a cinema projector) so mismatched source gamuts don't reintroduce a colour step. For a per-projector creative/measured trim without touching level/channelmix, set cdlmode=values and use the ASC-CDL controls: slope (gain per channel), offset (lift per channel), power (gamma per channel) + saturation -- the industry-standard grade primitive a colourist/projectionist will recognise. gain + gamma are quick global scalars. This is also where a supplied .cc/.ccc correction file (ccfile, cdlmode=ccfile) loads. Keep it AFTER white balance so gamut mapping sees neutral white. If you only need level+channelmix, leave useoutput off and cdlmode off (identity passthrough).

key_params.config: OCIO config path (absolute, under working dir)
key_params.useoutput: on to apply the Display/View transform

steps.geometry_out: gamut-normalized, CDL-trimmed projector feed

verify.pass_if: colour space landed in the target display/view; CDL trim visible if enabled (identity if off)

steps.note: UNIFORMITY / VIGNETTE-COMPENSATION MASK. A single projector is rarely flat across its own frame -- the centre is hotter than the corners (lens falloff, lamp hot-spot). Build a radial rampTOP (type=radial) whose bright centre / darker edge is the INVERSE of the projector's falloff, then MULTIPLY it into the feed (operand=multiply, combineinput=compres, swaporder as needed) to pull the hot centre down toward the corner level so the projector reads even. color white, position centred, period/phase shape the falloff radius; extendleft/extendright hold at the edge. Feather is inherent in the radial gradient (interpnotches=linear/hermite for a smooth curve). A rampTOP can also carry a per-corner uniformity notch table via its dat input for a measured 5- or 9-point grid. outputresolution=custom at the projector res so the mask aligns 1:1. This is a WITHIN-projector evenness fix, distinct from the BETWEEN-projector match above.
steps.geometry_out: radial uniformity-compensation mask at projector res

verify.pass_if: smooth radial falloff, white toward the hot region, dimmer where the projector is bright

steps.note: APPLY THE UNIFORMITY MASK + final clamp. Rather than a separate multiply node you may fold the mask in, but the clean data-only path is a second levelTOP as the FINAL guard on the corrected+masked feed: clamp on with clamplow/clamphigh so no correction pushes a value out of 0..1 (a lifted black or a >1 gain can clip on the projector otherwise), and a last gamma2/brightness2 nudge if the whole output needs a touch after masking. Wire the mask into the chain via a multiplyTOP (OUT_ocio0 x OUT_unimask0) feeding this node -- see the multiplyTOP in the manifest. This node is the per-projector deliverable's last colour touch before the match-wall preview.
steps.geometry_out: one projector's fully colour-matched + uniform feed

verify.pass_if: no clipped highlights/crushed blacks; feed matches the reference projector in level, WB, and evenness
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_uniform0 vs the reference projector's OUT_uniform -- black floor, white point, hue, and centre-to-corner evenness all match

steps.note: MATCH WALL = tile all N corrected outputs side by side so the operator judges the match at a glance (the whole point -- colour matching is comparative, not absolute). tops = OUT_uniform0, OUT_uniform1 ... OUT_uniformN; align=gridcols or horizlr; numrows/numcols to shape the grid; bgcolor black so gaps read neutral; outputresolution=custom. Feed a common test pattern (a grey ramp, a white field, a colour-bar rampTOP) through every projector's chain for this comparison so differences are obvious. This preview is a DIAGNOSTIC tap only -- it is NOT the projector feed; each projector still takes its own OUT_uniformN downstream. Save it for the operator (and the colorimeter step) to compare.
steps.geometry_out: N corrected projector feeds tiled for a side-by-side match check

verify.pass_if: all N tiles show the same test pattern with matched level/WB/evenness -- no visible tile stands out
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_matchwall on a grey field / colour bars -- adjacent tiles are indistinguishable in brightness, hue, and centre-to-corner falloff

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: colorimeter / projectionist-eye measurement on the real surface)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === The correction NUMBERS cannot be invented -- they come from measuring the actual projected light on the actual surface. A projectionist puts a colorimeter/spectroradiometer on the wall (or trusts a trained eye comparing lamps on a white field) and reads each projector's black level, peak white (nits), white-point (x,y or correlated colour temperature), and centre-to-corner falloff. WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds the full per-projector chain (level -> channelmix -> ocio -> uniformity mask -> guard level) and the match wall, and types the measured trims back via set_par: levelTOP blacklevel/brightness1/gamma1/outhigh, channelmixTOP red1/green2/blue3, opencolorioTOP slopex/offsetx/powerx (raw ASC-CDL components) or gain/gamma. The MCP cannot see colour or hold a meter; the human measures, the bridge parameterizes. Re-measure whenever a lamp is changed or after warm-up -- projector colour drifts with lamp hours and temperature.

key_params.set_par (after measurement): op=OUT_lumtrim0 pars={blacklevel,brightness1,gamma1,outhigh}; op=OUT_wb0 pars={red1,green2,blue3}; op=OUT_ocio0 pars={slopex,offsetx,powerx} (or gain,gamma)

steps.geometry_out: measured per-projector trims typed into the built chain

verify.pass_if: channelmix gains / level trims / CDL hold the measured on-site values (or identity/estimate for authoring)

steps.note: WIRE-ONLY HANDOFF. Each OUT_uniformN is the colour-corrected deliverable for projector N -- hand each to its own output op via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output (windowCOMP to that projector's display, or ndioutTOP / st2110outTOP / videodeviceoutTOP). Nothing here fires: windowCOMP not opened, ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active DEFAULT ON -> MUST set OFF, st2110outTOP.active default ON -> OFF. The match wall (OUT_matchwall) is a diagnostic and is NOT sent to any projector. Sibling recipes: multiprojector_edge_blend (geometry overlap + blend) and multiprojector_blacklevel_mask (raise the seam black floor) run BEFORE this colour pass -- this recipe completes the three-part projector-array match (geometry, black-level, colour).

key_params.per projector: OUT_uniformN -> its output op (active/record/winopen OFF -- wire-only)

steps.geometry_out: (reference -- each corrected feed handed off wire-only)

verify.pass_if: OUT_uniformN feeds one output op; that op's active/record is OFF

recipes.classify: make N projectors on one surface MATCH in colour -- white point / white balance / gamma / luminance / brightness match across a multi-projector array, colour uniformity, projector colour calibration, grey-scale match, lamp-to-lamp colour, vignette / hot-spot / centre-to-corner evenness compensation, ASC-CDL / OCIO per-projector trim; the colour step beyond edge-blend and black-level masking
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the entire per-projector correction chain -- the aligned-feed tap, the luminance levelTOP, the white-balance channelmixTOP, the gamut/CDL opencolorioTOP, the radial uniformity rampTOP + multiplyTOP, the guard levelTOP, and the layoutTOP match wall -- is created / wired / parameterized by the bridge. Every trim is a literal number (create tool or set_par); no expression, callback, or shader anywhere. The one optional code touchpoint (deriving WB gains from a measured ratio) is surfaced as an expr_opportunity (allow_expr, default OFF) with a data-only fallback, never baked in. (2) HUMAN / ON-SITE: the correction VALUES require a colorimeter/spectroradiometer reading (or a trained eye) on the real projected surface -- black level, peak nits, white-point, centre-to-corner falloff -- measured per projector and re-measured after lamp changes / warm-up. The MCP cannot see colour, hold a meter, or judge a match; it builds the chain and types the human's numbers back. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: nothing fires; each OUT_uniformN hands off via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output with the terminal op's active/record/winopen OFF (ndiout/spout/st2110out default ON -> set OFF). HONEST GAPS: there is NO dedicated projector-colour-calibration / colorimeter TOP in the catalog -- this chain is assembled from generic colour primitives; a true measured 3D-LUT correction would load via opencolorioTOP's file transform or a lookupTOP .cube (see color_grade_lut_delivery). SIBLINGS this completes: multiprojector_edge_blend (geometry + blend) and multiprojector_blacklevel_mask (seam black floor) -- run both BEFORE this colour pass. NC build cap renders live preview at 1280; swap resolutionw/h for the real projector res, topology identical.
tips: ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: luminance (level) -> white balance (channelmix) -> gamut/CDL (ocio) -> uniformity mask -> guard clamp. Re-order and a later stage silently undoes an earlier trim.

Match DOWN, never up: pull every projector toward the DIMMEST lamp's peak white (outhigh/brightness1 <= 1). You cannot make a weak lamp brighter than its maximum, so the array's ceiling is the worst unit.

channelmixTOP diagonal (red1/green2/blue3) = per-channel WB gain; the off-diagonal terms are a full colour matrix for a projector with an odd primary -- leave them 0 unless a straight WB won't converge.
