Feed a COMMON test pattern (grey ramp / white field / colour bars) through every projector's chain for the layoutTOP match wall -- differences on a flat field are obvious; differences on live content hide.

opencolorioTOP cdlmode=values gives the ASC-CDL slope/offset/power a colourist expects; raw set_par components are slopex/slopey/slopez, offsetx.., powerx.. -- the create tool takes the slope/offset/power vectors.

The radial uniformity rampTOP compensates WITHIN one projector (hot centre / dark corners); it is NOT the between-projector match -- keep the two masks conceptually separate or you'll chase your tail.
Colour drifts with lamp hours and temperature: re-run the colorimeter step after warm-up and after ANY lamp swap; the built chain stays, only the typed numbers change.
HELPER CANDIDATE: match_projector(feed, {black,white,gamma,wb_rgb,cdl}) -> level+channelmix+ocio+mask chain + a layoutTOP tile, in one call per projector.
variants: level_only: for a quick brightness/gamma match with no colour cast, build just the levelTOP (blacklevel/brightness1/gamma1/outhigh) + the match wall -- skip channelmix/ocio/mask.

cdl_grade: drive the whole per-projector trim from opencolorioTOP cdlmode=values (ASC-CDL slope/offset/power/saturation) so a colourist's .cc/.ccc file (cdlmode=ccfile) can be loaded directly per projector.

measured_lut: instead of parametric trims, load a measured correction as a 3D-LUT via opencolorioTOP's file transform or a lookupTOP .cube (hand off to color_grade_lut_delivery) -- for projectors needing a full characterised profile.
uniformity_grid: feed the rampTOP dat input a measured 5- or 9-point centre-to-corner luminance table for a precise within-projector evenness map instead of a single radial falloff.
full_array_wall: expand the layoutTOP to a grid (align=gridrows, numrows/numcols) covering every projector plus a reference tile, so the operator matches an 8- or 12-projector array in one view.

recipes.title: Content prep for SHEER / see-through surfaces -- scrim, gauze, HoloGauze, fog & water screen (mandatory BLACK bg constantTOP -> levelTOP black-crush -> crossTOP/layermixTOP front/back reveal -> flipTOP rear mirror -> cornerpinTOP steep keystone -> rampTOP+blurTOP edge feather -> compositeTOP over black -> OUT_sheeraligned, with an actor-safe holdout)
recipes.summary: Sheer media -- theatrical scrim, bobbinet gauze, HoloGauze, a fog screen or a water screen -- is nearly invisible until light hits it: it only shows the LIT pixels and lets everything else pass straight through to whatever is behind (a set, a performer, the back wall). That single fact drives the whole content prep and is the KEY GOTCHA: the background MUST be pure black, because any non-black value lifts the entire sheet into a visible grey haze that kills the see-through illusion and reveals the fabric. So the chain is: a mandatory BLACK constantTOP ground; a levelTOP BLACK-CRUSH that forces any codec/camera grey-lift, compression mush, or near-black detail hard to 0 so only the intended bright content survives; an optional layered FRONT/BACK reveal (crossTOP or layermixTOP dissolving a near layer to expose a far layer, the classic 'figure appears out of nothing' gauze effect, driven data-only by an lfoCHOP/keyframeCHOP on the cross via the EXPORT flag); a flipTOP that MIRRORS the image for REAR projection (sheer is almost always lit from behind so the audience reads it un-mirrored); a cornerpinTOP for the often STEEP keystone (a scrim/HoloGauze is frequently hung high and hit from a shallow floor angle); a rampTOP + blurTOP EDGE FEATHER so the content fades into the black surround instead of ending on a hard rectangle that would expose the sheet's border; then a compositeTOP stacks the feathered content OVER the black ground. Finally an ACTOR-SAFE HOLDOUT (reuse output_spill_garbage_mask) blacks out the region where a performer stands behind the scrim so projector light doesn't spill onto their face. DATA-ONLY: every value is a literal parameter; the reveal animates via a CHOP exported onto crossTOP.cross, never an expression. HUMAN boundary: hanging the scrim and measuring the actual throw/angle is on-site.

steps.note: MANDATORY BLACK GROUND -- the single most important node for sheer media. color [0,0,0], alpha 1.0 (opaque black), outputresolution=custom at the projector/canvas res (256px trap: leave it and the ground is 256x256). WHY BLACK IS NON-NEGOTIABLE: scrim/gauze/HoloGauze/fog/water only reflect the light that lands on them and transmit the rest -- a black pixel throws NO light, so the sheet stays invisible there and the audience sees THROUGH it; ANY grey/coloured pixel lights the fibres and the whole sheet materialises as a dull glowing rectangle, destroying the reveal and exposing the fabric weave. This ground is the base every layer composites over so nothing that isn't deliberately lit ever rises above black. Wire it as the FIRST input of the final compositeTOP.
steps.geometry_out: pure opaque-black canvas at projector resolution

verify.pass_if: resolution == projector res; every pixel exactly black

steps.note: FRONT-LAYER CONTENT (the imagery meant to appear ON the sheet). Set file via set_par with an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path UNDER the working dir AFTER create (a relative/external path is blanked by path confinement). For sheer media the content should be authored bright-on-black to begin with -- a figure, text, or glowing element on a black field -- so the crush below has little to fight. Any content TOP works (a generative composite tap, a still). Add a SECOND source for the back layer if you want the front/back reveal (next step).
steps.geometry_out: front-layer content image

verify.pass_if: clip resolution reported, bright content sits on a dark/black field

steps.note: LAYERED FRONT/BACK REVEAL (optional but the signature gauze move). A sheer sheet can show a NEAR image, then dissolve it away to reveal a FAR image (or a live performer lit behind) -- 'the figure emerges from nothing'. crossTOP (maxinputs=2): in0 = OUT_front, in1 = a back-layer content TOP; cross 0..1 blends between them. Animate cross DATA-ONLY: build an lfoCHOP (slow ramp/sine) or keyframeCHOP (cued dissolve) and EXPORT its channel onto crossTOP.cross via set_flags export=true, exportmethod=autoname on the CHOP (a CHOP driving a parameter -- NO expression). For a hard cue-driven reveal use a keyframeCHOP; for a breathing ambient reveal use an lfoCHOP. Skip this node entirely for a single-layer sheer look and feed OUT_front straight to the crush.
steps.geometry_out: front/back layers dissolved by a data-only CHOP

verify.pass_if: at cross=0 the front layer shows; at cross=1 the back layer shows; an exported CHOP moves cross

steps.note: BLACK CRUSH -- the make-or-break sheer step. Force everything that should be invisible hard to 0 so the sheet only lights where you truly want it. blacklevel raised (or inlow raised toward ~0.05-0.15) crushes codec grey-lift, compression blocking, sensor noise, and near-black gradient tails down to pure black -- on a scrim these otherwise read as an ugly grey wash across the whole sheet. Push contrast up and keep gamma1 low-ish to steepen the shadow rolloff so mid-darks fall to black rather than glowing. Be deliberate: crush too hard and you lose intended dim detail (smoke, soft edges); crush too little and the sheet hazes. Watch the alpha too -- if the content has a soft alpha, the same lift applies so semi-transparent pixels don't leak light. This is where 'looks fine on a monitor' content is rescued for sheer projection.

key_params.blacklevel: raise until non-content areas read exactly 0 (e.g. 0.05-0.15)
key_params.inlow: alternative: raise input black point to crush grey-lift

steps.geometry_out: content with all near-black lift crushed to pure black

verify.pass_if: non-content regions are exactly black (no grey haze); intended bright content survives
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_crushed and check the darkest supposed-invisible area reads 0,0,0 -- on the sheet that region will be fully see-through

steps.note: REAR-PROJECTION MIRROR. Sheer surfaces are almost always lit from BEHIND (the projector is upstage/backstage, the audience is downstage) so the raw image reaches the audience mirrored left-right. flipTOP flipx=on pre-mirrors the content so it reads correctly to the house. If the rig is FRONT projection (rare for scrim, common for a lit-from-front effect) leave flipx off. flipy handles an inverted/ceiling-hung projector. This is a pure per-frame flip -- no resolution change. Decide front vs rear at survey time; it flips the whole downstream chain, so set it before the keystone.

key_params.flipy: on only if the projector is inverted/ceiling-hung

steps.geometry_out: content mirrored for rear projection

verify.pass_if: image is mirrored L-R (text/faces read correctly once thrown from behind)

steps.note: STEEP KEYSTONE. Scrim / HoloGauze / a fog or water screen is often hung high and hit from a shallow floor angle (or thrown up from a low projector), giving an extreme keystone the four pin corners must correct. pin* (pintopleft/pintopright/pinbotleft/pinbotright, fraction of canvas) place + keystone the frame onto the sheet; mapping=perspective so straight edges stay straight under a steep angle (bilinear visibly bows them -- very obvious on a tall gauze). extend=zero + bgcolor alpha 0 so outside the mapped quad is transparent, not black-that-lights-the-sheet (it composites over the black ground later, so transparent is correct here). gridrefine higher (default 16) helps a very steep perspective sample cleanly. Set corners to a first estimate; the on-site measured numbers are typed back via set_par (HUMAN step).
steps.geometry_out: content keystoned onto the sheet's plane, transparent outside

verify.pass_if: content occupies the keystoned quad; straight edges stay straight; outside is transparent

steps.note: EDGE FEATHER MASK (build in canvas space to fade the content into the black surround). A hard-edged rectangle of light on a scrim exposes the sheet's border and the fabric edge; feathering the content to black at its edges hides where the sheet is. Build a rampTOP mask -- a radial (type=radial) white centre falling to black at the edges, or a pair of vertical/horizontal ramps for a soft-edged frame -- color white, that will MULTIPLY into the content's alpha (next steps). interpnotches=hermite for a smooth curve. outputresolution=custom to match the canvas so it registers 1:1 with the keyed content. Shape the falloff so only the very edge feathers (a large white plateau, soft border) unless you want a full vignette.

key_params.type: radial (or vertical/horizontal for a framed feather)

steps.geometry_out: white-centre / black-edge feather mask at canvas res

verify.pass_if: white interior fading smoothly to black at the borders

steps.note: SOFTEN THE FEATHER (and optionally the content edge). A small gaussian/box blur on the feather mask removes any banding in the ramp and widens the transition so the content dissolves into black with no visible line -- critical on sheer media where a crisp edge betrays the sheet. type=gaussian, size a few pixels up to a soft wide falloff; extend=hold so the blur doesn't wrap. You can alternately blur OUT_keyed directly for a dreamy soft-focus sheer look (fog/water screens especially suit a slightly soft image). Keep the blur modest -- over-blurring the mask eats into the content; over-blurring the image loses the crispness that makes a figure read.
steps.geometry_out: softened feather mask (no banding, wide falloff)

verify.pass_if: the mask edge is smooth with no banding; falloff is wide and clean

steps.note: APPLY THE FEATHER to the content. in0 = OUT_keyed, in1 = OUT_feathersoft (maxinputs=2). Multiplying the white-centre/black-edge mask into the keyed content drives the content's edges (and its alpha) to black at the borders so it fades into the surround. The product is bright in the centre, black at the edges -- exactly what a sheet needs. Wire THIS into the final compositeTOP. (compositeTOP operand=multiply would also work; multiplyTOP is the dedicated 2-input node.)
steps.geometry_out: keyed content feathered to black at its edges

verify.pass_if: content bright in the centre, fading to pure black at every edge

steps.note: STACK OVER THE BLACK GROUND = the deliverable sheer frame. operand=over, tops multi-input: wire OUT_blackbg FIRST, then OUT_feathered on top (add more sheer layers in draw order if the design has several). outputresolution=custom at projector res. Because the feathered content is transparent/black outside its region, over-compositing lands it on pure black -- guaranteeing every non-content pixel throws no light and the sheet stays see-through there. Re-confirm after this node that the black is DEAD black (no lift crept in from a premultiply or a stray alpha) -- one grey pixel here hazes the whole sheet. SWAPORDER: set swaporder=on -- compositeTOP's `over` draws INPUT 0 ON TOP, so swaporder=on makes input 0 the BOTTOM layer and the LAST input the top, matching the draw order described here (verified live: an opaque background on input 0 without swaporder hides everything above it).

key_params.swaporder: on (input 0 = BOTTOM layer; without it compositeTOP over draws input 0 on TOP)
key_params.tops: OUT_blackbg, OUT_feathered (draw order; last on top)

steps.geometry_out: sheer content composited over pure black at projector res

verify.pass_if: content on dead-black ground; sampling any non-content pixel reads 0,0,0
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_sheercomp -- content reads bright and clean; the entire surround is exactly black (the see-through region)

steps.note: STABLE ALIGNED TAP. Downstream output ops target THIS name so the physical output swaps without rewiring, and it's the point where the actor-holdout and the wire-only handoff attach. Wire OUT_sheercomp -> this. For rear projection the whole frame may still need a global cornerpinTOP keystone after this null (distinct from the content keystone above) to fit the projector to the sheet -- hand that to projection_align_and_output.
steps.geometry_out: final sheer frame, projector res, ready for holdout + wire-only output

verify.pass_if: the deliverable sheer frame at projector res

glsl_opportunity.why: a truly clean luminance-keyed soft holdout / black-crush (feathered matte from a threshold on luma) is one small GLSL pass, sharper than stacked level+ramp nodes for a moving performer edge
glsl_opportunity.propose_via: glsl_reference then set_glsl on a glslTOP inserted before the null
glsl_opportunity.consent: needs allow_glsl (default OFF); data-only fallback (the actual steps) = levelTOP black-crush + rampTOP/blurTOP feather + the reused garbage-mask holdout

steps.note: ACTOR-SAFE HOLDOUT (reuse, do not rebuild). A performer standing BEHIND a rear-lit scrim gets projector light on their face/body wherever the sheet in front of them is lit -- blinding and ugly. Reuse output_spill_garbage_mask to black out the region of the frame that overlaps the performer's position (and any offstage spill beyond the sheet's edge), so no light lands where a person is. That recipe builds a soft-edged black mask (rampTOP/rectangleTOP -> multiply/over) keyed to the stage geometry; feed OUT_sheeraligned through it. The holdout region is measured on site (where the actor actually stands) -- a HUMAN input typed back via set_par on the mask corners. This is a safety + aesthetic requirement for any sheer effect with a live performer behind it.

key_params.holdout region: black out where the performer stands / offstage spill (measured on site)

steps.geometry_out: (sheer frame with a performer/spill holdout blacked out)

verify.pass_if: the performer's region (and offstage) is pure black; no light spills onto them

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: hanging the scrim + measuring the throw/angle on site)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === Physically HANGING the sheer sheet (tensioning a scrim/gauze so it's flat and wrinkle-free, positioning the fog/water screen, aiming the rear projector) and MEASURING the real throw distance, projector angle, keystone corners, and the performer's holdout region cannot be emitted -- a person does it on site with the sheet lit. WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds the whole content chain (black ground, crush, reveal, mirror, keystone, feather, composite, holdout hook) and sets every corner/level numerically as an estimate. The measured numbers are typed back via set_par: cornerpinTOP pintopleftx/pintoplefty.../pinbotrighty for the keystone, levelTOP blacklevel/inlow for the crush target, and the garbage-mask corners for the actor holdout. Sheer materials also each behave differently (gauze grain, HoloGauze gain, fog-screen turbulence, water-screen ripple) -- the crush/feather amounts are dialed against the actual material lit, which only the on-site eye can judge.
steps.geometry_out: content landing correctly on the real lit sheet once measured numbers are typed in

verify.pass_if: keystone pins + crush levels hold on-site values (or estimate for authoring)

recipes.classify: project onto SHEER / see-through material -- theatrical scrim, bobbinet gauze, HoloGauze, holographic gauze, fog screen, water screen, mesh, net -- where only lit pixels show and black is transparent; sheer / gauze / scrim / holo / fog screen / water screen / see-through / transparent / rear projection reveal, front-to-back dissolve, figure-appears-from-nothing, black-crush content prep, actor-safe holdout behind a scrim
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the entire sheer content chain -- black constantTOP ground, moviefileinTOP source(s), the crossTOP front/back reveal (animated by an lfoCHOP/keyframeCHOP EXPORTED onto crossTOP.cross via the export flag -- a CHOP driving a parameter, never an expression), the levelTOP black-crush, the flipTOP rear mirror, the cornerpinTOP keystone, the rampTOP+blurTOP feather, the multiplyTOP + compositeTOP over black, and the aligned null -- is created / wired / parameterized by the bridge. Every value is a literal number; no script/expression/callback/shader anywhere. The one optional code touchpoint (a luminance-keyed soft holdout in one GLSL pass) is surfaced as a glsl_opportunity (allow_glsl, default OFF) with a data-only fallback, never baked in. (2) HUMAN / ON-SITE: hanging + tensioning the sheer sheet, aiming the rear projector, and measuring the throw / keystone corners / crush target / performer holdout region are done by a person with the sheet lit -- the measured numbers are typed back via set_par. The MCP cannot see the fabric or judge the crush against a real material. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: nothing fires; OUT_heldout (or OUT_sheeraligned) hands off via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output with the terminal op's active/record/winopen OFF (ndiout/spout default ON -> set OFF). HONEST GAPS: there is NO dedicated scrim/gauze/holo TOP -- this is assembled from generic primitives; fog-screen turbulence and water-screen ripple are physical, not simulated here. The actor holdout REUSES output_spill_garbage_mask (do not rebuild it). NC build cap renders live preview at 1280; swap resolutionw/h for the real projector res, topology identical.
tips: BLACK IS THE WHOLE GAME: the ground constantTOP must be exactly [0,0,0] and every non-content pixel must reach the projector as 0 -- one grey value hazes the entire sheet and reveals the fabric. Re-sample the final composite to confirm dead black.
Crush deliberately: raise blacklevel/inlow until the invisible areas hit 0 but STOP before you eat intended dim detail (smoke, soft glows). Over-crush loses the effect; under-crush hazes the sheet.
flipTOP flipx=on for REAR projection (the normal scrim rig) so the audience reads the image un-mirrored; leave it off for front projection. Decide at survey and set it before the keystone.
Feather EVERY edge to black (rampTOP + blurTOP -> multiply) so the content dissolves into the surround -- a hard rectangle of light exposes the sheet's border and the weave.
Animate the front/back reveal DATA-ONLY: an lfoCHOP (ambient breathing) or keyframeCHOP (cued) EXPORTED onto crossTOP.cross -- a CHOP drives the parameter; do NOT put an expression on cross.

The actor holdout is a SAFETY item, not just aesthetics -- a rear-lit performer gets blinding light on the face wherever the sheet is lit in front of them; reuse output_spill_garbage_mask and black out their region.
Different sheer materials gain differently (bobbinet vs HoloGauze vs fog vs water) -- dial the crush/feather against the actual lit material on site; the numbers won't transfer between fabrics.
HELPER CANDIDATE: sheer_prep(content, {crush, keystone, rear, feather, reveal_chop}) -> the black-ground->crush->mirror->keystone->feather->composite chain in one call.
variants: single_layer: drop the crossTOP reveal and feed OUT_front straight into the black-crush -- a plain lit-content-on-a-scrim look with no front/back dissolve.
front_projection: flipx off (no rear mirror) for a scrim lit from the audience side -- still black-crushed and feathered, but not mirrored.

holo_pepper_ghost: HoloGauze at a steep floor angle for a 'ghost' reveal -- crank the cornerpinTOP keystone, keep the crush hard and the content high-contrast bright, and drive the crossTOP reveal from a keyframeCHOP cue.

fog_or_water_screen: for a fog/water screen add a modest blurTOP on the CONTENT (not just the mask) for a soft, atmospheric image that suits the moving, turbulent surface; expect the physical screen to add its own shimmer.
layered_depth: stack multiple sheer planes (several scrims at different depths) -- build one chain per plane, each with its own keystone + crush, and composite/parallax them for a volumetric reveal.

recipes.title: Delivery-color pipeline -- colorspace transform + .cube 3D LUT + 1D curve trim + final black/white/gamma (opencolorioTOP colorspace -> opencolorioTOP file transform (.cube) -> lookupTOP curve -> levelTOP -> OUT_delivery) then output_handoff
recipes.summary: The delivery-color stage the library was missing: take the aligned mapped frame and put it into the client's target colorspace with their look LUT applied, so what the projector/LED shows matches the delivery spec. Order matters -- do a COLORSPACE transform first (opencolorioTOP with a loaded OCIO config: set the source colorspace and the display/view or out colorspace to move working <-> Rec709 / sRGB / DCI-P3), then apply the client's .cube LOOK LUT, then a small 1D curve/level trim. CRUCIAL CATALOG FACT: TouchDesigner's lookupTOP is a 1D / gradient remap (it maps input intensity through a gradient TOP on its second input, or a CHOP -- method=secondinput|chop), it is NOT a 3D .cube loader; the actual .cube / .3dl / .clf 3D LUT loads through opencolorioTOP's FILE TRANSFORM (usefiletransform=on + filesource=<path> + filedirection + interpolation=tetrahedral). So the pipeline uses opencolorioTOP twice (or one node's pre/file/post stages): once for the colorspace conversion, once to apply the .cube look; lookupTOP handles per-channel TONE-CURVE trims via a rampTOP gradient; levelTOP does the final black-point/white-point/gamma legalize (blacklevel, gamma1, inlow/inhigh -> outlow/outhigh). A nullTOP (OUT_delivery) hands off WIRE-ONLY. KEY GOTCHA: opencolorioTOP's colorspace menus (srccs / display / view / out) are POPULATED FROM THE LOADED CONFIG file -- with the default built-in config the named Rec709/sRGB/DCI-P3 spaces come from that config; point config at the client's OCIO config (or the studio ACES config) to get their exact named spaces, else the tokens will not match the delivery spec. Also LUT/OCIO transforms want float precision -- set format rgba16float on the OCIO nodes so a heavy grade does not band in 8-bit. HUMAN BOUNDARY / ASSET: the .cube LUT file AND the target colorspace both come from the client's delivery spec -- a person supplies the file (under the working dir) and names the target space; the MCP wires the pipeline and sets every param but cannot invent the look.

steps.note: GRADE INPUT TAP = the frame to be graded. Wire the mapped/aligned source here (typically OUT_aligned from multi_quad_mapper / signal_ingest_remap / projection_align_and_output). Grading LAST, on the composited deliverable, means one grade covers the whole output rather than grading each source separately. Set outputresolution=custom at the delivery res so the color chain runs at final size. Everything downstream targets this NAME so the color stage can be inserted/removed as a block.
steps.geometry_out: the ungraded mapped frame on a stable tap

verify.pass_if: fed by the mapped/aligned source; resolution == delivery res

steps.note: COLORSPACE TRANSFORM (working -> delivery space). Load the client/studio OCIO config into config (an absolute forward-slash .ocio path UNDER the working dir; default is the built-in $TT config). Use the Output stage: useoutput=on, then set srccs to the frame's working colorspace and display/view (or the out colorspace) to the delivery target -- Rec709, sRGB, or DCI-P3. IMPORTANT: the srccs / display / view menus are populated FROM the loaded config -- the named Rec709/sRGB/DCIP3 spaces are whatever that config defines, so a client delivering DCI-P3 needs a config that names it. gamma/gain are post-scalars, leave 1.0 here. Wire OUT_gradein -> in0. Set format rgba16float so the transform has float headroom. reloadconfig pulse re-reads the file if the client swaps it.

key_params.config: C:/work/color/client.ocio (absolute, under working dir; or default $TT config)
key_params.srccs: (working space -- from config, e.g. scene-linear / sRGB)
key_params.display: (delivery target -- Rec709 | sRGB | DCI-P3, from config)

steps.geometry_out: frame moved into the client's delivery colorspace

verify.pass_if: 16-bit float; visible colorspace shift vs OUT_gradein (or neutral if src==dst)

output_opportunity.why: the client OCIO config may declare custom named colorspaces or a display/view the default built-in config lacks, and getting the exact delivery space right is the whole point of the grade
output_opportunity.propose_via: operator_reference opencolorioTOP then set the config path + srccs/display/view to the client's named spaces
output_opportunity.consent: data-only -- config is a file path + menu tokens, no code; the CLIENT supplies the .ocio file and names the target space (human asset), the MCP only wires and sets it

steps.note: .CUBE 3D LUT (the client LOOK). This is the REAL .cube path in TouchDesigner -- lookupTOP does NOT load .cube files. Use the File Transform stage of a SECOND opencolorioTOP: usefiletransform=on, filesource=<absolute forward-slash path to the .cube/.3dl/.clf, under the working dir>, filedirection=forward (inverse to undo a LUT), interpolation=tetrahedral (best for 3D LUTs -- linear can show grid artifacts). This applies the client's creative look on top of the colorspace-correct image. Leave the colorspace stages of THIS node off (prexformop=none, useoutput=off) so it only does the file transform. Wire OUT_ocio -> in0. Keep format rgba16float. cdlmode=values here also gives an ASC-CDL slope/offset/power/saturation trim if the delivery uses a CDL instead of/with the cube.
steps.geometry_out: delivery-space frame with the client .cube look applied

verify.pass_if: the graded look is visible (compare to OUT_ocio); no banding/grid artifacts
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_lut vs OUT_gradein -- the client look LUT is unmistakably applied in the delivery colorspace

steps.note: 1D TONE-CURVE TRIM (optional per-channel curve). lookupTOP remaps input intensity through a GRADIENT on its second input -- method=secondinput, wire OUT_lut -> in0 and a rampTOP gradient -> in1; the ramp's shape IS the transfer curve (a gentle S-curve for contrast, a lifted toe to raise blacks). channel=independent to curve R/G/B separately (or luminance for a single curve); index1/index2 set the input range sampled. This is the data-only stand-in for a 1D .cube -- author the curve as a rampTOP (keys as gradient points), NOT as an expression. SKIP this node if the OCIO stages already deliver the look. (method=chop drives the curve from a CHOP instead of a gradient TOP.)
steps.geometry_out: frame with a 1D tone curve applied on top of the LUT

verify.pass_if: the curve shifts tones as authored (or pass-through if ramp is a linear identity)

steps.note: FINAL BLACK/WHITE/GAMMA LEGALIZE. The last trim before hand-off: blacklevel lifts/sets the black point, gamma1 the midtone gamma, inlow/inhigh -> outlow/outhigh remaps the range (e.g. outlow 0.0 outhigh 0.94 to clamp super-white for a projector that crushes near-white; outlow 0.06 to lift blacks off a projector's noise floor). brightness1/contrast for a small overall trim; per-channel lowr/highr/lowg/highg/lowb/highb for a white-balance nudge. This legalizes the delivery signal to the specific projector/LED without touching the creative LUT. Wire OUT_curve (or OUT_lut) -> in0. Values come from a meter or the operator's eye on the real wall (human).

key_params.outlow: 0.0 (raise to lift blacks off noise floor)

steps.geometry_out: final delivery-legal graded frame

verify.pass_if: black/white points and gamma sit within the delivery/projector spec
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_graded -- black point, white point, and gamma read correct for the target display

steps.note: STABLE DELIVERY TAP. Wire OUT_graded here; the output lane targets this NAME so the whole color block can be bypassed (target OUT_gradein's source directly) for an A/B of graded vs ungraded. Hand off WIRE-ONLY to output_handoff / projection_align_and_output. This is the last node the projectionist looks at before the signal leaves TouchDesigner.
steps.geometry_out: final graded deliverable frame, delivery res, ready for wire-only output

verify.pass_if: graded frame at delivery res on one stable tap

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: the .cube LUT file + target colorspace from the client delivery spec)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === The MCP wires the OCIO + LUT + curve + level chain and sets every param, but it CANNOT invent the look: the client's .cube / .3dl / .clf LUT file and the target colorspace (Rec709 / sRGB / DCI-P3) come from the DELIVERY SPEC -- a person places the .cube under the working dir (external paths are blanked by path confinement) and names the target space, and supplies the OCIO config that defines it. Final black/white/gamma values are read off a probe/meter or the operator's eye on the REAL projector/LED wall -- the MCP cannot see the wall. Once the human provides the file path, target space, and measured level values, they are typed in via set_par on filesource / srccs / display / the level* params.
steps.geometry_out: the client's exact delivery look, once the LUT + space + levels are supplied

verify.pass_if: filesource points at a real .cube under the working dir; OCIO target space set

steps.note: WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT HAND-OFF. Route OUT_delivery to the physical output via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output -- do NOT rebuild the output stage. Terminal ops are BUILT but never actuated by us: windowCOMP not opened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF; ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active DEFAULT ON -> set OFF; st2110outTOP active default ON -> OFF. If baking a graded master to disk, moviefileoutTOP stays record OFF until a person triggers it.
steps.geometry_out: (reference -- the output lane consumes OUT_delivery)

verify.pass_if: OUT_delivery is the single tap the output lane reads

recipes.classify: COLOR GRADE and deliver -- apply a LUT (.cube / .3dl / .clf 3D LUT), an OCIO / OpenColorIO colorspace transform (Rec709 / sRGB / DCI-P3 / P3 / ACES), a 1D tone curve, a look, final black-point / white-point / gamma legalize; color management, colorspace conversion, delivery color, grade the output, match the projector/LED color, ASC-CDL, apply my client's LUT, colour grading pipeline
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the whole color chain -- the grade-input null, the opencolorioTOP colorspace transform, the opencolorioTOP .cube file transform, the lookupTOP 1D curve (+ its rampTOP gradient), the levelTOP legalize, and the delivery null -- is created / wired / parameterized by the bridge. No script/execute/cplusplus op, no parameter expressions, no callbacks DAT; every value (colorspace tokens, file paths, slope/gamma/black-level) is a literal set via the create tool or set_par. The 1D curve is authored as a rampTOP gradient, NOT an expression. (2) HUMAN / ASSET: the .cube / .3dl / .clf LUT file and the target colorspace come from the CLIENT DELIVERY SPEC -- a person supplies the file (placed under the working dir; external/relative paths are blanked by path confinement) and the OCIO config that names the target space, and reads final black/white/gamma off a meter or the real projector/LED wall (the MCP cannot see the wall). WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: nothing here fires; output_handoff / projection_align_and_output handle the terminal ops (windowCOMP not opened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF; ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active DEFAULT ON -> MUST set OFF; st2110outTOP active default ON -> OFF). HONEST GAPS / CORRECTED ASSUMPTION: lookupTOP is a 1D / gradient remap (second-input gradient or CHOP), NOT a 3D .cube loader -- the .cube path is opencolorioTOP's File Transform (usefiletransform + filesource); a recipe that tried to feed a .cube into lookupTOP would be wrong. lookupTOP and opencolorioTOP are otherwise UNUSED across the other 33 recipes -- this recipe is where they earn their place. opencolorioTOP's named colorspace menus are populated from the loaded OCIO config, so the exact Rec709/sRGB/DCI-P3 tokens depend on that config (default built-in config vs the client/studio ACES config). NC build caps live render at 1280; swap resolutionw/h for 4K, topology identical.
tips: ORDER: colorspace transform FIRST (get into the delivery space), THEN the look .cube, THEN the 1D curve / level legalize -- grading before the colorspace transform bakes the look into the wrong space.

lookupTOP does NOT load .cube files -- it is a 1D/gradient remap (method=secondinput with a rampTOP on in1). The 3D .cube loads through opencolorioTOP's File Transform (usefiletransform + filesource). Do not confuse the two.
Set format rgba16float on the OCIO/LUT nodes -- an 8-bit pipeline bands visibly under a heavy grade or a steep LUT; float gives headroom.

opencolorioTOP colorspace menus come from the LOADED config -- point config at the client/studio .ocio (under the working dir) to get their exact named Rec709/sRGB/DCI-P3/ACES spaces; the default built-in config may not name the target.
interpolation=tetrahedral on the .cube File Transform -- linear interpolation of a 3D LUT can show grid-cell artifacts in smooth gradients.
filedirection=inverse UNDOES a LUT -- useful to strip a camera/monitor LUT before applying the delivery look.

levelTOP outlow/outhigh legalize the signal to the physical display (lift blacks off a projector's noise floor, tame near-white clip) WITHOUT touching the creative LUT -- keep legal-range trims here, look in the LUT/OCIO stages.
HELPER CANDIDATE: grade_delivery(config, src_space, target_space, cube_path, black, white, gamma) -> the two opencolorioTOP stages + levelTOP wired in one call.
variants: ocio_only: skip the .cube -- a pure colorspace/display transform (opencolorioTOP Output stage) when delivery just needs Rec709<->DCI-P3 correctness with no creative look.
cube_look: the full path -- colorspace transform then the client .cube look then a level legalize; the standard client-delivery grade.
asc_cdl: use opencolorioTOP cdlmode=values (slope/offset/power/saturation) or ccfile for an ASC-CDL grade instead of/with the .cube -- common on broadcast/film delivery.
curve_trim_only: lookupTOP with a rampTOP S-curve (no LUT) for a light contrast/tone adjustment when the source is already in the right space.

reference_still_match: load a client reference frame via moviefileinTOP and eyeball OUT_graded against it (place them side by side) to match the delivery look before locking values -- remove the reference before hand-off.

recipes.title: Data-only corporate / live-event stage-graphics package (ndiinTOP/videodeviceinTOP IMAG -> transformTOP picture-in-picture + reused text_title_content lower-third/credits + moviefileinTOP holding slide + timerCHOP countdown-to-start -> compositeTOP program over switchTOP program/standby bus -> OUT_showout) -- the operator-native show-graphics rig
recipes.summary: Assemble the standard corporate / conference / keynote stage-graphics PACKAGE data-only: an IMAG (image-magnification) inset of the live stage camera, a lower-third / name-super and credits layer, a holding/standby slide for pre-show and breaks, and a countdown-to-start clock -- combined into a PROGRAM feed with a program/standby switch. IMAG ingest is an ndiinTOP (NDI from the video village) or a videodeviceinTOP (SDI/HDMI via Blackmagic/AJA/Datapath/Deltacast -- set deinterlace + signalformat) whose active INPUT stays on; a transformTOP scales+places it as a picture-in-picture inset (or full-frame IMAG). Rather than rebuild ingest hygiene and the title layer, this recipe REUSES two siblings as meta-steps: signal_ingest_remap for the deinterlace/colour/format-locked capture-and-mask chain, and text_title_content for the lower-third, name supers, credits and the countdown-to-start (a timerCHOP -> choptoDAT -> textTOP, all code-free). A holding SLIDE is a moviefileinTOP (a still ident or a looping pre-show loop) or a constantTOP card. Everything meets at a compositeTOP (operand=over) that builds the PROGRAM, and a switchTOP (index 0=program, 1=holding/standby) selects the on-air bus with a second nullTOP as a preview/standby tap; a crossTOP gives a dissolve between them. All terminal output is WIRE-ONLY. KEY GOTCHA: an SDI IMAG feed is usually interlaced -- set videodeviceinTOP.deinterlace (bob/even/odd) and the correct signalformat or the inset combs on motion; and the ndiinTOP 'active' default-ON is CORRECT for an input (it is ingest, not the ndiOUToTOP whose active you must turn OFF). HUMAN BOUNDARY: the live camera, the vision mixer/switcher and IMAG source routing are the EVENT'S video system -- the bridge builds the graphics package that garnishes that feed; it does not run the camera or cut the show.

steps.note: IMAG FEED INGEST (the live stage camera as content). Create an ndiinTOP and set name to the NDI source from the video village (the switcher's program or ISO out published as NDI), bandwidth=high for full-res IMAG (low for a confidence-size inset), active=on -- for an INPUT active-on is correct (this is ingest; do NOT confuse it with ndioutTOP whose active you turn OFF). outputresolution=custom to lock the working res. SDI/HDMI ALTERNATIVE: a videodeviceinTOP with driver=blackmagic/aja/datapath/deltacast, the device selected, deinterlace set (bob/even/odd -- broadcast cameras are often interlaced) and the right signalformat (e.g. 1080i59.94) or the inset combs on motion. The live feed itself comes from the event's video system (see the human boundary).

key_params.name: the IMAG NDI source name
key_params.active: on (INPUT -- correct; not an output to disable)

steps.geometry_out: live IMAG camera image as a TOP

verify.pass_if: the feed resolution is reported (a real source, not the 256 default); on SDI, no combing on motion once deinterlaced

steps.note: REUSE INGEST HYGIENE -- do NOT rebuild it. Route OUT_imag through the signal_ingest_remap chain for the deinterlace/colour-space/format-lock, optional garbage mask, and any warp the IMAG needs before it is a clean content source. That recipe owns the videodeviceinTOP/ndiinTOP/st2110inTOP ingest conventions and the mask/warp; here you just reference it so the IMAG arrives colour-correct and clean. Its output is the tidy IMAG that the picture-in-picture transform below places.

key_params.reuse: signal_ingest_remap on OUT_imag -> a clean, colour/format-locked IMAG source

steps.geometry_out: (clean IMAG content from the ingest recipe)

verify.pass_if: the IMAG chain matches signal_ingest_remap (deinterlaced, colour-locked)

steps.note: IMAG PICTURE-IN-PICTURE PLACEMENT. Pass the clean IMAG through a transformTOP to scale it down (sx/sy ~0.4) and park it in a corner (tx/ty, tunit=fraction) as a picture-in-picture inset over the graphics bed -- or leave sx/sy=1 for a full-frame IMAG look. extend=zero + bgcolor alpha 0 so outside the inset is transparent for compositing. A levelTOP after this can add a subtle border/dim; a constantTOP/rectangleTOP behind gives a PiP frame. Animate tx/ty/sx with an lfoCHOP/keyframeCHOP EXPORT (as in text_title_content) for an inset that flies in on cue -- data-only.
steps.geometry_out: IMAG scaled+placed as a PiP inset on a transparent frame

verify.pass_if: the IMAG sits at the intended size/corner, transparent elsewhere

steps.note: HOLDING / STANDBY SLIDE (pre-show, breaks, technical standby). A moviefileinTOP loads the ident still or a looping pre-show loop -- set file to an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path UNDER the working dir (a relative/external path is blanked by path confinement), play=on for a loop or a single still. Use the allowlisted `pulse` (cue/reload) to re-cue the loop; never a script. A plain constantTOP card (brand colour) is the simplest standby. This slide is one input of the standby bus at the switch below and is what the audience sees before doors and during resets.
steps.geometry_out: holding/standby slide image

verify.pass_if: the slide/loop resolution is reported (real asset, not the 256 default)

steps.note: COUNTDOWN-TO-START over the holding slide. A timerCHOP (length = seconds until doors/start, play=on, cycle=off) is the code-free countdown value; bridge it to a textTOP via a choptoDAT (timerCHOP -> choptoDAT -> textTOP.dat, or textTOP.chop + chopvaluereplace with a %-token and the numeric formatter for zero-padded MM:SS) exactly as in text_title_content. Composite that countdown textTOP over OUT_holdslide so the standby screen shows 'STARTS IN 09:58' ticking down. Start/reset with the allowlisted parameterless `pulse` (start). This is the concrete countdown; for the lower-third supers and credits, reuse text_title_content wholesale (next step).

key_params.(bridge): choptoDAT -> textTOP.dat  (or textTOP.chop + chopvaluereplace), then compositeTOP over OUT_holdslide

steps.geometry_out: CHOP countdown -> textTOP over the holding slide (data-only)

verify.pass_if: the countdown decrements when play=on and the on-slide digits update; pulse start restarts it

steps.note: REUSE THE TITLE LAYER -- lower-thirds, name supers, credits. Do NOT rebuild titling: instantiate text_title_content for the speaker name-straps/lower-thirds, session titles, sponsor supers and end credits, and take its OUT_titleout (an alpha-keyable, animated super layer) as an input to the program compositor below. It already provides the code-free live-text, the lfoCHOP/keyframeCHOP slide-in/fade, and the 3D-title option. One instance can drive many supers by swapping the approved copy (a tableDAT of names loaded via write_csv -> tableDAT.file -> pulse(loadonstartpulse)).

key_params.reuse: text_title_content -> OUT_titleout (lower-third / name super / credits, alpha-keyable)
key_params.copy_source: a tableDAT of approved names (write_csv -> file -> pulse(loadonstartpulse))

steps.geometry_out: (lower-third / name-super / credits layer from the title recipe)

verify.pass_if: the super layer matches text_title_content and keys cleanly (transparent where no type)

steps.note: BUILD THE PROGRAM. operand=over, tops multi-input: wire the graphics BED / live content first (the show's main content, or the IMAG full-frame), then OUT_pip (the IMAG inset), then OUT_lowerthird (the super/credits) on top. outputresolution=custom at delivery res. This composited stack IS the program-bus image the audience sees when the show is live. Keep draw order deliberate: content bottom, IMAG inset middle, supers top so lower-thirds are never hidden behind the inset. SWAPORDER: set swaporder=on -- compositeTOP's `over` draws INPUT 0 ON TOP, so swaporder=on makes input 0 the BOTTOM layer and the LAST input the top, matching the draw order described here (verified live: an opaque background on input 0 without swaporder hides everything above it).

key_params.swaporder: on (input 0 = BOTTOM layer; without it compositeTOP over draws input 0 on TOP)
key_params.tops: content/bed, OUT_pip, OUT_lowerthird (draw order; supers last/on top)

steps.geometry_out: the live PROGRAM image (content + IMAG inset + supers)

verify.pass_if: content, IMAG inset and lower-third all read correctly in the right stacking order
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_program -- the assembled program frame reads as broadcast-clean (inset placed, supers legible, nothing clipped)

steps.note: PROGRAM / STANDBY BUS SELECT. A switchTOP (index 0 = OUT_program, 1 = OUT_holdslide/standby) chooses what goes on-air: standby slide before doors and during resets, program when live. index is a plain value -- drive it code-free from an operator/AI (set_par index) or an OSC/MIDI button EXPORTED onto index (a CHOP value, still data-only); a `pulse`-driven timerCHOP can gate an automated pre-show->program flip. For a soft take set blend=on (or use a crossTOP between the two buses, cross 0..1 animated by an lfoCHOP for a dissolve). outputresolution=custom. Wire OUT_program and OUT_holdslide as the two inputs.

key_params.(soft take alt): crossTOP cross 0..1 animated by an lfoCHOP for a dissolve

steps.geometry_out: the selected on-air bus (program or standby)

verify.pass_if: index 0 shows program, index 1 shows the standby slide/countdown

steps.note: PROGRAM + STANDBY TAPS, WIRE-ONLY HAND-OFF. Wire OUT_show into a nullTOP that downstream output targets by NAME (swap the physical output without rewiring). Build a SECOND nullTOP off OUT_holdslide (or a low-res resolutionTOP tap) as a dedicated STANDBY/preview bus so an operator always has a safe slide independent of program. Hand off both through output_handoff / projection_align_and_output -- all terminal ops WIRE-ONLY: windowCOMP not opened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF; ndioutTOP.active/syphonspoutoutTOP.active DEFAULT ON -> set OFF; st2110outTOP active default ON -> OFF. The bridge builds and wires these inactive; the operator/show system fires them.

key_params.program_tap: nullTOP off OUT_show (named target for output)
key_params.standby_tap: second nullTOP off OUT_holdslide (independent safe bus)

steps.geometry_out: named program + standby taps ready for wire-only output

verify.pass_if: the program tap holds the on-air frame; the standby tap holds the safe slide independently
verify.milestone_check: OUT_showout is the deliverable program the media server/projector shows; the standby tap survives even if program changes

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: live camera + switcher = the event's video system)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === The bridge builds the GRAPHICS package -- IMAG inset framing, lower-thirds, holding slide, countdown, program/standby bus -- but the LIVE VIDEO belongs to the event's production: the stage CAMERA(S), the vision mixer / VISION SWITCHER that cuts between them, and the routing that publishes the camera feed as the NDI/SDI source this recipe ingests are operated by the event's video crew. The MCP does not run the camera, cut the show, or decide the on-air moment; it consumes whatever feed the switcher hands over (set the ndiinTOP.name / videodeviceinTOP.device to the source the crew provides) and garnishes it. The on-air TAKE (program vs standby) and each super's keying are the operator's call -- the MCP exposes switchTOP.index and the copy params for them to drive. Content approval, name spelling and font licensing follow text_title_content's human boundary.

key_params.set_par (from the crew): op=OUT_imag ndiinTOP, pars={name:'<switcher NDI out>'}  OR videodeviceinTOP device=<the SDI card the crew feeds>

steps.geometry_out: graphics package garnishing the event video system's live feed

verify.pass_if: the ingest points at the crew-provided source; program/standby index is operator-drivable

recipes.classify: LIVE-EVENT / CORPORATE / CONFERENCE / KEYNOTE stage-graphics package -- IMAG (image magnification of the stage camera) as a picture-in-picture inset or full-frame, speaker lower-thirds / name straps, a holding / standby / pre-show slide, a countdown-to-start clock, sponsor supers and credits, and a program vs standby switch. Keywords: IMAG, image magnification, stage graphics, show graphics, corporate AV, conference, keynote, town hall, presentation graphics, holding slide, standby, pre-show, countdown to start, lower third, program feed, camera inset, picture in picture.
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the whole graphics package -- IMAG ingest (ndiinTOP/videodeviceinTOP, active-ON is correct for an INPUT), the picture-in-picture transformTOP, the holding-slide moviefileinTOP, the code-free countdown (timerCHOP -> choptoDAT -> textTOP), the reused text_title_content super layer, the program compositeTOP, and the switchTOP/crossTOP program-vs-standby bus -- is created, wired and parameterized by the bridge with literal values. No expression, no DAT callback/script, no code sink; the only actuators are the allowlisted parameterless `pulse` (timerCHOP start/cuepulse, moviefileinTOP cue/reload, tableDAT loadonstartpulse) and value EXPORTS (an OSC/MIDI button onto switchTOP.index or a transform param). (2) HUMAN / EVENT VIDEO SYSTEM: the live camera(s), the vision switcher that cuts the show, the routing that publishes the feed as NDI/SDI, the on-air TAKE decision, and content/name/font approval are the event crew's -- the bridge garnishes their feed, it does not produce it. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: program + standby taps hand off via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output with every terminal op inactive (windowCOMP not opened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF; ndioutTOP/syphonspoutoutTOP/st2110outTOP active -> OFF). HONEST GAPS: there is no single 'IMAG' or 'stage-graphics-template' operator -- the package is assembled from ingest + transform + composite + switch primitives (helper candidate: build_imag_package(source, holding, countdown)); auto-failover between program and standby needs external orchestration (see confidence_monitor_foldback). NC build caps live render at 1280; swap resolution for 1920/3840, topology identical.
tips: ndiinTOP.active default ON is CORRECT here -- it is an INPUT (ingest); the active you must turn OFF lives on ndioutTOP/syphonspoutoutTOP/st2110outTOP at the wire-only hand-off.
An SDI/HDMI IMAG feed is usually interlaced -- set videodeviceinTOP.deinterlace (bob/even/odd) and the exact signalformat, or the inset combs on every camera move.
Set the holding-slide moviefileinTOP.file to an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path UNDER the working dir; a relative/external path is blanked by path confinement and the slide goes black.
Countdown-to-start is code-free: timerCHOP -> choptoDAT -> textTOP (or textTOP.chop + chopvaluereplace with a %-token) -- reuse text_title_content rather than rebuilding the counter.
Composite draw order matters: content bottom, IMAG inset middle, lower-thirds top -- supers wired last so they are never hidden behind the PiP inset.
Program/standby take: switchTOP.index is a value an operator/OSC button drives; for a soft take use blend=on or a crossTOP whose cross 0..1 an lfoCHOP dissolves -- all data-only, no expression.
Keep a SECOND nullTOP standby/preview bus off the holding slide so the operator always has a safe screen independent of whatever program is doing.
Force outputresolution=custom at delivery res on every node -- an IMAG inset or a super left at 256 default is soft the moment it hits a 1080/4K program.
variants: full_frame_imag: transformTOP sx/sy=1 -- the live camera fills frame (classic IMAG) with only lower-thirds keyed over it, no inset.
pip_inset: transformTOP sx/sy~0.4 corner-parked -- a picture-in-picture speaker inset over a branded graphics bed.
preshow_countdown: switchTOP on the standby bus showing the holding slide + timerCHOP countdown-to-start; flip to program (index 0) on doors -- an unattended pre-show that runs itself.
soft_take: replace/augment the switchTOP with a crossTOP (cross animated 0..1 by an lfoCHOP or keyframeCHOP) for a dissolve between program and standby instead of a hard cut.
sdi_ingest: videodeviceinTOP (blackmagic/aja, deinterlace, signalformat) instead of ndiinTOP when the video village hands SDI rather than NDI -- the rest of the package is identical.

recipes.title: Animated instance-array motion graphics -- a deterministic kinetic 3D scene (boxSOP shape -> geometryCOMP CHOP-instancing driven by patternCHOP layout + lfoCHOP/noiseCHOP animation, constantMAT per-instance color, keyframeCHOP -> cameraCOMP fly-through -> renderTOP -> OUT_kinetic)
recipes.summary: Build a moving 3D motion-graphics scene from a large ARRAY of instanced copies -- a rippling grid of cubes, a swarm of tiles, a kinetic sculpture, a pulsing wall of blocks -- all deterministic and entirely code-free. The spine is geometryCOMP INSTANCING driven by a CHOP: one small shape SOP (boxSOP, or any unit geometry) is replicated N times, and a single instance-data CHOP supplies per-instance transform + color as channels (tx/ty/tz, rx/ry/rz, sx/sy/sz, r/g/b) where each SAMPLE is one instance. A patternCHOP lays out the base array (a grid/line via per-channel phase offset), and lfoCHOP + noiseCHOP MODULATE it over time -- because these CHOPs are time-based they cook every frame, so the array animates with NO expressions and NO callbacks (the motion is deterministic given the params, unlike a particle sim). A constantMAT with applypointcolor=on reads each instance's color. The camera flies through via keyframeCHOP playing an animationCOMP's keyed channels, EXPORTED (exportmethod=autoname) onto the cameraCOMP transform -- code-free camera motion. renderTOP bakes the frame. KEY GOTCHA #1: a fresh geometryCOMP renders its default torus1 -- delete it and set_flags render/display on the real shape SOP, or you instance nothing. KEY GOTCHA #2: geometryCOMP instance fields accept a CHOP/SOP/DAT even though the picker shows 'SOP' -- point instanceop at the CHOP and set instancecountmode=oplength so the instance count follows the CHOP's sample count. This is DISTINCT from facade_3d_render (a single static rendered mesh) and from particle_system_content (a stochastic GPU sim) -- here every instance's motion is authored and repeatable.

steps.note: THE INSTANCE SHAPE -- the single piece of geometry that gets replicated N times (a unit cube for a block wall, a thin plane for tiles/cards, a small sphere for a dot field). Keep it LOW-poly: it is drawn N times, so cost multiplies. This SOP lives INSIDE the geometryCOMP and is what the instancer stamps at each instance transform. Give it real UVs (texture=boxinside) if the instances will carry a texture; leave normals on for shaded looks. Size it around 1 unit so per-instance scale channels read intuitively.
steps.geometry_out: one low-poly shape to instance

verify.pass_if: a single low-poly SOP exists (the unit shape)

steps.note: BASE ARRAY LAYOUT -- the static grid/line the instances start from. patternCHOP makes a channel of exactly N samples (length=N = instance count). Build the positional channels here: for a LINE, a ramp channel (wavetype=ramp) across N gives evenly spaced tx; for a 2D GRID, combine two patternCHOPs (one ramp for column X, one stepped for row Y via numsteps) and merge as tx/ty; name channels tx ty tz. phasestep is the secret weapon: it offsets the phase PER CHANNEL/instance so a later wave sweeps across the array like a Mexican wave. left/right=cycle keeps it periodic. This is the deterministic skeleton the animation rides on.
steps.geometry_out: N-sample base layout channels (tx ty tz)

verify.pass_if: channels have N samples laying out the array footprint

steps.note: TIME ANIMATION -- what makes it kinetic, code-free. lfoCHOP (a free-running oscillator, play=on) and a noiseCHOP (organic drift) are ADDED to the layout to animate per-instance position/rotation/scale/color over time: an lfoCHOP sine on a scale channel makes the whole array PULSE; combined with the patternCHOP phasestep it becomes a traveling ripple; a noiseCHOP on rz gives each instance a wandering spin; a slow lfoCHOP on the color channels cycles hue. Merge layout + animation into ONE instance-data CHOP carrying tx ty tz rx ry rz sx sy sz r g b, each with N samples. Because lfoCHOP/noiseCHOP are time-based they re-cook every frame -- the array moves with zero expressions or scripts (the data-only motion mechanism). Deterministic: same params -> same motion every run.

key_params.channelname: sx (or rz / r -- the animated attribute)

steps.geometry_out: N-sample instance-data CHOP (transform + color, animated)

verify.pass_if: one CHOP, N samples, channels tx..tz rx..rz sx..sz r g b advancing over time

steps.note: THE INSTANCER -- the heart. Put OUT_shape inside this geometryCOMP; CRITICAL -- delete_op the default torus1 and set_flags render=true/display=true on OUT_shape or the instancer stamps nothing. Set instancing=on, instancecountmode=oplength (count follows the CHOP sample count), instanceop=OUT_instdata (the CHOP -- the field accepts a CHOP even though it reads 'SOP'). Map channels to transforms: instancetx='tx', instancety='ty', instancetz='tz'; instancerx/ry/rz='rx/ry/rz'; instancesx/sy/sz='sx/sy/sz'; instancer/g/b='r/g/b' for per-instance color. Assign a constantMAT via the material param (see next). Now N copies of the shape move independently per the CHOP -- an instanced kinetic array.
steps.geometry_out: N animated instances of the shape

verify.pass_if: instancing on, instanceop set, torus1 gone, shape render/display on
verify.milestone_check: read_network @OUT_instgeo -- instancing reads OUT_instdata, count == N, and the shape (not torus1) is the render geometry

expr_opportunity.why: a compact per-instance transform FORMULA (e.g. radius*sin(phase+index) placement) can be terser than merging several CHOPs
expr_opportunity.propose_via: expr_reference then set_expr on the instance* fields or a mathCHOP
expr_opportunity.consent: needs allow_expr (default OFF); data-only fallback = patternCHOP layout + lfoCHOP/noiseCHOP merged into the instance-data CHOP (this recipe's actual path)

steps.note: PER-INSTANCE MATERIAL. constantMAT is unlit (flat motion-graphics look, no lights needed) -- set applypointcolor=on so it reads each instance's r/g/b from the instancer (the color channels you animated). color/alpha tint the whole array; a colormap TOP can texture every instance (with instance texture-coords). For a SHADED kinetic look (light catching the cubes), swap constantMAT for a pbrMAT/phongMAT and add a lightCOMP -- but constant is the reliable flat default and keeps the render cheap. Assign it on the geometryCOMP.material param (step 4).
steps.geometry_out: unlit per-instance-colored material

verify.pass_if: applypointcolor on so instances take their animated colors

steps.note: CAMERA FLY-THROUGH -- code-free camera motion. keyframeCHOP plays back an animationCOMP's KEYED channels (author key poses in the animationCOMP: name channels tx ty tz rx ry rz). Set exportmethod=autoname and autoexportroot=the cameraCOMP so each channel auto-drives the camera's matching transform param via the EXPORT flag -- no expression. cameraCOMP: projection=perspective, fov ~45, near/far bracketing the array. The camera sweeps the kinetic scene on rails. SIMPLER code-free alternative: skip keyframes and export an lfoCHOP (slow orbit on ry) + noiseCHOP (subtle handheld drift) onto the camera transform -- same data-only export path, less authoring. One exporter per parameter (disable others).

key_params.animation: the animationCOMP holding the camera keys

steps.geometry_out: camera transform driven by keyed channels (exported)

verify.pass_if: camera tx/ty/tz/r* are Export-driven and change over time

steps.note: RENDER THE KINETIC SCENE. Wire the cameraCOMP + the instance geometryCOMP into renderTOP. Force outputresolution=custom at delivery res (256px trap otherwise); bgcolora=0 for a transparent plate to composite over the map (judge over black, not the white preview). antialias=aa8 to clean the many instance edges. For a huge array watch the instance count x shape polys -- that is the render cost, and the NC preview cap is 1280 (build there, deliver at 1920/3840). This TOP is the deliverable kinetic content frame.
steps.geometry_out: rendered animated instance array, delivery res

verify.pass_if: the instance array renders and clearly moves between frames
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_kinetic at two times -- the kinetic array is visibly animating (pulse/ripple/spin) and the camera has moved

steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN + HARDWARE SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds the shape, the instance-data CHOP, the instancer, the material, the camera move, the render, and sets every number. WHAT A PERSON DOES: approves scale and TEMPO on the real surface (cube size vs building modules, ripple speed vs music, brightness vs projector) and returns tweaks via set_par on the lfoCHOP frequency/amp, patternCHOP phasestep, or the camera keys. HANDOFF is WIRE-ONLY: OUT_kinetic feeds the map/output lane (multi_quad_mapper / projection_align_and_output / output_handoff); terminal output ops are BUILT but never fired here (windowCOMP not opened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF; ndioutTOP/syphonspoutoutTOP active OFF). To BAKE a perfect loop of the kinetic scene, hand to seamless_loop_authoring (the layout+lfo can be made periodic).

recipes.classify: animated instance array / instanced motion graphics -- a rippling grid or wall of cubes, a swarm of tiles/cards, a kinetic sculpture, a pulsing block wall, a field of dots, repeated 3D copies moving in a designed pattern; geometryCOMP instancing driven by CHOP channels (patternCHOP layout, lfoCHOP/noiseCHOP animation), per-instance color via constantMAT, camera fly-through via keyframeCHOP; deterministic authored motion, NOT a particle simulation and NOT a single static mesh render; also copySOP / replicatorCOMP arrays
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY: the shape, the instance-data CHOP, the geometryCOMP instancer, the material, the camera move and the render are all built, wired and parameterized by the bridge with literal numbers. Motion is CODE-FREE: per-instance transform/color come from time-based CHOPs (patternCHOP/lfoCHOP/noiseCHOP) read directly by the instancer, and the camera is driven by the CHOP EXPORT flag (exportmethod=autoname) -- no parameter expressions, no callbacks, no script/execute anywhere. HUMAN / HARDWARE: scale/tempo approval on the surface and the physical output are off-MCP; wire-only terminal ops are BUILT but not fired (moviefileoutTOP.record OFF; ndiout/spout active OFF) and handed to the output lane. HONEST CATALOG GAPS: (1) copySOP and replicatorCOMP are alternative array builders and BOTH exist -- BUT replicatorCOMP's real power is its callbacks DAT (tscript / callbacks params) which are CODE SINKS forbidden by the data-only boundary; use replicatorCOMP ONLY in method=bytable with a template DAT and LEAVE tscript/callbacks EMPTY (it then just clones a master per table row), and prefer geometryCOMP instancing or copySOP for anything animated. (2) geometryCOMP instance fields read 'SOP' in the schema but accept CHOP/DAT at runtime -- point instanceop at the instance-data CHOP and set instancecountmode=oplength. (3) keyframeCHOP needs an animationCOMP to hold the keys; if that is heavier than wanted, the lfoCHOP/noiseCHOP-exported camera is the lighter data-only equivalent. NC render cap 1280: instance count x shape polys is the cost -- build/preview at <=1280, deliver at 1920/3840, topology identical.
tips: A fresh geometryCOMP renders its default torus1 -- delete_op it and set_flags render=true/display=true on the real shape SOP, else the instancer replicates nothing.
Set instancecountmode=oplength so the instance count equals the instance-data CHOP's sample count -- change N by changing the CHOP length, no manual numinstances edits.
patternCHOP phasestep is how you get a TRAVELING wave across the array: it offsets each instance's phase so a ripple sweeps the grid instead of every copy pulsing in unison.
The instance fields accept a CHOP even though the picker says SOP -- CHOP-instancing (one sample per instance, channels = attributes) is the cleanest code-free animated path.
constantMAT applypointcolor=on is what makes per-instance color work; without it every instance takes the flat material color and your animated r/g/b channels do nothing.
Keep the shape SOP low-poly -- render cost is instanceCount x shapePolys; a 40x40 grid of 12-poly cubes is 19,200 polys before AA.

replicatorCOMP: if you must use it, method=bytable + a template DAT + LEAVE the callbacks DAT and Script param EMPTY (they are code sinks) -- it then just clones a master per row; for motion prefer geometryCOMP instancing.

swarm_drift: noiseCHOP on tx/ty/tz + slow rz spin -> an organic drifting swarm of tiles/cards (bridges toward particles but stays deterministic and repeatable).

copySOP_array (SOP-only, no CHOP-instancing): copySOP stamps the shape onto a point SOP whose point attributes (pscale, Cd, orient) are animated via choptoSOP from the CHOPs -- heavier geometry but a pure-SOP path, and every copy is real geometry (good for boolean/again-instancing).

replicatorCOMP_grid (data-only subset): method=bytable + template DAT clones a master COMP per row, tscript/callbacks LEFT EMPTY -- for a fixed structured array of addressable sub-comps rather than GPU instances.

loopable_kinetic: choose lfoCHOP frequency + patternCHOP numcycles so the whole animation is periodic over a chosen length, then hand OUT_kinetic to seamless_loop_authoring to bake a seam-free loop file.

recipes.title: Bake a seam-free generative loop -- guarantee frame N wraps to frame 0 (timerCHOP loop length + periodic patternCHOP/lfoCHOP phase OR a head/tail crossTOP dissolve -> nullTOP -> moviefileoutTOP WIRE-ONLY bake)
recipes.summary: Turn a live generative texture into a perfectly looping clip whose LAST frame flows into its FIRST with no visible seam -- the generative analog of media_clip_player's loop-crossfade. Two mechanisms, and the recipe builds both: (A) PERIODIC PHASE -- drive the generator from a phase that RETURNS TO ITS START, so the image at the loop end is bit-for-bit the image at the start. A timerCHOP defines the exact loop length; a patternCHOP (left/right=cycle, integer numcycles) or an lfoCHOP whose frequency fits a whole number of cycles into the loop produces a 0->1->0 phase; feed that phase into the generator's animating input (a noiseTOP moving on a CLOSED path in its 4th dimension via t4d, a transformTOP scroll of an integer number of tile-widths, a rampTOP sweep). Guarantee: loop_length_seconds x cycles_per_second = an INTEGER, and every animated driver is periodic over that length -- then frame N == frame 0 by construction. (B) HEAD/TAIL DISSOLVE -- for generators that CANNOT be made periodic (feedbackTOP trails, chaotic sims), crossTOP-dissolve the loop's TAIL into its HEAD over an overlap window so the seam is hidden under a crossfade. A timerCHOP still fixes the length; the crossTOP's cross parameter is driven from the loop phase inside the overlap region only. The finished loop terminates in a nullTOP, and a moviefileoutTOP (codec=hap for playback, length=the loop) BAKES it -- WIRE-ONLY: we build and wire the recorder but NEVER fire it (record OFF); the operator arms the bake. KEY GOTCHA: the seam test is comparing the FIRST and LAST rendered frames -- if they differ, the driver is not truly periodic (a non-integer cycle count, a feedback tail still decaying, or a noise field not on a closed loop). Method B masks that; method A eliminates it.

steps.note: DEFINE THE LOOP LENGTH -- the master clock every phase derives from. length = the loop duration in seconds; play=on; cycle=on so it wraps 0->length->0 forever. Its timer_fraction output is the canonical LOOP PHASE (0 at the first frame, ->1 approaching the last). Everything periodic in this recipe reads timer_fraction (or a channel derived from it), so 'wrap' is defined once, here. Pick a length that is a clean integer number of frames at the delivery fps (e.g. 10.0s x 60fps = 600 frames) -- fractional frames are the #1 cause of a one-frame stutter at the loop point.

key_params.length: loop seconds (choose an integer frame count at fps)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (timer_fraction = loop phase 0..1)

verify.pass_if: timer_fraction ramps 0->1 over length and resets; length*fps is an integer

steps.note: THE PERIODIC DRIVE (method A) -- the phase that guarantees the wrap. patternCHOP with wavetype=sin/cos/rampcyclic and left=cycle/right=cycle is inherently periodic; set numcycles to an INTEGER so the wave completes whole cycles across the loop and its value at the end equals its value at the start. Alternatively an lfoCHOP with frequency = cycles / loop_length (an integer numerator) gives the same 0->start phase. This channel is what you export/wire into the generator's animating parameter. THE RULE that makes frame N wrap to frame 0: every driver that moves the image must be periodic over exactly the loop length -- one non-periodic driver (a stray free-running lfo at a fractional rate) breaks the seam even if everything else is perfect.
steps.geometry_out: a strictly periodic drive channel (value@end == value@start)

verify.pass_if: the channel's first and last sample values are equal (an integer number of cycles)

steps.note: THE GENERATOR made periodic (method A). Drive the generator's animating input from OUT_phase so the motion is a closed loop. noiseTOP is the cleanest case: type=simplex4d/perlin4d treats t4d as a 4th spatial axis -- move t4d around a CLOSED CIRCLE over the loop (t4d = radius*cos(phase), a second field = radius*sin(phase)) and the 3D slice returns exactly to its start; or scroll tz by an INTEGER multiple of period so the field wraps. For a transformTOP scroll, translate by a whole number of tile-widths over the loop (with extend=repeat) so it seams. For a rampTOP/polar sweep, sweep phase 0->1 of a cyclic gradient. The generator is whatever content you want -- the discipline is that its ONLY time input is the periodic phase.

key_params.t4d: driven by OUT_phase on a CLOSED path (cos/sin pair)

steps.geometry_out: generative image whose motion is periodic over the loop

verify.pass_if: content animates and is driven ONLY by the periodic phase (no free-running input)

steps.note: HEAD/TAIL DISSOLVE (method B) -- the fallback for generators that CANNOT be made periodic (feedbackTOP trails, accumulation, chaotic sims). Idea: overlap the loop's TAIL onto its HEAD and crossfade so the seam hides under a dissolve. Cache/time-offset the stream so in0 = the running content and in1 = the same content shifted by (loop_length - overlap); crossTOP.cross is held at 0 for most of the loop, then ramps 0->1 across the final 'overlap' seconds (drive cross from OUT_loopclock's timer_fraction, remapped so it only moves inside the overlap window). The result blends the end back into the beginning. This never gives a mathematically identical wrap (method A does) but it makes the seam invisible -- the standard trick for trails/feedback loops. maxinputs=2.

key_params.cross: 0 most of loop, ramp 0->1 over the overlap tail (from timer_fraction)

steps.geometry_out: loop with tail dissolved into head (seam masked)

verify.pass_if: the transition across the loop point is a smooth crossfade with no hard cut
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_gen (or OUT_seamless) at phase~0.0 and phase~0.999 -- the two frames MATCH (method A) or blend seamlessly (method B): the seam test

steps.note: STABLE LOOP TAP. Wire the finished loop (OUT_gen for method A, or OUT_seamless for method B) into a nullTOP so downstream (the bake, or the map/output lane) targets this NAME and the loop source can be swapped without rewiring. Confirm outputresolution=custom at delivery res here too. This is the clean deliverable the recorder reads and the map consumes.
steps.geometry_out: final seam-free loop, delivery res

verify.pass_if: delivery resolution, the seam-free loop image

steps.note: BAKE THE LOOP -- WIRE-ONLY. Wire OUT_loop -> moviefileoutTOP. Set type=movie, videocodec=hap (GPU-fast playback for VJ/media servers; h264 for a smaller delivery file, prores for mastering), file = an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path UNDER the working dir, fps = the delivery rate (must match the frame count math from step 1), limitlength=on + length = the loop length + lengthunit=seconds/frames so the bake captures exactly one loop. CRITICAL WIRE-ONLY: leave record=OFF. We BUILD and wire the recorder but NEVER actuate it -- the operator arms record to run the bake (it writes a file, an irreversible side effect off the data-only boundary). The recipe's job is a correct, armed, one-loop recorder graph.
steps.geometry_out: an armed one-loop recorder (not fired)

verify.pass_if: record==off, file path set under working dir, length == one loop, fps matches

steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN + ACTUATION SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds the loop clock, the periodic drive (or the head/tail dissolve), the generator, the tap, and the armed recorder -- and sets every number so the loop is correct by construction. WHAT A PERSON DOES: eyeballs the loop point playing back (a person's eye is the final seam judge, especially for method B dissolves) and FIRES the bake -- moviefileoutTOP.record is toggled ON by the operator to write the file (an irreversible file-write, off the data-only boundary; the MCP never toggles it). After baking, the clip is played back via media_clip_player and handed to the map/output lane (output_handoff). If the seam fails, the fix is upstream: make every driver periodic (method A) or widen the crossfade overlap (method B).
