recipes.classify: bake a seamless / seam-free perfectly looping generative clip -- make frame N wrap to frame 0, loopable texture, VJ loop, endless background loop, no-seam loop, tileable-in-time animation; periodic phase driver (timerCHOP length + patternCHOP/lfoCHOP cyclic phase, 4D noise on a closed path) OR head/tail crossTOP dissolve for feedback/trail loops; moviefileoutTOP bake wire-only; the generative analog of a media clip loop-crossfade
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY up to the bake: the loop clock, the periodic drive (or the crossTOP dissolve), the generator and the armed recorder are all built/wired/parameterized with literal numbers -- no expressions, no callbacks, no script. The periodicity is achieved by CHOP phase (timerCHOP/patternCHOP/lfoCHOP) read by the generator, not by any evaluated formula. WIRE-ONLY / ACTUATION: moviefileoutTOP is BUILT and armed but its record is LEFT OFF -- baking writes a file (an irreversible side effect), so the OPERATOR fires record; the bridge never toggles it. The final seam judgement (especially for method-B dissolves) is a human eye watching the loop point. HONEST NOTES / GAPS: (1) method A (periodic phase) yields a mathematically identical wrap (frame N == frame 0); method B (head/tail crossTOP dissolve) only MASKS the seam and is required for non-periodic generators (feedbackTOP trails, accumulation) -- there is no operator that 'auto-seamlesses' arbitrary content, so pick the method to match the generator. (2) Frame-count discipline: loop_length x fps MUST be an integer or a one-frame stutter appears at the wrap regardless of method. (3) hap codec is GPU-fast for playback but larger on disk; prores/h264 trade size vs quality -- codec choice is delivery-driven. NC render cap 1280: author/preview at <=1280, bake at 1920/3840, topology identical.
tips: The seam test is literally: save_top the first frame (phase 0) and the last frame (phase ~1) and compare -- if they don't match under method A, a driver isn't truly periodic.
loop_length_seconds x fps MUST be a whole number of frames -- 10.0s at 60fps = 600 frames is safe; 10.0s at 59.94 is not, and you get a one-frame hitch at the wrap.
4D noise loops cleanly when t4d travels a CLOSED path (cos/sin pair of the phase) -- scrolling t4d linearly does NOT return to start; moving it on a circle does.
For a scrolling transformTOP, translate by an INTEGER number of tile widths over the loop with extend=repeat -- a fractional scroll leaves a visible jump.
feedbackTOP trails can NEVER be made perfectly periodic (the tail is still decaying at the wrap) -- use method B (crossTOP head/tail dissolve) or let the trail fully settle before the loop window.
Drive crossTOP.cross from timer_fraction remapped to move ONLY inside the overlap tail (0 for the bulk of the loop, 0->1 across the last ~1s) so the dissolve is confined to the seam.

Keep the moviefileoutTOP.record OFF in every built graph -- it is the one irreversible action here; the operator arms it. Confirm the file path is absolute and under the working dir or the write is blanked.
HELPER CANDIDATE: bake_loop(source, length_s, fps, method='periodic'|'dissolve', codec='hap') -> timer + phase/crossTOP + null + armed moviefileoutTOP (record off) in one call.
variants: periodic_noise: 4D noiseTOP with t4d on a closed cos/sin path over the loop -> a mathematically perfect wrap; the cleanest method for flow/organic backgrounds.
scrolling_tile: a transformTOP scroll of an integer number of tile-widths (extend=repeat) over the loop -> seamless drifting patterns/stripes/ribbons.
feedback_dissolve: a feedbackTOP trail loop that can't be periodic -> method B crossTOP head/tail dissolve over a ~1s overlap masks the seam.
instanced_scene_loop: feed OUT_kinetic from instanced_kinetic_content (its lfo/pattern set to integer cycles) into this recipe to bake a seam-free loop of a 3D kinetic scene.
long-master vs vj-loop: bake prores for an archival master and a second hap pass for the live media-server loop from the same OUT_loop tap (two armed recorders, both record OFF).

recipes.title: Operator confidence multiview + low-res foldback feed + hot-standby tap (labelled nullTOP taps -> textTOP labels -> compositeTOP panes -> layoutTOP grid, resolutionTOP downscale -> ndioutTOP foldback) -- eyes on every feed
recipes.summary: The operator MONITORING layer: a single confidence multiview that tiles every key tap (program, preview, each projector output) into one grid the operator watches, plus a bandwidth-cheap foldback feed for a downstream/onstage monitor, plus a hot-standby tap kept warm and ready to cut to. Spine: each feed is tapped at a stable nullTOP; a per-pane textTOP label ('PGM', 'PVW', 'PROJ 1') is composited over its tap with a compositeTOP so panes are identifiable; all panes wire into ONE layoutTOP set to a grid (align=gridcols/gridrows, numrows/numcols, fit=fitbest, a bcolor border and black bgcolor to separate panes) -- that grid IS the confidence monitor image. For foldback, a chosen feed (usually program) runs through a resolutionTOP downscaled to a small res (e.g. 640x360, highqualresize on) then an ndioutTOP to a downstage/onstage monitor. A second nullTOP taps a complete parallel content/output graph kept cooking as a HOT STANDBY the operator can cut to. HONEST BOUNDARY: TouchDesigner builds the taps, the multiview, the foldback feed, and keeps the standby graph warm -- but TRUE AUTO-FAILOVER (detect a black/frozen output and automatically switch to standby) needs external orchestration: a human watching the confidence monitor, or a watchdog process. A data-only freeze/black detector (analyzeTOP luminance -> logicCHOP threshold) can RAISE a flag, but the CUT decision and the physical confidence displays are human. KEY GOTCHA: the 256px trap and wire-only outputs apply -- force outputresolution=custom on the layout and the foldback resolutionTOP, and set the ndioutTOP active OFF (it defaults ON). The confidence monitor is for the OPERATOR, not the audience -- never route it to a program output.

steps.note: STABLE FEED TAPS -- one nullTOP per feed you want eyes on. Create a tap for each of: the program bus (from emergency_blackout_and_standby OUT_program_bus), the preview bus (OUT_preview), and EACH projector/zone output (the aligned null of each output chain, e.g. from multizone_independent_outputs / projection_align_and_output). Naming each tap (OUT_tap_pgm, OUT_tap_pvw, OUT_tap_proj1 ...) means the multiview re-sources without rewiring. outputresolution=useinput -- the layout will fit each pane, so the taps keep native res. This step is the pattern: repeat it per feed; the OUT_tapN nulls are the multiview inputs.

key_params.outputresolution: useinput (native res per feed; the layout fits panes)

steps.geometry_out: one stable tap per monitored feed

verify.pass_if: each tap carries its live feed at native res

steps.note: PER-PANE LABEL so the operator can identify each tile at a glance ('PGM', 'PVW', 'PROJ 1', 'PROJ 2', 'STANDBY'). text=<the pane name>; fontcolor bright, fontsizex modest (e.g. 28 points), alignx=left/aligny=top, positionx/positiony a small inset so the label sits in a pane corner; bgalpha=0.0 so ONLY the text (not a black card) composites over the feed. outputresolution=custom matching the tap so the label overlays cleanly. Build one label per pane. Skip labels for a bare grid (fewer nodes) -- but on a busy multi-projector show, unlabelled panes are a real operator-error risk.
steps.geometry_out: a pane label as white/yellow text on transparent

verify.pass_if: the label text reads on transparent (bgalpha 0)

steps.note: LABEL OVER FEED -> one identified pane. operand=over, in0=OUT_tap0 (the feed, bottom), in1=OUT_label0 (the label, on top); the transparent-background label lays onto the feed. outputresolution=useinput so the pane keeps the feed's size. Repeat per feed to make OUT_pane0..OUT_paneN. These composited panes are what the layout tiles; without the label step you can wire the taps straight into the layout instead (fewer nodes). Keep the label small and cornered so it never obscures the content the operator is judging. SWAPORDER: set swaporder=on -- compositeTOP's `over` draws INPUT 0 ON TOP, so swaporder=on makes input 0 the BOTTOM layer and the LAST input the top, matching the draw order described here (verified live: an opaque background on input 0 without swaporder hides everything above it).

key_params.swaporder: on (input 0 = BOTTOM layer; without it compositeTOP over draws input 0 on TOP)

steps.geometry_out: one labelled confidence pane

verify.pass_if: the feed with its label in the corner

steps.note: THE CONFIDENCE MULTIVIEW -- tiles every pane into one grid. maxinputs=9999: wire OUT_pane0, OUT_pane1 ... (or the raw taps) in the order you want them read. align=gridcols (fill columns first) or gridrows; set numrows/numcols to the grid you want (e.g. 2x2 for four feeds, 3x3 for up to nine). fit=fitbest so mixed-aspect feeds letterbox rather than distort. bcolor a mid-grey with a small border (bunit=pixels) and bgcolor black so panes are visually separated. outputresolution=custom at the operator monitor res (e.g. 1920x1080) -- NOT useinput, or the grid inherits one pane's size. This one node IS the confidence monitor.

Wire OUT_multiview into this null so the display can be re-pointed (a different monitor, an NDI monitor app) without touching the grid. Hand off WIRE-ONLY: a windowCOMP on the operator's second display (specifydisplay, NOT opened by us), or an ndioutTOP (active OFF) to an NDI monitor. This monitor is FOR THE OPERATOR ONLY -- never wire it to a program/projector output; it is diagnostic, not content.

Wire the source (e.g. OUT_tap_pgm or OUT_confidence) in; outputresolution=custom, resolution small (e.g. 640x360 or 960x540); highqualresize=on for a clean downscale. Foldback (a.k.a. 'foldback feed' / 'downstage monitor') gives a presenter or stage manager a low-latency, low-bitrate look at what is going out without a full-res link. Keeping it small is the point -- it rides a cheap NDI/network path.

This is the foldback twin of the program output but deliberately tiny. For a wired monitor instead of NDI, substitute videodeviceoutTOP / directdisplayoutTOP (also active/wire-only).

steps.note: HOT-STANDBY TAP -- the ready-to-cut backup. A complete PARALLEL content/output graph (a second full show chain, or a duplicate of the program chain from a redundant source) is kept COOKING so it is warm and frame-current; tap its aligned output at THIS null so the operator can cut program to it in one move if the primary fails. Because it is already cooking, the cut is instant (no cold-start decode stall). Add it as a pane in the multiview (wire OUT_hotstandby back as another layout input) so the operator can SEE the standby is healthy before switching. TD keeps it warm; the CUT itself is a switchTOP flip (reuse emergency_blackout_and_standby / multizone) driven by the operator -- not automatic.

steps.note: OPTIONAL FAILOVER FLAG (data-only, advisory only). To RAISE a health flag on a feed, reduce it to a single luminance value: analyzeTOP operation=average over a tap, then toptoCHOP -> logicCHOP thresholds (e.g. mean luminance < epsilon for N frames == 'output went black/frozen'). That FLAG is legitimate data-only monitoring. But do NOT wire the flag to auto-cut program: an automatic failover that misfires on a legitimately dark cue is worse than the fault it guards. The flag informs the operator (light a tally, or add a red pane border); the CUT stays human. A frozen-frame detector (difference of successive frames ~ 0) is the same pattern.

steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === The MCP builds every tap, the labelled multiview, the confidence tap, the foldback downscale + NDI endpoint, the hot-standby tap, and an advisory health flag. What it CANNOT do: BE the physical confidence monitor and foldback displays (real screens the operator and stage watch), and DECIDE to fail over -- true auto-failover (auto-detect a dead output and auto-switch to standby) needs external orchestration: a human watching the multiview, or a dedicated watchdog process / hardware seamless switcher outside TD. recipes.classify: operator CONFIDENCE MONITOR / multiview / preview grid / quad-split / eyes on every feed / program + preview + per-projector monitoring / FOLDBACK feed / downstage monitor / onstage monitor / low-res return feed / HOT STANDBY / redundancy / backup feed / failover flag / tally -- the operator monitoring + foldback + standby layer
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY, no code path. The monitoring layer is stable nullTOP taps -> per-pane textTOP labels -> compositeTOP panes -> one layoutTOP grid (the confidence multiview) -> a resolutionTOP downscale -> an ndioutTOP foldback endpoint, plus a hot-standby nullTOP tap and an optional analyzeTOP/toptoCHOP/logicCHOP health flag -- all created / wired / parameterized by the bridge. No expression, callback, or script: the health flag is honest CHOP threshold logic, surfaced as an expr_opportunity only if the operator opts into set_expr. HUMAN / ON-SITE: the physical confidence and foldback DISPLAYS are real screens the bridge cannot be, and the FAILOVER DECISION is a human's (or an external watchdog's) -- the MCP raises a flag and keeps the standby warm but does not auto-cut. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: OUT_confidence and OUT_foldback_ndi terminate in a windowCOMP (not opened) or ndioutTOP/videodeviceoutTOP/directdisplayoutTOP with active DEFAULT ON -> MUST set OFF; the operator actuates them. The confidence monitor is diagnostic and must NEVER be wired to a program/projector output. HONEST GAPS: TouchDesigner has NO failover / redundancy / seamless-switch / tally / multiview-widget operator -- layoutTOP IS the multiview and this network is the primitive; genuine auto-failover is external orchestration. NC render cap 1280 for previews; the operator monitor and foldback res are set explicitly.
tips: layoutTOP IS the multiview -- align=gridcols/gridrows with numrows/numcols; force outputresolution=custom at the operator-monitor res or the grid inherits one pane's size (and the 256 default).
fit=fitbest letterboxes mixed-aspect feeds instead of distorting them -- essential when program (16:9) and a portrait projector share a grid.
Label panes with a bgalpha=0 textTOP composited over each tap -- unlabelled tiles on a multi-projector show are a real cue-to-the-wrong-output risk.
Keep the foldback SMALL (resolutionTOP 640x360, highqualresize on) -- the whole point is a cheap, low-latency return feed; a full-res foldback defeats it.
ndioutTOP.active DEFAULTS ON -- set it OFF at build for both the foldback and any confidence NDI; the operator enables streams on site (wire-only).
Never route the confidence multiview to a program output -- it is an operator diagnostic; keep it on a separate windowCOMP/NDI the audience never sees.
Keep the hot-standby chain COOKING (do not bypass it) so the cut is instant -- a cold standby stalls on first decode; add it as a multiview pane to prove it is healthy before you rely on it.
An analyzeTOP luminance/freeze flag is fine for ALERTING, but do not auto-cut on it -- a misfire on a legitimately dark cue is worse than the fault; leave the cut to the operator.
variants: quad_split: numrows=2/numcols=2 for the classic PGM/PVW + two-projector 2x2 confidence grid; scale numrows/numcols up (3x3, 4x4) as feeds grow.
foldback_of_multiview: feed OUT_confidence (not just program) into the resolutionTOP so the downstage monitor sees the whole grid at low res -- useful for a roaming stage manager.
wired_foldback: replace ndioutTOP with videodeviceoutTOP (SDI/HDMI via a capture card) or directdisplayoutTOP for a hard-wired downstage monitor instead of NDI; still active OFF / wire-only.

health_tally: take the analyzeTOP/logicCHOP flag and drive a red pane border (a constantTOP border colour bound to the flag) or a tally light so a failing feed is visible at a glance -- alert only, no auto-cut.
standby_in_grid: wire OUT_hotstandby back as an extra layout pane labelled 'STBY' so the operator confirms the backup is warm and frame-current before ever cutting to it.

recipes.title: Operator control surface + remote -- build the on-screen console that RUNS the show (containerCOMP + buttonCOMP/sliderCOMP widgets -> panelCHOP -> bind_chop drives target params, code-free; oscinCHOP for a phone/tablet remote)
recipes.summary: Build the operator's OWN control surface -- the panel + remote the projectionist actually touches to run the show -- not just consume external control data. Spine: a containerCOMP panel holds buttonCOMP toggles (master GO, DBO kill-to-black, standby) + a radio buttonCOMP group or sliderCOMP for cue selection + sliderCOMP faders (master fade, per-layer opacity); a panelCHOP reads each widget's live panel value; those channels are renamed/merged into one OUT_panelstate bus; then bind_chop (or the CHOP export flag) drives the target params CODE-FREE -- a master-fade slider onto a levelTOP opacity, a cue slider onto a switchTOP index, a DBO toggle onto a crossTOP between the program bus and a black constantTOP. The SAME OUT_panelstate targets are reachable from an oscinCHOP so a TouchOSC/phone/tablet fader is interchangeable with the on-screen one. KEY GOTCHA 1: the DRIVE is panelCHOP -> bind_chop / export, with NO callbacks DAT -- a buttonCOMP/listCOMP callbacks DAT (and a webserverDAT browser remote) are Python code sinks the data-only bridge refuses, so the whole panel-to-parameter path stays code-free by reading panel VALUES, never running callbacks. KEY GOTCHA 2: a momentary GO cannot fire a `pulse` from a CHOP (that needs an expression); the GO button instead drives a TOGGLE exported onto a timerCHOP (reuse show_control_timecode), while `pulse` remains the MCP/operator GO path. Distinct from realtime_input_driver (consumes OSC/MIDI/DMX IN as data; authors no UI) and confidence_monitor_foldback (monitors feeds; does not control). HUMAN BOUNDARY: laying the panel out visually (dragging widgets, sizing, colours) and pairing the remote device (TouchOSC layout + IP/port on the phone) are on-glass/on-device human acts; the MCP builds every widget + the whole read/bind graph and sets initial geometry numerically.

steps.note: THE CONSOLE SHELL = the on-screen panel every widget lives in (the surface the operator runs the show from). Create it sized for a control strip (w/h in pixels), give it a dark opaque background (bgcolor near-black, bgalpha 1) so it reads as a console, and set align=verttb (or gridrows) + spacing so child widgets auto-stack instead of piling at 0,0. TUPLET trap: the create tool takes bgcolor=[r,g,b] as a vector; to nudge one component later use set_par raw names (bgcolorr/bgalpha). This container is a Panel COMP -- its children's states are what the panelCHOP will read. Actual visual LAYOUT (where each widget sits, final sizes, colour theme) is the human's on-glass job; here we build the shell and a sane initial geometry.

key_params.align: verttb (stack children top-to-bottom; gridrows for a matrix)

steps.geometry_out: an empty opaque panel container ready to hold widgets

verify.pass_if: containerCOMP exists, align=verttb, bgalpha 1

steps.note: THE ACTION WIDGETS (create one per control; all parented into OUT_panel). buttontype picks behaviour: toggledown for a latching DBO / STANDBY / layer-enable, momentary for a GO (pressed = 1 for one frame), radiodown for a mutually-exclusive CUE-SELECT group (set the same buttongroup string on each so only one is active). label names it on-screen. IMPORTANT (data-only boundary): the button's live state is its PANEL VALUE, read by the panelCHOP in the next steps -- do NOT wire a callbacks DAT (that Python execute path is refused by the bridge). value0 is the initial/toggle state. Build at minimum: btn_go (momentary), btn_dbo (toggledown), btn_standby (toggledown), and a 4-8 button radio group btn_cue0..N (radiodown, buttongroup='cues') for cue recall.

key_params.label: 'GO' / 'DBO' / 'STANDBY' / 'CUE 1'...
key_params.buttongroup: 'cues' (same string on every cue button = one-active radio set)

steps.geometry_out: labelled push/toggle/radio widgets inside the panel

verify.pass_if: buttontype=toggledown; radio buttons share buttongroup='cues'

steps.note: THE CONTINUOUS WIDGETS (create one per fader, parented into OUT_panel). slidertype=slideru for a horizontal fader (sliderv vertical, slideruv an XY pad). value0 is the live output; valuerange0l/valuerange0h map the slider's 0..1 travel to a useful range (e.g. 0..1 for a master fade, 0..N for a cue index, 0..1 for a per-layer opacity). Build at least: sld_master (master dimmer 0..1), sld_cue (0..N cue index -> switchTOP), and sld_op1..sld_opK (per-layer opacity 0..1). Like the buttons, its value is a PANEL VALUE read by panelCHOP -- code-free, no callbacks. A sliderCOMP cue index is the cleanest data-only cue selector; the radio button group (step 2) is the friendlier UI and its index is derived by CHOP math (step 5) -- both stay data-only.
steps.geometry_out: labelled faders inside the panel

verify.pass_if: sliderCOMP, slidertype=slideru, valuerange0h set

steps.note: READ THE WIDGETS AS DATA = the code-free bridge from UI to CHOP channels (this is the whole point of the recipe). A panelCHOP reads ONE Panel COMP's panel values, so create one per widget: set component to the widget (e.g. OUT_sld_master) and select the panel value you want -- 'v' for a slider/button output value, 'state' for a button's held state. maxinputs=0 (it pulls from the component param, nothing is wired in). This replaces the callbacks-DAT approach entirely: no script ever runs; the operator's touch becomes a number. Name the widgets clearly so the channels are legible. Repeat per widget (a helper could batch this).

key_params.exportmethod: autoname (only if this single CHOP will drive one param directly; otherwise leave and aggregate in step 5)

steps.geometry_out: one CHOP channel per widget = the live UI state

verify.pass_if: channel present and tracks the slider as its value changes

steps.note: AGGREGATE + STABLE UI BUS. Rename each per-widget panelCHOP channel to a meaningful name with a renameCHOP (renamefrom='v', renameto='master' / 'dbo' / 'cue' / 'op1'...), mergeCHOP them into one multi-channel CHOP, then tap it with this nullCHOP -- the ONE named bus every driver binds against, so widgets can be added/renamed without rewiring downstream. To turn the radio cue GROUP into a single index WITHOUT an expression: multiply each cue-button channel by its ordinal (patternCHOP/constantCHOP weights) and add the channels (mathCHOP combine=add) -- pure CHOP math, still data-only. OUT_panelstate now holds master/dbo/standby/cue/op1.. as clean channels.

key_params.(upstream) mergeCHOP: collect all renamed channels into one CHOP

steps.geometry_out: one CHOP holding every widget state, cleanly named

verify.pass_if: channels master/dbo/cue/op1.. all present and live
verify.milestone_check: inspect @OUT_panelstate while moving each widget -- every channel moves with its control

steps.note: THE PROGRAM BUS the panel drives (build the targets, then bind in the next step). DBO MASTER: a crossTOP with in0 = the program content, in1 = a black constantTOP (color [0,0,0], alpha 1, outputresolution=custom at show res -- 256px trap); its 'cross' param 0..1 fades program->black, so the DBO toggle drives cross (1 = blackout). MASTER FADE: a levelTOP on the program with 'opacity' (or 'brightness1') as the dimmer target. CUE SELECT: a switchTOP (maxinputs=9999, 'index' selects the live cue's content; blend=on to crossfade cues). Force outputresolution=custom on each at the real show resolution. These three params (crossTOP.cross, levelTOP.opacity, switchTOP.index) are the code-free hooks the UI binds to.

key_params.cross: 0.0 (0=program via in0, 1=black via in1) -- bind target for DBO
key_params.size: input1 (or input2) to fix output size

steps.geometry_out: program bus with DBO/fade/cue params exposed for binding

verify.pass_if: program shows through at cross=0; goes black at cross=1
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_programbus at cross 0 then 1 -- program vs full black

steps.note: THE CODE-FREE DRIVE = OUT_panelstate channels -> target params, NO expression, NO callbacks. bind_chop binds one CHOP channel to one parameter so the parameter tracks the channel every frame (data-only, same risk class as the export flag): bind master->levelTOP.opacity, dbo->crossTOP.cross, cue->switchTOP.index, op1->the layer1 levelTOP.opacity, etc. Alternative equivalent: set the panelCHOP/nullCHOP exportmethod=autoname + set_flags export=true and name the channel exactly like the target param (CHOP export needs the target's node cooking -- a viewer/active downstream -- to actually drive; bind_chop avoids that footgun). ONE driver per parameter: if you bind a param, don't also export onto it. This step is the recipe's heart: the operator's on-screen fader now moves a real projection parameter with zero script.

key_params.channel -> param: master->levelTOP opacity; dbo->crossTOP cross; cue->switchTOP index; op1->layer1 levelTOP opacity
key_params.note: one driver per param; do not double-drive

steps.geometry_out: target params now track the panel widgets live

verify.pass_if: crossTOP.cross / levelTOP.opacity are bind-driven and change when the widget moves
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_programbus while dragging sld_master and toggling btn_dbo -- the image dims and blacks out from the panel alone

steps.note: ON-PANEL CONFIDENCE READOUT (optional but standard) = live numeric feedback so the operator sees the current master level / cue number on the console. GOTCHA: textTOP's 'text' param DEFAULTS to the placeholder 'derivative' -- when you drive the text from a source you MUST clear it first (set text=''), then feed values via chopvaluereplace=on + chop=OUT_panelstate (%-replace the channel into a format string) or via dat=<a status tableDAT> with rowindex/colindex. Set fontcolor bright, bgalpha 0 for an overlay. If you COMPOSITE this readout onto an opaque panel/background with a compositeTOP (operand=over): 'over' draws INPUT 0 ON TOP, so wire the readout as input0 (top) and the opaque background LAST -- or set swaporder=on (then input0=bottom, last input=top). Getting that backwards hides the readout behind the panel.

key_params.(compositeTOP) operand: over -- input0 draws on top; put opaque bg LAST or swaporder=on

steps.geometry_out: a live text readout of the console state

verify.pass_if: shows the live value (NOT the word 'derivative'); readable over the panel

steps.note: THE REMOTE (phone / tablet / TouchOSC / console over the network) = the same controls, off-glass. An oscinCHOP listens on a port and turns each incoming OSC address into a numeric channel (maxinputs=0). Set port + oscaddressscope to filter to your remote's addresses (e.g. '/console/*'); channels arrive live. MERGE these channels into OUT_panelstate (or bind them onto the SAME target params) so a TouchOSC fader and the on-screen sliderCOMP are interchangeable -- last-writer-wins per param, so scope them to distinct params or pick one authority per control. Use oscinDAT only to INSPECT raw addresses/strings (splitmessage into columns) -- its callbacks DAT is a code sink and is not needed for value routing. A webserverDAT browser remote is NOT data-only here: serving a page + handling posts requires its callbacks DAT (Python) -- flagged in governance; OSC is the data-only remote path.

key_params.active: on
key_params.exportmethod: autoname (or merge into OUT_panelstate and bind)

steps.geometry_out: remote fader/button values as CHOP channels feeding the same targets

verify.pass_if: channels appear and move when the phone/tablet control moves

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: panel layout + remote device pairing)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === The MCP creates every widget, the panelCHOP read graph, the bind/export drive, the program-bus targets and the OSC remote, and sets initial geometry/ranges numerically. What a PERSON does on site: (1) VISUAL LAYOUT -- drag widgets to where they want them, tune sizes/colours/labels against the operator's eye and the venue lighting (the aesthetic of the console is human judgement, not emittable). (2) REMOTE PAIRING -- build/import the TouchOSC (or other) layout on the phone/tablet, put both devices on the same network, and enter TD's IP + the oscinCHOP port on the device (and open any firewall). The MCP can pre-set the port and the address scope; it cannot type the IP into someone's phone or draw their touch layout. Hand the numeric widget geometry back via set_par (x/y/w/h) once the operator has decided the layout.
steps.geometry_out: a console the operator can actually run, paired to their remote device

verify.pass_if: widget geometry holds the operator's chosen layout (or the initial estimate for authoring)

steps.note: GO -> TRANSPORT (cross-recipe): the momentary GO button CANNOT fire a `pulse` from a CHOP (a CHOP firing a pulse would need an expression). So bind/export the GO button's panel value onto a timerCHOP's play/cue TOGGLE (a value = data-only), or gate it with a triggerCHOP, and let show_control_timecode own the actual cue transport (segments table, gotonextseg, timecode lock). The `pulse` actuator remains the MCP/operator GO path; the panel's GO is the external-input path exactly as show_control_timecode describes. Likewise route the DBO/standby/opacity binds from THIS panel into the same show rig -- this recipe is the human-facing console; show_control_timecode is the clock/cue engine it drives. (Do not rebuild the transport here; reuse it.)

key_params.GO button -> timer: bind/export btn_go value onto timerCHOP play/cue toggle (data-only)
key_params.reuse: show_control_timecode for cue table + goto* transport

steps.geometry_out: (the console now runs the show transport)

verify.pass_if: timer play/cue toggle is driven by the GO widget; pulse still available as the operator GO

recipes.classify: build the operator's OWN control panel / control surface / on-screen console / GUI to RUN the show -- buttons, sliders, faders, a cue-select radio grid, master dimmer, DBO kill, per-layer opacity, plus a phone/tablet/TouchOSC remote and a browser remote; make a custom UI, operator console, front panel, show-control panel, remote control surface, code-free panel that drives parameters; distinct from consuming external OSC/MIDI/DMX input (realtime_input_driver) and from confidence monitoring (confidence_monitor_foldback)
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the entire console -- containerCOMP shell, every buttonCOMP/sliderCOMP widget, the per-widget panelCHOP reads, the renameCHOP/mergeCHOP/nullCHOP aggregation into OUT_panelstate, the crossTOP/levelTOP/switchTOP program-bus targets, the bind_chop (or export-flag) drive, the textTOP readout, and the oscinCHOP remote -- is created/wired/parameterized by the bridge. The panel-to-parameter path is CODE-FREE by construction: it reads panel VALUES and binds/exports them; it NEVER installs a callbacks DAT or an expression. (2) HUMAN / ON-SITE: the visual layout of the console (widget placement, sizing, colour theme) is on-glass human judgement, and pairing a phone/tablet remote (TouchOSC layout + entering TD's IP/port on the device, firewall) is on-device -- the MCP sets ports/scopes/initial geometry numerically but cannot draw a touch layout or type an IP into someone's phone. HONEST GAPS / DENIED SINKS: buttonCOMP and listCOMP CALLBACKS DATs (onClick/onSelect Python) are refused -- that is why the recipe drives everything through panel-VALUE reads instead; a listCOMP is usable for a scrolling cue list but its selection is normally consumed via its callbacks DAT, so for a fully data-only cue selector prefer a radio buttonCOMP group or a sliderCOMP index (derive an index from a radio group with CHOP math, not an expression). A webserverDAT BROWSER remote is genuinely NOT data-only: serving the page and handling posts needs its callbacks DAT (Python) -- listed as an op but flagged here as a code-sink gap; OSC (oscinCHOP) is the data-only remote. A momentary GO cannot fire a `pulse` from a CHOP (that needs an expression) -- the GO drives a timerCHOP toggle instead (show_control_timecode). CHOP EXPORT (the bind_chop alternative) only DRIVES when the target node cooks (a viewer/active downstream) -- bind_chop avoids that footgun. Create-tool TUPLET convention: create tools take vectors (bgcolor=[r,g,b], resolution=[w,h]); set_par takes raw components (bgcolorr, resolutionw). NC render cap 1280 on preview; swap resolution for the real show size, topology identical.
tips: The whole console is code-free because it reads panel VALUES via panelCHOP -- never attach a buttonCOMP/listCOMP callbacks DAT (that Python execute path is refused). One panelCHOP per widget: component=the widget, select='v' (value) or 'state' (held).

bind_chop is the clean drive: bind a channel to a param and it tracks every frame with no viewer needed. CHOP EXPORT is equivalent but only drives when the target node is cooking (active/viewed) -- prefer bind_chop to dodge the silent no-op.
ONE driver per parameter. If master->levelTOP.opacity is bound, do not also export another channel onto opacity; the second silently fights the first.
textTOP 'text' defaults to the placeholder 'derivative' -- set text='' BEFORE driving it from chopvaluereplace/chop or a DAT, or the readout shows the literal word 'derivative'.

compositeTOP/textTOP 'over' draws INPUT 0 ON TOP: to overlay a readout on the opaque program/panel, wire the readout as input0 and the opaque background LAST, or set swaporder=on. Note compositeTOP.operand DEFAULTS to 'multiply' -- set it to 'over' for a normal stack.
A momentary GO can't fire a `pulse` from a CHOP -- bind/export the GO value onto a timerCHOP play/cue TOGGLE (reuse show_control_timecode); keep `pulse` as the MCP/operator GO.

Cue select: a radio buttonCOMP group (shared buttongroup string) is the friendliest UI; a sliderCOMP with valuerange 0..N is the simplest data-only index. Turn a radio group into one index with CHOP math (weight each button by its ordinal, add) -- no expression.

Make the remote interchangeable: merge oscinCHOP channels into OUT_panelstate or bind them onto the SAME target params, and scope each control to one authority (oscaddressscope) so the phone fader and the on-screen fader don't fight.

HELPER CANDIDATE: build_panel(widgets=[{kind:button|slider, name, type, range, target_param}]) -> the container, all widgets, per-widget panelCHOPs, rename/merge/null bus, and the bind_chop drive in one call.
variants: on_screen_only: containerCOMP + widgets + panelCHOP + bind_chop, no remote -- a self-contained console for a booth operator on the show machine.
phone_tablet_remote: add the oscinCHOP + a TouchOSC layout (human) so the operator walks the room with the show on a tablet; merge into OUT_panelstate so on-screen and remote track together.

cue_grid_console: a gridrows containerCOMP of a radio buttonCOMP group (cue recall) + master fade + DBO -- the classic playback console; cue index -> switchTOP, GO -> timerCHOP toggle (show_control_timecode).

dbo_and_standby_desk: minimal safety desk -- btn_dbo (crossTOP to black) + btn_standby (switch to a holding textTOP/still) + sld_master -- the operationally essential kill/hold controls (pairs with emergency_blackout_and_standby).

browser_remote (NOT data-only): a webserverDAT serving a web panel needs its callbacks DAT (Python) to handle posts -- owner-gated code sink, out of the data-only lane; use the OSC remote instead unless the code lane is enabled.

recipes.title: Live show-health watchdog -- system telemetry + threshold alarm overlay (performCHOP fps/frame-time/dropped-frames/GPU mem/GPU temp -> mathCHOP normalize -> logicCHOP thresholds -> choptoTOP+textTOP readout + constantTOP alarm flash -> layoutTOP dashboard) so the operator sees a show DEGRADING before it fails
recipes.summary: The reliability instrument that sits beside a running show: a performCHOP samples the engine's own health -- fps, msec frame-time, cook time, droppedframes, gpumemused/totalgpumem, gputemp -- once per frame; a mathCHOP normalizes each metric into a comparable 0..1 (and derives a VRAM-used ratio via chopop=div of gpumemused/totalgpumem); a logicCHOP fires a per-metric over/under-threshold flag and ORs them into one master 'alarm' channel; that alarm drives a red constantTOP overlay (alpha bound to the alarm channel, data-only) while a choptoTOP bar strip + a textTOP numeric readout show the live values, all tiled into one operator dashboard by layoutTOP. KEY GOTCHA #1: textTOP's Text param DEFAULTS to the literal string 'derivative' -- you MUST clear it and drive the readout from a CHOP (chop + chopvaluereplace, %-token in the text) or a DAT (dat + rowindex/colindex), or the dashboard reads 'derivative' forever. KEY GOTCHA #2: compositeTOP over draws INPUT 0 ON TOP -- wire the alarm flash as input 0 (or set swaporder=on / put the opaque dashboard LAST) or the alarm hides behind the readout. DATA-ONLY mechanism: performCHOP is a passive telemetry source; thresholds are CHOP math; the alarm reaches the constantTOP's alpha via bind_chop / the EXPORT flag -- no expressions, no callbacks. HUMAN/WIRE boundary: WHAT the thresholds should be, and any AUTO-RECOVERY (kill a runaway process, fail over to a backup machine, restart playback) live OFF the data-only surface -- TD shows and alarms; a person (or external orchestration) acts. Continuous disk-LOGGING is also limited: a fileoutDAT log tap is BUILT but its Write pulse is not on the allowlist, so we wire the tap, not run it. Distinct from confidence_monitor_foldback, which watches the VIDEO feeds (is the picture right?); this watches SYSTEM performance (is the engine keeping up?).

steps.note: THE TELEMETRY SOURCE = the engine's own per-frame health, sampled with zero extra cost (maxinputs 0, it reads the process). Turn ON exactly the metrics you monitor -- each toggle adds a same-named channel: fps (default on), msec (Frame Time ms), cook (cook time ms), droppedframes (the single most important reliability number), gpumemused + totalgpumem (VRAM MB, pair them for a % used), gputemp (GPU Temperature -- labelled 'Slow', it updates on a slower interval, so lag/limit it downstream). Leave the battery/expression toggles OFF for a show machine. This CHOP is the spine every threshold and readout hangs off.

key_params.totalgpumem: on (VRAM MB total -- for a % ratio)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (fps, msec, cook, droppedframes, gpumemused, totalgpumem, gputemp)

verify.pass_if: the enabled channels are present and updating each frame (fps ~ target, droppedframes 0 at rest)

steps.note: NORMALIZE + DERIVE so every metric is comparable and alarm-ready. Two jobs: (1) rescale a raw metric into a 0..1 headroom figure with fromrange/torange (e.g. gputemp fromrange 40..90 -> torange 0..1 = 'thermal load'; fps fromrange 0..60 -> 0..1); (2) DERIVE the VRAM-used FRACTION with chopop=div feeding gpumemused / totalgpumem (a second mathCHOP or select the two channels first) -> a 0..1 'vram_frac'. Keep raw channels too (a parallel tap) so the readout can show real fps/temp numbers while the alarm logic uses the normalized ones. SMOOTHING: the gputemp channel is slow/steppy and fps can jitter -- pass those through a lagCHOP (lag ~0.2-0.5s) before thresholding so a single-frame blip doesn't false-trigger the alarm.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (normalized 0..1 health metrics + vram_frac)

verify.pass_if: each metric sits in 0..1; vram_frac ~ gpumemused/totalgpumem; healthy state near the safe end

steps.note: THRESHOLD -> ALARM (data-only comparison, no expression). Set convert to a comparison: 'gt'/'ge' fires 1 when a channel exceeds the bound (use for droppedframes>0, gputemp load>0.85, vram_frac>0.9, frame-time>budget), 'lt'/'le' for fps below target. The bound value is boundmin (the 'Bounds' field). Feed the normalized OUT_health so all bounds live in one 0..1 frame (or run one logicCHOP per metric with its own bound and merge). Then combine every per-metric flag into ONE master alarm with chanop=or (any metric tripping raises the alarm); chanop=and would need ALL to trip. Result: a clean 0/1 'alarm' channel (+ the individual flags for a per-metric light). This is the whole alarm brain.

key_params.boundmin: the threshold in the channel's units (0..1 if fed OUT_health)
key_params.chanop: or (any metric trips the master alarm)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (per-metric 0/1 flags + one master 'alarm' 0/1)

verify.pass_if: alarm is 0 in a healthy state and goes 1 when a fed metric crosses its bound (force it by lowering a bound to test)

steps.note: READOUT BARS = the live values as an image (the visual meter row). Point chop at OUT_health (normalized) so each channel becomes a horizontal bar/level; dataformat=r (or rgb for a colour-coded strip), layout=rowscropped stacks one channel per row. outputresolution=custom at a small readout size (e.g. 512x256) -- leave it at 256 default and the strip is a tiny square. This is the operator's at-a-glance 'are the bars in the green' surface; pair it with the numeric textTOP next.
steps.geometry_out: readout bar image of the live health metrics

verify.pass_if: one bar per metric, lengths track the live values

steps.note: NUMERIC READOUT -- fps / temp / dropped-frames as text. GOTCHA: the Text param DEFAULTS to the literal 'derivative' -- CLEAR it. Data-only live values two ways: (a) set chop=<the raw-metric tap>, chopvaluereplace=on, and put %-tokens in the text so the CHOP values substitute in (e.g. 'FPS %1  TEMP %2  DROP %3'); or (b) drive from a DAT with dat=<a choptoDAT/mergeDAT of the metrics>, rowindex/colindex picking the cell (the totaldigits/decimaldigits fields format it). fontcolor bright, bgalpha 0 for a transparent overlay, alignx=left, outputresolution=custom. This is the exact-number readout beside the bars.

key_params.text: CLEAR the default 'derivative'; e.g. 'FPS %1  TEMP %2C  DROP %3'

steps.geometry_out: numeric health readout as a transparent text image

verify.pass_if: live numbers render (NOT the word 'derivative'); values change as the engine load changes

steps.note: ALARM FLASH LAYER = a full-frame red the operator cannot miss. color red [1,0,0], outputresolution=custom at dashboard res. Make it appear ONLY on alarm, data-only: bind_chop the OUT_alarm master channel onto this constantTOP's ALPHA (or a nullCHOP with the export flag set -> autoname onto 'alpha') so alpha follows 0/1 -- transparent when healthy, opaque-red on trip. For a pulsing attention flash, multiply the alarm by an lfoCHOP square wave before the bind (still data-only). No expression, no callback -- the alarm value drives the parameter through the export/bind path, the same mechanism the rest of the rig uses for animation.

key_params.alpha: bind_chop OUT_alarm master -> alpha (0 healthy / 1 tripped)

steps.geometry_out: red overlay whose alpha = the master alarm (0/1)

verify.pass_if: alpha is bind/Export-driven by OUT_alarm; save_top shows transparent when healthy, red when a bound is forced

steps.note: DASHBOARD GRID = tile the readouts into one operator panel. tops multi-input (maxinputs 9999): wire OUT_bars, OUT_readout, and any per-metric lights; align=gridrows (or verttb for a stacked strip), numrows/numcols to shape it, fit=fitbest so each tile scales cleanly, bgcolora>0 for a dark panel backing. outputresolution=custom at the confidence-monitor/corner-of-program res. This is the single surface the projectionist glances at -- feed it to confidence_monitor_foldback's multiview or a corner of the program via the next composite.
steps.geometry_out: assembled health dashboard image

verify.pass_if: bars + numeric readout tiled into one legible panel at dashboard res

steps.note: ALARM OVER DASHBOARD = the deliverable watchdog surface. GOTCHA: compositeTOP over draws INPUT 0 ON TOP -- so wire OUT_alarmlayer as input 0 and OUT_dashboard as input 1 (or set swaporder=on / list the opaque dashboard LAST) so the red flash sits ABOVE the readout, not behind it. operand=over, outputresolution=custom. The result is one image: the health dashboard, overlaid by a red flash the instant any metric trips. Hand it to an operator window / confidence monitor / a corner overlay on the program bus (all WIRE-ONLY downstream). MILESTONE.

steps.note: LOG TAP (WIRE-ONLY / BUILT-NOT-FIRED). To retain a health history, wire a choptoDAT/mergeDAT of the metrics into a fileoutDAT (file = an absolute forward-slash .csv/.dat UNDER the working dir; append=on for a growing log). HONEST LIMIT: fileoutDAT's Write is a Pulse and it is NOT on the data-only allowlist -- so we BUILD the tap and set its file, but the bridge does not fire the write, and there is no data-only per-frame auto-write. Continuous disk-logging therefore needs a person to run the write, or external orchestration. For a one-shot snapshot of current values, write_csv (confined) captures a row on demand. Treat this as the reliability-record hook, not a running logger.

key_params.write: NOT fired -- not on the allowlist; wire-only

steps.geometry_out: log-file tap (built; write not actuated data-only)

verify.pass_if: file points under the working dir; tap wired -- (continuous auto-write is a known data-only gap)

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: threshold values + operator response / auto-recovery)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable telemetry + alarm + readout. === WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds the performCHOP tap, the normalize/threshold math, the readout image, the alarm-bound overlay, the dashboard, and the (unfired) log tap; sets every threshold NUMBER via set_par on the logicCHOP bounds. WHAT A PERSON DECIDES/DOES: (1) the actual THRESHOLDS -- the safe fps floor, the VRAM ceiling, the thermal limit, the dropped-frame tolerance -- are venue/machine specific and are judged by the operator, then typed back via set_par on the logicCHOP boundmin fields; (2) the RESPONSE -- an alarm is an alert, not a fix. Killing a runaway process, failing over to a backup machine, restarting playback, or lowering render load are ACTIONS off the data-only surface (they need scripts / OS control / external show orchestration). TD makes the degradation VISIBLE early; the human or an external watchdog acts. Auto-recovery and continuous disk-logging are the two honest data-only gaps here.

key_params.set_par (after operator sets limits): op=<the threshold logicCHOP>, pars={boundmin:<fps floor / temp ceiling / dropped tolerance>}

steps.geometry_out: thresholds tuned to the machine; response owned by a person/external system

verify.pass_if: logicCHOP bounds hold the operator's tuned values; alarm behaviour matches the venue's tolerances

recipes.classify: watch the show's HEALTH / RELIABILITY -- live system telemetry and a threshold alarm: frames per second (fps), frame time, cook time, DROPPED FRAMES, GPU memory / VRAM usage, GPU temperature -- with a warning overlay + numeric readout dashboard so the operator sees the show degrading (stutter, overheating, running out of VRAM, missed frames) BEFORE it fails; performance monitor, watchdog, health check, uptime, perfect-playback discipline, no dropped frames; distinct from confidence monitoring of the video feeds
recipes.governance: TELEMETRY + ALARM + READOUT are fully DATA-ONLY: performCHOP is a passive per-frame health source (no side effect); normalization/thresholding are CHOP math (mathCHOP/logicCHOP/lagCHOP); the alarm reaches the constantTOP alpha via bind_chop or the EXPORT flag (autoname) -- the same code-free animation path the rest of the rig uses. No evaluateDAT, no parameter expressions, no callbacks DAT, no script anywhere. HUMAN / OFF-SURFACE: (1) the THRESHOLD numbers are venue/machine judgement, typed back via set_par on the logicCHOP bounds; (2) the RESPONSE to an alarm -- process kill, machine failover, playback restart, load-shed -- is an ACTION the data-only surface cannot take (needs OS/script/external orchestration); TD alerts, a person or an external watchdog acts. HONEST GAPS: continuous disk-LOGGING is limited -- fileoutDAT is buildable but its Write pulse is NOT on the allowlist, so the log tap is wired but not run data-only (write_csv gives on-demand snapshots only); there is NO auto-recovery primitive. gputemp is the slow-updating 'GPU Temperature (Slow)' channel -- lag/limit it so it doesn't false-trigger. Everything is wire-only downstream: the watchdog image feeds an operator window / confidence_monitor_foldback multiview / a program corner, none of which this recipe opens or records. NC render cap 1280 -- author the dashboard at 1280-wide; swap to 1920 on the show machine, topology identical.
tips: textTOP's Text param defaults to the literal 'derivative' -- clear it and drive the readout from a CHOP (chop + chopvaluereplace, %-tokens) or a DAT (dat + rowindex/colindex), or the dashboard shows 'derivative' forever.
compositeTOP over draws INPUT 0 on top: wire the red alarm flash as input 0 (or swaporder=on / opaque dashboard last) so the alarm sits ABOVE the readout, not behind it.
droppedframes is the single most important channel -- threshold it at > 0 (any dropped frame is an event); it is the truest 'is the show keeping up' signal.
Pair gpumemused with totalgpumem and take the ratio (mathCHOP chopop=div) for a 0..1 VRAM-used figure -- an absolute MB number means nothing without the card's total.
gputemp is the slow-updating channel (labelled 'Slow') and fps jitters -- run both through a lagCHOP (lag ~0.2-0.5s) before the logicCHOP so a one-frame blip doesn't false-alarm.
Force outputresolution=custom on every TOP (choptoTOP, textTOP, constantTOP, layoutTOP, compositeTOP) -- any node left at the 256 default renders a tiny unreadable square.
Drive the alarm onto the constantTOP alpha with bind_chop (or a nullCHOP + export flag autoname) -- never an expression; multiply by an lfoCHOP square wave first for an attention-grabbing pulse.
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_watchdog(metrics=[fps,dropped,vram,temp], thresholds={...}, res) -> performCHOP + normalize/threshold math + readout + alarm overlay + dashboard, wired, in one call.
variants: minimal_dropped_frames_light: performCHOP droppedframes only -> logicCHOP gt 0 -> a small red constantTOP corner light; the cheapest 'is anything dropping' tell-tale for a locked-off show.
full_dashboard: all metrics normalized + bars (choptoTOP) + numeric (textTOP) + per-metric lights tiled by layoutTOP -- the full operator health panel for an attended show.
alarm_only_overlay: skip the dashboard; just the master-alarm-driven red constantTOP composited as a corner flash over the PROGRAM bus, so any degradation is visible on the output monitor itself.
logged_run: add the fileoutDAT/choptoDAT log tap (WIRE-ONLY) plus periodic write_csv snapshots for a post-show reliability record -- honest limit: no data-only continuous auto-write.
foldback_feed: route OUT_watchdog into confidence_monitor_foldback's multiview so the health panel travels with the low-res confidence feed to front-of-house.

recipes.title: Anamorphic naked-eye-3D across a 90-degree corner LED wall (ONE off-axis eyepoint cameraCOMP over a to-scale geometryCOMP scene -> renderTOP -> cropTOP split at the fold + per-face cornerpinTOP homography -> compositeTOP LED canvas -> led_wall_pixelmap_feed) -- the 'object floats out of the corner' billboard
recipes.summary: Build the forced-perspective, glasses-free-3D corner-LED illusion (the Seoul/Chengdu 'wave in a box', d'strict-style out-of-bounds billboard) where a hero object appears to bulge out of an L-shaped LED wall. The mechanism is ONE anamorphic camera at ONE fixed viewer eyepoint: model the hero object to real-world scale in a geometryCOMP scene whose world origin sits on the corner's vertical fold edge, place a single cameraCOMP AT the measured design eyepoint looking into the corner with an OFF-AXIS / asymmetric frustum (perspective projection, a wide fov that spans BOTH faces, plus winx/winy lens-shift to re-centre the frustum on the fold edge and hold verticals vertical for a high/low eye), render ONCE, then SPLIT that single eye-view into the two physical faces with a cropTOP at the fold column and a per-face cornerpinTOP (mapping=perspective) that maps each face's subtended image quad onto that face's exact LED pixel rectangle, composite both onto the combined LED canvas over black, and hand off WIRE-ONLY to led_wall_pixelmap_feed / ndioutTOP. WHY IT WORKS: an eye-ray through any face pixel hits the scene at exactly the point the single eye-render already captured, and image-region -> flat-face-rectangle is a plane-to-plane homography = the cornerpin perspective map, so the split render reconstructs the eye's view of the 3D scene and the object reads as floating out -- but ONLY from the design eyepoint (walk off it and the illusion shears). KEY DISTINCTION: this is ONE camera ACROSS both faces (single-viewpoint), NOT immersive_room_mapping's anamorphic-FLOOR mode which uses one camera PER surface. KEY GOTCHAS: renderTOP defaults to a 256 canvas and renders the geometryCOMP's default torus1 not your SOP (force outputresolution=custom + delete the torus + set_flags render/display on the real SOP); the single frustum must be wide enough to contain both faces (a close eye at a hard 90 fold needs a very wide fov -> edge resolution loss -> escalate to the per-face quad-reproject variant); compositeTOP over draws input 0 ON TOP, so place the opaque black canvas LAST or set swaporder=on or the black paints over the faces.

steps.note: THE HERO OBJECT, modelled to REAL-WORLD SCALE in the same world the LED faces live in (a box stands in for any hero mesh -- swap in fileinSOP/alembicSOP for a real model). Everything hinges on scale + placement: put the world origin ON the corner's vertical fold edge, then position/scale the hero so it straddles or bulges past that edge (that is what sells the 'out of the box' pop). Use sizex/sizey/sizez in metres to match the real install; tx/ty/tz to sit it at the corner (e.g. tz pushed slightly toward the eye so it appears to breach the plane). texture=boxinside gives clean UVs if you map content onto it. This SOP becomes the geometryCOMP's rendered child in step 3 -- do NOT leave the geometryCOMP on its default torus.

key_params.tz: small +Z toward the eye so it breaches the corner plane

steps.geometry_out: to-scale hero polygon mesh centred on the corner fold edge

verify.pass_if: box exists at the intended metre-scale size/position near the fold edge

steps.note: HERO SURFACE / CONTENT SKIN. A pbrMAT shades the object so it reads as a solid 3D volume in the eye render (naked-eye-3D depends on convincing shading + shadow, not just silhouette). Set basecolor + metallic + roughness for a lit look, or drive basecolormap / emitmap from a content TOP (a moviefileinTOP of a clip -- set its file via set_par with an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path UNDER the working dir; a relative/external path is blanked by path confinement). For a glowing/energy hero raise emit. This MAT is assigned on the geometryCOMP (material param) next step. TUPLET trap: the create tool takes basecolor=[r,g,b] / emit=[r,g,b] vectors; set_par uses raw basecolorr / emitr.

key_params.basecolormap: optional content TOP (moviefileinTOP clip) for a textured hero

steps.geometry_out: PBR material for the hero object

verify.pass_if: basecolor/metallic/roughness (or basecolormap) set as intended

steps.note: THE 3D SCENE CONTAINER placed in corner-world coordinates. Wire OUT_hero into it (or object-merge the hero SOP inside). CRITICAL default trap: a fresh geometryCOMP renders its internal torus1, NOT your SOP -- delete the torus (delete_op) and set_flags render=true, display=true on the real hero SOP inside, or you will render a torus. Assign material=OUT_heromat. Keep the COMP transform at identity so the hero's world position (set in step 1) is the truth the camera sees; the corner fold edge = world Z-axis (the vertical line where the two LED faces meet), Face A on one side (e.g. the -X wall), Face B on the other (e.g. the +Z wall), each a physical plane at 90 degrees. Model the two LED faces as un-rendered reference quads here (gridSOP, render=off) if you want an in-scene guide for the human's corner measurements.

key_params.(delete default torus1 + set_flags on he: mandatory so the hero renders, not the torus

steps.geometry_out: renderable 3D scene: hero at the corner, faces as world planes at 90 degrees

verify.pass_if: hero SOP has render/display flags on; default torus deleted; material assigned

steps.note: LIGHT THE SCENE so the hero has depth cues (shading gradients + optional shadows are what make it read as protruding, not a flat decal). lighttype=point or cone for a keylight, distant for even fill; dimmer for intensity; c=[r,g,b] colour. Position (tx/ty/tz) it to rake across the hero from the eye side so the near face is bright and the receding face falls off -- the luminance gradient is a primary monocular depth cue for naked-eye-3D. Turn on shadowtype (hard2d/soft2d) with shadowcasters=* for a contact shadow that anchors the object to the corner. Add a second fill lightCOMP for a studio look. renderTOP.lights=* picks up all lights.

key_params.tx/ty/tz: rake from the eye side across the hero
key_params.shadowtype: soft2d for a grounding contact shadow (shadowcasters=*)

steps.geometry_out: scene lighting (key + optional shadow)

verify.pass_if: lighttype/dimmer/position set; shadow on if a contact shadow is wanted

steps.note: === THE ANAMORPHIC OFF-AXIS EYE -- the heart of the whole illusion. === ONE camera at the SINGLE fixed viewer eyepoint (tx/ty/tz = the measured design viewing position in corner-world metres) looking into the corner (aim -Z at the fold edge, or set lookat to a null at the corner; keep the camera axis level so the virtual world's verticals stay vertical). projection=perspective. Give it a wide enough fov (viewanglemethod=horzfov) that the frustum's angular width CONTAINS BOTH faces as seen from the eye -- at a hard 90 corner viewed from nearby this can be 90-120 deg+, which is the practical ceiling (very wide fov = edge resolution loss; that is exactly when you switch to the per-face quad-reproject variant). Then apply the OFF-AXIS / ASYMMETRIC frustum with the lens-shift params: winx re-centres the frustum horizontally on the fold edge so both faces get balanced image area without yawing the camera off the scene; winy shifts it vertically so a high or low eyepoint keeps verticals parallel (no virtual keystone) instead of tilting the camera; winsize zooms the frustum. Set near small / far past the hero. This single asymmetric-frustum render, split next, is what 'one camera across both faces' means. DATA-ONLY off-axis fallbacks if lens-shift is not enough: projmatrixop can take a constantCHOP/tableDAT holding a bespoke 4x4 asymmetric projection matrix (pure data), and quadreprojsop reprojects the frustum exactly through a gridSOP screen-quad (the per-face-exact path).

key_params.lookat: a null at the corner fold edge (or aim -Z level)
key_params.fov: wide enough to span BOTH faces (often 90-120 deg)
key_params.winx: off-axis H shift -> re-centre frustum on the fold edge
key_params.winy: off-axis V shift -> hold verticals for a high/low eye
key_params.projmatrixop: OPTIONAL data-only: a CHOP/DAT 4x4 asymmetric matrix
key_params.quadreprojsop: OPTIONAL: gridSOP screen-quad for exact per-face reproject (variant)

steps.geometry_out: single off-axis eyepoint camera framing both LED faces

glsl_opportunity.why: a hard corner fold with an off-centre or very close eyepoint wants a bespoke single-pass off-axis / corner-fold projection matrix (exact asymmetric frustum, or a per-pixel fold that avoids the wide-fov resolution penalty) beyond what winx/winy lens-shift can express
glsl_opportunity.propose_via: glsl_reference then set_glsl to author a Custom Projection GLSL DAT on the cameraCOMP customproj parameter
glsl_opportunity.consent: needs the gated GLSL lane (default OFF); DATA-ONLY fallback used as the actual step = cameraCOMP winx/winy off-axis lens-shift + a projmatrixop CHOP/DAT 4x4 matrix, with quadreprojsop for exact per-face reprojection

verify.pass_if: projection=perspective, eyepoint tx/ty/tz set, fov spans both faces, winx/winy off-axis shift applied

steps.note: SINGLE EYE-VIEW RENDER. camera=OUT_eye, geometry=OUT_scene, lights=* (or OUT_light). This is the ONE render of the 3D scene from the design eyepoint that both faces are carved out of -- render once, split after. Force outputresolution=custom at the COMBINED working canvas resolution (wide enough to hold both faces at full LED pixel density AFTER the split; e.g. sum the two faces' widths plus headroom). rendermode=render2d. bgcolor alpha 0 so everything but the hero is transparent for clean compositing (white-on-transparent looks blank over a white preview -- judge it on save_top, not the preview page). 256px trap: leave outputresolution=useinput/default and you render a tiny 256 canvas. NC build cap: live render is limited to 1280 -- author at 1280, swap to full LED res on the show machine (topology identical).

key_params.resolution: [combined canvas w, h] (wide; NC preview cap 1280)

steps.geometry_out: single off-axis eye-view of the 3D scene (hero on transparent)

verify.pass_if: the hero renders (not a torus) from the off-axis eye at the custom resolution
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_eyeview -- the to-scale hero appears in one wide off-axis frame, transparent around it, spanning where both faces will be carved

steps.note: SPLIT THE EYE-VIEW AT THE FOLD COLUMN. The vertical fold edge projects to one column of the eye render; everything left of it belongs to Face A, everything right to Face B (swap L/R to match your face layout). Duplicate this cropTOP per face: Face A = cropleft 0 -> cropright at the fold fraction; Face B = cropleft at the fold fraction -> cropright 1 (cropleftunit/croprightunit=fraction; use pixels for exact panel columns). croptop/cropbottom trim height if the faces differ in height. extend=zero + outputresolution=custom keeps each slice clean. This is the coarse carve; the cornerpin next does the exact plane-to-plane rectification. Find the fold fraction from the eyepoint+corner geometry (human measurement) or by reading where the reference face-quad lands in the render.

key_params.cropleft: Face A: 0 | Face B: fold fraction
key_params.cropright: Face A: fold fraction | Face B: 1
key_params.cropleftunit: fraction (or pixels for exact panel columns)
key_params.croptop/cropbottom: trim per-face height if faces differ

steps.geometry_out: the eye-view slice subtended by one face (repeat for the other)

verify.pass_if: the slice holds only the Face-A side of the fold (mirror crop = OUT_faceBcrop)

steps.note: PER-FACE EXACT RECTIFICATION (the reason the split is geometrically correct, not a fudge). Each physical LED face is a flat plane; the region of the eye-view it subtends maps to the face's rectangular pixel grid by a plane-to-plane HOMOGRAPHY -- which is exactly cornerpinTOP with mapping=perspective. EXTRACT page (extracttl/tr/bl/br) = the four image-plane corners of the face's subtended quad in the eye render (identity if the cropTOP already isolated a clean rectangle; non-identity to undo the off-axis skew of that face's region). PIN page (pintopleft/topright/botleft/botright, unit fraction of the OUTPUT) = the face's exact rectangle on its own LED canvas. mapping=perspective (bilinear bows straight architecture -> the classic curved-edge bug), extend=zero, bgcolor alpha 0, outputresolution=custom at THAT face's LED resolution. Duplicate for Face B (its own extract/pin). A transformTOP before the pin flips (flip via negative scale) or nudges a rear-throw or mirrored face; a transformTOP after can fine-place the rectified face into the combined canvas. The human's measured corner numbers are typed back here via set_par on pintopleftx / pintoplefty / ... / pinbotrighty.

key_params.extracttl/extracttr/extractbl/extractbr: the face's subtended image-plane quad in OUT_eyeview
key_params.pintopleft/pintopright/pinbotleft/pinbot: the face's exact rectangle on its LED canvas (fraction)

steps.geometry_out: one face rectified onto its exact LED pixel rectangle (repeat for Face B)

verify.pass_if: the face's slice fills its LED rectangle with straight verticals; transparent outside
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_faceA + @OUT_faceB -- laid edge-to-edge at the fold the two faces read as ONE continuous eye-view of the hero (the fold is seamless from the design eyepoint)

steps.note: ASSEMBLE BOTH FACES ONTO THE COMBINED LED CANVAS. tops multi-input (maxinputs=9999): the two rectified faces (OUT_faceA, OUT_faceB) placed side-by-side (or per your LED processor's canvas layout) over a black constantTOP ground, operand=over, outputresolution=custom at the FULL combined LED canvas resolution. GOTCHA (bake this in): compositeTOP over draws INPUT 0 ON TOP -- so if you wire the opaque black canvas first it paints OVER the faces; wire the black LAST, or set swaporder=on, or keep the black canvas as a transparent-alpha sized ground. Because each face is transparent outside its pin rectangle, over-compositing drops each exactly where its transform/pins put it. If the LED processor wants the two faces as separate feeds instead of one canvas, skip the composite and take each OUT_faceX straight to its own output (see next steps).

key_params.tops: OUT_faceA, OUT_faceB (+ black constantTOP LAST or swaporder=on)
key_params.swaporder: on (so the opaque black lands UNDER the faces)

steps.geometry_out: both faces composited into the one combined LED canvas

verify.pass_if: both faces present at their canvas positions over black; neither painted out
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_ledcanvas -- the full corner-LED canvas at combined resolution, both faces in place, ready for the processor map

steps.note: STABLE ALIGNED TAP. Every downstream output op targets this NAME so the physical feed can be swapped without rewiring. Wire OUT_ledcanvas -> this. Hand off WIRE-ONLY to led_wall_pixelmap_feed (canvas -> per-tile map for the Novastar/Brompton processor) or straight to ndioutTOP / st2110outTOP / videodeviceoutTOP -- all built but NOT actuated by us (ndiout/st2110out active DEFAULT ON -> set OFF; windowCOMP not opened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF). For a two-independent-feeds LED processor, tap each OUT_faceX with its own null instead of the combined canvas.
steps.geometry_out: final corner-LED canvas, ready for wire-only output

verify.pass_if: combined corner-LED canvas at full resolution
verify.milestone_check: top_info @OUT_aligned -- holds the deliverable corner-LED frame the processor will ingest

steps.note: HAND OFF to the LED pixelmap lane. OUT_aligned (or each OUT_faceX) feeds led_wall_pixelmap_feed, which carves the canvas into the per-tile regions the LED processor (Novastar/Brompton/Linsn/Colorlight) ingests and wires the wire-only output TOP (active OFF). Do NOT rebuild the tiling here -- reuse that recipe. The PHYSICAL panel map (panel positions, gaps, rotation, colour calibration, and the two faces' pixel dimensions) lives in the processor software, set on site by a person; TD only delivers the correctly-sized, correctly-split canvas.
steps.geometry_out: (canvas handed to the LED processor pixelmap lane)

verify.pass_if: OUT_aligned is the input to the pixelmap/output lane; no output op is actuated

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: measure the corner, choose the eyepoint, map the LED processor)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === Three things ONLY a person on site can supply, and the illusion is exactly as good as they are: (1) the REAL CORNER GEOMETRY -- each face's physical size in metres, the pixel dimensions of each LED face, and the true dihedral angle of the fold (rarely a perfect 90); these set the scene scale, the fold fraction for the cropTOP, and the per-face cornerpin pin* rectangles. (2) the CHOSEN VIEWER EYEPOINT -- the single design position (camera-phone spot / hero photo viewpoint) the illusion is authored for; naked-eye-3D only holds from there, so the client must commit to it (height + distance + lateral offset). (3) the LED PROCESSOR MAP -- panel layout, gaps, rotation, and colour calibration live in the Novastar/Brompton software, set by hand. The MCP builds the whole anamorphic network and sets the eyepoint / frustum / crop / pins to a first estimate; the human's MEASURED numbers are typed back via set_par on cameraCOMP tx/ty/tz + winx/winy + fov, the cropTOP fold fraction, and each cornerpin's pintopleftx.../pinbotrighty. There is NO corner-LED / naked-eye-3D operator and no auto-calibration solver in the catalog -- this typed off-axis-camera network is the data-only substitute.

key_params.set_par (after measurement): cameraCOMP {tx,ty,tz,winx,winy,fov}; cropTOP {cropleft/cropright at fold}; cornerpinTOP {pintopleftx..pinbotrighty per face}

steps.geometry_out: the hero floating out of the real corner once the measured eyepoint + fold + face rectangles are typed in

verify.pass_if: eyepoint/frustum hold on-site values (or a first estimate for authoring)

recipes.classify: naked-eye 3D / naked eye 3D / glasses-free 3D / anamorphic corner LED / L-shaped LED wall / 90-degree corner LED / forced-perspective billboard / object floats or bulges out of the screen / out-of-bounds 3D / illusory depth billboard / the Seoul wave-in-a-box / Chengdu / d'strict-style corner LED / single-viewpoint off-axis anamorphic content / asymmetric frustum hero camera / make a 3D object pop out of a corner LED wall for one design eyepoint (ONE camera across both faces, split to the two LED faces) -- NOT immersive room / anamorphic floor (that is one camera PER surface)
recipes.governance: DOMAIN = render: the deliverable is rendered 3D content (an anamorphic eye-view of a to-scale scene), and the crop/cornerpin fold-split is its geometry-correction tail; it sits beside facade_3d_render, not with the surface-warp mapping recipes. TWO-PHASE. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the whole anamorphic network -- hero SOP, PBR material, geometryCOMP scene at the corner, lights, the SINGLE off-axis eyepoint cameraCOMP (perspective + winx/winy lens-shift, optionally a projmatrixop CHOP/DAT 4x4 matrix or a quadreprojsop screen-quad), the single renderTOP, the cropTOP fold-split, the per-face cornerpinTOP homographies, the compositor, and the aligned null -- is created / wired / parameterised by the bridge with literal numbers. No script/execute/cplusplus op, no parameter expressions, no callback DATs; the off-axis frustum is done entirely with data (lens-shift params + optional matrix-in-a-CHOP). (2) HUMAN / ON-SITE: the corner's real face sizes + pixel dimensions + true fold angle, the CHOSEN design eyepoint (the illusion is single-viewpoint and only holds from there), and the LED processor's panel/colour map are measured/decided by a person and typed back via set_par. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: nothing here is actuated -- led_wall_pixelmap_feed / ndioutTOP / st2110outTOP / videodeviceoutTOP are wired with active OFF (defaults ON), windowCOMP never opened. GEOMETRIC HONESTY: the single-eye render + perspective-cornerpin split is EXACT (an eye-ray through a face pixel hits the scene point the render already captured; image-region -> flat-face is a homography = the cornerpin), with ONE practical limit -- a single planar image plane can only span < 180 deg, and a close eye at a hard 90 fold needs a very wide fov that costs edge resolution; when that bites, escalate to the per-face quad-reproject VARIANT (each face = its own eyepoint-shared off-axis frustum via cameraCOMP quadreprojsop, geometrically exact with no wide-fov penalty -- which edges toward, but is not, immersive_room_mapping's one-camera-per-surface because the eyepoint is shared). HONEST GAPS: there is NO corner-LED / naked-eye-3D operator and NO projector<->LED auto-calibration solver in the catalog -- this typed off-axis-camera network is their data-only substitute; a truly bespoke single-pass corner-fold projection is the glsl_opportunity (customproj, gated). NC render cap 1280: author at 1280 preview res, swap resolution to full LED canvas on the show machine (topology identical).
tips: ONE camera, ONE eyepoint, ONE render, then split -- that single-viewpoint pipeline IS the illusion. If you find yourself making a camera per face you have drifted into immersive_room_mapping; come back unless you specifically want the exact quad-reproject variant (which still shares the one eyepoint).

winx/winy are LENS-SHIFT (off-axis), not camera rotation: shift the frustum to re-centre on the fold and to hold a high/low eye's verticals vertical. Rotating the camera instead introduces virtual keystone that shears the hero.

Keep the hero straddling / breaching the corner fold edge -- an object that pokes past the physical plane toward the eye is what reads as 'floating out'; a hero parked flat on one face just looks like a video.

mapping=perspective on every cornerpin (and extract) -- bilinear bows straight architecture and long edges (the 'why is my building curved' bug). Perspective IS the plane-to-plane homography that makes the split exact.
Force outputresolution=custom on the renderTOP, both cropTOPs, both cornerpinTOPs, and the compositor. Any node left at useinput/256 renders the 256px trap or composites at the wrong size.
Delete the geometryCOMP default torus1 and set_flags render/display on the real hero SOP, or you will render a torus with a perfect off-axis frustum.

compositeTOP over draws input 0 ON TOP: wire the opaque black canvas LAST or set swaporder=on, or the black paints over both faces. Each face must stay transparent (bgcolor alpha 0, extend=zero) outside its pin rectangle to over-composite cleanly.

Judge the render on save_top, not the transparent preview page: a white/emissive hero on alpha-0 background looks blank over a white UI. HELPER CANDIDATE: build_anamorphic_corner(eyepoint, faceA_rect, faceB_rect, fold_angle) -> scene + off-axis camera + split + pins in one call.
variants: per_face_quad_reproject (geometrically exact, no wide-fov penalty): instead of one wide render, model each LED face as a gridSOP quad (rows=2, cols=2 -> 4 points) in corner-world space and give each face its OWN renderTOP from a cameraCOMP that SHARES the eyepoint but sets quadreprojsop=that face's grid + quadreprojpts1-4 to its corner point indices. Exact off-axis per face, no split needed -- use when a close eye at a hard fold makes the single-frustum fov too wide/lossy.

custom_projection_matrix (data-only exact off-axis): drive cameraCOMP projmatrixop from a constantCHOP/tableDAT holding a bespoke 4x4 asymmetric-frustum matrix (16 values, still pure data, no expression) when winx/winy lens-shift cannot express the required skew -- a precise off-axis frustum without the GLSL lane.

textured_hero / video-out-of-the-box: drive the pbrMAT basecolormap or emitmap from a moviefileinTOP (or a generative composite tap) so a playing clip appears wrapped on the protruding object -- the animated 'liquid/creature in the box' look; keep the content TOP path absolute + under the working dir.

animated hero + eyepoint-locked move: keyframeCHOP / lfoCHOP / patternCHOP -> exported (set_flags export) onto the hero geometryCOMP tx/ty/tz/rx/ry/rz for the object to lunge out and recede; the CAMERA stays pinned to the design eyepoint (moving it breaks the single-viewpoint illusion).

two_independent_feeds: some LED processors want each face as its own source, not one canvas -- skip the compositeTOP and tap OUT_faceA / OUT_faceB each with its own nullTOP straight into led_wall_pixelmap_feed / per-face ndiout (active OFF).

4K / full-wall delivery: set every outputresolution=custom to the real per-face and combined LED resolutions; topology identical (NC preview cap 1280 downscales for authoring, full res on the show machine).

recipes.title: Lidar presence interaction -- 2D laser scanner drives an interactive floor/wall (hokuyoCHOP/leuzerod4CHOP -> blobtrackCHOP -> lag/math calibration -> logic zone gates -> bind_chop onto reactive content / interaction mask -> OUT_aligned) -- the large-area interactive-install sensor lane, distinct from camera vision
recipes.summary: Build a large-area INTERACTIVE FLOOR/WALL driven by a 2D laser range scanner -- the standard interactive-install sensor (Hokuyo UST/URG, Leuze ROD4), NOT a camera. A hokuyoCHOP (serial or ethernet) sweeps a fan of range samples across the floor plane and outputs them as polar (distance-per-step) or cartesian (x,y-per-point) channels; a blobtrackCHOP clusters those points into per-person BLOBS with a centroid + velocity; a lagCHOP smooths the jitter; a mathCHOP RE-RANGES the raw scan-space metres into 0..1 projection UV (this is the scan-to-canvas calibration, the numbers a human measures on site); a logicCHOP turns positions into zone/presence GATES. Those channels then drive reactive content code-free -- the cleanest example is a circleTOP 'spotlight' whose centerx/centery are bind_chop-bound to the blob position so a pool of light follows each visitor, feedbackTOP adds trails, and the same presence channels can instead feed the reveal/mask of vision_interactive_mask downstream (reuse it -- do NOT rebuild the reveal). KEY GOTCHA: hokuyoCHOP/leuzerod4CHOP are HARDWARE-bound with active=on default -- with no scanner attached they cook zero channels (like every device-in CHOP), so authoring/estimation uses a constantCHOP/patternCHOP stand-in of fake blob coords until the real sensor is live; and the mathCHOP re-range is meaningless until a human measures where the scan fan lands on the real floor. DISTINCT from vision_interactive_mask, which is explicitly camera/depth-scoped -- lidar is THE interactive-floor sensor (works in the dark, huge coverage, no camera-cone occlusion), and this recipe is its dedicated lane.

steps.note: THE SCANNER = the interactive surface's eyes. hokuyoCHOP talks to a Hokuyo 2D laser rangefinder over interface=serial (USB URG) or interface=ethernet (UST -- set netaddress to the sensor IP). It returns one channel-set per angular step from startstep..endstep (the sub-arc of the fan you care about -- trim to just the floor area to cut noise); output=cartesiancoords gives x,y per point (feed this to blobtrack), output=polarcoords gives raw distance-per-step. active is on by default. HARDWARE REALITY: no sensor plugged in => zero channels cooked; for authoring/estimation wire a constantCHOP or patternCHOP emitting a couple of fake x,y 'people' so the rest of the graph can be built and verified, then swap the real hokuyoCHOP in. leuzerod4CHOP is the Leuze ROD4 equivalent (ethernet, netaddress/port) and has its OWN built-in blob tracker (outputmode=blobtracking) -- use it to SKIP the blobtrackCHOP step (see variants).

key_params.startstep: first angular step of the floor arc
key_params.active: on (default; hardware-bound)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP fan of scan points (x,y per step, cartesian)

verify.pass_if: per-step x/y channels present and moving when a person crosses the fan (or the stand-in emits fake points)

steps.note: PEOPLE OUT OF POINTS. blobtrackCHOP (maxinputs=1) takes the scan point-cloud and CLUSTERS nearby points into blobs = visitors.
