Turn outputcentroid on (per-blob x,y centre) and outputvelocity on (per-blob dx,dy -- drives motion-reactive looks); maxblobs caps how many people you track; minblobpoints and maxpointdistance reject noise/reflections and set how tight a cluster must be; areaofinterest=rectangle with center/size masks the tracker to just the interactive rectangle (points outside are ignored -- kill the crowd behind the barrier); predicttype=kalman smooths and bridges brief dropouts. This node is the heart of the presence lane: its centroid channels are what the content follows.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP of per-blob centroid (+velocity) = tracked people

verify.pass_if: one centroid sample per person inside the AOI; count rises/falls as people enter/leave
verify.milestone_check: inspect @OUT_blobs while a person walks the fan -- a distinct centroid appears, tracks their path, and disappears on exit

steps.note: SMOOTH THE JITTER. Raw lidar centroids twitch sample-to-sample; a lagCHOP (lagmethod=value, lag1/lag2 in seconds, lagunit=seconds) low-passes the x/y so the reactive light glides instead of snapping. Small lag (0.05-0.15 s) keeps it responsive; larger lag = dreamier follow. overshoot adds a little spring/lead. Do this BEFORE the calibration re-range so the smoothing is in stable sensor units. Keep lag modest on velocity channels or fast gestures wash out.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP of smoothed per-blob centroid

verify.pass_if: centroid channels follow the person but without frame-to-frame twitch

steps.note: === SCAN-SPACE -> PROJECTION-SPACE CALIBRATION (the numbers a human measures). === The scanner reports metres from the sensor origin; the content wants 0..1 across the projector canvas. A mathCHOP re-ranges each axis: fromrange1/fromrange2 = the measured scan-space extents of the interactive rectangle (e.g. x from -3.0..3.0 m, y from 0.5..6.0 m), torange1/torange2 = 0..1 (the UV the content uses). Use gain/preoff/postoff for flips/offsets, chanop=len to derive distance-to-a-point if you want radial reactions. These fromrange numbers are the on-site calibration -- until a person measures where the fan lands on the real floor they are estimates. One mathCHOP per axis (x,y) or scope both. This is the data-only stand-in for a homography; a true 4-corner perspective map is a glsl_opportunity.

key_params.gain: sign flip if the axis is mirrored
key_params.chanop: len (optional: distance from a reference point)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP of blob position in 0..1 projector UV

glsl_opportunity.why: a rectangular re-range only corrects axis-aligned scaling; a scanner mounted off-axis to the floor needs a full 4-corner perspective (homography) to land blobs accurately across the whole area
glsl_opportunity.propose_via: glsl_reference then set_glsl on a glslTOP that applies a measured 3x3 homography to the position UV
glsl_opportunity.consent: needs allow_glsl (default OFF); data-only fallback = the mathCHOP rectangular re-range plus a modest AOI, accepting mild corner error

verify.pass_if: a person at a known floor spot reads the matching 0..1 UV (corner=~0/1, centre=~0.5)

steps.note: ZONE / PRESENCE GATES. A logicCHOP turns the calibrated position into on/off triggers: convert=bound with boundmin/boundmax fires 1 while a blob's coordinate sits inside a zone band (a hotspot tile, a doorway, a 'stepped here' pad); convert=gt/lt thresholds a velocity or distance; chanop=or/and across channels combines zones (any-person-in-any-zone, or all-zones-occupied). preop=rise/fall gives a one-frame edge for 'just entered'. The output gate channels drive discrete reactions (swap a look, arm a cue, light a tile) while OUT_stagecoords drives continuous follow. Feed either/both into the content step. For a per-tile floor, build a bound logic per tile and merge.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP of presence/zone gate channels (0/1)

verify.pass_if: gate goes 1 when a blob enters the zone band, 0 when it leaves

steps.note: REACTIVE CONTENT (concrete example) = a pool of light that FOLLOWS the visitor. A circleTOP with a soft-edged fill is the moving spotlight: fillcolor bright, fillalpha 1, softness > 0 for a feathered glow, bgalpha 0 so it composites cleanly, operand=over, outputresolution=custom at canvas res (256px trap: leave it and the light is a 256px chip). The DATA-ONLY drive: bind_chop the blob's OUT_stagecoords x -> centerx and y -> centery (centerunit=fraction, so 0..1 UV maps straight to the circle centre) -- the spotlight tracks the person with no code. Scale radius from velocity (bind a lagged speed channel) for a reactive pulse. For a FEW people, one circleTOP per blob; for MANY, drive an instanced pointspriteMAT from OUT_stagecoords via choptoTOP instead (see variants).
steps.geometry_out: soft spotlight TOP centred on the visitor

verify.pass_if: centerx/centery are bind-driven and track the blob; light moves with the person

steps.note: STACK REACTIONS OVER BLACK = the deliverable content frame. Wire a black constantTOP (color 0, alpha 1, outputresolution=custom at canvas res) as the FIRST/bottom input, then OUT_reactive (and each additional per-person spotlight) above it; operand=over, tops multi-input (maxinputs=9999), outputresolution=custom. GOTCHA: compositeTOP draws INPUT 0 ON TOP by default -- either set swaporder=on so input order reads bottom-to-top, or make the opaque black canvas the LAST input so it doesn't paint over the lights. Insert a feedbackTOP (target this composite, small fade via a levelTOP in the loop) just before/after to leave motion TRAILS -- a comet tail behind each visitor. This composited frame is what the projector shows.

key_params.swaporder: on (so input0 is the bottom, not the top)

steps.geometry_out: reactive content composited over black at canvas res

verify.pass_if: spotlights render over black exactly where the people stand
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_content with a person (or the stand-in) mid-floor -- a lit pool sits under them and moves as they move

steps.note: REUSE THE REVEAL DOWNSTREAM -- do NOT rebuild it. vision_interactive_mask already owns the presence-driven REVEAL/MASK chain (a soft alpha that unveils/erodes underlying content where people are). This recipe simply supplies BETTER presence data: feed OUT_stagecoords / OUT_presence (or OUT_reactive as the mask source) into that recipe's mask input in place of its camera/depth front-end. That recipe is explicitly camera/depth-scoped; lidar swaps the sensor and keeps the identical downstream reveal, blending, and holdout. Choose: use OUT_content (the spotlight look) as finished content, OR route the lidar presence into vision_interactive_mask to mask a richer video/generative layer.

key_params.keep: that recipe's reveal / blend / actor-safe holdout

steps.geometry_out: (lidar presence driving the existing interactive reveal)

verify.pass_if: the reveal responds to lidar presence, not a camera

steps.note: STABLE ALIGNED TAP. Wire OUT_content (or the vision_interactive_mask output) -> this null; every downstream output op targets this NAME so the physical output swaps without rewiring. Hand off WIRE-ONLY to projection_align_and_output / output_handoff (windowCOMP to the floor projector, or ndioutTOP -- active OFF by default here, so set it OFF; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF). A global cornerpinTOP/mesh warp AFTER this null keystones the whole interactive canvas onto the physical floor at once.
steps.geometry_out: final interactive frame, canvas res, ready for wire-only output

verify.pass_if: holds the composited reactive frame the floor projector will show
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_aligned -- the deliverable interactive canvas at projector resolution

steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable once the sensor streams. === On site a PERSON must: (1) physically MOUNT the scanner at the right height/angle so its 2D fan skims the interactive plane (floor-grazing for a floor, wall-parallel for a wall) -- the MCP cannot place hardware; (2) MEASURE where the fan lands on the real surface and type those extents into the mathCHOP fromrange (and the blobtrackCHOP AOI center/size) so scan metres map to canvas UV; (3) confirm the projector and the scanner cover the SAME rectangle. The MCP builds the entire graph, sets the AOI/calibration to estimates, and provides the reactive content + presence gates; the measured mount + calibration numbers are typed back via set_par on the mathCHOP fromrange* and blobtrackCHOP center/size. No scanner attached => hokuyoCHOP/leuzerod4CHOP cook nothing (use the stand-in until live).

key_params.set_par (after human measures): op=<mathCHOP>, pars={fromrange1:<measured>, fromrange2:<measured>}; op=OUT_blobs, pars={centerx:<measured>, centery:<measured>, sizex:<measured>, sizey:<measured>}

steps.geometry_out: people landing at the right canvas UV once mount + calibration are measured

verify.pass_if: fromrange/AOI hold on-site measured values (or estimates for authoring)

recipes.classify: INTERACTIVE FLOOR / interactive wall driven by a 2D LASER SCANNER (lidar) -- Hokuyo UST/URG, Leuze ROD4 safety laser -- for a presence-reactive projection install: people walking on a projected floor, a spotlight/pool of light that follows you, step-on hotspot zones, footfall/presence tracking over a large area without a camera, works in the dark, no camera occlusion; blob tracking, centroid, velocity, zone logic, scan-to-projection calibration; distinct from camera/depth vision -- lidar is the interactive-floor sensor
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the whole presence graph -- scanner CHOP, blobtrackCHOP clustering, lag smoothing, mathCHOP calibration re-range, logicCHOP zone gates, the reactive circleTOP spotlight bind_chop-bound to the blob position, feedback trails, the composite over black, and the aligned null -- is created / wired / parameterized by the bridge. Animation is CODE-FREE: bind_chop and the export flag carry live blob channels onto content params; no evaluateDAT, no parameter expressions, no callbacks/script/execute anywhere; every calibration number is a literal set via set_par. A true off-axis homography (vs the rectangular re-range) is surfaced as a glsl_opportunity, not baked. (2) HUMAN / HARDWARE: the scanner is a real device -- hokuyoCHOP/leuzerod4CHOP cook ZERO channels with no sensor attached (active=on default, same as every device-in CHOP), so authoring uses a constantCHOP/patternCHOP stand-in of fake blob coords; and a person must mount the sensor and MEASURE the scan-space->projection-space calibration (the mathCHOP fromrange + blobtrack AOI). WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: nothing here fires; downstream terminal ops (windowCOMP not opened; ndioutTOP.active default ON -> set OFF; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF) are handed off via projection_align_and_output / output_handoff. HONEST GAPS: this is DISTINCT from vision_interactive_mask (camera/depth-scoped) -- reuse that recipe's reveal downstream rather than duplicating it. There is NO dedicated lidar-calibration/homography tool -- the mathCHOP re-range is the data-only stand-in; there is no built-in occupancy-heatmap TOP (assemble from choptoTOP + feedback). blacktraxCHOP/optitrackinCHOP/posistagenetCHOP are 3D beacon trackers (see tracked_surface_content), a different sensor class. Depth-camera presence (orbbecTOP/realsenseTOP/kinectazureTOP + kinectazureCHOP skeleton) is NOW in the catalog as an alternative short-range presence/skeleton source (vision_interactive_mask); the scanning-lidar hokuyoCHOP/leuzerod4CHOP path here stays the long-range wide-area option. NC build caps live render at 1280; swap resolutionw/h for 1080p/4K, topology identical.
tips: hokuyoCHOP/leuzerod4CHOP are HARDWARE-bound (active on by default) -- with no sensor they cook nothing; author against a constantCHOP/patternCHOP stand-in of 1-2 fake x,y 'people', then swap the real scanner in and re-verify.
Feed blobtrackCHOP the CARTESIAN output (output=cartesiancoords) -- polar distance-per-step does not cluster cleanly into x,y blobs.
Trim startstep/endstep to just the floor arc and set the blobtrack areaofinterest=rectangle to the interactive zone -- it rejects the crowd/wall behind the barrier and kills most false blobs.

The mathCHOP fromrange IS the calibration -- until a human measures where the fan lands on the real floor, treat those numbers (and the AOI center/size) as estimates and expect to type the measured values back via set_par.
bind_chop the calibrated x/y (centerunit=fraction) straight onto circleTOP centerx/centery -- 0..1 UV maps directly to the circle centre; no expression needed.
compositeTOP over-draws INPUT 0 ON TOP -- set swaporder=on (or make the opaque black canvas the LAST input) or the spotlights vanish under the black ground.
leuzerod4CHOP has a BUILT-IN blob tracker (outputmode=blobtracking, maxblobs/areaofinterest/lowerleft-upperright) -- use it to skip the separate blobtrackCHOP when the ROD4 is the sensor.

HELPER CANDIDATE: build_lidar_presence(sensor='hokuyo'|'leuze', interface, aoi=[cx,cy,w,h], scan_to_uv=[[xmin,xmax],[ymin,ymax]]) -> scanner + blobtrack + lag + math calibration + logic gates, wired and named, in one call.
variants: leuze_builtin_tracker: use leuzerod4CHOP with outputmode=blobtracking (maxblobs, maxpointdistance, areaofinterest, lowerleft/upperright AOI corners) as the sensor -- it clusters internally, so drive lag/math/logic straight off it and drop the blobtrackCHOP.

spotlight_follow (base): one soft circleTOP per blob, centerx/centery bind_chop-bound to OUT_stagecoords -- a pool of light follows each visitor; scale radius from a lagged velocity channel for a reactive pulse.

instanced_crowd: choptoTOP the OUT_stagecoords into a geometryCOMP instancing (or pointspriteMAT) so an arbitrary number of tracked people each drive an instance -- one render, no per-person node cloning.

zone_trigger_show: use only OUT_presence (logicCHOP bound zones, preop=rise) to arm cues -- stepping into a tile swaps a look or fires a facade_cue_choreography cue (a step-on interactive floor rather than a continuous follow).

reveal_mask_handoff: feed OUT_stagecoords/OUT_reactive into vision_interactive_mask as its mask source -- lidar presence unveils/erodes a rich video or generative layer using that recipe's existing reveal, blend, and actor-safe holdout.

recipes.title: Line/contour mapping -- animated light-lines that trace a building's real architecture (traced contour SOP: dattoSOP/polysplineSOP -> carveSOP chase -> linethickSOP + lineMAT -> geometryCOMP/ortho renderTOP -> feedbackTOP trails -> OUT_content) -- the neon-outline / edge-tracing facade look, distinct from region masks
recipes.summary: Author the signature architectural-mapping look where ONLY the light moves along the building's lines -- neon outlines, edge tracing, contour reveals, running/chasing light on cornices, window frames, and structural edges. The contour SOURCE is the real architecture TRACED as line geometry: a survey/photo trace of the facade's edges becomes CV rows (write_csv -> tableDAT -> dattoSOP) that a polysplineSOP smooths into clean curves following the building, resampleSOP evens the point spacing; a carveSOP then extracts an ANIMATED sub-segment (domainu1..domainu2 bound to a patternCHOP rampcyclic phase) so a lit run CHASES along each contour; linethickSOP thickens the line into a ribbon and a lineMAT renders it as glowing neon (near/far colour, additive blending); a geometryCOMP holding that geometry is shot by an ORTHOGRAPHIC cameraCOMP into a renderTOP so the line-art stays flat and pixel-registered to the facade, with a feedbackTOP adding comet trails, all composited over black. KEY GOTCHA: a fresh geometryCOMP renders its default torus1 not your line SOP -- delete the torus and set_flags render/display on the real geometry; and renderTOP defaults to a 256px canvas (outputresolution=custom) with a black bg where white-on-black neon is invisible over a white preview page. DATA-ONLY animation is code-free: patternCHOP/lfoCHOP phase is exported/bound onto the carveSOP domain and the material, feedbackTOP makes the trails -- no expressions, no shader required. DISTINCT from facade_mask_atlas, which masks REGIONS (fills areas of the facade); this animates LINE-ART ALONG the contours. The alternate lane (variant) auto-traces a facade photo via edgeTOP -> tracePOP or multiplies an edge-outline mask into emit (extending facade_mask_atlas). HUMAN BOUNDARY: tracing the real architectural lines from a rectified photo/survey is a person's judgement -- the MCP builds the render/chase rig and consumes the traced CVs.

steps.note: THE TRACED CONTOUR = the building's real lines as geometry. A person traces the facade's edges (cornice, window frames, columns, structural seams) from a rectified photo/survey into ordered CV coordinates; author them as a CSV and load it code-free: write_csv the rows (x,y,z per CV, one polyline's worth) to a confined path, set the tableDAT file, then pulse(loadonstartpulse) (setting file alone does NOT read it mid-session). dattoSOP with pointsdat=<that tableDAT>, build=polyrow, closed off (open contour) turns the rows into a polyline SOP that literally follows the architecture. One tableDAT+dattoSOP per contour, or stack multiple polylines in one table. This is the data-only stand-in for hand-drawing in the viewport (no live-mouse tool exists in the catalog).
steps.geometry_out: polyline SOP tracing the facade edges

verify.pass_if: point count == CV rows; the polyline follows the traced architecture

steps.note: SMOOTH TO FOLLOW THE ARCHITECTURE. Raw traced CVs are angular; a polysplineSOP (maxinputs=1) fits a smooth curve through them -- basis=bspline for gentle flowing edges, basis=bezier/linear to keep hard corners crisp (a window frame wants corners, a swoosh wants bspline); polydivs/edgedivs set the output resolution of the smoothed curve. Then chain a resampleSOP (dolength on, length small; or dosegs) so points are EVENLY spaced along the arc -- essential so the carve chase moves at constant speed and linethick width is uniform. Uneven CV density otherwise makes the running light lurch. Keep OUT_smooth as the clean, evenly-sampled master contour.
steps.geometry_out: smoothed, evenly-resampled contour curve

verify.pass_if: curve is smooth and point spacing is even along the arc

steps.note: THE CHASE PHASE (the thing that moves). A patternCHOP generates the running-light phase: wavetype=rampcyclic sweeps 0..1 repeatedly (a chase that loops around the contour), numcycles/length set how many lit runs and the loop period, phasestep offsets multiple channels so several runs chase at once. Its 0..1 output is EXPORTED (set_flags export=true, exportmethod=autoname, channel named to the target) or bind_chop-bound onto the carveSOP domain in the next step. Swap wavetype=pulse/square for a blinking dash, sin for a breathing pulse. lfoCHOP is the simpler single-channel alternative (wavetype=ramp, frequency=runs/sec). This is the data-only motor of the whole look -- no expression, just a CHOP driving a parameter.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP 0..1 chase phase (exported/bound to carve)

verify.pass_if: channel ramps 0..1 and loops at the intended rate

steps.note: THE RUNNING LIGHT = an animated sub-curve reveal. carveSOP (method=extract, keepin on) extracts the portion of the contour between domainu1 and domainu2 (0..1 along the curve); BIND the OUT_phase chase channel onto domainu2 (and domainu1 offset behind it by the run length) so a lit segment SWEEPS along the architecture -- the 'light running along the lines'. A short u-gap = a comet; domainu1=0/domainu2=phase = a progressive draw-on reveal; wrap-around via the cyclic phase gives an endless chase. This is where the traced geometry becomes the moving light. Feed the extracted segment to the thicken/render; keep the full OUT_smooth as a dim underlay if you want the whole outline faintly lit under the bright runner.

key_params.domainu1: bind_chop <- OUT_phase minus run length (trailing edge)

steps.geometry_out: the lit sub-segment sweeping along the contour

verify.pass_if: extracted segment length is constant and its position advances along the curve as OUT_phase ramps
verify.milestone_check: inspect @OUT_chase across a few frames -- the lit portion slides along the traced contour (the running-light chase)

steps.note: THICKEN THE LINE INTO A RIBBON. A polyline has zero width; linethickSOP (maxinputs=1) builds a camera-facing ribbon around it -- startwidth/endwidth set the stroke weight (taper the ends for a comet by making endwidth < startwidth, shape=easeout), divisions/rows the tessellation, symmetric on to centre the ribbon on the line. This gives the neon its body and lets the glow read at projector distance. (Alternatively skip this and let lineMAT draw width directly via widthnear/widthfar -- see the lineMAT step; linethickSOP is the SOP-geometry route that also UV-maps the ribbon for gradient textures.)
steps.geometry_out: thickened line ribbon (camera-facing stroke)

verify.pass_if: the contour is now a ribbon of the intended width, tapered at the ends if set

steps.note: NEON MATERIAL = how the light-line looks. lineMAT renders line/ribbon geometry as glowing strokes: linenearcolor/linefarcolor set the near/far gradient (drive a bright saturated neon), linenearalpha/linefaralpha the falloff, widthnear/widthfar an additional distance-based width, linejointtype=round + round caps for smooth bends, and CRUCIALLY blending=on with blendop=add (srcblend=one) so overlapping strokes and the feedback trail SUM into an additive glow instead of flat over-paint. Assign this MAT to the geometryCOMP's material (or the renderTOP overridemat). Bind a lineMAT colour/alpha channel to OUT_phase for a pulse that travels with the runner. This is the difference between a dull line and convincing neon.
steps.geometry_out: neon line material (assigned to the geometryCOMP)

verify.pass_if: additive blending on; near/far colours set; MAT assigned to the render geometry

steps.note: RENDER THE LINE-ART, REGISTERED TO THE FACADE. Put OUT_ribbon (with the lineMAT) inside a geometryCOMP -- and DELETE its default torus1 + set_flags render=on/display=on on the real line SOP, or the render shows a torus not your contour (the classic fresh-geometryCOMP trap). Shoot it with an ORTHOGRAPHIC cameraCOMP (projection=ortho, orthowidth framing the facade extents) so the lines stay FLAT and pixel-registered to the building's real geometry -- a perspective camera would foreshorten and break alignment. renderTOP: camera=that cam, bgcolora 0 (transparent) or 0 alpha over a separate black, outputresolution=custom at projector res (256px + black-bg traps), antialias aa8 so thin neon doesn't crawl. This is the lit contour frame.

key_params.geometry: the geometryCOMP (torus deleted, real SOP render/display on)

steps.geometry_out: neon line-art rendered flat, registered to the facade

verify.pass_if: the traced contours render as bright lines on transparent/black -- NOT a torus, not a 256px chip
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_lines -- the running light reads as neon strokes tracing the facade at projector resolution

steps.note: COMET TRAILS. A feedbackTOP (target=the composite/render, maxinputs=1) feeds the previous frame back, dimmed, so each chase run leaves a fading TAIL along the contour -- the trail that sells the 'light streaking along the edges' look. Wire OUT_lines -> feedbackTOP, put a levelTOP (brightness1 ~0.9, or gamma) in the feedback loop to set the decay length, and composite the fresh render OVER the faded feedback (operand=over/add). resetpulse clears it on a cue. Longer decay = longer comet; add blend keeps trails glowing additively. Skip for a hard, trail-free line.
steps.geometry_out: line render with fading motion trails

verify.pass_if: each run leaves a decaying tail along the contour behind the bright leading edge

steps.note: OVER BLACK -> the deliverable, and the aligned tap. Composite OUT_trails (and any dim full-outline underlay) over a black constantTOP (color 0, alpha 1, outputresolution=custom at projector res): operand=over, outputresolution=custom. GOTCHA: compositeTOP draws INPUT 0 ON TOP -- set swaporder=on (or make the opaque black canvas the LAST input) so the neon isn't buried under black. Then a nullTOP(OUT_aligned) is the stable tap every output op targets; hand off WIRE-ONLY to projection_align_and_output / output_handoff (a global cornerpinTOP/mesh warp here keystones the whole line frame onto the facade; windowCOMP not opened; ndioutTOP.active default ON -> set OFF; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF).

key_params.tops: black constantTOP + OUT_trails (+ dim outline underlay)

steps.geometry_out: neon contour animation composited over black at projector res

verify.pass_if: bright animated line-art over solid black, ready for the facade
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_content over 2-3 frames -- the light chases along the traced architecture over black; nullTOP OUT_aligned holds the deliverable

steps.note: ALTERNATE LANE + REGION REUSE (distinct recipe). Two crossovers: (1) INSTEAD of tracing geometry, AUTO-TRACE a rectified facade photo -- an edgeTOP (select=luminance, strength high, alphaoutputmenu=edge) extracts the outlines as a TOP mask; MULTIPLY that edge mask into a content layer's emit/alpha (like facade_mask_atlas multiplies region masks) for an edge-outline glow with no SOP geometry; or feed the edge TOP into a tracePOP (top=edgeTOP, threshold, twodimensions=contourls) to auto-generate contour line geometry to render exactly as above. (2) facade_mask_atlas masks REGIONS (fills areas); this recipe animates LINE-ART along edges -- combine them: mask a region AND run a contour chase around its border. Reuse the atlas's per-region masks to GATE which contours light when.

key_params.edge_lane: edgeTOP -> multiplyTOP into emit  (or edgeTOP -> tracePOP -> render)
key_params.distinct_from_atlas: atlas = region fills; this = line-art along contours

steps.geometry_out: (auto-trace edge lane / region gating via the atlas)

verify.pass_if: edgeTOP isolates the facade outlines (edge-mask lane) or feeds tracePOP contours

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: trace the real architectural lines from a photo/survey)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable once the contour CVs exist. === A PERSON must TRACE the building's actual edges -- from a rectified/orthorectified photo or a survey drawing -- deciding WHICH lines to light (cornice, reveals, columns, joints) and their exact CV positions in canvas UV; that architectural judgement and the manual trace against the real facade cannot be emitted. The MCP builds the ENTIRE render/chase/trail rig and consumes the traced CVs (write_csv -> tableDAT -> dattoSOP), then aligns the whole frame with a global warp downstream. The traced numbers arrive as the CSV; on-site nudges are typed back via set_par on the contour points (or re-authored CSV + reload). The auto-trace variant (edgeTOP/tracePOP from a photo) reduces but does not remove this -- someone still picks the source photo, threshold, and which edges matter.

key_params.human_provides: traced facade contour CVs in canvas UV (the write_csv rows)
key_params.reload: set tableDAT file -> pulse(loadonstartpulse) after a re-trace

steps.geometry_out: lines landing on the real architecture once the trace is authored + globally aligned

verify.pass_if: contour SOP reflects the on-site traced CVs (or an estimate for authoring)

recipes.classify: animated CONTOUR / edge / outline light-lines that TRACE a building's real architecture -- neon outline facade, edge tracing, line-art mapping, running light / chase along the lines, light streaking along cornices and window frames, only the light moving aligned with the edges, contour reveal, draw-on outline, festival facade line tracing, architectural edge lighting; distinct from region masks -- this animates line-art along the contours, not fills of areas
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the whole line/contour rig -- the traced-contour SOP (dattoSOP from a write_csv/tableDAT survey, loaded via loadonstartpulse), polyspline smoothing + resample, the carveSOP chase, linethickSOP ribbon, lineMAT neon material, the geometryCOMP + orthographic cameraCOMP + renderTOP, feedbackTOP trails, and the composite over black -- is created / wired / parameterized by the bridge. Animation is CODE-FREE: a patternCHOP/lfoCHOP phase is exported (export flag, autoname) or bind_chop-bound onto the carveSOP domain and the material; feedbackTOP makes trails; no evaluateDAT, no parameter expressions, no callbacks/script/execute, no shader anywhere -- the neon look is plain lineMAT additive blending, not GLSL. (2) HUMAN: a person TRACES the real architecture (which edges, exact CV positions in canvas UV) from a rectified photo/survey -- that judgement is the input this rig consumes; on-site alignment of the whole frame is a downstream global warp. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: nothing here fires; windowCOMP not opened, ndioutTOP.active default ON -> set OFF, moviefileoutTOP.record OFF, handed off via projection_align_and_output / output_handoff. DISTINCT from facade_mask_atlas (masks REGIONS/area fills) -- this animates LINE-ART along contours; the two combine (mask a region, chase its border). HONEST GAPS: there is NO live in-viewport line-drawing tool (kantan-style) in the catalog -- the write_csv->dattoSOP CV path and the edgeTOP/tracePOP auto-trace are the data-only stand-ins for hand-drawing; tracePOP emits POP line geometry (render it inside a geometryCOMP like the SOP). NC build caps live render at 1280; swap resolutionw/h for 1080p/4K, topology identical.
tips: A fresh geometryCOMP renders its default torus1, not your line SOP -- delete the torus and set_flags render=on/display=on on the real contour geometry, or the neon never appears.

renderTOP defaults to a 256px canvas with a black background -- force outputresolution=custom at projector res, and remember white/neon-on-black looks blank over a white preview page (save_top to judge it, not the page).
Use an ORTHOGRAPHIC cameraCOMP (projection=ortho, orthowidth = facade width) so lines stay flat and pixel-registered; a perspective camera foreshortens and breaks alignment to the real edges.
resampleSOP the contour to EVEN spacing before carve -- uneven CV density makes the running light lurch and the linethick width pulse.
The chase = a patternCHOP wavetype=rampcyclic phase exported/bound onto carveSOP domainu2 (with domainu1 trailing by the run length) -- change wavetype to pulse for a dash, sin for a breathing pulse.
lineMAT blending=on + blendop=add + srcblend=one gives additive NEON glow so trails and overlaps sum; without it strokes flatly over-paint and the feedback trail looks muddy.
compositeTOP over-draws INPUT 0 ON TOP -- set swaporder=on (or put the opaque black canvas LAST) or the lines disappear under the black ground.

HELPER CANDIDATE: build_contour_chase(contour_csv, smooth='bspline', width, chase='rampcyclic', trail=0.9) -> dattoSOP + polyspline + resample + carve + linethick + lineMAT + ortho render + feedback, wired and named, in one call.
variants: progressive_draw_on: carveSOP domainu1=0, domainu2 bound to a one-shot ramp (lfoCHOP wavetype=ramp, no cycle) -- the outline DRAWS ON from one end, a reveal rather than an endless chase.

auto_trace_edge_mask (no SOP): edgeTOP (select=luminance, strength high, alphaoutputmenu=edge) on a rectified facade photo -> multiplyTOP into a content layer's emit/alpha -- an edge-outline glow with zero geometry, extending facade_mask_atlas.
auto_trace_geometry: edgeTOP -> tracePOP (top=edgeTOP, threshold, twodimensions=contourls) auto-generates contour line geometry from the photo, then carve/thicken/render exactly as the SOP lane.
breathing_neon: drive lineMAT linenearalpha / linenearcolor from an lfoCHOP sin instead of (or with) the carve chase -- the whole outline pulses/breathes rather than a run travelling along it.
region_plus_contour: combine with facade_mask_atlas -- fill a region with the atlas mask AND run a line_contour chase around that region's border, gated by the atlas per-region mask.

recipes.title: Show soundtrack playback + routing (audiofileinCHOP / audiomovieCHOP -> shuffleCHOP/reorderCHOP speaker map -> audiodeviceoutCHOP, timecode-locked) -- PLAY and ROUTE the show audio, not just react to it
recipes.summary: Every other audio recipe (audio_reactive_content, realtime_input_driver) CONSUMES audio to drive visuals; NOTHING in the library PLAYS or ROUTES the show soundtrack. This fills that hole: a CHOP-domain audio-OUT chain that plays a soundtrack file, keeps a clip's own track synced to its picture, spreads/orders the channels onto a multichannel or spatial speaker layout, and locks the whole thing to the show timeline/timecode so A and V stay frame-tight. Spine: an audiofileinCHOP plays a soundtrack .wav/.aiff (play/repeat/volume, cue for a hard start), OR an audiomovieCHOP references a moviefileinTOP and hands back that movie's OWN audio track kept in sync (syncoffset default -0.15s) so lip/beat sync holds; multiple stems merge (mergeCHOP), a master trim rides on mathCHOP/the deviceout volume. shuffleCHOP splits or replicates the stereo/mono bed into an N-channel bed and reorderCHOP puts the channels in the exact physical output order (FL,FR,C,LFE,SL,SR,...); renameCHOP labels them to speaker names so the patch is legible. audiodeviceoutCHOP is the actual hardware out (driver default/asio, per-speaker enables, outputs, volume/pan). SYNC: point audiofileinCHOP.playmode=timecodeop at a timecodeCHOP/ltcinCHOP, or export the show timerCHOP onto the index, so the soundtrack chases the same clock as the visuals (reuse show_control_timecode as master, timecode_chase_slave as follower). KEY GOTCHA: audiodeviceoutCHOP.active DEFAULTS ON and immediately routes to the system DEFAULT device -- build it and sound goes live to whatever Windows picked, which is almost never the show interface; enumerate with audiodevicesDAT and set device/driver BEFORE trusting it, and mind that channel indices are 0-based and a wrong reorder silently sends the LFE stem to a full-range top. HUMAN BOUNDARY: the physical audio interface, the speaker patch/amp gains, and the master-clock (LTC/word-clock) feed are all on-site hardware the bridge cannot see or wire.

steps.note: KNOW THE OUTPUT INTERFACE FIRST. audiodevicesDAT enumerates the available audio devices and their channel counts per driver -- set driver to the show interface's API (default = WASAPI/system, asio for a pro low-latency card, or blackmagic/aja/deltacast/datapath when audio rides an SDI/capture card), output=on to list playback devices. Read the table to learn the exact device name and how many output channels it exposes -- that channel count is the ceiling for the whole speaker map downstream. This is a pure read; it drives NO audio. Refresh with the refresh pulse if you hotplug an interface.

key_params.driver: default | asio | blackmagic | aja | deltacast | datapath

steps.geometry_out: table of audio devices, drivers, and channel counts

verify.pass_if: the show interface appears with its real output-channel count

steps.note: THE SOUNDTRACK SPINE. audiofileinCHOP plays a soundtrack file straight to CHOP channels (chan1/chan2 for stereo, N channels for a multichannel master). Set file via set_par to an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path UNDER the working dir AFTER create -- a relative or external path is blanked by path confinement (F2). play=on runs it, repeat=on loops an ambient bed, volume trims it, fade=on soft-starts. For a HARD cue start use cue + the cuepulse (a parameterless allowlisted action -- reloadpulse re-reads the file off disk). Leave playmode=sequential for free-run; switch to timecodeop in the SYNC step to chase show time. This CHOP is the audio the whole chain carries.

key_params.repeat: on for a loop; off for a one-shot cue
key_params.playmode: sequential (free-run) | timecodeop (chase -- set in SYNC step)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP audio channels (stereo/multichannel soundtrack)

verify.pass_if: audio channels present with non-zero sample values while play=on

steps.note: A/V-LOCKED CLIP AUDIO (use INSTEAD of the file-in when the sound lives inside a video). audiomovieCHOP references a moviefileinTOP by name (moviefileintop) and returns THAT movie's own audio track as CHOP channels, kept in step with the picture -- syncoffset (default -0.15s) nudges audio ahead of video to correct decode/display latency, audiotrack picks the track for multi-track files. This is how you keep beat/lip sync when the content is a movie rather than a separate stem: the picture path is the moviefileinTOP (reuse media_clip_player), the sound path is this CHOP into the same speaker map. Merge it with (or switch between) OUT_soundtrack via a mergeCHOP when a show mixes stems and clip audio.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP audio track of a movie, synced to its picture

verify.pass_if: channels carry the clip's audio and advance with the movie's frames

steps.note: BUILD THE MULTICHANNEL BED. shuffleCHOP restructures a stereo/mono soundtrack into the N discrete channels a spatial rig needs -- method=splitall / splitn spreads samples across channels, seqall/seqn re-sequences, swap flips L/R. Common spatial patterns: replicate a mono stem across several speakers (fan a voice-over to a cluster), or split a pre-authored multichannel master so each channel is its own CHOP channel ready to place. Pair with mathCHOP (gain / torange) for per-channel level trim, or a fanCHOP-style spread when you need copies. The output is the raw channel bed BEFORE it is put in physical output order. Keep channel count <= the interface's output count from OUT_devices.

key_params.method: splitall | splitn | seqall | swap (pick per spatial layout)
key_params.nval: N (channels per group when using *n / splitn)

steps.geometry_out: N-channel audio bed (one CHOP channel per speaker feed)

verify.pass_if: channel count matches the intended speaker count; each channel holds its stem

steps.note: MAP CHANNELS TO THE PHYSICAL SPEAKER ORDER. The interface expects a fixed channel order (typically FL, FR, C, LFE, SL, SR, then rears/heights); reorderCHOP (method=numeric with a numpattern, or character) reshuffles OUT_chanbed's channels into that exact hardware order so channel k lands on physical output k. Follow it with a renameCHOP (renamefrom/renameto) to LABEL the channels 'FL FR C LFE SL SR ...' so the patch is legible and audiodeviceoutCHOP's per-speaker enables line up by name. Getting this wrong silently sends, e.g., the LFE stem to a full-range top box -- there is no visual to catch it, so verify channel-by-channel. This ordering IS the speaker patch expressed in data.

key_params.method: numeric (order by number) | character | reverse | random
key_params.renameCHOP.renameto: FL FR C LFE SL SR ... (label to speaker names)

steps.geometry_out: channels in physical output order, labeled to speaker names

verify.pass_if: channel order + names match the interface's physical output map
verify.milestone_check: inspect @OUT_spkorder -- channel N carries the stem meant for physical speaker N, named for that speaker

steps.note: THE ACTUAL AUDIO OUT (hardware). audiodeviceoutCHOP sends OUT_spkorder to the interface: set driver (asio for a pro card) + device to the exact unit from OUT_devices, enable the per-speaker toggles you are feeding (frontleft/frontright/frontcenter/lowfrequency/backleft/backright/sideleft/sideright/top* -- or leave cyclechan=on to wrap channels onto outputs in order), and ride the master with volume/pan. GOTCHA / boundary: active DEFAULTS ON and, on create, immediately routes to the system DEFAULT device -- so sound can go live to the wrong output the instant this node exists; set device/driver via set_par BEFORE relying on it, and confirm against OUT_devices. Unlike ndiout/spout (which we force OFF), audio playing is the POINT here -- but WHICH device it plays to is the human's call. bufferlength trades latency vs stability.

key_params.active: on (default) -- audio goes LIVE to the selected device; pick the device FIRST
key_params.device: the show interface (from OUT_devices) -- set via set_par after create
key_params.cyclechan: on to wrap N channels onto N outputs in order

steps.geometry_out: (hardware audio out -- drives the interface's speaker outputs)

verify.pass_if: the node carries the ordered speaker channels; device/driver point at the show interface
verify.milestone_check: inspect @OUT_audioout -- channels equal the enabled speaker outputs; a level meter / the interface confirms sound on the right speakers

steps.note: LOCK AUDIO TO THE SHOW (A/V sync). To keep the soundtrack frame-tight with the visuals, give both the SAME clock. Build a timecode source -- a timecodeCHOP reading system time / an external feed, or an ltcinCHOP decoding SMPTE LTC off an audio input (totalsec on) -- then set audiofileinCHOP.playmode=timecodeop and point its timecodeop param at that CHOP so the soundtrack's play index CHASES show time. Alternatively export the show's master timerCHOP (its outseg/fraction) onto the audio index via the EXPORT flag (data-only, no expression). When the visuals are driven by show_control_timecode (master) the audio rides the same timer; when TD is a follower, timecode_chase_slave decodes the incoming code and both A and V chase it. Standalone loops skip this -- audiofileinCHOP.repeat carries them.

key_params.timerCHOP.exttcop: the same timecode source, so A and V share one clock

steps.geometry_out: CHOP running timecode -> audio play index (A/V frame-lock)

verify.pass_if: timecode advances; the audio index tracks it in step with the visuals' clock

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: physical interface, speaker patch, master clock)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === The bridge builds and orders the entire audio graph and names every channel, but three things live in the physical world and CANNOT be emitted: (1) the AUDIO INTERFACE itself -- the actual ASIO/SDI card, its driver install, and WHICH physical outputs exist -- the MCP can enumerate it (audiodevicesDAT) and target it (set_par device/driver) but cannot plug it in; (2) the SPEAKER PATCH -- the wiring from interface output k to the real speaker, amp gains, LFE crossover, and delay/EQ per zone -- all measured/tuned by a person with a meter and ears, then reflected back into the reorder/rename map; (3) the MASTER CLOCK feed -- the LTC/MTC or word-clock cable from the show's master into the audio input the ltcinCHOP/timecodeCHOP reads. WHAT THE MCP DOES: build the play + route + sync graph, set channel order/labels, target the device by name. WHAT THE HUMAN DOES: rig the interface, patch/tune the speakers, feed the clock, and confirm on the right speakers at the right level.

key_params.set_par (after human confirms the rig): op=OUT_audioout, pars={device:<measured device>, driver:<asio/...>, volume:<house level>}; reorder/rename to match the measured patch

steps.geometry_out: the show soundtrack playing on the correctly patched, clock-locked speaker rig

verify.pass_if: device/driver + channel map hold the on-site values (or a sensible default for authoring)

recipes.classify: PLAY and ROUTE the show soundtrack / audio playback -- play a soundtrack .wav/.aiff or keep a movie's own audio synced to its picture, send it OUT to the audio interface (audio out / audio device out / sound output), spread it to a MULTICHANNEL or SPATIAL / surround speaker layout (5.1 / 7.1 / immersive / speaker routing / channel map / spatial audio), and lock audio to the timeline / timecode for A/V sync; NOT audio-reactive (that consumes audio for visuals) -- this is soundtrack playback and speaker routing and the audio-out lane of running the whole show
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY: the whole play-route-sync audio graph -- source (audiofileinCHOP / audiomovieCHOP off a moviefileinTOP), merge/trim (mergeCHOP / mathCHOP), the multichannel bed (shuffleCHOP), the physical-order speaker map (reorderCHOP + renameCHOP labels), and the timecode lock (timecodeCHOP / ltcinCHOP feeding audiofileinCHOP.playmode=timecodeop, or the show timerCHOP exported onto the index) -- is created, wired, and parameterized by the bridge with literal numbers only. No script/expression/callbacks anywhere: A/V sync is done CODE-FREE via the EXPORT flag or the playmode=timecodeop reference, and cue starts use the allowlisted parameterless pulses (audiofileinCHOP cuepulse/reloadpulse, timerCHOP start/cuepulse/goto*). HARDWARE / HUMAN boundary: audio needs a real interface, a real speaker patch, and a real clock feed -- the MCP enumerates the device (audiodevicesDAT) and targets it (set_par device/driver) but a person rigs, patches, tunes (amp gains, LFE crossover, per-zone delay/EQ), and feeds LTC/word-clock. NOTE audiodeviceoutCHOP.active DEFAULTS ON and routes to the SYSTEM DEFAULT device on create -- unlike the video wire-out ops we intentionally leave audio audible, but the correct DEVICE must be set first or sound goes to the wrong output. There is NO save_top for audio -- verify every stage with inspect on the CHOP channels (channel count, names, sample values), not an image. HONEST GAPS: the catalog has no dedicated spatial-panner / object-audio / Ambisonics-decode / VBAP op -- discrete channel routing (shuffle+reorder to a fixed speaker layout) is the data-only stand-in; true object-based panning (Spat, d&b Soundscape, Dolby Atmos) lives in an external audio engine the show feeds. audioplayCHOP is an alternative fire-and-forget triggered player (mode=trigger, built-in device output + per-speaker index params) for stingers/one-shots rather than a continuous routed soundtrack. NC render cap 1280 is irrelevant here (no TOP render), but this recipe still contributes zero render load.
tips: Enumerate BEFORE you route: read audiodevicesDAT for the real device name + output-channel count; that count caps your whole speaker map, and the name is what you set on audiodeviceoutCHOP.device.

audiodeviceoutCHOP.active is DEFAULT ON and grabs the SYSTEM DEFAULT device on create -- set device/driver first or the show audio blasts out of the wrong (often built-in) output the instant the node exists.
Verify audio with inspect, never save_top -- check channel count, channel NAMES, and non-zero sample values at each stage; there is no picture to eyeball.

Keep A and V on ONE clock: playmode=timecodeop + a timecodeCHOP/ltcinCHOP on the soundtrack, or export the show timerCHOP onto the index -- do NOT let the audio free-run against a timecode-locked picture or it will drift.
For movie content use audiomovieCHOP (references the moviefileinTOP) not a separate file -- and tune syncoffset (default -0.15s) to your decode latency so beats/lips line up.

Channel indices are 0-based and reorder is silent when wrong -- label channels with renameCHOP (FL FR C LFE SL SR ...) so the audiodeviceoutCHOP per-speaker enables line up by name and a mispatch is visible in inspect.
asio driver = low latency for pro cards; drop bufferlength for tighter sync but raise it if you hear dropouts. Default (WASAPI) is fine for a simple stereo bed.

HELPER CANDIDATE: play_soundtrack(file, layout='stereo'|'5.1'|'7.1', device=None, timecode=None) -> audiofileinCHOP + shuffle/reorder to the named layout + renamed channels + audiodeviceoutCHOP targeted at the device, in one call.
variants: stereo_bed: a simple L/R soundtrack -- audiofileinCHOP (2 channels) straight into audiodeviceoutCHOP (frontleft/frontright on); skip shuffle/reorder. The minimal 'just play the show music' path.

surround_5_1_or_7_1: a pre-authored multichannel master split by shuffleCHOP and ordered FL,FR,C,LFE,SL,SR(,BL,BR) by reorderCHOP into the interface's surround map -- classic cinematic surround for a themed room.

spatial_multispeaker: many speakers around an installation -- fan/replicate stems with shuffleCHOP, place each on its physical output via reorderCHOP; discrete-channel stand-in for object panning (external Atmos/Spat engine does true object audio).
movie_av_sync: audiomovieCHOP off the show's moviefileinTOP (syncoffset tuned) so the clip's own track stays locked to its picture -- for video content rather than a separate music stem.

timecode_chase: playmode=timecodeop with an ltcinCHOP decoding SMPTE LTC (or timecodeCHOP off an external feed) so the soundtrack chases a festival/broadcast master clock -- pairs with timecode_chase_slave on the visuals.
triggered_stingers: audioplayCHOP (mode=trigger, per-speaker index params, built-in device out) fired by a cuepulse for one-shot stingers/SFX layered over the continuous routed bed.

recipes.title: SMPTE ST 2110 uncompressed video-over-IP delivery + PTP lock (st2110outTOP wire-only ACTIVE=OFF <- st2110deviceCHOP PTP <- content nullTOP) -- the broadcast-grade OUT scaffold that completes the NDI/Spout/SDI/2110 delivery matrix
recipes.summary: Deliver the finished projector/content frame off the machine as UNCOMPRESSED SMPTE ST 2110 video-over-IP (the broadcast / large-venue IP-fabric standard: separate essence flows for video, audio and ancillary, PTP-synchronised) instead of NDI, Spout, SDI or Direct-Display. The spine is exactly two nodes: an st2110deviceCHOP that owns the physical 2110 NIC and the PTP clock discipline, and an st2110outTOP that takes one content input (maxinputs 1) and transmits it, linked to the device CHOP via st2110devicechop. Everything is a STATIC LITERAL -- destination IP/port, signalformat, colorspace (including the HDR tokens rec2020st2084pq and rec2020hlg), outputbitdepth, PTP profile/domain/priority -- no dynamic params, no expressions, no missing operator: this is the cleanest wire-only OUT scaffold in the library. KEY GOTCHA / WIRE-ONLY CONVENTION: st2110outTOP.active DEFAULTS ON (it would start transmitting the instant it cooks), so this recipe MUST build it with active=off and hold it off -- arming the transmit is the operator's on-site step, identical to how ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active are forced off. HONEST HARDWARE BLOCKER (governance): a working 2110 flow needs a 2110-capable NIC (Blackmagic/AJA/Deltacast IP card or a Mellanox/Intel NIC with a 2110 stack) AND a PTP grandmaster clock on the network (the device CHOP is a follower by default, ptpfolloweronly=on). The MCP builds the correct, fully-parameterised data-only graph; the NIC, the grandmaster and the arm-live are pure hardware/wire steps a person performs on site.

steps.note: CONTENT TAP = the stable input the 2110 transmitter reads. Wire the finished deliverable frame into this null and target it by NAME so the physical output can be re-pointed without rewiring the map. This is normally the OUT_aligned / OUT_final tap handed over by projection_align_and_output / output_handoff or led_wall_pixelmap_feed -- do NOT rebuild the content chain here, just reference its output. Force the upstream resolution to match the intended signalformat (a 1080p 2110 flow wants a 1920x1080 source; a UHD flow wants 3840x2160) so the transmitter is not silently rescaling.

key_params.(input): wire OUT_aligned / OUT_final from the upstream output recipe into this null

steps.geometry_out: the finished projector-res frame, stable-named for output

verify.pass_if: resolution matches the target signalformat (e.g. 1920x1080), RGBA present

steps.note: THE NIC + PTP CLOCK. This CHOP owns the physical 2110 network interface and the Precision Time Protocol discipline that frame-locks the whole 2110 fabric. driver selects the card vendor {blackmagic | deltacast | aja}; device picks the specific board (menu is populated from real hardware -- empty in authoring, chosen on site). Network identity is either usedhcp=on (default) or a static ipaddress/subnet/gateway. The PTP block is the heart of 2110 sync: ptpprofile=st2059-2 is the SMPTE broadcast profile (aes67 for audio-led plants), ptpaddress/ptpdomain/ptppriority1/ptppriority2 must MATCH the plant's grandmaster, and ptpfolloweronly stays ON (default) so TD slaves to the house grandmaster rather than trying to become master. Set every value as a literal now; the values are inert until a real 2110 NIC is present. active defaults ON but does nothing without hardware -- the real transmit gate is the outTOP's active (next step).

key_params.driver: blackmagic | deltacast | aja (match the installed 2110 card)
key_params.ptppriority1: 128 (leave unless the plant assigns a priority)
key_params.ptpfolloweronly: on -- TD follows the house grandmaster, never becomes master

steps.geometry_out: CHOP describing the 2110 NIC + PTP follower config

verify.pass_if: driver/ptpprofile/ptpdomain hold the intended literals; ptpfolloweronly on

steps.note: THE TRANSMITTER -- BUILT ACTIVE=OFF (the whole point of the scaffold). This TOP takes the content null on its single input and emits it as an uncompressed 2110 video essence flow. active DEFAULTS ON and would begin transmitting the moment it cooks, so CREATE it with active=off and leave it off -- exactly the ndiout/syphonspout/direct-display wire-only pattern. Set the delivery literals: videodestip + videodestport (the receiver/switch multicast or unicast address), signalformat (menu, default f1920x1080 -- pick the raster+rate token the plant expects; device-dependent list), outputbitdepth {fixed8 | fixed8key8 | fixed10} (2110 broadcast usually 10-bit = fixed10), and colorspace -- for SDR use rec709, and for HDR delivery use rec2020st2084pq (PQ/ST2084) or rec2020hlg (HLG). LINK the device CHOP via st2110devicechop=OUT_ptpdevice so the transmit inherits the PTP timing. Force outputresolution=custom at the signalformat's raster (leave it useinput and it can inherit the wrong size / the 256px default on a bare graph). Optionally point timecodeop at a timecodeCHOP to embed SMPTE timecode in the ancillary flow.

key_params.active: off (build + hold OFF -- transmit is the operator's on-site arm; default is ON)
key_params.signalformat: f1920x1080 (default; pick the raster+rate the plant expects)

steps.geometry_out: a fully-configured, NOT-transmitting 2110 video-out node

verify.pass_if: active == off; st2110devicechop points at OUT_ptpdevice; dest IP/port/signalformat/colorspace/bitdepth hold the intended literals
verify.milestone_check: read_network @OUT_st2110out -- the transmitter is fully parameterised, linked to the PTP device CHOP, and ACTIVE=OFF (the deliverable graph, ready for the operator to arm once hardware is present)

steps.note: OPTIONAL SMPTE TIMECODE EMBED (broadcast/festival sync). 2110 carries an ancillary essence flow that can include SMPTE timecode; to embed it, build a timecodeCHOP (source = LTC off an audio input, MTC over MIDI, or tod = wall clock) and point the outTOP's timecodeop at it. Match rate (25 / 30 fps) to the plant master. Skip this step for a plain video-only 2110 flow; add it when the receiver expects frame-accurate timecode alongside the essence. This is data-only -- the timecodeCHOP just reads a running value; no expression or script.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP (running SMPTE timecode -> ancillary embed)

verify.pass_if: a running timecode value is present (or system time if standalone)

steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HARDWARE SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable and fully parameterised; NOTHING above transmits. === Going live is a pure hardware/wire operation the projectionist/broadcast engineer performs ON SITE: (1) install a 2110-capable NIC -- a Blackmagic/AJA/Deltacast IP card, or a Mellanox/Intel NIC running a 2110 stack -- and pick it in the device CHOP's device menu (empty until real hardware enumerates); (2) confirm a PTP GRANDMASTER clock exists on the network and that ptpaddress/ptpdomain/ptppriority match it, then verify the device CHOP has achieved PTP lock (a follower, ptpfolloweronly=on); (3) confirm the 2110-aware switch/receiver is subscribed to the multicast group at videodestip; (4) ONLY THEN set st2110outTOP active=on to begin transmission. The MCP cannot see the NIC, the grandmaster or the switch, and by wire-only convention never arms the transmit. If the on-site engineer changes dest IP/port/format, those measured values are typed back via set_par on OUT_st2110out (raw names videodestip / videodestport / signalformat) and on OUT_ptpdevice (ptpaddress / ptpdomain).

key_params.set_par (after engineer confirms hardwar: op=OUT_st2110out, pars={active:on} -- ONLY once NIC + PTP lock + receiver are confirmed on site

steps.geometry_out: a live 2110 essence flow, once real NIC + grandmaster + receiver are present and the operator arms active

verify.pass_if: active stays off in authoring; holds the operator's on-site values once armed

recipes.classify: send the show off the machine as SMPTE ST 2110 uncompressed video-over-IP (broadcast IP fabric, 2110-20/2110-30/2110-40 essence flows) with PTP grandmaster sync; ST2110 / SMPTE 2110 / 2110 output / video over IP / IP video / uncompressed IP / PTP / precision time protocol / broadcast delivery / Blackmagic-Deltacast-AJA IP card / rec2020 HDR PQ HLG 10-bit out; the broadcast-grade alternative to NDI / Spout / TouchOut / SDI / Direct-Display
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE, HARDWARE-GATED. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the entire 2110 graph -- content tap null, st2110deviceCHOP (NIC driver + full PTP follower config), st2110outTOP (dest IP/port, signalformat, colorspace incl. HDR rec2020st2084pq/rec2020hlg, outputbitdepth, device link), optional timecodeCHOP embed -- is created, wired and parameterised with STATIC LITERALS only. No script/execute/cplusplus op, no parameter expressions, no callbacks DAT; every value is a literal set via the create tool or set_par. This is the cleanest OUT scaffold in the library: 2110 has NO dynamic/unknowable params and NO missing operator. (2) WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT -- CRITICAL: st2110outTOP.active DEFAULTS ON (would transmit on first cook), so the recipe builds it active=off and HOLDS it off; arming the transmit is the operator's on-site step (same class as ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active / directdisplayoutTOP, all forced off). (3) HUMAN / HARDWARE: a live flow REQUIRES a 2110-capable NIC (Blackmagic/AJA/Deltacast IP card or a Mellanox/Intel NIC with a 2110 stack) AND a PTP grandmaster clock on the network (the device CHOP is a follower by default) AND a 2110-aware switch/receiver -- none of which the MCP can supply or see. HONEST GAPS: the device menu on both nodes is populated only from real enumerated hardware (empty in authoring); PTP lock status is observable only on the live machine; no 2110-INPUT is built here (that is signal_ingest_remap / st2110inTOP). This recipe completes the output-delivery matrix (NDI / Spout / TouchOut / SDI-HDMI / Direct-Display already shipped; 2110 is the broadcast-grade gap) -- it is niche but it is the correct, honest scaffold. NC build caps live render at 1280; the scaffold's dest raster (1920x1080 / 3840x2160) is a transmit format, independent of that preview cap.
tips: st2110outTOP.active defaults ON -- always CREATE it with active=off and confirm via read_network; forgetting this is the one way this scaffold could transmit unintended (it won't without a NIC, but hold the convention).
Link the device CHOP explicitly: set st2110outTOP.st2110devicechop = the st2110deviceCHOP, or the transmit has no PTP timing and no NIC binding.
ptpfolloweronly stays ON -- TD must slave to the house grandmaster; letting TD try to be PTP master fights the plant clock and breaks fabric sync.
Match ptpaddress / ptpdomain / ptppriority to the grandmaster exactly; a mismatched PTP domain means the device never achieves lock even with a NIC present.
10-bit broadcast: set outputbitdepth=fixed10 (fixed8key8 carries an 8-bit key/alpha); HDR delivery = colorspace rec2020st2084pq (PQ) or rec2020hlg (HLG), not rec709.
Force outputresolution=custom at the signalformat raster and match the upstream content resolution, so the transmitter is not silently rescaling the essence.
signalformat is a device-dependent menu (default f1920x1080); pick the exact raster+rate token the receiver expects -- a rate mismatch is a common no-signal cause.
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_2110_out(dest_ip, dest_port, signalformat, colorspace, driver, ptp_domain) -> device CHOP + out TOP (active OFF) + link, in one call.
variants: sdr_1080p: signalformat f1920x1080, outputbitdepth fixed10, colorspace rec709 -- the standard broadcast 1080p flow.
hdr_uhd: signalformat a 3840x2160 token, colorspace rec2020st2084pq (PQ) or rec2020hlg (HLG), resolution [3840,2160] -- HDR UHD delivery to a 2110 receiver.
timecode_embedded: add the timecodeCHOP step and set timecodeop, so SMPTE timecode rides the 2110 ancillary flow frame-locked to the plant master (broadcast/festival A-V sync).
aes67_audio_led: ptpprofile=aes67 for an audio-led plant whose PTP is disciplined by the AES67 audio network rather than the ST2059-2 video profile.
static_ip_no_dhcp: usedhcp=off with a fixed ipaddress/subnet/gateway on the device CHOP -- a locked-down show network with assigned addresses instead of DHCP.

recipes.title: Projector throw / lens / lumens / coverage PLANNING sheets (write_csv -> tableDAT spec sheet + constantCHOP/mathCHOP derived columns -> choptoDAT -> write_csv plan; optional cameraCOMP+renderTOP frustum preview) -- a data-only pre-production deliverable
recipes.summary: A PRE-PRODUCTION planning deliverable, not a live show graph: assemble a projector rig spec sheet (one row per projector: model, lens throw-ratio, lumens, native resolution, throw distance, surface size) as a tableDAT, compute the derived planning numbers -- image width = throw distance / throw ratio, coverage brightness = lumens / image area, edge-blend overlap -- with a small constantCHOP + mathCHOP block, tabulate the results back with choptoDAT, and export the finished plan with write_csv so it can go into a rigging/production document. An optional cameraCOMP frustum preview (a camera per projector at the numeric pose/lens, rendered through renderTOP) visualises coverage. KEY GOTCHA + HONEST LANE BOUNDARY (governance): the CLEAN, re-parameterisable form -- a table where each row's throw/coverage cells are LIVE per-row formulas over the input columns -- wants evaluateDAT, which is the GATED EXPRESSION LANE (allow_expr defaults OFF). This recipe does NOT bake that in; it surfaces it as an expr_opportunity and builds the DATA-ONLY FALLBACK as the actual steps: constantCHOP channels (one channel per projector) fed through mathCHOP (chopop=div / gain / range) to derive each column element-wise, then choptoDAT to reassemble a table. That fallback is honest and shippable but clumsy for many columns -- CHOP channels are per-sample, not per-row, so each derived column is its own little CHOP chain. The real lens / lumens / throw-ratio NUMBERS come from the manufacturer datasheet and the on-site measured throw distance -- a human supplies the source data; the recipe supplies the compute frame + the export.

steps.note: AUTHOR THE INPUT SPEC SHEET as a confined CSV -- one ROW per projector, columns for the raw datasheet + site values: name, model, throw_ratio, lumens, native_w, native_h, throw_distance_m (and optionally surface_w_m). write_csv writes to a path UNDER the working dir (relative/external paths are blanked by path confinement). These numbers are HUMAN input (manufacturer datasheet + tape-measure distance) -- the recipe does not invent them; it gives them a structured home. This CSV is the single source the rest of the sheet computes from.
steps.geometry_out: confined CSV file of raw projector specs (human-sourced numbers)

verify.pass_if: the CSV exists at the confined path with a header row + one row per projector

steps.note: LOAD THE SPEC SHEET into a tableDAT. Setting file alone does NOT read it mid-session: set file to the confined CSV path, then pulse(loadonstartpulse) to actually load (the tableDAT.file-does-not-auto-load gotcha). Optionally set loadonstart=on so it also reloads with the project. This DAT is the readable spec table the human reviews and the compute block reads its numbers from. Keep includenames aligned with whether your CSV has a header row.

key_params.loadonstartpulse: pulse it after setting file -- file alone does not read mid-session

steps.geometry_out: the projector spec table, loaded and readable

verify.pass_if: rows == projector count + header; throw_ratio/lumens/throw_distance columns present and populated

steps.note: LIFT THE NUMERIC INPUT COLUMNS INTO CHANNELS = the data-only compute substrate. Build one constantCHOP whose CHANNELS are the per-projector values of a column: e.g. a 'throw_distance' CHOP with one channel per projector (const0name=P1 const0value=9.0, const1name=P2 const1value=9.0, ...), and a second constantCHOP 'throw_ratio' with a channel per projector. single=on (one sample -- these are static planning constants, not a signal). NOTE the CHOP-per-row limitation baked into governance: CHOP channels are per-SAMPLE not per-ROW, so each input column becomes its own constantCHOP with N channels; this is the clumsy-but-honest fallback for the elegant evaluateDAT per-row-formula version. Values here mirror the spec table's columns (author them from OUT_specs by hand, or set_par from the loaded table).

key_params.const1name: P2, const1value = its throw_distance ... (one channel per projector)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP: one channel per projector for a given input column

verify.pass_if: one channel per projector holding that column's per-projector value

steps.note: DERIVE THE PLANNING COLUMNS element-wise across projectors = the compute. IMAGE WIDTH (m) = throw_distance / throw_ratio: wire the 'throw_distance' constantCHOP and the 'throw_ratio' constantCHOP into one mathCHOP and set chopop=div (Combine CHOPs -> chan-by-chan divide, matched by index or name) -> one channel per projector holding its image width. Other columns reuse the same node type: image AREA = width * height (chopop=mul on width + height CHOPs); COVERAGE brightness (lumens/m^2) = lumens / area (chopop=div); a simple scalar column (e.g. apply a global de-rate) uses gain / preoff / postoff; a normalise-to-range column uses fromrange/torange. Build one small mathCHOP chain per derived column -- clumsy for many columns, which is exactly why the elegant per-row-formula form wants the gated expression lane (see expr_opportunity).

key_params.chopop: div (image width = distance/ratio; coverage = lumens/area) | mul (area = w*h)
key_params.gain: a global de-rate / unit scale factor when needed
key_params.preoff: additive offset applied before gain (e.g. bezel/overlap allowance)
key_params.fromrange: [min,max] and torange [0,1] to normalise a column for a preview

steps.geometry_out: CHOP: one derived planning channel per projector (e.g. image width)

verify.pass_if: each projector's derived value equals the hand-checked distance/ratio (etc.)

expr_opportunity.why: the CLEAN, re-parameterisable plan is a table whose per-row throw/image-size/coverage/overlap cells are LIVE formulas over the input columns (each row: throw_distance/throw_ratio, lumens/area, ...) -- a single evaluateDAT sheet expresses all columns for all N projectors at once and re-computes when any input cell changes, where the CHOP-math fallback needs one constantCHOP+mathCHOP chain per column and manual reassembly
expr_opportunity.propose_via: expr_reference to compose the per-row cell expressions, then set_expr / the evaluateDAT expression lane on a table whose cells reference the spec columns
expr_opportunity.consent: needs allow_expr (default OFF, owner-gated); the DATA-ONLY fallback built in steps 3-5 (constantCHOP -> mathCHOP -> choptoDAT) ships now without it and is correct, just clumsier for many columns / large rigs

steps.note: TABULATE the derived channels back into a table for export/review. Point chop at the mathCHOP result (or a mergeCHOP of all derived columns), names=on so each projector's channel name becomes a row/col label, output=rowperchan (one row per projector) or colperchan (one column per metric) to match the sheet layout you want. This turns the per-projector CHOP channels back into the human-readable plan table that pairs with the input spec sheet.

key_params.chop: OUT_planmath (or a merged CHOP of all derived columns)
key_params.output: rowperchan (one row per projector) | colperchan (one column per metric)

steps.geometry_out: DAT: the computed plan (derived columns) as a table

verify.pass_if: one row (or column) per projector with the derived planning values labelled

steps.note: MILESTONE -- EXPORT THE FINISHED PLAN SHEET. write_csv the computed plan table (OUT_plantable), and/or a joined sheet of spec + derived columns, to a confined path so it can drop into a rigging/production document. This is the deliverable: a static planning CSV a projectionist hands to a rigger. Re-run the constantCHOP values -> mathCHOP -> choptoDAT -> this export whenever the input specs change (the manual re-parameterise loop the gated expression lane would automate).

key_params.source: OUT_plantable (the computed plan) -- optionally join spec + derived columns first

steps.geometry_out: confined CSV file: the finished throw/lens/lumens/coverage plan

verify.pass_if: the plan CSV exists with per-projector derived columns
verify.milestone_check: read_network @OUT_plancsv -- the exported plan holds each projector's image size / coverage / brightness, hand-checkable against distance/throw-ratio, ready for the rigging document

steps.note: OPTIONAL FRUSTUM / COVERAGE PREVIEW (visualise the plan). Build one cameraCOMP per projector as a stand-in for its light cone: projection=perspective, fov set from the lens (a tighter throw-ratio = a narrower fov -- use viewanglemethod=horzfov and derive the angle from the throw ratio, or focalaperture from the datasheet), t/r = the numeric projector pose, near/far bracketing the surface distance. Aim it with lookat at a null on the surface, or set r directly. Render the cameras against a simple surface proxy (a gridSOP the size of the wall) through renderTOP (next step) to SEE where each projector covers and where two frusta overlap (edge-blend zones). This is a planning visual, not the show output; keep it a preview.

key_params.viewanglemethod: horzfov (derive fov from throw ratio) | focalaperture (from datasheet)
key_params.fov: the horizontal angle for that lens (narrower for a longer throw ratio)
key_params.t: [x,y,z] the projector's numeric position; r=[rx,ry,rz] its aim
key_params.near: just before the surface; far just beyond it

steps.geometry_out: one camera per projector = its throw frustum, at numeric pose/lens

verify.pass_if: projection perspective; fov/t/r hold the per-projector lens+pose literals

steps.note: OPTIONAL -- RENDER THE FRUSTUM PREVIEW. Render the projector cameras against a surface proxy (a gridSOP wall in a geometryCOMP -- remember a fresh geometryCOMP renders its default torus1, so delete it and set_flags render/display on the real grid SOP) to produce a top/coverage view showing each projector's footprint and the overlaps. camera = the frustum cameras, outputresolution=custom (avoid the 256px default). This is a preview image for the plan; it is NOT a show deliverable -- no output op is armed. Save it beside the CSV as documentation of coverage.

key_params.geometry: the surface-proxy grid geometryCOMP (delete its default torus1 first)

steps.geometry_out: a coverage/footprint preview image of the projector rig

verify.pass_if: each projector's footprint is visible on the surface proxy; overlaps read as brighter

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: datasheet numbers + on-site measured throw)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable -- the spec table, the CHOP-math compute, the CSV export, the frustum preview. === What the MCP CANNOT supply is the SOURCE NUMBERS: the real lens throw-ratio, lumens and native resolution come from the MANUFACTURER datasheet, and the actual throw distance + surface size come from a TAPE MEASURE / laser rangefinder on site. The recipe provides the compute frame and the deliverable; the projectionist provides the truth values. Type the measured/datasheet numbers into the input spec CSV (step 1) and the constantCHOP channels (step 3), then re-run the compute + export. Nothing here is armed or transmitted -- it is a planning artefact.

key_params.human_supplies: throw_ratio + lumens + native_res (datasheet); throw_distance + surface_size (on-site measurement)

steps.geometry_out: a correct plan once real datasheet + measured numbers are entered

verify.pass_if: the spec table holds real datasheet + measured values (or placeholders in authoring)

recipes.classify: plan a projector rig on paper -- throw ratio / lens / lumens / brightness / coverage / image size / overlap planning sheet; projector calculator, throw distance calculator, lens selection, lumens per square meter, coverage map, projector spec sheet, rigging plan, pre-production planning table, CSV export of a projector plan, frustum coverage preview; NOT a live show graph -- a planning deliverable
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE, PLANNING ARTEFACT (not a show output). (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the spec tableDAT (loaded via write_csv -> file -> pulse loadonstartpulse), the constantCHOP -> mathCHOP -> choptoDAT compute of derived columns, the write_csv plan export, and the optional cameraCOMP + renderTOP frustum preview -- all created and parameterised with STATIC LITERALS. No script/execute/cplusplus op and no parameter expressions are baked in. (2) EXPRESSION-LANE BOUNDARY (the honest limit): the ELEGANT form -- a single evaluateDAT sheet whose per-row cells are LIVE formulas over the input columns (throw = distance/ratio, coverage = lumens/area, overlap, ...) that re-compute when any input changes -- is the GATED EXPRESSION LANE (evaluateDAT.expr/datexpr; allow_expr defaults OFF, owner-gated). It is surfaced as an expr_opportunity, NOT baked in. The data-only CHOP-math fallback SHIPS NOW and is correct, but it is clumsy for many columns / large rigs: CHOP channels are per-sample not per-row, so every derived column is its own constantCHOP+mathCHOP chain reassembled by choptoDAT. (3) HUMAN: the SOURCE numbers are not MCP-derivable -- lens throw-ratio / lumens / native res come from the manufacturer datasheet, and throw distance / surface size from an on-site measurement. HONEST GAPS: there is no dedicated projector-calculator / throw-ratio operator in the catalog -- this recipe assembles primitives (table + CHOP math + CSV); the frustum preview approximates a light cone with a perspective cameraCOMP (fov derived from throw ratio), not a photometric model. NC render cap 1280 applies to the optional preview only; the CSV export is unaffected.
tips: tableDAT.file does NOT auto-load mid-session: set file, then pulse(loadonstartpulse). Setting loadonstart=on makes it reload with the project too.
CHOP channels are per-SAMPLE, not per-row: put one channel per projector in a constantCHOP (const0name/const0value...) and keep single=on -- these are static planning constants, not a signal.
Image width (m) = throw_distance / throw_ratio: mathCHOP chopop=div across the distance CHOP and the ratio CHOP (matched by name or index) gives it per projector in one node.
Coverage brightness (lumens/m^2) = lumens / (width*height): one mathCHOP chopop=mul for area, a second chopop=div for lumens/area -- build a short chain per derived column.
choptoDAT names=on carries the projector channel names as labels; output=rowperchan for one row per projector, colperchan for one column per metric.

The frustum preview is a PLANNING visual only -- nothing is armed/output; a fresh geometryCOMP renders its default torus1, so delete it and set_flags render/display on your real surface-proxy grid SOP.

Derive the preview camera fov from the throw ratio (narrower fov = longer throw); it approximates the light cone, it is not photometric -- use it for footprint/overlap intuition, not brightness proof.

HELPER CANDIDATE: plan_projectors(specs=[{name,throw_ratio,lumens,native,distance}]) -> spec tableDAT + derived-column CHOP math + choptoDAT + CSV export, in one call (the clean version would use the gated expression lane).
variants: csv_only (no preview): steps 1-6 only -- the spec sheet, the CHOP-math derived columns, and the exported plan CSV; skip the cameraCOMP/renderTOP frustum entirely for a pure paper deliverable.
frustum_coverage_preview: add steps 7-8 (cameraCOMP per projector + renderTOP against a surface proxy) to visualise each projector's footprint and the edge-blend overlaps between adjacent frusta.
single_projector_calc: one row, one channel -- a quick throw-distance / image-size calculator for a single projector rather than an array plan.

coverage_brightness_focus: emphasise the lumens/m^2 column (lumens / image area) across the rig to check every surface meets a target nit/brightness spec -- the derived column drives a pass/fail note.

expression_lane_upgrade (owner-gated): with allow_expr ON, replace the constantCHOP->mathCHOP->choptoDAT fallback with a single evaluateDAT sheet of per-row formulas over the spec columns (the expr_opportunity) -- one table, all columns, re-computing live when any input cell changes.

recipes.title: Notch .dfx Block playback transport wrapper (notchTOP block/layer/playmode/play + levelTOP conditioning + standby switchTOP fallback -> OUT_playout) -- a LICENSE-GATED integration scaffold, honestly flagged
recipes.summary: Play a Notch .dfx Block inside TouchDesigner the data-only way: a notchTOP is the playback engine (it LOADS a .dfx and RENDERS its layers), wrapped in a typed transport that this bridge CAN set completely -- block file pointer, layer select, playmode {lockedtotimeline | specifyindex | sequential}, play toggle, speed, index/indexunit, crop, and output resolution/format. Downstream a levelTOP conditions the block output (gamma/brightness/opacity, or crush to black) and a switchTOP crossfades to a data-only STANDBY graph (black constantTOP + a textTOP caption) so the show has something safe to show when the Block is absent or unlicensed. KEY HONESTY: the notchTOP is a real operator and its BUILT-IN transport params are fully data-only, but playback itself depends on THREE things the MCP was never meant to supply -- (1) a Notch Playback/Builder LICENSE on the machine (dongle/key), (2) the .dfx asset itself (authored in Notch Builder; TD cannot create it), and (3) AUTHOR-DEFINED dynamic Block parameters that only appear on the notchTOP AFTER the Block loads, so the artistically-meaningful controls are unknowable at build time and are wired later via set_par once the Block is present. This recipe therefore builds the correct SKELETON -- point the notchTOP at the Block, wire transport + conditioning + a standby fallback, hand off WIRE-ONLY -- and is scrupulous that it is a license-dependent integration scaffold, not a self-contained content generator. GOTCHA: notchTOP maxinputs=0 (it is a source, nothing feeds it); play defaults ON and active defaults ON, so the data-only RUN mechanism is the play TOGGLE (not a pulse); its resolution defaults to the 256px trap -- force outputresolution=custom.

steps.note: THE NOTCH PLAYBACK ENGINE + its typed transport. maxinputs=0 -- it is a SOURCE node (nothing wires into it); it loads the .dfx named in `block` and renders the selected `layer`.
