Set block to an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path UNDER the working dir (a relative/external path is blanked by path confinement, and with no license/asset the node simply renders nothing -- that is expected, the standby step covers it). playmode picks how time advances: lockedtotimeline follows TD's timeline, sequential free-runs, specifyindex scrubs by the index param. play is a TOGGLE and defaults ON -- this is the DATA-ONLY run mechanism (no pulse needed); speed scales playback; index/indexunit scrub when playmode=specifyindex. clearparams (default ON) wipes stale custom params when a new Block loads. Force outputresolution=custom at the show resolution (256px trap otherwise). The `init`/`start` params are PULSE actuators that (re)initialize the Block at runtime -- they are NOT in the documented parameterless pulse-allowlist, so treat them as operator/runtime actions, not an MCP step; the play toggle is all the bridge needs to arm playback.

key_params.playmode: sequential (or lockedtotimeline for timeline sync, specifyindex to scrub)
key_params.active: on (default on)

steps.geometry_out: the Notch Block's rendered layer (or empty if no license/asset)

verify.pass_if: node exists at custom resolution; renders the Block when license+asset present, empty/black otherwise (both are valid build states)

steps.note: OUTPUT CONDITIONING for the block feed -- data-only projector prep and a soft kill. gamma1/brightness1 trim the Block to the projector's response, opacity fades the whole layer, blacklevel lifts crushed shadows. Setting opacity=0 (or brightness1=0) crushes the block to black without touching the Notch engine -- a clean data-only 'hold' distinct from the standby graph. Leave outputresolution=custom to keep the show res. Purely a value chain; no expressions, no callbacks.
steps.geometry_out: conditioned Notch layer, show res

verify.pass_if: resolution == show res; opacity/gamma applied

steps.note: STANDBY CANVAS -- the data-only safety layer shown when the Block is not loaded/licensed or the operator selects HOLD. Pure black at show res, alpha 1 (opaque, so it fully covers). outputresolution=custom (256 trap). This is the base the standby caption sits on and the fallback input of the crossfade switch.
steps.geometry_out: opaque black standby canvas at show res

verify.pass_if: black opaque canvas at show res

steps.note: STANDBY CAPTION over the black canvas (wire OUT_standbybg -> textTOP in0, operand=over, combineinput=compres). IMPORTANT: textTOP's `text` defaults to the literal 'derivative' -- you MUST set text explicitly (e.g. 'STANDBY -- NOTCH BLOCK NOT LOADED'). Font size is fontsizex/fontsizey (NOT 'fontsize'), fontcolor is the RGB tuplet, alignx/aligny center it. This gives the operator an unambiguous on-screen state when the license/asset is missing -- honest UX for a license-gated scaffold.
steps.geometry_out: standby caption over black, show res

verify.pass_if: white 'STANDBY...' caption centered over black

steps.note: PROGRAM SELECT -- crossfade between the live Block and the standby graph. in0 = OUT_blockcond, in1 = OUT_standby; index 0 shows the Block, 1 shows standby (blend=on for a soft dissolve during load). The operator (or a load-state check) picks the index; because it is a plain parameter it can be driven data-only by an exported CHOP or bind_chop later, but a literal index is the honest default. outputresolution=custom at show res. This node makes the scaffold safe to arm before the Block/license are present -- default index to standby.

key_params.index: 1 (default to standby; 0 once the Block is live)

steps.geometry_out: selected program (block or standby), show res

verify.pass_if: index selects between block and standby feeds

steps.note: STABLE PLAYOUT TAP. Every downstream output op targets this NAME so the physical output can be swapped without rewiring. Wire OUT_switch -> this. Hand off WIRE-ONLY via output_handoff / projection_align_and_output (windowCOMP to the wall NOT opened by us; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF; ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active DEFAULT ON -> set OFF). Nothing here is actuated.
steps.geometry_out: final Notch/standby program, show res, ready for wire-only output

verify.pass_if: holds the block feed (or standby) at show res

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: Notch license + .dfx asset + author-defined dynamic Block params)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / EXTERNAL-DEPENDENCY SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable. === The bridge builds the transport, conditioning, standby and playout, and points the notchTOP at the Block -- but it CANNOT supply the three runtime pieces: (1) a Notch Playback/Builder LICENSE (dongle/key) must be present on the machine or the notchTOP renders nothing; (2) the .dfx BLOCK is authored in Notch Builder -- TD cannot create or export it; (3) DYNAMIC BLOCK PARAMETERS -- a valid Block exposes CUSTOM params on the notchTOP that appear only AFTER the Block loads (page beyond the 34 built-ins). Those are the artistically-meaningful controls and are unknowable at build; once the licensed Block is loaded, read them with read_network @notch1 pars=true and set them via set_par (still data-only -- literal values on real params). init/start are runtime pulse actuators outside the documented parameterless-allowlist, so (re)initializing the Block is an operator/runtime action, not an MCP step.

key_params.set_par (after the licensed Block loads): op=OUT_notchblock, pars={<author-defined custom param>:<value>, ...} -- discovered via read_network once the Block is live

steps.geometry_out: a live Notch Block once license + asset + custom params are present

verify.pass_if: built-in transport params hold; custom Block params appear only after a licensed Block loads

steps.note: MILESTONE -- prove the scaffold end to end, honestly. With NO license/asset: OUT_playout shows the STANDBY caption (switch index=1) -- proof the safety path works. With a licensed Block loaded and switch index=0: OUT_playout shows the Block's rendered layer, and changing play/speed/index or a custom param changes the image -- proof the transport drives the engine. Capture both states so the build's license-gated nature is documented, not hidden.
steps.geometry_out: TOP preview (inline)

verify.cheap: save_top @OUT_playout at switch index 1 (standby), then index 0 (block if licensed)
verify.pass_if: standby caption renders with no asset; the Block layer renders when license+asset present
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_playout -- standby caption without a license; the live Notch layer once license + .dfx + custom params are in place

recipes.classify: play / trigger / transport a Notch .dfx Block (Notch LC, notchTOP) in TouchDesigner -- load a dfx, select a layer, set playmode/play/speed/index, condition and hand off the output, with a standby fallback; Notch integration, block playback, dfx, notch playback license, real-time generative block, broadcast/large-venue Notch content
recipes.governance: TWO-PHASE, LICENSE-GATED. (1) DATA-ONLY MCP-buildable: the whole transport skeleton -- notchTOP created with every BUILT-IN param set (block pointer, layer, playmode, play toggle, speed, index, crop, resolution/format), levelTOP conditioning, a standby constantTOP+textTOP graph, the program switchTOP, and the playout null -- is created/wired/parameterized by the bridge with literal values only. No script/execute/cplusplus op, no parameter expressions, no callbacks DAT; the RUN mechanism is the play TOGGLE (data-only), not a pulse. (2) EXTERNAL DEPENDENCIES the MCP cannot supply and does not pretend to: a Notch Playback/Builder LICENSE on the machine; the .dfx Block asset (authored in Notch Builder -- there is NO data-only way to create or export a .dfx); and the Block's AUTHOR-DEFINED dynamic parameters, which materialize on the notchTOP only after a licensed Block loads and are then set via set_par (discover with read_network). WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: nothing here fires; downstream terminal ops (windowCOMP not opened; moviefileoutTOP.record OFF; ndioutTOP.active / syphonspoutoutTOP.active DEFAULT ON -> MUST set OFF) are handled by output_handoff / projection_align_and_output. HONEST GAPS: notchTOP.init/start are runtime pulse actuators NOT in the documented parameterless pulse-allowlist -- (re)init is an operator action; without a license the notchTOP renders nothing (the standby graph is the honest fallback). This is a skeleton for venues already running Notch, not a self-contained content generator. NC build render cap 1280 (previews downscale; swap resolutionw/h for full/4K show res, topology identical).
tips: notchTOP maxinputs=0 -- it is a SOURCE. Do not try to wire content into it; the .dfx IS the content. Feed its OUTPUT into levelTOP/switchTOP.
The RUN control is the play TOGGLE (default ON), not a pulse. init/start pulses (re)initialize the Block at runtime and are outside the allowlist -- leave them to the operator.
Force outputresolution=custom on the notchTOP: it defaults to the 256px trap, which silently downscales your Block.
textTOP.text defaults to the literal 'derivative' -- always set the standby caption text explicitly, or your safety layer reads 'derivative'.
Default the program switchTOP to STANDBY (index 1) so arming the network before the license/asset arrive shows a safe caption, not a black or broken frame.
Discover author-defined Block params only AFTER a licensed Block loads: read_network @notch1 pars=true, then set them with set_par (literal values -- still data-only).
Kill the block cleanly without touching the engine: levelTOP opacity/brightness1 -> 0 crushes to black; use the switch for a full crossfade to standby.
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_notch_transport(block, layer, res, standby_text) -> notchTOP + levelTOP + standby + switch + playout null wired in one call.
variants: timeline_locked: playmode=lockedtotimeline so the Block's time follows TD's timeline/timecode -- use with show_control_timecode / timecode_chase_slave for frame-locked Notch playback in a cue stack.

index_scrub: playmode=specifyindex + drive the index param from a keyframeCHOP/lfoCHOP via bind_chop for hands-on scrubbing or effect-parameter sweeps (data-only animation of the transport, not of the Block internals).
multi_layer: several notchTOPs pointed at the same .dfx with different `layer` selections, composited/switched -- render independent Block layers as separate feeds.

no_standby_minimal: drop the constantTOP+textTOP+switch and hand the conditioned notchTOP straight to the playout null when a license/asset are guaranteed present (loses the safe fallback -- not recommended for unattended venues).

hap_prebake_fallback: where no license is available on show machines, a variant records the Block on a licensed machine to a HAP clip (moviefileoutTOP, record OFF here / armed there) and swaps media_clip_player in as the license-free playout -- a delivery workaround, not a live Notch integration.

recipes.title: MQTT / IoT / building-automation trigger input -- smart-facade + sensor-driven content (mqttclientDAT subscribe -> dattoCHOP parse -> selectCHOP/lagCHOP/mathCHOP/logicCHOP condition -> bind_chop/EXPORT onto content & params) -- the MQTT extension of the realtime_input_driver family
recipes.summary: Bring building-automation and IoT signals into the show over MQTT: an mqttclientDAT connects to a broker and receives messages on the topics it is subscribed to (occupancy sensors, door contacts, lighting scenes, HVAC, a smart-facade controller, a phone/dashboard publishing state); a dattoCHOP turns the received-message table into numeric channels; selectCHOP isolates one topic; lagCHOP debounces; mathCHOP rescales the payload into a parameter range; logicCHOP turns a value into a clean 0/1 EVENT (motion detected, door open, scene = 'night'); and the same downstream apply-block used by realtime_input_driver -- bind_chop / the EXPORT flag -- drives content and parameters (a moviefileinTOP index, a constantTOP colour, a transformTOP, a switchTOP crossfade). This recipe EXTENDS the realtime_input_driver family, which lists OSC / DMX / MIDI / audio inputs but NOT MQTT -- MQTT is the pub/sub bus of building automation and consumer IoT, a different transport with the same data-only downstream. TWO HONEST BOUNDARIES: (1) mqttclientDAT RECEIVES on topics, but issuing the SUBSCRIBE (and TLS auth, and any publish-back) is done in the DAT's callbacks (a Python touch) -- a broker/subscription step that lives on the human/gated side, not the data-only surface; (2) a numeric or single-string payload maps to a value data-only via dattoCHOP, but PARSING a structured JSON payload (fields, nested keys) wants the gated expression lane -- surfaced below as an expr_opportunity with a data-only fallback (subscribe to already-split leaf topics instead). The broker, the topic schema, and the sensors themselves are the human/hardware boundary.

steps.note: THE BROKER CONNECTION + RECEIVE. Set netaddress to the broker URL (tcp://host:1883, or tls:// / ssl:// for an encrypted broker), username/password if the broker authenticates, keepalive as needed, active=on to connect. The DAT's output is the RECEIVED-MESSAGE table -- each incoming message on a subscribed topic lands as a row (topic + payload; turn on the bytes column for binary payloads). maxinputs 0 -- it is a pure source. HONEST BOUNDARY: this DAT receives on the topics it is SUBSCRIBED to, but the subscribe() call (and any publish back to the broker) is issued from the DAT's Callbacks DAT in Python (onConnect -> op(...).subscribe('topic')). That callbacks touch is a CODE step on the human/gated side; the bridge builds and connects the client and reads its received table, but does not author the callbacks script. For a purely data-only intake, the broker/gateway can be configured to feed TD topics the client is auto-subscribed to, or use a broker bridge -- see the HUMAN BOUNDARY step.

key_params.active: on

steps.geometry_out: DAT table of received MQTT messages (topic + payload rows)

verify.pass_if: the DAT shows connected and rows appear as messages arrive on subscribed topics (empty until a message is published)

steps.note: PARSE the message table into numeric CHANNELS. Point dat at OUT_mqtt; use extractrows/extractcols (byname/byindex) to pick the payload column and the topic(s) you want; output=chanperrow (a channel per message row) or chanpervalue; firstcolumn=names so the topic string names the channel, firstrow to taste. A numeric payload (a sensor level, a 0/1 contact, a scene number) becomes a live channel here data-only. defval covers an empty/absent message. This is the table->control bridge; keep a nullDAT tap on OUT_mqtt first if you want a stable named source to parse from.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP -- one channel per topic/payload (numeric)

verify.pass_if: a numeric channel appears per parsed topic, updating as messages arrive

expr_opportunity.why: a numeric or single-string payload maps to a value data-only via dattoCHOP, but a STRUCTURED JSON payload (e.g. {"temp":21.4,"occupied":true,"scene":"night"}) needs field extraction / key lookup / string->number parsing that is an expression, not a wire
expr_opportunity.propose_via: expr_reference then set_expr (or a jsonDAT parse) to pull named fields from the payload
expr_opportunity.consent: needs allow_expr (default OFF); DATA-ONLY FALLBACK = have the broker/publisher split the JSON into leaf topics (site/facade/temp, site/facade/occupied) and subscribe to those, so each arrives as a plain scalar dattoCHOP can read directly -- no expression needed

steps.note: ISOLATE ONE TOPIC'S value = the specific signal this content responds to. channames picks the channel by name (the topic string from the parse step), rename it to something stable (renamefrom/renameto) so downstream wiring survives a topic-name change. When several topics drive one scene, keep them as parallel named channels here and fan out. This is the 'which sensor' selector -- the equivalent of picking an OSC address or a DMX channel in realtime_input_driver.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP -- the single selected topic channel

verify.pass_if: exactly the chosen topic's value is present under the stable name

steps.note: DEBOUNCE + SMOOTH. IoT messages arrive irregularly and can chatter (a motion sensor re-firing, a noisy analogue level); a lagCHOP (lag ~0.2-1.0s) smooths the value and prevents a flicker from strobing the content. For an on/off contact, a small lag gives a graceful fade instead of a hard cut; snap=on lets it settle cleanly. Tune lag to the sensor's behaviour -- longer for jittery occupancy, near-zero for a deliberate button.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP -- the smoothed/debounced trigger value

verify.pass_if: the value follows the sensor but without single-message chatter

steps.note: RESCALE the payload into the target PARAMETER range. A sensor's native units (0..1023 ADC, 0..100 %, a lux value) rarely match the param you drive (a 0..1 crossfade, a 0..360 rotation, an emit brightness); fromrange = the payload's real min/max, torange = the parameter's range. Use gain/preoff/postoff for a simple scale+offset. This makes the IoT value directly bindable to content without an expression -- the core data-only mapping move.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP -- payload rescaled to the driven parameter's range

verify.pass_if: the value spans the target param range as the sensor spans its own

steps.note: EVENT / STATE from a value = the discrete IoT trigger. convert=gt/ge/lt/le with boundmin turns an analogue level into a clean 0/1 (motion above threshold, temperature over a limit, occupancy present); convert=eq matches a scene number; preop=rise/fall extracts the moment of change (a door OPENING vs merely open) for a one-shot cue; chanop=or/and combines several topics ('lobby occupied AND after sunset'). This 0/1 event drives a switchTOP/triggerCHOP/GO downstream, while OUT_driveval covers the continuous-value path.
steps.geometry_out: CHOP -- clean 0/1 IoT event (+ combined conditions)

verify.pass_if: flag is 0/1 and flips exactly when the sensor crosses its threshold / a scene matches

steps.note: TOPIC -> CONTENT MAP (optional but recommended for multi-topic installs) = a lookup that says 'topic X selects clip/scene N'. Author it with write_csv (a confined .csv: columns topic,index,name), set this tableDAT's file to that path, then pulse(loadonstartpulse) to READ it -- setting file alone does NOT load mid-session (the tableDAT.file gotcha). A dattoCHOP/lookup then maps the live topic to its content index. Keeps the routing declarative and editable without rewiring -- change the CSV, re-pulse, done.

key_params.loadonstartpulse: pulse AFTER setting file (file alone does not load)

steps.geometry_out: topic->content lookup table (loaded via pulse)

verify.pass_if: the map rows are present after the load pulse (not empty)

steps.note: BIND input -> content/params via the SHARED apply-block (do NOT rebuild it). MQTT is just another transport into the realtime_input_driver family -- from here the mechanism is identical: bind_chop (or a nullCHOP + the EXPORT flag, exportmethod=autoname) drives OUT_driveval / OUT_iotflag onto the target -- a moviefileinTOP index (topic map -> clip), a constantTOP colour (lighting scene -> emit), a transformTOP (level -> motion), a switchTOP/crossTOP (event -> scene change). One exporter per parameter (disable others before binding a new driver). Reuse realtime_input_driver's downstream rather than authoring a parallel one. MILESTONE: publish a test message on the broker and watch the content respond.

key_params.drive: bind_chop OUT_driveval -> a content param; OUT_iotflag -> a switchTOP index

steps.geometry_out: (content & params driven by the live MQTT signal)

verify.pass_if: the target param is bind/Export-driven; publishing a test message on the topic changes the content
verify.milestone_check: save_top @<driven content> before/after publishing a test MQTT message -> the visual changes in response to the IoT signal

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: broker + topic schema + subscription callbacks)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HUMAN SPLIT LINE. Everything above (parse -> condition -> bind) is MCP-buildable once messages arrive. === WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds and connects the mqttclientDAT, parses the received table, conditions the value, and binds it to content via the shared apply-block. WHAT A PERSON / EXTERNAL SYSTEM OWNS: (1) the BROKER itself (Mosquitto/HiveMQ/cloud) -- its address, auth, and TLS certs; (2) the TOPIC SCHEMA -- which sensors publish where, payload format and units -- a design decision made with the building-automation/IoT integrator; (3) the SUBSCRIPTION -- mqttclientDAT receives on subscribed topics, but the subscribe() call is issued from the DAT's Callbacks DAT in Python (a one-line onConnect touch), which is a CODE step outside the data-only surface: either the integrator adds it, or the broker is bridged so TD's client is auto-subscribed; (4) the SENSORS/actuators and network. The bridge cannot stand up a broker, author the callbacks script, or wire a sensor -- it consumes the stream once it flows.

key_params.human: broker URL/auth/TLS, topic schema + payload units, the callbacks-DAT subscribe() call, sensors + network

steps.geometry_out: a live MQTT stream the data-only network consumes

verify.pass_if: messages arrive on the agreed topics with the agreed payload format once the broker + subscription are in place

recipes.classify: drive content from MQTT / IoT / BUILDING-AUTOMATION / smart-facade / smart-building signals -- occupancy & motion sensors, door contacts, lighting scenes, HVAC, thermostats, pub/sub message bus, sensor triggers, home/building automation, a phone or dashboard publishing state; the MQTT transport extension of the realtime input driver (OSC/DMX/MIDI/audio) family; subscribe to a broker topic and map the payload to visuals
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY once the stream flows: parsing (dattoCHOP), conditioning (selectCHOP/lagCHOP/mathCHOP/logicCHOP), and binding (bind_chop / the EXPORT flag autoname) are all code-free -- the same downstream as realtime_input_driver, of which this is the MQTT extension (that recipe covers OSC/DMX/MIDI/audio but not MQTT). No evaluateDAT, no parameter expressions, no callbacks logic authored by the bridge. TWO HONEST BOUNDARIES on the intake side: (1) mqttclientDAT RECEIVES on subscribed topics, but the subscribe() call is issued from the DAT's Callbacks DAT in Python -- a CODE step that lives on the human/gated side, not the data-only surface; a purely data-only intake relies on the client being auto-subscribed or the broker bridging the topics to it. (2) A numeric or single-string payload is data-only; a STRUCTURED JSON payload needs field extraction (an expression / jsonDAT) -- surfaced as an expr_opportunity (gated set_expr) with a data-only fallback of subscribing to pre-split leaf topics. HUMAN / HARDWARE: the broker (address/auth/TLS), the topic schema + payload units, the subscription callbacks, and the sensors/network are owned by a person / the building-automation integrator. The tableDAT topic-map is loaded with the write_csv -> set file -> pulse(loadonstartpulse) pattern (file alone does not load mid-session). Downstream output stays wire-only. NC render cap 1280.
tips: mqttclientDAT receives on SUBSCRIBED topics only -- the subscribe() call is a Python touch in its Callbacks DAT (onConnect), which is off the data-only surface; plan for the integrator to add it or the broker to auto-subscribe the client.

Structured JSON payloads need an expression to parse -- the data-only escape is to have the publisher split the JSON into leaf topics (site/facade/temp, site/facade/occupied) so each arrives as a plain scalar dattoCHOP reads directly.
Debounce EVERY sensor with a lagCHOP -- IoT messages arrive irregularly and chatter; a raw motion/contact channel will strobe the content without smoothing.
Rescale with mathCHOP fromrange->torange so the payload's native units map to the driven param's range; binding a raw 0..1023 ADC value straight onto a 0..1 crossfade just pins it at 1.
Use logicCHOP preop=rise/fall for one-shot EVENTS (a door OPENING, a button PRESS) vs convert=gt for a sustained STATE (occupied) -- edges fire a cue, levels hold a look.
Keep a nullDAT tap on the mqttclientDAT output and a nullCHOP on the conditioned value as stable named handles, so re-subscribing or renaming a topic doesn't break downstream wiring.
Load the topic->content tableDAT with write_csv -> set file -> pulse(loadonstartpulse); setting the file alone does not read it mid-session.
This is the MQTT lane of realtime_input_driver -- reuse that recipe's bind/export apply-block onto content and params; don't author a parallel downstream.
variants: sensor_level_to_content: an analogue topic (occupancy density, sound level, lux) -> dattoCHOP -> lag -> mathCHOP -> bind onto a continuous param (emit brightness, motion speed) -- a facade that breathes with the building.
event_scene_switch: a discrete topic (scene number / door contact) -> logicCHOP eq/rise -> switchTOP or crossTOP index -> a hard scene change on the IoT event.
multi_topic_map: many topics -> a tableDAT topic->content map (write_csv + loadonstartpulse) -> lookup to a moviefileinTOP/switchTOP index, so each sensor selects its own clip declaratively.

combined_condition: chanop=and across topics ('lobby occupied' AND 'after sunset' from scheduled_playback_dayparting's clockCHOP) -> a context-aware trigger that only fires under the right conditions.

json_leaf_topics: the data-only alternative to JSON parsing -- subscribe to pre-split leaf topics so every payload is a scalar; no expression lane needed (the expr_opportunity's fallback as a first-class mode).

recipes.title: UV-layout registration template export (model SOP -> geometryCOMP -> renderTOP rendermode=uvunwrap over a wireframe constantMAT -> composite over a reference grid -> save_top OUT_uvtemplate) -- paint-registered artwork guide for a per_section_material_rig
recipes.summary: Render a model's UV LAYOUT as a flat registration template so an external content artist paints pixel-registered artwork that lands exactly on the mapped surfaces of a per_section_material_rig. The data-only key is that renderTOP has a native rendermode=uvunwrap (uvunwrapcoord=uv0) that FLATTENS the geometry into UV [0,1] space -- no shader or expression needed to move points to UV: the render engine does it. So the spine is: the section model SOP (with its uv0 texture coords) inside a geometryCOMP, a constantMAT set to wireframe=topology as an override material so the render draws the mesh EDGES as an atlas guide, a renderTOP in uvunwrap mode producing the flat UV wireframe atlas, that composited over a mid-gray reference grid + corner labels so the artist can register, and save_top writing the PNG/EXR the artist paints into. KEY GOTCHA: a fresh geometryCOMP renders its default torus1 not your SOP -- delete the torus and set_flags render/display on the real SOP; and renderTOP.resolution defaults to 256, so force the atlas resolution (2048^2 / 4096^2) explicitly. There is NO dedicated UV-unwrap-export operator -- this assembles the guide from primitives around renderTOP's uvunwrap mode. HUMAN BOUNDARY: the artist paints the artwork externally (Photoshop/Substance) and the finished map is re-imported as the section colormap by per_section_material_rig -- the MCP renders the guide, not the art.

steps.note: SOURCE GEOMETRY = the per-section model whose UVs the artist will paint into. Import the real segmented model (it must live UNDER the working dir -- external/relative paths are blanked by confinement) so its uv0 texture coordinates are the ones the render flattens; real building sections DO carry UVs (a prior bug once loaded TD's default box instead -- verify the imported SOP is the actual model, not a default primitive). For a quick test/authoring pass with no asset, substitute a gridSOP (texture=rowcol gives clean uv0). The uv0 attribute is REQUIRED -- uvunwrap has nothing to lay out without it.

key_params.note_fallback: gridSOP with texture=rowcol as a UV-bearing test stand-in

steps.geometry_out: the section model SOP carrying uv0 texture coordinates

verify.pass_if: real model geometry present with a uv0 attribute (not a default torus/box)

steps.note: RENDERABLE CONTAINER for the SOP. GOTCHA: a fresh geometryCOMP ships a default torus1 and will render THAT, not your model -- delete the torus (delete_op the internal torus1) and place/point the container at OUT_uvsrc with set_flags render=on + display=on on the REAL SOP. The geometryCOMP is what renderTOP's `geometry` references. Transform is irrelevant here (uvunwrap ignores world placement and camera -- it flattens by UV), so leave it at identity.

key_params.delete_op: the default torus1 inside the geometryCOMP
key_params.set_flags: render=on, display=on on OUT_uvsrc (the real SOP)

steps.geometry_out: geometryCOMP wrapping the real UV-bearing model

verify.pass_if: contains the real SOP with render/display on; default torus removed

steps.note: WIREFRAME ATLAS MATERIAL -- the guide look. Set wireframe=topology so the render draws the mesh EDGES (the UV island outlines once flattened), wirewidth ~2 for legible lines, color a high-contrast hue (e.g. green [0,1,0]) that an artist can paint under and still see. applypointcolor=off so the constant color wins. This is used as the renderTOP OVERRIDE material so every section renders as wireframe regardless of its real shader. (constantMAT.wireframe {off,tesselated,topology}; topology = the clean mesh edges.)

key_params.wireframe: topology (draw mesh edges = UV island outlines)

steps.geometry_out: wireframe override material for the atlas guide

verify.pass_if: wireframe=topology, contrast color, applypointcolor off

steps.note: CAMERA REFERENCE for the renderTOP. In uvunwrap mode the camera is effectively IGNORED (the geometry is flattened into UV space, not projected through a lens), but renderTOP still requires a camera reference to exist -- create a plain cameraCOMP (ortho is tidy) and point renderTOP.camera at it. Do NOT spend effort framing it; UV flatten does not use its transform. Its presence just satisfies the render pipeline.

key_params.projection: ortho (tidy; transform is unused by uvunwrap)

steps.geometry_out: a camera reference to satisfy renderTOP (unused by the flatten)

verify.pass_if: camera exists and is referenceable by renderTOP.camera

steps.note: THE UV ATLAS -- renderTOP's native rendermode=uvunwrap flattens the geometry into UV [0,1] space using uvunwrapcoord=uv0, so the mesh is drawn AS ITS UV LAYOUT (this is the data-only unwrap; no glsl/expr needed). Set overridemat=OUT_wiremat so every section renders as the wireframe guide, camera=OUT_cam, geometry=OUT_geo. CRITICAL: renderTOP.resolution defaults to 256 -- force outputresolution=custom at the ATLAS resolution the artist paints at (2048x2048 or 4096x4096, square, matching the section map res). Give bgcolor an OPAQUE mid value (e.g. [0.5,0.5,0.5,1]) -- a transparent/white background makes a white-or-light wireframe read as blank when the PNG is opened (the white-on-transparent trap). antialias aa8 keeps the lines clean.
steps.geometry_out: flat UV wireframe atlas of the model at atlas resolution

glsl_opportunity.why: per-island NUMBERED labels and per-section island COLORING (so the artist knows which flattened island is which physical section) need per-primitive text placement / id-to-color, which is a per-primitive shader or expression task -- not expressible with a single override material
glsl_opportunity.propose_via: glsl_reference then validate_glsl then set_glsl on a glslMAT used as the render override
glsl_opportunity.consent: needs allow_glsl (default OFF); data-only fallback = the plain wireframe uvunwrap atlas + a manual textTOP corner legend used as the actual steps here, which is a fully usable registration guide

verify.pass_if: the model's UV islands appear as green wireframe over opaque mid-gray, filling the 0..1 atlas
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_uvatlas -- the flattened UV islands/seams of the real model read clearly at atlas resolution

steps.note: REFERENCE GRID / BACKING for registration. A mid-gray opaque backing (or a subtle grid) at the SAME atlas resolution, over which the wireframe atlas is composited so the artist has neutral ground + 0..1 reference. Keep alpha 1. (A finer grid can be built by compositing a rampTOP-derived tick pattern, but a flat neutral backing is the honest minimum -- the wireframe islands are the real registration.)
steps.geometry_out: neutral opaque backing at atlas res

verify.pass_if: opaque mid-gray backing at atlas res

steps.note: ASSEMBLE THE GUIDE = wireframe atlas over the backing. operand=over; tops multi-input in draw order: OUT_refgrid FIRST (bottom), then OUT_uvatlas (on top). recipes.classify: export / render a model's UV layout / UV map / UV atlas / unwrap as a registration template or guide so an external artist paints pixel-registered / texture-registered artwork for the mapped surfaces; uvunwrap, UV template, texture template, paint reference, per-section material map, wireframe atlas
recipes.governance: MOSTLY DATA-ONLY, a pipeline convenience around per_section_material_rig. (1) MCP-buildable: the entire guide -- source model SOP (import_segmented_model / gridSOP with uv0), geometryCOMP (default torus deleted, real SOP render/display on), a constantMAT wireframe=topology override, a renderTOP in the native rendermode=uvunwrap (uvunwrapcoord=uv0) that FLATTENS the mesh into UV space with NO shader/expression, a neutral backing, the compositor, and save_top export -- all literal params, no code sink, no callbacks. renderTOP's uvunwrap mode is the load-bearing native feature that makes the UV-atlas render data-only (there is no separate 'move points to UV' op, and pointSOP-style P<-uv would need expressions, which we do NOT use). (2) HUMAN / EXTERNAL: the actual ARTWORK is painted by a content artist in an external tool and re-imported as the section colormap by per_section_material_rig -- the MCP produces the registration guide, not the art. HONEST GAPS: no dedicated UV-unwrap-EXPORT operator exists (assembled from primitives here); per-island NUMBERED labels / id-based island coloring need the gated GLSL lane (glsl_opportunity on the renderTOP step) -- the data-only deliverable is the plain wireframe atlas + a textTOP legend, which is fully usable. GOTCHAS baked in: fresh geometryCOMP renders its default torus (delete it); renderTOP.resolution defaults to 256 (force atlas res); white/light wireframe on transparent/white reads as blank (opaque mid-gray bg); compositeTOP over-draws input0 on top (swaporder). NC build render cap 1280 -- for a 2K/4K atlas set the render resolution explicitly (previews downscale; the saved file honors the set res).
tips: renderTOP.rendermode=uvunwrap + uvunwrapcoord=uv0 IS the unwrap -- it flattens geometry into UV space natively, so no shader/expression is needed to 'move points to UV'.
The model MUST carry a uv0 attribute or uvunwrap has nothing to lay out -- verify the imported SOP's UVs (gridSOP texture=rowcol is a clean UV-bearing test stand-in).
Fresh geometryCOMP renders its internal torus1, not your model -- delete_op the torus and set_flags render/display on the real SOP, or the atlas is a donut.
renderTOP.resolution defaults to 256 -- force outputresolution=custom at the SECTION MAP resolution (2048^2 / 4096^2, square) so the template matches what the artist paints.
Give the render an OPAQUE mid-gray bgcolor -- a white or light wireframe over transparent/white reads as blank when the PNG is opened (the white-on-transparent trap).
compositeTOP draws input0 ON TOP by default -- set swaporder=on (or order inputs) so the backing stays behind the wireframe; confirm with save_top.
Match the atlas resolution to the per_section_material_rig's colormap resolution so painted pixels map 1:1 -- a mismatched template forces the artist to guess registration.
HELPER CANDIDATE: export_uv_template(model, coord=uv0, res=2048, wirecolor) -> geometryCOMP + wireframe constantMAT + uvunwrap renderTOP + backing composite + save_top in one call.

recipes.title: Structured-light calibration pattern SEQUENCE generator (binary gray-code stripes via rampTOP->mathTOP + sinusoidal phase-shift via patternCHOP->choptoTOP, sequenced by timerCHOP->switchTOP at native res -> OUT_patternfeed) -- the auto projector<->camera geometry-capture source
recipes.summary: Generate the ANIMATED pattern SEQUENCE that an automatic structured-light pipeline projects to capture projector<->camera geometry -- distinct from test_pattern_generator (static grids/crosshatch/alignment charts): this emits a timed series of BINARY GRAY-CODE stripes and SINUSOIDAL PHASE-SHIFT fringes, plus all-white/all-black reference frames, at exact native projector resolution. Gray-code bits are built data-only as a repeating rampTOP gradient (period = 1/2^n across the frame, extend=repeat) hard-thresholded to black/white by a mathTOP with integer=round -- each successive bit halves the stripe width; inverses come from a levelTOP invert. Phase-shift fringes are a patternCHOP sine (length = projector width, N cycles, phase 0/120/240 deg) turned into an image by choptoTOP and stretched to full height. A timerCHOP walks the pattern list as timed segments and its 'segment' index is bound (bind_chop) onto a switchTOP that selects the current frame; pulse(gotonextseg) advances it in lock-step with the camera. KEY GOTCHA: structured light decodes SUB-PIXEL stripe edges, so the whole chain must stay 1:1 NATIVE resolution with NEAREST filtering and NO anti-alias / NO mipmap / NO scaling -- any bilinear/mipmap/resample blurs the stripe edges and the external solve fails. DATA-ONLY covers PATTERN GENERATION only; the synced camera capture and the decode/solve that turns captured frames into a projector geometry map are external/human. WIRE-ONLY output: the terminal op is armed OFF and handed downstream.

steps.note: GRAY-CODE BIT SOURCE (repeat per bit n = 0..k). A horizontal ramp with extendright=repeat tiles a 0..1 gradient across the frame; period sets how many stripes: period = 1/2^n gives 2^n cycles (bit 0 = period 1.0 = one edge, bit 1 = 0.5 = two, bit 2 = 0.25 ...). This gradient is the raw signal the next node hard-thresholds into a crisp binary stripe. outputresolution=custom at NATIVE projector res, filtertype/inputfiltertype=nearest so nothing is pre-smoothed. Build one rampTOP per gray-code bit you need (ceil(log2(projector_width)) bits resolves every column).
steps.geometry_out: repeating 0..1 horizontal gradient for one gray-code bit

verify.pass_if: native res, N=2^n gradient cycles across width

steps.note: HARD-THRESHOLD the gradient to a BINARY stripe -- the core data-only trick. integer=round maps every pixel <0.5 to 0 and >=0.5 to 1, converting the repeating ramp into a crisp 50%-duty black/white square wave = one gray-code bit plane. NO gain/offset needed for a centered ramp; if you shift duty, use preoff/gain before the round. Keep filtertype=nearest and format at 8-bit fixed so edges land exactly on pixel boundaries. The INVERSE bit plane (needed by most decoders for robustness) is a levelTOP with invert=1 on this output. Repeat this ramp->round pair per bit; the set of bit planes + inverses is the gray-code half of the sequence.
steps.geometry_out: crisp binary black/white stripe (one gray-code bit)

glsl_opportunity.why: a true gray-code/phase-shift generator is a one-line fragment shader (bit = (int(gl_FragCoord.x)>>n)&1; fringe = 0.5+0.5*sin(2*PI*f*u+phase)) and is exact to the pixel/sub-pixel, avoiding any ramp-quantization or duty drift across the array
glsl_opportunity.propose_via: glsl_reference then validate_glsl then set_glsl on a glslTOP
glsl_opportunity.consent: needs allow_glsl (default OFF); data-only fallback = the rampTOP->mathTOP(round) binary stripe and patternCHOP->choptoTOP sine used as the actual steps here, which are sufficient for standard gray-code + 3-step phase capture

verify.pass_if: hard black/white stripes, no gray transition pixels, edges on pixel boundaries
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_bitplane across bits 0..k -- stripe count doubles each bit and edges stay crisp at native res

steps.note: SINUSOIDAL PHASE-SHIFT SOURCE (repeat per phase, e.g. 0/120/240 deg). wavetype=sin, length = projector WIDTH in samples (one sample per column), numcycles = the fringe frequency, phase offsets the wave (phase in cycles: 0, 0.333, 0.667 for a 3-step). This is a 1-D sine along X, data-only, that choptoTOP will rasterize. Phase-shift fringes give the decoder sub-pixel column precision that binary gray-code alone cannot; the two are captured together (gray-code = coarse absolute stripe index, phase = fine within-stripe position).

key_params.numcycles: 16 (fringe frequency; higher = finer, must stay resolvable)

steps.geometry_out: 1-D sine along the projector width (one phase step)

verify.pass_if: single 'fringe' channel, length=width, numcycles sine, phase applied

steps.note: RASTERIZE the sine channel to an image. chop=OUT_sinchan, dataformat=r (mono luminance), layout=rowscropped -> a WIDTH x 1 texture holding the fringe. Then FILL HEIGHT: the W x 1 strip must cover the full frame as vertical fringes -- feed it to a levelTOP/constantTOP-composite with extend=repeat or a transformTOP scaled in Y (nearest filter) so every row is identical. Keep outputresolution=custom at native res and filter=nearest so the fringe is not vertically interpolated. Remap the sine's -1..1 to 0..1 via the patternCHOP torange (0..1) or a mathTOP so it is a displayable 0..1 fringe.
steps.geometry_out: full-frame vertical sinusoidal fringe (one phase step)

verify.pass_if: smooth vertical sine fringe filling the frame at native res

steps.note: REFERENCE FRAMES -- all-WHITE and all-BLACK (build two). Structured-light decoders need a fully-lit (white, color [1,1,1]) and fully-dark (black, [0,0,0]) capture to normalize ambient light and per-pixel albedo before decoding stripes. alpha 1, outputresolution=custom native res. These are two of the switch inputs and are usually captured first and last in the sequence.
steps.geometry_out: flat white and flat black reference frames

verify.pass_if: flat [1,1,1] and [0,0,0] frames at native res

steps.note: SEQUENCE CLOCK -- walk the pattern list as timed SEGMENTS, one segment per pattern (white, black, gray bit0..k + inverses, phase0/1/2). outseg=on emits a live 'segment' index = the current pattern; segmethod=serial plays them in order; per-segment length = the projector dwell (long enough for the camera to expose + settle). play=on free-runs; for CAMERA-LOCKED capture set a long dwell and advance manually with pulse(gotonextseg)/cuepulse so each pattern is held until the camera has grabbed it. Author the segment list with write_csv -> tableDAT (set file, then pulse(loadonstartpulse)) -> segdat, or a fixed per-segment length. The 'segment' channel is the spine that selects the current frame.

key_params.play: on (or hold and advance via pulse gotonextseg for camera lock-step)
key_params.cycle: off (one pass through the capture set)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP ('segment' pattern index + running/done)

verify.pass_if: 'segment' increments through the pattern count as it plays / on gotonextseg

steps.note: PATTERN SELECTOR -- the sequence output. Wire ALL pattern frames as inputs in capture order: white, black, gray bit0, bit0-inv, bit1, bit1-inv, ..., phase0, phase1, phase2. bind_chop the timerCHOP 'segment' channel onto this switch's `index` param (clean data-only drive -- no export-viewer gotcha) so the displayed frame follows the sequence clock. CRITICAL: extend=clamp, blend=OFF (a blended/dissolving frame is un-decodable), outputresolution=custom at NATIVE res, filtertype=nearest. This one node is the whole animated capture sequence.

key_params.blend: off (NEVER blend -- frames must be discrete)

steps.geometry_out: the current calibration pattern for this sequence step

verify.pass_if: switching 'segment' cycles white/black/gray-bits/phase frames, each crisp and discrete
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_pattern at segments 0..N -- the full white/black/gray-code/phase sequence renders in order at native res with hard edges

steps.note: STABLE NATIVE-RES FEED for wire-only output. Wire OUT_pattern -> this; keep filtertype=nearest, no resolution change. Downstream the projector output op is BUILT but armed OFF and handed off (windowCOMP specifydisplay NOT opened by us; ndioutTOP.active / st2110outTOP.active DEFAULT ON -> set OFF; videodeviceoutTOP not actuated) via direct_projector_output / output_handoff. The projector MUST show these 1:1 with scaling disabled -- any projector-side keystone/scaler re-interpolation also blurs the stripes.

key_params.filtertype: nearest (preserve crisp edges to the wire)

steps.geometry_out: native-res pattern feed, ready for wire-only projector output

verify.pass_if: native res, nearest filter, unscaled

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: synced camera capture + external decode/solve)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / EXTERNAL SPLIT LINE. Everything above (pattern GENERATION) is MCP-buildable. === The bridge projects the sequence; a CAMERA rigidly mounted relative to the projector must CAPTURE each frame in sync (trigger the camera per pattern, or dwell long enough per segment and grab), and an EXTERNAL structured-light SOLVER (e.g. an OpenCV gray-code/phase-shift decoder or a commercial projector-cal tool) turns the captured stack into a per-pixel projector<->camera correspondence and, with intrinsics, the surface geometry / projector calibration. The MCP cannot see the camera, cannot judge exposure, and cannot run the solve. WHAT THE MCP DOES: emits the exact pattern sequence at native res and advances it in lock-step (pulse gotonextseg). The captured images and the resulting geometry map return via the external pipeline; a computed keystone/warp can be typed back into cornerpinTOP/remapTOP downstream.

key_params.capture_sync: camera grab per pattern (or long per-segment dwell); advance with pulse @OUT_seqclock par=gotonextseg

steps.geometry_out: a projector<->camera correspondence + geometry, produced by the external solver

verify.pass_if: sequence advances one pattern per capture; decode/solve is external

steps.note: OPTIONAL DETERMINISTIC BAKE (WIRE-ONLY, record OFF). To replay an IDENTICAL sequence every session (so captures are comparable run-to-run), bake OUT_pattern to an image sequence: type=imagesequence, imagefiletype=png (lossless -- NEVER a lossy codec, it would soften stripe edges), file under the working dir. record DEFAULTS OFF and STAYS OFF here -- the bake is armed by the operator on a capture pass, not by the bridge. This is the structured-light analog of a pre-rendered pattern set.

key_params.record: off (WIRE-ONLY -- operator arms on the capture pass)

steps.geometry_out: (wire-only) a lossless pattern image sequence when armed

verify.pass_if: record=off (default); png lossless; path under working dir

recipes.classify: structured light / gray code / graycode / phase shift / phase-shift fringe patterns for AUTOMATIC projector camera calibration + geometry capture / scanning -- an animated timed SEQUENCE of binary stripe and sinusoidal patterns (plus white/black reference frames) beyond static alignment charts; projector camera correspondence, auto-calibration, 3D scan patterns
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY covers PATTERN GENERATION + SEQUENCING only. (1) MCP-buildable: the binary gray-code stripes (rampTOP repeat -> mathTOP integer=round, inverses via levelTOP invert), the sinusoidal phase-shift fringes (patternCHOP sin -> choptoTOP rasterize -> fill height), white/black reference frames (constantTOP), the timed sequencer (timerCHOP segments, list authored via write_csv -> tableDAT -> pulse loadonstartpulse), and the frame selector (switchTOP with index driven by bind_chop off the 'segment' channel -- no expressions, no callbacks). Advance is the allowlisted pulse actuator (timerCHOP gotonextseg/cuepulse) for camera lock-step. (2) HUMAN / EXTERNAL: a rigidly-mounted camera must capture each frame in sync, and an EXTERNAL solver (OpenCV gray-code/phase decoder or a commercial projector-cal tool) computes the projector<->camera correspondence + geometry -- the MCP neither sees the camera nor runs the solve. WIRE-ONLY OUTPUT: the projector output op is armed OFF and handed off (direct_projector_output / output_handoff); the optional moviefileoutTOP bake stays record=OFF. HONEST GAPS: there is NO dedicated structured-light / gray-code / phase-pattern operator in the catalog -- patterns are assembled from primitives (this recipe); a pixel-exact generator wants the gated GLSL lane (glsl_opportunity on the mathTOP step). CRISPNESS is the whole game: everything stays 1:1 native res with NEAREST filtering, no AA/mipmap/scaling, blend OFF -- any interpolation blurs stripe edges and the external decode fails. This is DISTINCT from test_pattern_generator (static grids/crosshatch/alignment charts). NC build render cap 1280 -- for real capture set native projector res on every node (previews downscale; keep the delivered feed native).
tips: Binary stripe in one move: rampTOP (horizontal, period=1/2^n, extend=repeat) -> mathTOP integer=round. round() thresholds the 0..1 ramp into a hard 50%-duty square wave -- no shader needed.
Number of gray-code bits = ceil(log2(projector_width)) to resolve every column (11 bits for 1920). Capture each bit AND its inverse for robust decoding.
Phase-shift needs >=3 phases (0/120/240 deg = phase 0/0.333/0.667) for a solvable 3-step; higher fringe frequency = finer precision but must stay resolvable by the camera.

CRISPNESS OR BUST: filtertype/inputfiltertype=nearest, antialias off, no mipmap, no resample, native res on EVERY node, switch blend=OFF. One bilinear/mipmap anywhere softens edges and the solve fails.
Drive the switch index with bind_chop off the timerCHOP 'segment' channel -- avoids the CHOP-export-needs-viewer-cook gotcha; a bound param just follows the channel.
Camera lock-step: hold a long per-segment dwell and advance with pulse @timer par=gotonextseg only after the camera has grabbed -- do not free-run faster than the capture.
Also project a flat WHITE and flat BLACK frame (constantTOP) -- decoders use them to normalize ambient light and albedo before reading stripes.
The projector itself must show these unscaled: disable any projector-side keystone/scaler/overscan, or it re-interpolates and blurs the stripes after TD sent them crisp.
variants: gray_code_only: white + black + gray bits + inverses (no phase) -- coarse per-stripe correspondence, simplest to decode; good for a quick projector-region map.
phase_shift_only: white + black + 3-12 phase-shifted fringes -- high sub-pixel precision within a continuous surface, but needs unwrapping; pair with a few gray bits to resolve absolute phase.
combined_graycode_phase: gray bits (coarse absolute stripe) + phase fringes (fine within-stripe) -- the standard high-accuracy set; the sequence here is authored for this.

two_axis: run the whole sequence once with horizontal stripes then again with VERTICAL stripes (rampTOP type=vertical / patternCHOP rasterized along Y) to solve both projector axes for full 2D correspondence.

prebaked_sequence: bake OUT_pattern to a lossless png image sequence (moviefileoutTOP, record armed on a capture pass only) so every calibration run projects a byte-identical set for comparable results.

recipes.title: Control a projector directly over PJLink (power / input / shutter / status) -- a tcpipDAT client to <ip>:4352 + the consent-gated device_send tool firing CLOSED-ALLOWLIST PJLink Class-1 tokens; async status replies read back via inspect
recipes.summary: Drive a real projector's OWN control protocol from the show: PJLink Class 1 over TCP (port 4352). Build a tcpipDAT client pointed at the projector's IP:4352, then fire allowlisted commands with the device_send utility tool -- power_on / power_off, input_* select, shutter_open / shutter_close (AV-mute), and read-only queries (power_query, lamp_query, input_query, error_status_query, name_query, ...). device_send is CLOSED-ALLOWLIST + CONSENT-GATED: it maps a fixed command TOKEN to the exact reviewed PJLink wire bytes (no caller string ever reaches the wire) and REFUSES unless allow_device_control is set in arm.json (default OFF, parity with allow_expr/allow_glsl). Query replies arrive ASYNCHRONOUSLY in the tcpipDAT rows -- read them with inspect. This is the projector-brain sibling of dmx_artnet_output (DMX fixtures). HONEST BOUNDARY: this is the ONE outbound-.send() path in the server; it needs (1) allow_device_control ON and (2) a REAL projector reachable at that IP -- the .send() round-trip is unprovable without hardware; and it is UNAUTHENTICATED PJLink Class 1 (RS-232 and PJLink auth are out of this first cut).

steps.note: PJLink TRANSPORT. Create a tcpipDAT as a CLIENT to the projector: mode=client, address=<projector IP>, port=4352 (the PJLink TCP port), active=on so it connects. This is the ONLY thing device_send will write to -- the tool refuses any target that is not a writable tcpipDAT. One tcpipDAT per projector; name them per fixture (proj_l, proj_r). Many projectors accept only ONE PJLink TCP connection at a time, so do not also point another controller at it. Leave callbacks / DAT-script params EMPTY (data-only).

key_params.active: on

steps.geometry_out: DAT: a live PJLink TCP client socket to the projector

verify.pass_if: tcpipDAT mode=client, address set, port=4352, active on

steps.note: POWER ON. device_send(op=OUT_pjlink, command='power_on') -- the executor emits the exact reviewed PJLink body (%1POWR 1) CR-terminated; the caller never supplies wire text. REFUSED unless allow_device_control=on in arm.json (default OFF; activates on re-arm) -- correct: do NOT enable consent just to author. Warm-up takes seconds; poll power_query until it reports on before selecting input. Show-start sequence: power_on -> (poll) -> input_* -> shutter_open.

key_params.command: power_on  (allowlist also: power_off, input_rgb1/rgb2, input_video1, input_digital1/digital2, input_network1, shutter_open/shutter_close, video_mute_on/off)

steps.geometry_out: projector receives the reviewed POWR 1 bytes (consent + hardware permitting)

verify.pass_if: with allow_device_control ON + a real projector the tcpipDAT shows the PJLink ack rows; without consent the tool refuses -- expected in authoring

steps.note: SELECT INPUT + OPEN SHUTTER. device_send(op=OUT_pjlink, command='input_digital1') routes the projector to its digital/HDMI 1 input (input_rgb1/rgb2, input_video1, input_digital1/digital2, input_network1 cover the PJLink INPT classes); device_send(op=OUT_pjlink, command='shutter_open') lifts AV-mute (shutter_close blanks it -- the projector-side blackout, complementary to emergency_blackout_and_standby's content-side kill). Each is a separate allowlisted call; token->physical-connector mapping is projector-specific.
steps.geometry_out: projector switches input / opens the shutter

verify.pass_if: input_query / mute_query echo the new state (real hardware)

steps.note: READ STATUS (read-only). Query tokens -- power_query, input_query, mute_query, lamp_query (lamp hours + on/off), error_status_query (fan/lamp/temp/cover/filter/other), name_query, manufacturer_query, product_query, other_info_query, class_query -- change NOTHING; their PJLink replies arrive ASYNCHRONOUSLY in the tcpipDAT rows a moment later. Fire the query, then inspect @OUT_pjlink to read the reply cells. lamp_query for lamp-life; error_status_query for a health watchdog (pair with show_health_watchdog).
steps.geometry_out: DAT rows: the projector's async PJLink reply (read via inspect)

verify.pass_if: after a query the tcpipDAT rows carry the projector's reply string (real hardware)

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: consent flag + real PJLink projector)
steps.note: === CONSENT + HARDWARE SPLIT LINE. === What the MCP does: builds the tcpipDAT client and fires the CLOSED-ALLOWLIST device_send tokens (reviewed wire bytes only). What a PERSON must do: (1) set allow_device_control=on in ~/.touchdesigner-bridge-mcp/arm.json (or the mcp_bridge Allowdevicecontrol toggle) and RE-ARM -- default OFF, stays off in authoring; (2) put a REAL PJLink projector on the network at that IP with PJLink/TCP enabled (many ship it off); (3) accept UNAUTHENTICATED PJLink Class 1 -- projector-side PJLink auth or RS-232 is out of this first cut. The .send() round-trip is the ONE thing unprovable without hardware -- flagged, not faked.

key_params.set (person, off-bridge): allow_device_control=on in arm.json, then re-arm; enable PJLink on the projector

steps.geometry_out: live projector control once consent is granted + hardware present

verify.pass_if: with consent ON + a real projector, power/input/shutter actuate and queries read back

recipes.classify: control a PROJECTOR directly -- power on/off, select input, open/close shutter (AV-mute), read lamp-hours / error / status; PJLink; projector device control; turn the projectors on for the show; projector health / lamp monitoring; device send
recipes.governance: CONSENT-GATED + HARDWARE. device_send is the server's ONLY outbound .send() and is modeled on the `pulse` allowlist: the caller picks a COMMAND TOKEN from a CLOSED reviewed set and the executor emits the exact reviewed PJLink bytes -- NO caller string reaches the wire, so there is no arbitrary-payload path. It REFUSES before touching anything unless allow_device_control is set in arm.json (default OFF; parity with allow_expr/allow_glsl; activates on re-arm). Data-only in spirit (fixed typed tokens, no code sink) but NOT wire-only -- it actuates real hardware, so it sits behind the extra consent flag. Target MUST be a writable tcpipDAT (the tool refuses any other optype). Scope: PJLink Class 1, UNAUTHENTICATED, over TCP:4352 -- RS-232 and PJLink auth are out of this first cut. HONEST LIMITS: (1) the .send() round-trip + reply parsing need a REAL projector, unprovable in authoring -- flagged not faked; (2) many projectors ship PJLink disabled and accept a single TCP control connection at a time; (3) input-token->physical-connector mapping is projector-specific. Completes the device-control matrix: DMX/Art-Net fixtures via dmx_artnet_output, the projector's own brain via PJLink here.
tips: device_send is CLOSED-ALLOWLIST: you pick a token, the executor owns the bytes -- there is no way to send an arbitrary PJLink string, by design.
Consent is real: allow_device_control defaults OFF and the tool refuses without it -- do NOT flip it on just to author; the operator arms consent on site.
Queries are async: fire the query token, then inspect @OUT_pjlink a moment later to read the reply rows -- device_send does not return the projector's answer inline.
One PJLink TCP connection per projector: don't point a second controller at the same IP:4352 while this tcpipDAT is connected.
shutter_close is a projector-side blackout (complements the content-side emergency_blackout_and_standby); error_status_query + lamp_query feed a projector health watchdog (show_health_watchdog).
variants: multi_projector: one tcpipDAT + control sequence per projector (proj_l, proj_r, ...); a show-start macro fires power_on across all, polls power_query, then input + shutter_open in lockstep.
health_poll: periodic lamp_query + error_status_query per projector, replies read via inspect, surfaced on an operator_control_panel / show_health_watchdog dashboard.
blackout_pairing: shutter_close on every projector as a hardware AV-mute alongside the content-side emergency_blackout_and_standby DBO -- belt-and-suspenders kill.

recipes.title: Frame-locked render cluster: shared timeCOMP timeline -> MASTER syncoutCHOP broadcasts a frame heartbeat over multicast -> each NODE's syncinCHOP gates its cook to the master -> engineCOMP hosts the per-node .tox content (clock=synced) -> nullTOP content tap -- SOFTWARE frame-sync across N machines, with genlock (Quadro Sync) as the honest HARDWARE boundary
recipes.summary: Drive one giant canvas (a very wide facade, a dome, an LED volume) from SEVERAL machines that each render a slice, and make every node cook the SAME frame at the SAME instant so the seams never tear or drift. The spine is a MASTER/NODE pair of sync CHOPs on a dedicated show LAN: on the master machine a syncoutCHOP broadcasts a per-frame heartbeat (plus any channels wired into its one input) to a multicastaddress:port group; on every node machine a syncinCHOP joins the SAME multicastaddress:port and GATES that machine's cook until the master's packet for the frame arrives, so all nodes advance in lockstep. timeout + timeoutunit set how long a node waits for the packet before it proceeds on its own (the 'maxwait' behaviour) -- too short and a slow node free-runs and drifts, too long and one stalled node stalls the whole wall. A shared timeCOMP gives the cluster a common transport (rate/tempo/range) that node content references, and each node hosts its slice of content in an engineCOMP running the show .tox in a separate process with clock=synced + matchrate=on so the engine's time follows the host node's synced clock rather than free-running. A nullTOP taps each node's rendered slice for wire-only handoff to that node's projector/output. CRITICAL HONEST BOUNDARY: syncin/syncout give SOFTWARE frame-sync (packet-gated cook) -- they do NOT give true GENLOCK. Genlock/framelock (all GPUs scanning out the exact same pixel-clock phase, required to kill tearing on hard-edged content and stereo) is a HARDWARE concern: matching Nvidia RTX/Quadro GPUs, Quadro Sync II cards daisy-chained with an optional house black-burst/tri-level reference, and Nvidia Control Panel / Mosaic setup, all provisioned and cabled by a person. The MCP builds the sync-CHOP + engineCOMP + timeline graph and sets the multicast group, roles and timeout; the human provisions identical hardware + identical project files per node, wires the genlock cards, assigns master vs node, and RUNS the cluster.

steps.note: THE SHARED SHOW TIMELINE = the common transport every node references so 'frame 4021' means the same beat on every machine. Create one timeCOMP and set rate to the show frame rate (e.g. 60), and the transport range (start/end, rangelimit=loop for a looping installation or hold for a one-shot show); tempo/signature if the content is beat-driven. Leave independent=OFF so this timeline follows the master TD timeline rather than free-running. On the MASTER this is the authored show clock; on each NODE the engineCOMP is set clock=synced so its content reads THIS shared time rather than its own. This is the numeric spine the frame-sync heartbeat keeps aligned -- syncin/syncout keep the COOK in step, the shared timeline keeps the CONTENT's notion of 'now' in step.

key_params.rate: 60 (the show frame rate -- must match on every node)
key_params.independent: off (follow the master TD timeline, not a free-running clock)

steps.geometry_out: COMP (the shared show transport: rate/range/tempo)

verify.pass_if: rate == the show fps; range set; independent off

steps.note: THE MASTER HEARTBEAT -- BUILT ON THE MASTER NODE ONLY. This CHOP broadcasts a per-frame sync packet to a multicast group that every node's syncinCHOP listens to; it is the 'everybody step now' pulse that keeps the cluster's cooks aligned. Set multicastaddress to the show sync group (default prefix 239.255.0.x -- pick ONE address the whole cluster shares) and port (default 15000, same on every machine). Its single input is OPTIONAL: wire a CHOP here (e.g. a control-channel bundle -- current cue, master transport seconds) and those channels ride the sync packet to every node, a clean data-only way to distribute show state alongside the heartbeat. WIRE-ONLY / ROLE POSTURE: active DEFAULTS ON; leave it OFF until the operator assigns THIS machine as the sync master (exactly the syncoutCHOP posture in direct_projector_output) -- two machines both broadcasting on the same group fight each other. timeout/timeoutunit here govern client-timeout bookkeeping; banclients OFF for a trusted show LAN. Only ONE syncoutCHOP (one master) per sync group.

key_params.active: off until the operator assigns THIS machine as sync master (DEFAULT ON)
key_params.multicastaddress: 239.255.0.1 (ONE shared show sync group for the whole cluster)
key_params.localaddress: the master's show-LAN NIC address (pin it if the machine is multi-homed)
key_params.(input): OPTIONAL -- wire a control-channel CHOP to ride the heartbeat to every node

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (the broadcast frame-sync heartbeat + optional distributed channels)

verify.pass_if: multicastaddress/port hold the shared group; active per the assigned master role (off in authoring)

steps.note: THE NODE LOCK -- BUILT ON EVERY NODE (INCLUDING, USUALLY, THE MASTER MACHINE ITSELF). This CHOP joins the SAME multicastaddress:port the master broadcasts on and GATES this machine's cook until the master's packet for the current frame arrives, so all nodes advance frame-for-frame together. multicastaddress + port MUST match OUT_syncmaster exactly or the node never locks. THE KEY TUNING PARAM is the wait behaviour: timeout + timeoutunit (default 0.5, unit=frames) = how long this node waits for the master packet before it gives up and cooks anyway. Set it long enough to absorb LAN jitter but short enough that one dead node cannot freeze the wall -- this is the 'maxwait' knob (note: the param is literally named 'timeout', there is no param called maxwait). active DEFAULTS ON; leave OFF until the operator confirms this machine is a follower on the assigned group. If the master feed drops, the node falls through after timeout and free-runs (it will visibly drift) -- pair with a health watch (reuse show_health_watchdog) to alarm on lock loss.

key_params.active: off until the operator confirms this machine as a follower (DEFAULT ON)
key_params.timeout: 0.5 (the 'maxwait' -- how long to wait for the master packet before cooking anyway)
key_params.localaddress: this node's show-LAN NIC address (pin if multi-homed)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (this node's cook, gated to the master frame -- the received heartbeat + distributed channels)

verify.pass_if: the node receives the master heartbeat (channels present, advancing); multicastaddress/port match the master; timeout set for the LAN
verify.milestone_check: with the master broadcasting on the group, OUT_synced advances in step with the master's frame -- two nodes read the same frame number at the same instant (software frame-lock achieved)

steps.note: HOST THIS NODE'S CONTENT SLICE in a separate engine process running the show .tox. Set file to the node's content .tox (an ABSOLUTE forward-slash path UNDER the working dir -- external/relative paths are blanked by path confinement). THE SYNC-CRITICAL PARAMS: clock=synced (default) so the engine's time is driven by THIS host node's clock (which is itself frame-locked by OUT_synced) rather than free-running -- clock=independent would let the slice drift; matchrate=on so the engine cooks at the host component rate. reloadoncrash=on so a node that faults reloads itself unattended. startoninit=on / oncompcreate=initialize so it comes up ready. Per-node addressing: each machine loads the SAME project but points its engineCOMP (or a parameter) at its own slice/region of the canvas -- that per-node offset is a human-provisioned config value, not something the MCP guesses. NOTE: 'initialize'/'start'/'launch'/'reload' are PULSE params that spin the engine process -- the bridge sets the toggles/paths but leaves firing the live launch to the operator's showtime step (wire-only posture).

key_params.clock: synced (engine follows the host node's frame-locked clock -- NOT independent)
key_params.matchrate: on (cook at the host component rate)
key_params.initialize/start/launch: PULSE -- the operator fires these to spin the engine process at showtime

steps.geometry_out: COMP (the node's content slice, hosted in a synced engine process)

verify.pass_if: file points at the node .tox; clock == synced; matchrate on; launch/initialize NOT pulsed in authoring

steps.note: STABLE PER-NODE CONTENT TAP. This node's rendered canvas-slice terminates here so the physical output (this machine's projector / LED feed) can be swapped without rewiring the sync + engine graph. Wire the engineCOMP's rendered output (OUT_nodecontent) into this. Hand off WIRE-ONLY to that node's output recipe (direct_projector_output for a perform window / Direct Display, led_wall_pixelmap_feed, st2110_ip_video_out, or output_handoff) -- terminal ops stay unactuated (windowCOMP not opened, ndiout/syphonspout .active forced OFF). The frame-sync graph guarantees this slice is the SAME frame every other node is showing; mapping/warp for this machine's surface lives after this tap.

key_params.(input): wire OUT_nodecontent (the node's rendered canvas slice) into this null

steps.geometry_out: TOP (this node's frame-locked canvas slice, ready for wire-only output)

verify.pass_if: holds this node's canvas slice at output resolution
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_aligned on two nodes at the same master frame -> the two slices are the matching halves of one coherent canvas (no drift, no tear across the seam)

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: identical hardware + per-node project provisioning + genlock cabling + assign roles + RUN the cluster)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HARDWARE + OPS SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable on ONE machine's project; NOTHING above provisions the fleet or achieves true genlock. === The cluster is stood up and run by a person: (1) IDENTICAL NODES -- matching GPUs (Nvidia RTX/Quadro of the same class), matching drivers, and BYTE-IDENTICAL project files distributed to every machine (a mismatched .tox on one node = a mismatched slice); (2) DEDICATED SHOW LAN -- a clean, low-jitter switch carrying only the sync multicast group + content, NICs pinned via localaddress; (3) TRUE GENLOCK is HARDWARE, distinct from the software frame-sync built above: Quadro Sync II cards in each machine, daisy-chained, optionally locked to a house black-burst / tri-level SYNC reference, configured in the Nvidia Control Panel + Mosaic to span outputs -- this is what removes tearing and phase-aligns the scan-out that syncin/syncout alone cannot; (4) ASSIGN ROLES -- pick ONE master (set its syncoutCHOP active=on), set every node's syncinCHOP active=on on the shared group, tune timeout for the measured LAN jitter; (5) RUN -- fire each engineCOMP's launch/initialize, open each node's output. The MCP cannot see GPUs, cable genlock cards, copy files between machines, or arm the fleet. If the operator changes the sync group / port / timeout on site, those measured values are typed back via set_par on OUT_syncmaster / OUT_synced.

key_params.human_owns: matching GPUs + drivers; byte-identical per-node project files; the dedicated show LAN; Quadro Sync genlock cards + house sync reference + Nvidia Control Panel/Mosaic; master/node role assignment; launching the engines + opening outputs
key_params.set_par (on site): op=OUT_synced, pars={active:on, timeout:<measured>} on each node; op=OUT_syncmaster, pars={active:on} on the one master

steps.geometry_out: a running, frame-locked (and, with Quadro Sync, genlocked) multi-machine canvas -- once hardware is provisioned and the operator arms the fleet

verify.pass_if: multicast group/port consistent across nodes; genlock + role assignment + fleet launch documented as the human handoff

recipes.classify: run a multi-machine render cluster / distributed rendering / render farm for one big canvas -- frame-lock / frame-sync / lockstep several TouchDesigner machines so a wide facade, dome, or LED volume never tears or drifts; syncoutCHOP master heartbeat + syncinCHOP node lock over multicast, engineCOMP per-node content, shared timeCOMP timeline; genlock / Quadro Sync / framelock across GPUs; the software frame-sync scaffold whose hardware genlock + identical-node provisioning is the human boundary
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY build, WIRE-ONLY + ROLE-GATED posture. The whole graph -- shared timeCOMP, syncoutCHOP master heartbeat, syncinCHOP node lock, engineCOMP synced content host, per-node nullTOP tap -- is created and parameterised with STATIC LITERALS via the create tools / set_par; no script/execute op, no parameter expressions, no callbacks DAT (syncinCHOP HAS a Callbacks DAT slot but this recipe leaves it EMPTY -- lock is packet-gated, not code). ROLE POSTURE: syncoutCHOP.active AND syncinCHOP.active both DEFAULT ON; the recipe builds them OFF and the operator turns on exactly one master + N followers once roles are assigned (two masters on one group fight). WIRE-ONLY: engineCOMP launch/initialize/start/reload are PULSE params the bridge never fires; per-node output ops (windowCOMP open, ndiout/syphonspout .active) are handed off inactive to direct_projector_output / led_wall_pixelmap_feed / st2110_ip_video_out / output_handoff. HONEST HARDWARE GAP -- the whole point: syncin/syncout are SOFTWARE frame-sync (they gate the COOK per frame) and do NOT provide true GENLOCK (phase-aligned GPU scan-out). Real genlock/framelock needs matching Nvidia RTX/Quadro GPUs + Quadro Sync II cards + optional house black-burst/tri-level reference + Nvidia Control Panel/Mosaic setup -- all hardware/OS steps a person performs; the MCP sets no hwframelock here (that lives on the per-node windowCOMP/directdisplayoutTOP in direct_projector_output). PROVISIONING is human: identical GPUs/drivers and byte-identical project files per node, a dedicated low-jitter show LAN, and the physical cabling. NC build cap renders live preview at 1280; the cluster's real per-node raster is set on the node's output op, independent of that preview cap.
tips: One master, many nodes: exactly ONE syncoutCHOP broadcasts a group; every machine (master included) runs a syncinCHOP joined to it. Two masters on one multicast group corrupt the lock.
multicastaddress + port MUST be identical on the syncoutCHOP and every syncinCHOP, and the group must be routable on the show switch (IGMP snooping configured, or a flat show LAN).

syncinCHOP.timeout is the 'maxwait': long enough to ride out LAN jitter, short enough that one dead node cannot freeze the wall. There is NO param literally named 'maxwait' -- it is timeout + timeoutunit.
engineCOMP clock=synced (not independent) is what ties the node's content time to the frame-locked host clock; independent lets the slice drift even while the cook is packet-synced.

Software frame-sync (syncin/syncout) != genlock. For tear-free hard-edged/stereo content you STILL need Quadro Sync hardware genlock (set hwframelock on the per-node windowCOMP/directdisplayoutTOP in direct_projector_output).
Pin localaddress on multi-homed machines so the sync traffic uses the dedicated show NIC, not the house/internet NIC.
Distribute BYTE-IDENTICAL project files to every node -- a one-line difference in a node's .tox is a mismatched canvas slice that no amount of frame-sync fixes.
Pair each syncinCHOP with a lock-loss alarm (reuse show_health_watchdog) -- when the master feed drops, a node falls through timeout and free-runs, visibly drifting; you want to know immediately.
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_cluster_node(role=master|node, group, port, timeout, tox, region) -> timeCOMP + sync CHOP (correct for the role, active OFF) + engineCOMP(clock=synced) + tap, in one call.
variants: master_node (the master machine also renders): the master runs BOTH a syncoutCHOP (heartbeat) and its own syncinCHOP/engine slice, so it contributes a canvas region as well as leading the clock.

distribute_show_state: wire a control-channel CHOP (current cue index, master transport seconds, global intensity) into the syncoutCHOP input so it rides the heartbeat to every node -- data-only distribution of show state alongside the frame lock.
dedicated_sync_only_group: use a separate multicastaddress for the sync heartbeat vs content streams (NDI/2110), so heavy content traffic never jitters the lock packets.

genlock_pair (hardware): add Quadro Sync II + set hwframelock on each node's windowCOMP/directdisplayoutTOP (via direct_projector_output) on top of the software frame-sync, for tear-free hard-edged or stereo content.

engine_farm_on_one_box: multiple engineCOMPs (each clock=synced) on a single powerful machine render separate slices in parallel processes, frame-locked to the host -- the single-box degenerate case of the cluster.

loss_failover: a logicCHOP on syncin lock presence -> switchTOP to a standby/hold graphic per node when the master heartbeat drops (reuse emergency_blackout_and_standby), so a lost lock fails to a safe frame rather than a drifting one.

recipes.title: disguise RenderStream closed loop: renderstreaminCHOP receives the schema (camera pose + projection + canvas) from disguise -> cameraCOMP driven data-only via projection=custommatrix + projmatrixop/xformmatrixop CHOP refs -> renderTOP renders TD content at the requested canvas res -> nullTOP tap -> renderstreamoutTOP sends frames BACK to disguise (active OFF); optional renderstreaminTOP composites disguise's own layers -- the standalone bidirectional disguise workflow, distinct from the multi-lane live_media_server_feed
recipes.summary: Make TouchDesigner a RENDER NODE inside a disguise show: disguise owns the stage model, the projectors, the mapping and the timeline, and it drives TD's virtual camera and canvas over RenderStream while TD renders content and streams the frames back for disguise to project. This is the STANDALONE, bidirectional disguise loop -- discoverable on its own -- where live_media_server_feed only exposes RenderStream as one send-lane among Spout/NDI/Touch Out and never closes the return loop. The loop has an IN half and an OUT half. IN: a renderstreaminCHOP joins the RenderStream network and receives the SCHEMA disguise publishes -- the requesting camera's transform + projection (disguise sends a full, often OFF-AXIS/asymmetric frustum for real projector geometry) and the requested canvas resolution; scene0name identifies which disguise-defined scene/stream this maps to and a Schema DAT can carry the field definitions. The camera is driven DATA-ONLY (the key improvement over the old 'needs matrix expressions' caveat): set the cameraCOMP projection=custommatrix and point projmatrixop at the projection-matrix CHOP and xformmatrixop at the transform-matrix CHOP sourced from the renderstreaminCHOP (shaped into the 16-value matrix layout with a data-only renameCHOP/shuffleCHOP if the schema exposes discrete pose channels instead of a ready matrix) -- a CHOP REFERENCE, not an expression. That camera renders the TD scene through a renderTOP at disguise's requested canvas resolution. OUT: a renderstreamoutTOP takes that rendered frame on its single input and streams it back to disguise on a streamindex, and (like every live-send op) it DEFAULTS active=ON so this recipe builds it active=OFF -- the operator arms the return stream once the disguise side is live. An optional renderstreaminTOP receives frames FROM disguise (its own notch/media layers) to composite before returning. HONEST BOUNDARY: RenderStream requires the disguise software stack (disguise Designer/d3 + the RenderStream asset/plugin registered so TD appears as a render node) and a working disguise machine on the network publishing the schema -- none of which the MCP supplies or sees.
