With no disguise peer, renderstreaminCHOP cooks no schema and the frustum stays default; the MCP builds the fully-wired, correctly-parameterised loop and the human provisions and runs disguise.

steps.note: THE IN HALF -- receive disguise's schema (the camera + canvas request). This CHOP joins the RenderStream network and receives, per frame, the requesting projector-camera's transform and projection plus the requested canvas dimensions. Set scene0name to the disguise scene/stream this node serves (the 'scene' sequence lets one node answer multiple disguise scenes); saveschemajson=on and pulse saveschemajsonpulse to dump the received field schema for inspection, or point scene0schemadat at a DAT holding the schema definition. streamindex selects which stream if disguise publishes several. overridenearfar + near/far let you clamp the depth range TD renders (leave off to honour disguise's planes). WIRE-ONLY POSTURE: active DEFAULTS ON; build it OFF until the disguise peer is present (same posture as live_media_server_feed) -- with no peer it cooks nothing. The channels here (the pose + projection) are what drive the camera next; do NOT read them with an expression -- reference them as CHOPs.

key_params.active: off until the disguise RenderStream peer is present (DEFAULT ON)
key_params.scene0name: the disguise scene/stream name this node serves
key_params.streamindex: 0 (which published stream, if disguise sends several)
key_params.saveschemajson: on (dump the received schema for inspection) + pulse saveschemajsonpulse
key_params.overridenearfar: off (honour disguise's near/far) | on + near/far to clamp TD's render depth

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (disguise's requested camera transform + projection + canvas res)

verify.pass_if: with a disguise peer live, the transform/projection/canvas channels are present and updating; without a peer, the node exists and is active=off
verify.milestone_check: with disguise publishing, OUT_rsschema carries a moving camera pose + a canvas-resolution channel that matches the disguise stream's configured raster

steps.note: THE RENDERSTREAM CAMERA -- driven DATA-ONLY from the schema (the crux, and the reason this is no longer 'expression-only'). disguise sends a full projection matrix, frequently an OFF-AXIS / asymmetric frustum matching a real projector's throw -- which the discrete fov/near/far params cannot express -- so use the matrix path: set projection=custommatrix and point projmatrixop at the projection-matrix CHOP, and set xformmatrixop to the camera transform CHOP, BOTH sourced from OUT_rsschema. These are CHOP REFERENCES (the 'Proj Matrix/CHOP/DAT' and 'Xform Matrix/CHOP/DAT' params), NOT parameter expressions -- fully inside the data-only surface. If the live schema exposes the matrices as a flat 16-value channel-set they wire straight in; if it exposes discrete pose/lens channels, reshape them into the expected matrix order with a data-only renameCHOP/shuffleCHOP first (still no expression). FALLBACK for a plain symmetric perspective stream: leave projection=perspective and EXPORT the schema's fov + t + r channels onto fov/tx.. /rx.. via set_flags export -- also data-only, but it will NOT reproduce an off-axis frustum, so prefer the custommatrix path for real projector geometry. Verify the rendered frame registers on disguise's surface before trusting the frustum.

key_params.projection: custommatrix (accept disguise's full, possibly off-axis, projection matrix)
key_params.projmatrixop: the projection-matrix CHOP from OUT_rsschema (Proj Matrix/CHOP/DAT ref -- NOT an expression)
key_params.xformmatrixop: the transform-matrix CHOP from OUT_rsschema (Xform Matrix/CHOP/DAT ref)
key_params.near: honour disguise (or set if overridenearfar was used upstream)
key_params.far: honour disguise (or set if overridenearfar was used upstream)

steps.geometry_out: COMP (a camera whose frustum tracks disguise's requesting projector-camera)

verify.pass_if: projection == custommatrix; projmatrixop / xformmatrixop reference the schema CHOP (no expressions on t/r/fov)

expr_opportunity.why: the matrix-CHOP path above is fully data-only and is the PREFERRED route; an expression lane is only wanted if you must algebraically DERIVE or blend the projection matrix (e.g. cross-fade between disguise's frustum and a locally authored one, or apply a per-node correction) rather than pass it through verbatim
expr_opportunity.propose_via: expr_reference to compose the matrix blend/correction, then set_expr on a helper CHOP/DAT feeding projmatrixop
expr_opportunity.consent: needs allow_expr (default OFF, owner-gated); NOT required for the standard pass-through loop, which ships data-only via the custommatrix + matrix-CHOP references

steps.note: RENDER THE TD SCENE THROUGH THE RENDERSTREAM CAMERA at disguise's requested canvas resolution. Set camera=OUT_rscam, geometry=<your scene's Geometry COMP(s)>, lights=<your Light COMP(s)> -- this is the content disguise will project (a facade animation, a volumetric scene, generative geometry). CRITICAL: match outputresolution=custom + resolution to the canvas size disguise requested in OUT_rsschema (a mismatch means disguise up/downscales your frame and the mapping softens) -- read the requested raster from the schema channel and set it here; if disguise changes the stream raster, retype it via set_par. Keep it a clean render (antialiasing as the scene needs). This TOP's image is the payload streamed back.

key_params.geometry: the scene Geometry COMP(s) to render for disguise
key_params.resolution: [canvas_w, canvas_h] -- MATCH the canvas res disguise requested in OUT_rsschema

steps.geometry_out: TOP (the TD content rendered through disguise's camera at the requested canvas res)

verify.pass_if: the scene renders through OUT_rscam at the disguise-requested resolution

steps.note: OPTIONAL -- receive frames FROM disguise to composite before returning (the other IN direction). disguise can send its OWN layers (media, notch blocks, other render nodes) into TD as an image via renderstreaminTOP; composite them with OUT_rsrender (compositeTOP/overTOP -- mind the compositeTOP input-0-on-top order) when TD is doing the final assembly rather than pure content generation. Set name/streamindex to match the disguise-published image stream. Set outputresolution=custom to the canvas res so it aligns with OUT_rsrender. active DEFAULTS ON; build OFF until the disguise peer is present. SKIP this step entirely for the common case where TD only GENERATES content and disguise does all compositing/mapping downstream -- add it only when disguise feeds imagery back for TD-side compositing.

key_params.active: off until the disguise peer is present (DEFAULT ON)
key_params.name: the disguise-published image stream name

steps.geometry_out: TOP (disguise's own layers received into TD for compositing)

verify.pass_if: with disguise sending an image stream, its frame arrives; otherwise the node exists active=off (skip if not compositing disguise layers)

steps.note: STABLE RETURN TAP. The finished frame to send back to disguise terminates here so the return stream can be re-pointed without rewiring the render. Wire OUT_rsrender (pure content) OR the composite of OUT_rsrender + OUT_rsimagein (TD-side assembly) into this. Confirm its resolution still matches the disguise-requested canvas. The renderstreamoutTOP reads THIS null.

key_params.(input): wire OUT_rsrender (or the OUT_rsrender + OUT_rsimagein composite) into this null

steps.geometry_out: TOP (the frame to return to disguise, at canvas res)

verify.pass_if: resolution matches the disguise-requested canvas; RGBA present

steps.note: THE OUT HALF -- stream the frame BACK to disguise, BUILT ACTIVE=OFF. Wire OUT_rsreturn into this TOP's single input. Set streamindex to the return stream disguise expects (0 for a single stream; increment for a multi-stream node). Set outputresolution=custom + resolution to the canvas res so disguise receives the exact raster it asked for. WIRE-ONLY / CRITICAL: active DEFAULTS ON and would start transmitting the instant it cooks, so CREATE it active=OFF and hold it off -- identical to the ndiout/syphonspout/st2110out posture; arming the return stream is the operator's step once the disguise show is live. Optionally point profilechop at a CHOP to report render timing back to disguise. This closes the loop: disguise drove the camera (IN), TD rendered, and this returns the frame (OUT).

key_params.active: off (build + hold OFF -- the operator arms the return once disguise is live; DEFAULT ON)
key_params.streamindex: 0 (the return stream disguise expects; increment for multi-stream)
key_params.profilechop: optional -- a CHOP reporting render timing back to disguise

steps.geometry_out: TOP (the return-to-disguise stream node, fully configured, NOT transmitting)

verify.pass_if: active == off; input wired to OUT_rsreturn; streamindex + resolution hold the intended values
verify.milestone_check: read_network @OUT_rsout -- the return stream is fully parameterised, fed by OUT_rsreturn, and ACTIVE=OFF (the closed loop, ready for the operator to arm once disguise is live)

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: the disguise software stack + registered RenderStream asset + arm the return)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / SOFTWARE + LICENSE SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable; NOTHING above works without a live disguise peer. === RenderStream is a disguise technology: a person must (1) run disguise Designer/d3 with a project whose stage/mapping defines the render stream(s), and REGISTER this TD project as a RenderStream asset so disguise launches/drives it as a render node (the RenderStream plugin/DLL must be present for TD -- an install-time step); (2) put the disguise machine and this TD machine on the same network so the schema publishes and the renderstreaminCHOP receives the camera + canvas; (3) confirm the scene/stream names and the canvas raster match between disguise and this node (scene0name / streamindex / resolution); (4) ONLY THEN arm the return by setting renderstreamoutTOP active=on. The MCP cannot install the RenderStream plugin, run disguise, register the asset, or see the schema peer, and by wire-only convention never arms the return. If the disguise operator changes the canvas raster or stream index on site, retype those via set_par on OUT_rsrender / OUT_rsout / OUT_rsschema. NOTE: with no disguise peer this loop is inert but VALID -- the frustum stays default and no frames transmit; that is the expected authoring state.

key_params.human_owns: disguise Designer/d3 + the show's stage/mapping; the RenderStream plugin installed for TD; this project registered as a RenderStream asset; the shared network; scene/stream names + canvas raster agreement; arming renderstreamoutTOP.active
key_params.set_par (after disguise confirms): op=OUT_rsout, pars={active:on} -- ONLY once the disguise peer is live and the schema is received

steps.geometry_out: a live bidirectional RenderStream loop -- once disguise is running, the asset is registered, and the operator arms the return

verify.pass_if: active stays off in authoring; the disguise stack + asset registration is documented as the human handoff

recipes.classify: run TouchDesigner as a disguise RENDER NODE over RenderStream -- the full bidirectional loop where disguise drives TD's camera + canvas and TD streams rendered frames back; disguise / d3 / RenderStream / render node / cluster render, renderstreaminCHOP schema (camera pose + off-axis projection + canvas res) driving a cameraCOMP via custommatrix, renderstreamoutTOP return stream (active OFF), optional renderstreaminTOP layer composite; the standalone disguise workflow distinct from the multi-lane live_media_server_feed
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY build, WIRE-ONLY posture, SOFTWARE-GATED. The whole loop -- renderstreaminCHOP (schema in), cameraCOMP (projection=custommatrix + projmatrixop/xformmatrixop CHOP references), renderTOP, optional renderstreaminTOP, return nullTOP, renderstreamoutTOP -- is created and parameterised with literals + CHOP references via the create tools / set_par / set_flags. The camera frustum is driven by CHOP REFERENCES (projmatrixop/xformmatrixop) or by EXPORT flags (fov/t/r for a symmetric fallback), NOT by parameter expressions: this recipe is fully inside the data-only surface and SUPERSEDES the older 'RenderStream camera needs matrix expressions' caveat noted in live_media_server_feed (the matrix-op path is the clean data-only route). No script/execute op, no callbacks DAT. WIRE-ONLY: every RenderStream I/O op DEFAULTS active=ON; renderstreaminCHOP / renderstreaminTOP are built active=OFF until the peer is present, and renderstreamoutTOP is built active=OFF and HELD off -- arming the return transmit is the operator's on-site step. HONEST SOFTWARE/LICENSE GAP: RenderStream requires the disguise software stack -- disguise Designer/d3 running the show, the RenderStream plugin installed for TD, and this project registered as a RenderStream asset so disguise drives it as a render node -- plus a live disguise peer on the network publishing the schema. None of that is MCP-suppliable or visible; with no peer the loop is inert but valid (default frustum, no frames transmit). The off-axis projection matrix's correctness can only be confirmed live against disguise's surface. NC build cap renders live preview at 1280; the actual canvas raster is set from the disguise schema on renderTOP/renderstreamoutTOP, independent of that preview cap.
tips: Use projection=custommatrix + projmatrixop for disguise's frustum -- it is usually OFF-AXIS/asymmetric (real projector throw), which discrete fov/near/far CANNOT express. The symmetric fov/t/r export path is a fallback only.
projmatrixop / xformmatrixop are CHOP REFERENCES, not expressions -- driving the camera this way stays inside the data-only surface (the reason this loop no longer needs the expression lane).
Match renderTOP + renderstreamoutTOP resolution to the canvas raster disguise requests in the schema; a mismatch makes disguise rescale your frame and softens the mapping.
Every RenderStream op defaults active=ON: build renderstreamoutTOP active=OFF and hold it; the operator arms the return once disguise is live (ndiout/syphonspout/st2110out convention).
scene0name / streamindex must match the disguise-side stream configuration, or renderstreaminCHOP receives the wrong (or no) schema.

If the live schema exposes discrete pose channels instead of a ready 16-value matrix, reshape with a data-only renameCHOP/shuffleCHOP into the matrix order projmatrixop expects -- still no expression.
Only add renderstreaminTOP when disguise feeds imagery BACK for TD-side compositing; for pure content generation (disguise composites/maps downstream) skip it.
With no disguise peer the loop is inert but VALID -- default frustum, no transmit. Do not mistake the inert authoring state for a broken graph.
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_renderstream_loop(scene, streamindex, geometry, lights) -> renderstreaminCHOP(off) + cameraCOMP(custommatrix) + renderTOP + renderstreamoutTOP(off) wired in one call.
variants: content_only (most common): renderstreaminCHOP -> cameraCOMP -> renderTOP -> renderstreamoutTOP; TD generates content, disguise does all compositing/mapping. No renderstreaminTOP.
td_side_composite: add renderstreaminTOP to receive disguise's own layers and compositeTOP them with the TD render before the return, when TD is the final assembler.

multi_stream_node: one node answers several disguise scenes -- multiple scene entries on renderstreaminCHOP and multiple renderstreamoutTOPs on incrementing streamindex, each rendered through its own schema-driven camera.

symmetric_perspective_fallback: for a plain symmetric stream, projection=perspective + EXPORT the schema fov/t/r onto the camera (set_flags export) -- data-only but will not reproduce an off-axis frustum.
profiled_return: point renderstreamoutTOP.profilechop at a timing CHOP so disguise sees this node's render performance and can balance the render cluster.
cluster_node: combine with machine_cluster_sync so several TD RenderStream nodes frame-lock to each other while disguise drives each one's camera -- a synced disguise render farm.

recipes.title: Depth-sensor presence + skeleton interaction: orbbecTOP/realsenseTOP/kinectazureTOP (image=depth) -> lumalevelTOP DEPTH GATE (inlow/inhigh window a near..far slab) -> blurTOP soft mask -> reveal via vision_interactive_mask; PLUS kinectazureCHOP world-space joints -> lagCHOP -> mathCHOP calibrate -> logicCHOP zones -> bind_chop onto reactive content -> OUT_aligned -- the true-3D depth lane, immune to projected light, distinct from plain-camera (vision_interactive_mask) and 2D laser (lidar_presence_interaction)
recipes.summary: Make the wall REACT to people using a true DEPTH sensor -- an Intel RealSense, an Orbbec Femto/Astra, or a Microsoft Azure Kinect -- which is the RIGHT presence source for a projection-mapping venue precisely because it is IMMUNE to light: the projectors blast the scene with changing content light that wrecks a plain-camera luma silhouette (the honest weak spot of vision_interactive_mask), whereas a depth camera measures DISTANCE and does not care what colour or brightness is being projected. Two capabilities stack. (1) THE DEPTH-GATE MASK (data-only core, any of the three sensors): a depth-image TOP feeds a lumalevelTOP whose inlow/inhigh WINDOW a physical near..far slab -- only pixels whose distance falls inside the interaction volume survive, so you get a clean foreground silhouette of whoever is standing in the zone, with threshold/soften/clamp shaping the edge; a blurTOP feathers it into a soft reveal mask. That mask then reveals generative content through the SAME matte/multiply reveal built in vision_interactive_mask (reuse it -- do NOT rebuild the reveal). (2) THE SKELETON DRIVER (the depth-unique value-add, Azure Kinect or Orbbec Femto via the Kinect Azure body-tracking path): a kinectazureCHOP reads its paired kinectazureTOP and emits per-player WORLD-SPACE joint positions -- real XYZ, which neither vision_interactive_mask (2D luma) nor lidar_presence_interaction (2D floor blobs) can give. A lagCHOP smooths the joint jitter, a mathCHOP RE-RANGES the raw metres into 0..1 projection UV (the sensor-to-canvas calibration, numbers a human measures on site -- reuse the calibration philosophy from lidar_presence_interaction), and a logicCHOP turns positions into zone/presence GATES. Those channels drive reactive content code-free via bind_chop -- e.g. a circleTOP spotlight whose centerx/centery follow a tracked hand joint. HARDWARE/SDK BOUNDARY (honest): each sensor needs its vendor SDK installed (Intel RealSense SDK, Orbbec SDK, or the Azure Kinect Sensor SDK), and body tracking additionally needs the Azure Kinect Body Tracking SDK + its ONNX model file (kinectazureTOP.modelpath) and a capable GPU; the sensor must be mounted, aimed and (like every device-in op) present or the node cooks nothing. The MCP builds the depth-gate + skeleton + calibration + bind graph; the human provides the sensor, the SDK, the model, the mount and the on-site calibration measurement.

steps.note: THE DEPTH SENSOR = the light-immune presence source. Pick ONE of three depending on the hardware on hand and set image=depth (the distance image the gate windows): realsenseTOP for Intel RealSense D4xx -- set model to the exact unit (d415/d435/d455...), image=depth (or depthalignedtocolor if you also use colour), maxdepth to the far edge of your interaction volume in metres, and LEAVE the built-in spatial/temporal/holefilling filters ON (this sensor's on-board depth cleanup is a real advantage for a stable mask). orbbecTOP is the Orbbec Femto/Astra equivalent (image=depth, depthalignmode=hardware|software, devicesource=auto or ipaddress+ip for a networked Femto). kinectazureTOP is the Azure Kinect (library=microsoft) OR an Orbbec Femto through the Azure path (library=orbbec), image=depth, depthmode=narrowunbinned (tight FOV, longer range) or wideunbinned (wide FOV) -- and it is the ONLY one of the three that also feeds the skeleton driver below. HARDWARE REALITY: no sensor / no vendor SDK => zero channels cooked (like every device-in op); build the graph against the node and swap the live sensor in. CRITICAL 256px trap: outputresolution=custom + resolutionw/h (the sensor's native depth res, e.g. 640x480 / 1280x720 -- it need not be 4K for tracking).

key_params.image: depth (the distance image the gate windows) | pointcloud | ir
key_params.model: d415 | d435 | d455 ... (realsenseTOP -- match the unit)
key_params.maxdepth: the far edge of the interaction volume in metres (realsenseTOP)
key_params.active: on (hardware-bound; no sensor => no cook)
key_params.resolution: [640,480] or [1280,720] (native depth res -- avoid the 256 trap)

steps.geometry_out: TOP (a live depth/distance image of the interaction volume)

verify.pass_if: with the sensor + SDK present, a depth image cooks (nearer surfaces read as a distinct luminance from the background); without hardware the node exists active=on and cooks empty

steps.note: THE DEPTH GATE = the light-immune silhouette, the data-only core. Window a physical near..far SLAB out of the depth image so only people standing in the interaction volume survive. source=luminance (or red -- depth is a single-channel distance encoded as brightness). Set inlow/inhigh to the normalized distances bounding the slab (nearer/farther than the slab map outside 0..1 and clip away), then threshold to knock the windowed region to a clean mask and soften for a feathered edge; clamplow/clamphigh keep it in 0..1. invert if your sensor encodes near as dark. The RESULT is a binary-ish foreground mask of whoever is inside the depth band -- and because it is built from DISTANCE, it is UNAFFECTED by the projected content light hitting the scene (the exact failure mode of a plain-camera luma silhouette). The inlow/inhigh values ARE the depth calibration -- a human sets them from the measured stand-off distance to the interaction zone.

key_params.inlow: near edge of the interaction slab (normalized distance)
key_params.inhigh: far edge of the interaction slab (normalized distance)
key_params.threshold: knock the windowed slab to a clean mask
key_params.invert: 1.0 if the sensor encodes near as dark

steps.geometry_out: TOP (a clean foreground presence mask of people inside the depth slab)

verify.pass_if: a person standing in the slab shows as a solid silhouette while the background (and projected light) is rejected
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_depthmask with content projecting on the scene -> the silhouette is unchanged by the projected light (the depth advantage over vision_interactive_mask's luma silhouette)

steps.note: SOFTEN the mask into a clean reveal edge. A small blur (size ~ a few px) removes depth-sensor speckle at the silhouette boundary and gives a gradient the reveal can feather against, killing the hard aliased edge a raw depth threshold produces. Keep it modest -- over-blurring smears the presence boundary and makes the interaction feel laggy. Set outputresolution=custom to match OUT_depthmask (256 trap). This soft mask is what the content reveal multiplies against.

key_params.size: a few px (despeckle the silhouette edge; do not over-blur)

steps.geometry_out: TOP (the soft-edged presence mask)

verify.pass_if: the silhouette has a soft feathered edge with no hard speckle

steps.note: CROSS-REFERENCE -- do NOT rebuild the reveal. The soft presence mask (OUT_presencemask) plugs straight into the matteTOP/multiplyTOP reveal already built in vision_interactive_mask: it reveals generative_texture_fx content through the person's silhouette (touch-to-reveal, shadow-play, presence bloom), and its MOTION-ENERGY and centroid variants apply here too. THE ONLY DIFFERENCE is the mask SOURCE -- this recipe supplies a depth-gated, light-immune mask instead of a plain-camera luma mask, which is strictly cleaner in a projection-mapping venue. Reuse that recipe's reveal block; this recipe's contribution is the depth mask (above) and the skeleton driver (below), not a duplicate reveal.

key_params.relationship: vision_interactive_mask owns the matte/multiply REVEAL; this recipe supplies a cleaner depth-gated MASK source into it

steps.geometry_out: (reference -- reuse the vision_interactive_mask reveal, fed by OUT_presencemask)

verify.pass_if: the reveal block is reused (not rebuilt) with OUT_presencemask as its mask input

steps.note: THE SKELETON DRIVER = the depth-unique value-add (Azure Kinect, or Orbbec Femto via library=orbbec on the kinectazureTOP). This CHOP reads BODIES from its paired sensor: set top = the kinectazureTOP (OUT_depth if that is the Azure/Femto node) so it tracks against that sensor's stream. worldspace=on (default) emits per-player joint positions in real-world XYZ metres -- the capability NEITHER vision_interactive_mask (2D luma) NOR lidar_presence_interaction (2D floor blobs) can provide. maxplayers sets how many skeletons to track. Enable confidence for per-joint reliability (drop low-confidence joints), imuchans if you need the sensor's own orientation. The output channels are per-player, per-joint tx/ty/tz you can drive anything with. HARDWARE/SDK GATE: body tracking needs the Azure Kinect Body Tracking SDK installed AND the ONNX model file set on the kinectazureTOP (modelpath) AND a capable GPU (proccessingmode=gpudefault or directml on the TOP); with those absent it tracks nothing even if the depth image cooks. SKIP this whole skeleton half if you only need the presence mask (RealSense/Orbbec depth-gate) and do not have an Azure/Femto body-tracking rig.

key_params.top: OUT_depth (the kinectazureTOP the bodies are tracked from)
key_params.worldspace: on (per-joint real-world XYZ metres -- the 3D advantage)
key_params.confidence: on (per-joint reliability -- gate out low-confidence joints)
key_params.active: on (hardware + Body Tracking SDK + model bound)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (per-player, per-joint world-space XYZ positions)

verify.pass_if: with a body-tracking rig live, per-player joint tx/ty/tz channels are present and move with the person; otherwise skip this half

steps.note: SMOOTH the joint jitter. Raw depth-derived joints (and the mask centroid) are noisy frame-to-frame; a lagCHOP low-passes the position channels so the driven content glides instead of stuttering. Tune the lag so it feels responsive but not laggy (a small amount hides sensor noise; too much makes the interaction feel underwater). Feed OUT_joints (or a selected subset -- e.g. just the two hand joints) in. This is the same smoothing role lagCHOP plays in lidar_presence_interaction.

key_params.lag: a small smoothing amount (hide sensor jitter without making the interaction feel laggy)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (smoothed joint / centroid positions)

verify.pass_if: the position channels are smooth and still track the person with acceptable latency

steps.note: CALIBRATE sensor-space -> canvas UV = the sensor-to-projection mapping. The joints arrive in the sensor's real-world metres (or the mask centroid in sensor pixels); a mathCHOP RE-RANGES them into 0..1 projection UV so a position in the room maps to the right place on the wall: set fromrange to the measured min/max extent of the interaction zone in sensor units and torange to [0,1] (or to canvas pixels). gain/preoff/postoff apply any flip or offset. THESE NUMBERS ARE HUMAN-MEASURED on site -- where the sensor is mounted and how its volume lands on the real surface -- exactly as in lidar_presence_interaction; the recipe supplies the compute frame, the human supplies the measured extents. Until calibrated, the mapping is meaningless (a person at stage-left may light up stage-right).

key_params.fromrange: [min,max] measured extent of the interaction zone in sensor units
key_params.preoff: offset applied before gain (recentre the zone)

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (positions in 0..1 projection UV -- calibrated to the wall)

verify.pass_if: a person at a known spot in the room produces the matching 0..1 UV (hand-checked against the measured calibration)

steps.note: ZONE / PRESENCE GATES (optional -- triggers, not just continuous position). Turn the calibrated positions (or the mask coverage) into discrete GATES: logicCHOP convert=bound emits 1 while a coordinate sits inside a [min,max] zone window, so you can light a region only when someone stands in it, count occupants, or fire a cue on entry. Combine several bound gates for multi-zone floors/walls. This is the same zone-gate pattern as lidar_presence_interaction -- reuse it. The gate channels drive switches/triggers downstream; the continuous UV (OUT_uv) drives followers.

key_params.convert: bound (1 while the coordinate is inside the zone window)
key_params.bound (low/high): the zone's min/max in calibrated UV
key_params.combine: AND/OR several zones for multi-region logic

steps.geometry_out: CHOP (per-zone presence gates)

verify.pass_if: a gate reads 1 exactly while a person is inside its zone and 0 otherwise

steps.note: DRIVE REACTIVE CONTENT CODE-FREE. bind_chop binds a content parameter directly to a tracked channel with a live two-way link (data-only, no expression, no callback): the cleanest example is a circleTOP 'spotlight' whose centerx/centery are bound to a hand joint's calibrated UV (OUT_uv) so a pool of light FOLLOWS the visitor; a feedbackTOP adds trails; a zone gate (OUT_zones) bound to an opacity/switch reveals a region on entry. Bind the smoothed, calibrated channels (OUT_uv / OUT_zones), NOT the raw joints, so the content moves cleanly. This is the same bind_chop drive used in lidar_presence_interaction and choreography recipes.

key_params.target: the content parameter to drive (e.g. circleTOP centerx/centery, a level/opacity)

steps.geometry_out: reactive content parameters driven live by presence/skeleton

verify.pass_if: the bound parameter tracks the person's calibrated position / zone in real time

steps.note: STABLE INTERACTIVE-CONTENT TAP. The reactive content (mask-revealed generative + follower/zone-driven elements) terminates here so the physical output swaps without rewiring the sensor graph. Wire the composited reactive result into this. Hand off WIRE-ONLY to projection_align_and_output / output_handoff / direct_projector_output -- terminal ops stay unactuated. The sensor drives the CONTENT; mapping/warp onto the real surface lives after this tap.

key_params.(input): wire the composited reactive content into this null

steps.geometry_out: TOP (the depth-driven interactive content, ready for wire-only output)

verify.pass_if: holds the reactive content at canvas res
verify.milestone_check: save_top @OUT_aligned while a person moves through the volume -> the content reveals/follows their real position, unaffected by the projected light

steps.tool: (HUMAN BOUNDARY: sensor + vendor SDK + body-tracking model + mount/aim + on-site calibration)
steps.note: === DATA-ONLY / HARDWARE + SDK SPLIT LINE. Everything above is MCP-buildable; NOTHING above works without the physical sensor and its software. === A person owns: (1) the SENSOR -- a RealSense D4xx, Orbbec Femto/Astra, or Azure Kinect, physically MOUNTED and AIMED over the interaction zone (mount height/angle set the usable volume); (2) the VENDOR SDK installed on the machine -- Intel RealSense SDK, Orbbec SDK, or the Azure Kinect Sensor SDK -- without which the device-in TOP cooks nothing; (3) for SKELETON tracking additionally the Azure Kinect Body Tracking SDK + its ONNX model file (set kinectazureTOP.modelpath) + a capable GPU (proccessingmode gpudefault/directml); (4) the ON-SITE CALIBRATION -- the measured near/far slab distances (the lumalevelTOP inlow/inhigh) and the sensor-to-canvas extents (the mathCHOP fromrange/torange), which map the physical volume onto the real surface. The MCP cannot mount hardware, install an SDK, supply the model file, or measure the room. WHAT THE MCP DOES: builds the depth-gate mask + skeleton driver + calibration + bind graph and sets every param; the human provides the sensor, software, model, mount and measurements, and tunes the calibration values via set_par on OUT_depthmask (inlow/inhigh) and OUT_uv's mathCHOP (fromrange/torange) on site.

key_params.human_owns: the depth sensor + mount/aim; the vendor SDK; (skeleton) the Body Tracking SDK + ONNX model + GPU; the measured slab distances (inlow/inhigh) and sensor-to-canvas extents (fromrange/torange)
key_params.set_par (on site): op=OUT_depthmask, pars={inlow, inhigh}; and the OUT_uv mathCHOP fromrange/torange -- from the measured calibration

steps.geometry_out: a live depth-driven interactive install -- once the sensor, SDK, (model) and calibration are provided

verify.pass_if: the depth graph is built and parameterised; sensor + SDK + model + calibration are documented as the human handoff

recipes.classify: make the wall react to people with a true DEPTH sensor -- depth-camera presence / silhouette / skeleton interaction, RealSense / Orbbec Femto/Astra / Azure Kinect (image=depth), a depth-gate mask that is IMMUNE to projected light (unlike a plain camera), plus per-player world-space skeleton joints (Azure/Femto body tracking) driving followers and zone gates via bind_chop; the true-3D interactive lane, distinct from plain-camera (vision_interactive_mask) and 2D laser-scanner (lidar_presence_interaction)
recipes.governance: DATA-ONLY build, HARDWARE + SDK GATED. The whole graph -- depth-sensor TOP (image=depth), lumalevelTOP depth gate, blurTOP soft mask, kinectazureCHOP skeleton, lagCHOP/mathCHOP/logicCHOP calibration + zones, bind_chop drive, nullTOP tap -- is created and parameterised with STATIC LITERALS via the create tools / set_par; the content drive is a bind_chop LINK (data-only), NOT an expression or callback. The reveal itself is REUSED from vision_interactive_mask (matte/multiply), not rebuilt here -- this recipe's contribution is a cleaner, light-immune depth mask SOURCE plus the true-3D skeleton driver. WIRE-ONLY: the interactive content is handed off inactive to projection_align_and_output / output_handoff / direct_projector_output. HONEST HARDWARE/SDK GAPS: (a) each sensor is a device-in op -- no sensor / no vendor SDK (Intel RealSense SDK, Orbbec SDK, or Azure Kinect Sensor SDK) => zero channels cooked; (b) SKELETON tracking (kinectazureCHOP) is Azure-Kinect / Orbbec-Femto ONLY and additionally needs the Azure Kinect Body Tracking SDK + its ONNX model file (kinectazureTOP.modelpath) + a capable GPU (proccessingmode gpudefault/directml) -- RealSense/Orbbec-via-orbbecTOP give the depth-gate mask but NOT this skeleton; (c) the depth calibration (lumalevelTOP inlow/inhigh) and the sensor-to-canvas mapping (mathCHOP fromrange/torange) are HUMAN-measured on site and meaningless until set; (d) the sensor must be physically mounted and aimed. blobtrackTOP's per-blob TABLE and any AI-segmentation remain out-of-surface (callbacks = code); this recipe's per-player skeleton via kinectazureCHOP is the data-only path to multi-person tracking. NC build cap renders live preview at 1280; the real canvas raster is set on the output op downstream, independent of that cap.
tips: Choose the sensor by need: RealSense = cleanest on-board depth filtering for a stable MASK; Azure Kinect / Orbbec Femto = the only path to SKELETON joints; Orbbec (orbbecTOP) = networked (ip) depth without body tracking.

The depth gate's whole point: a mask built from DISTANCE (lumalevelTOP inlow/inhigh on the depth image) is UNAFFECTED by the projected content light -- this is why depth beats a plain camera (vision_interactive_mask) in a projection-mapping venue.
inlow/inhigh ARE the depth calibration -- set them from the measured near/far stand-off to the interaction zone; too wide and background bleeds in, too tight and people at the zone edge drop out.
worldspace=on gives real XYZ metres per joint -- the true-3D advantage over 2D luma (vision_interactive_mask) and 2D floor blobs (lidar_presence_interaction).

Skeleton tracking needs the Body Tracking SDK + the ONNX model on kinectazureTOP.modelpath + a GPU (proccessingmode=directml if no CUDA); with those absent the depth image still cooks but bodies do not.
Always smooth (lagCHOP) and calibrate (mathCHOP fromrange->torange) BEFORE bind_chop -- bind the clean UV/zone channels, never the raw jittery joints.

Reuse, don't rebuild: the reveal is vision_interactive_mask's matte/multiply; the zone-gate + calibration philosophy is lidar_presence_interaction's -- this recipe just supplies a better mask + skeleton.
Every depth-in op is a device op with active=on default -- with no hardware it cooks nothing (not an error); build against the node and swap the live sensor in.
HELPER CANDIDATE: build_depth_presence(sensor=realsense|orbbec|azure, slab=[near,far], skeleton=on|off, zones=[...]) -> depth TOP + gate + mask (+ skeleton + calibration + zones) in one call.
variants: mask_only (RealSense/Orbbec, no body tracking): depth TOP -> lumalevelTOP gate -> blurTOP -> vision_interactive_mask reveal; the light-immune silhouette with no skeleton rig required.
skeleton_follower (Azure/Femto): kinectazureCHOP hand joint -> lag -> math -> bind_chop onto a circleTOP spotlight, so a pool of light follows each visitor's hand in true 3D.
multi_person_zones: maxplayers > 1 + per-player logicCHOP bound gates -> independent content per occupant / per floor zone (multi-user interactive floor).
pointcloud_content: set the sensor image=pointcloud to feed the point-cloud content lane (point_cloud_content) instead of a 2D mask -- the depth camera as a live scan source.
playerindex_matte (Azure): kinectazureTOP image=playerindex gives a per-person segmentation index directly, an alternative clean multi-person matte source into the reveal.
networked_orbbec: orbbecTOP devicesource=ipaddress + ip for a Femto over the network, when the sensor cannot be USB-tethered to the render machine.

depth_motion_energy: difference successive depth frames (reuse vision_interactive_mask's cache/feedback/difference motion block) on the depth image for a light-immune MOVEMENT field instead of a static presence mask.

routing_note: The router is the front door: classify=<what you have / what you want to do> -> a lane -> its entry_recipe. Then call recipe=<entry_recipe> for the ordered, verifiable steps. axis=content-source rows are reached by classifying the input you were handed (a model, a scan, a brief for abstract content); axis=task-intent rows (camera framing, output hand-off) are invoked as a task on content you already have. Every recipe plants OUT_ null taps and verifies each step (top_info/save_top/read_network); output steps are WIRE-ONLY.
